title: Project and engine paths
content:
All paths are on the user's Windows machine.

- Project root: <project>
- Game code: <project>\Code\Components\{Player,Npc}.{h,cpp}, Code\GamePlugin.cpp, Code\CMakeLists.txt
- Level: <project>\Assets\levels\example\example.level
- Layer (all placed objects + entities): <project>\Assets\levels\example\layers\main.lyr
- Materials: <project>\Assets\materials\*.mtl (each with a sibling .cryasset)
- AI agent types: <project>\Assets\scripts\AI\Navigation.xml
- Tooling and docs: <project>\
- Engine install: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CRYENGINE Launcher\Engines\crytek\cryengine-57-lts\5.7.1
- Full engine SOURCE (read-only reference): <engine source checkout>
- Scratch, logs, screenshots, helper scripts: <engine source checkout>*.{log,txt,py,bmp}

Engine version is CRYENGINE 5.7.1 LTS. The project started from the "Blank" template.

title: Moving files between the container and the Windows machine
content:
Both <engine source checkout> and the project folder are connected folders, so
device_stage_files (Windows -> container) and device_commit_files (container -> Windows)
reach them.

device_commit_files only accepts staged paths under /mnt/user-data/outputs/.

There is no device_bash in this setup. The only way to run a process on the Windows
machine is through Sandbox's Python interpreter (cryengine__execute_python), which can
subprocess.Popen a detached process.

title: The three command registries (and why a command seems missing)
content:
CRYENGINE Sandbox has THREE separate command registries that do not overlap. Picking the
wrong one is the most common time-waster; a command absent from one is usually present in
another.

1. IConsole - CVars and true console commands.
   Tool: cryengine__run_console_command
   Examples: e_TimeOfDay 15, ai_DebugDraw 1, r_DeferredShadingEnvProbes 0,
   claude_player_walk 6

2. ICommandManager - the "module.command" namespace registered via
   REGISTER_EDITOR_AND_SCRIPT_COMMAND / REGISTER_PYTHON_COMMAND.
   Tool: cryengine__execute_editor_command
   Examples: asset.edit levels/example/example.level, general.save_level,
   game.toggle_game_mode, ai.regenerate_agent_type_all, ai.show_navigation_areas

3. Sandbox's Python interpreter - REGISTER_ONLY_PYTHON_COMMAND_WITH_EXAMPLE.
   Tool: cryengine__execute_python
   Examples: general.new_object, general.get_current_level_name,
   general.get_current_view_position, plus arbitrary Python (file I/O, subprocess)
   running ON the Windows machine.

execute_editor_command returning ok:true only means the command did not throw. An unknown
object typeName just logs a warning and silently no-ops - always check the "log" field.

title: The ClaudeBridge raw socket and its verbs
content:
The ClaudeBridge Sandbox plugin listens on 127.0.0.1:37778 and speaks newline-delimited
JSON: send {"id":1,"cmd":"<verb> <args>"}\n, read one line back.

Verbs (from ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp, which lives at
<engine source checkout>):

  bridge.camera.get / bridge.camera.set / bridge.camera.look_at
  bridge.cvar_get / bridge.cvar_set
  bridge.entities.list / bridge.entities.teleport
  bridge.env.list / bridge.env.set / bridge.env.time
  bridge.execute_command / bridge.execute_python / bridge.execute_python.b64 / .raw
  bridge.file.read_b64 / bridge.file.write_b64
  bridge.input.click / .drag / .scroll / .key / .text / .move
  bridge.object.create / .delete / .list / .material / .select / .transform / .types
  bridge.terrain.* (generate_height, get_heights_raw, set_heights_raw, info,
                    list_layers, select_layer, set_layer_texture, set_layer_params,
                    generate_surface_texture, delete_layer)
  bridge.vegetation.add / .clear / .list / .paint / .place
  bridge.viewport.screenshot
  bridge.window.list

Argument forms seen in use:
  bridge.camera.look_at <eyeX> <eyeY> <eyeZ> <targetX> <targetY> <targetZ>
  bridge.viewport.screenshot settle=<ms> <absolute/out/path.bmp>
  bridge.input.click <x> <y>            (coordinates are MAIN-WINDOW-RELATIVE)
  bridge.env.time <hours>
  bridge.cvar_set <name> <value>

title: Screenshots and input work while the main thread is blocked
content:
bridge.viewport.screenshot and bridge.input.* are handled OUT OF BAND by the plugin -
they still respond while Sandbox's main thread is blocked.

This is the mechanism that makes modal dialogs survivable: you dispatch the blocking
command from one process and the window-list + click from a second process, both talking
to the bridge at the same time. Everything else (bridge.execute_command,
bridge.execute_python, most of the MCP tools) queues behind the main thread and will time
out with "the main thread is genuinely blocked, not merely not drawing".

title: TRAP: execute_python collapses whitespace, breaking indentation
content:
cryengine__execute_python collapses runs of whitespace somewhere in transit, so any
indented multi-line Python arrives with its indentation flattened and fails with
"IndentationError: expected an indented block". Literal \n inside a string does not help -
the leading spaces after it are collapsed too.

Working pattern - one physical line, indentation carried by a placeholder character:

    exec("\n".join(s.replace('~','    ') for s in [
        "import os",
        "for root, dirs, files in os.walk(p):",
        "~for f in files:",
        "~~if f.endswith('.cpp'):",
        "~~~print(f)",
    ]))

The same trick is needed when WRITING a Python file to disk from execute_python: build the
file content through the same replace, or the file itself lands unindented.

title: TRAP: sys.executable inside Sandbox is Sandbox.exe
content:
Inside Sandbox's embedded Python, sys.executable is Sandbox.exe, NOT python.exe.

Launching a helper script with it starts a SECOND EDITOR and pops a modal:
"CRYENGINE Sandbox is already running - Do you want to open a new instance anyway?"
The script never runs, the log stays empty, and the dialog blocks the user.

The real interpreter is:
    %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python311\python.exe

If it happens: the spawned process can be killed with a detached taskkill
(subprocess.Popen(['taskkill','/PID',str(pid),'/T','/F'], creationflags=0x8|0x200)),
which also dismisses the dialog. ctypes TerminateProcess was tried and returned 0.

title: TRAP: never block the editor main thread from execute_python
content:
Code run through execute_python executes ON Sandbox's main thread. Anything synchronous
and slow deadlocks the bridge for its whole duration:

- subprocess.run(...) or any socket round-trip back into the bridge: instant deadlock.
- os.walk over a large tree: an os.walk of the engine source froze the editor for about a
  minute and returned "timed out waiting for the editor main thread". It recovers on its
  own; wait rather than restarting anything.

Always dispatch detached:
    subprocess.Popen([...], creationflags=0x8|0x200)   # DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NO_WINDOW

For searching the engine source, use the detached helper claude_grep.py rather than
walking trees in-process.

title: TRAP: device_commit_files appears to cache by stagedPath
content:
Committing a CHANGED file from the SAME stagedPath silently wrote the OLD bytes. It
happened twice in one session and cost two full build cycles: the build log kept showing
an error on a line that had already been fixed.

Rules:
1. Stage every re-commit under a NEW filename: Npc_v2.cpp, Npc_v3.cpp, Player_v2.cpp.
   The devicePath stays the same; only the staged name changes.
2. Verify on the device before building:
     exec("\n".join(s.replace('~','    ') for s in [
       "import os",
       "p=r'C:\\...\\Npc.cpp'",
       "t=open(p,errors='replace').read()",
       "print(os.path.getsize(p), 'some_new_marker' in t)"]))
3. Compare the byte size against the container copy. A size that matches the PREVIOUS
   version is the tell.

title: TRAP: CryLog output cannot be read from outside the running editor
TRAP: warnings are errors in this build
content:
The Game project builds with warnings-as-errors. A C4244 int->float narrowing killed a
build (Player.cpp calling GetTerrainZ((int)x,(int)y)).

Write explicit casts: (float)i, (int)m_waypoints.size(). Prefer
gEnv->p3DEngine->GetTerrainElevation(float x, float y) over GetTerrainZ(int, int).

title: TRAP: IConsole::AddCommand is protected - use REGISTER_COMMAND
content:
gEnv->pConsole->AddCommand(...) does not compile:
  error C2248: 'IConsole::AddCommand': cannot access protected member declared in class 'IConsole'

The public path is the macro in CrySystem/ConsoleRegistration.h:

    #include <CrySystem/ConsoleRegistration.h>
    ...
    REGISTER_COMMAND("claude_player_walk", CmdPlayerWalk, VF_NULL,
                     "Walk forward for N seconds and write a per-frame trace");

which expands to ConsoleRegistrationHelper::AddCommand - a friend of IConsole. Guard the
registration with a static bool so re-entering game mode does not register twice.

title: Building Game.dll (scheduled task, because the DLL is locked)
content:
Game.dll is locked while Sandbox runs, so the build must close the editor first. That is
wrapped in a Windows Scheduled Task so it survives the editor being killed:

    import subprocess
    subprocess.Popen(['schtasks','/Run','/TN','ClaudeGameBuild'],
                     creationflags=0x8|0x200)

<engine source checkout> does:
  taskkill Sandbox -> wait for exit ->
  cmake --build "<project>/solutions/win64" --target Game --config Profile ->
  restore projects.json -> copy the DLL -> relaunch Sandbox -> release the deploy lock.

Output: <engine source checkout>

title: ALWAYS read the build log - a failed build still relaunches Sandbox
content:
The build batch relaunches Sandbox whether the build succeeded or not. "The editor came
back" is NOT evidence that the build worked.

Always read <engine source checkout> and look for:
    --- cmake --build exit code 0 ---
A non-zero exit code with "--- relaunched Sandbox ---" right after it means you are about
to test the OLD DLL.

title: Timing budget for a code iteration
content:
Per full code iteration, end to end, roughly 4 minutes:

  build (cmake, incremental)            ~8 s
  Sandbox relaunch + splash             ~60-90 s
  reopen level (asset.edit)             ~10-20 s
  regenerate navmesh (+ modal click)    ~30-55 s
  enter game mode + observe             ~20-25 s

Because of this, make each build carry as much instrumentation as possible rather than
iterating one question at a time. Two builds were burned in this session on a commit that
silently wrote stale bytes, and one on a logging threshold that was set too high.

title: The watchdog that restores Sandbox after a crash
content:
<project>\bridge_watchdog.py runs as scheduled task ClaudeBridgeWatchdog,
polling every 5 minutes. If Sandbox is gone it:
  1. relaunches Sandbox
  2. waits for the bridge
  3. sends: bridge.execute_command asset.edit levels/example/example.level
  4. sleeps ~8 s, then re-applies ENV_AFTER_RELOAD

ENV_AFTER_RELOAD currently sets time of day 15.0 plus fog / volumetric-fog values. If you
change the level's intended time of day, change it here too or the watchdog will undo you.

It stands down while a deploy lock is held ("deploy in progress -- standing down").
State: claude_watchdog_state.json. Log: claude_watchdog.log.

Verified recovering a real crash unattended: 16:03:02 relaunch -> 16:03:10 level reopened
-> 16:03:18 environment restored.

So: if the bridge goes unreachable mid-session, wait up to 5 minutes and re-ping before
concluding anything is wrong. NOTE the navmesh does NOT come back with it unless the level was exported once - see
nav-inmemory and nav-export-persists.

title: Helper: claude_bridge_cmd.py - run a list of bridge commands
content:
<engine source checkout> <cmdfile> <outfile>

Sends each line of cmdfile as a bridge command and writes ">>> cmd" plus the raw JSON
response to outfile, flushing as it goes. Blank lines and lines starting with # are
skipped, except "#sleep N" which pauses N seconds.

Dispatch it detached from execute_python:

    PY = r'%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python311\python.exe'
    subprocess.Popen([PY,'-u', r'<engine source checkout>',
                      cmdfile, outfile], creationflags=0x8|0x200)

This is the workhorse for anything that must run while the main thread is busy, and for
sequences (move camera -> settle -> screenshot -> change cvar -> screenshot).

title: Helper: claude_nav_regen.py - regenerate the navmesh through the modal
content: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-15: ai.regenerate_agent_type_layer0 regenerates with no dialog at all (see nav-regen-no-modal, MCP regenerate_navigation). This dialog-clicking helper is only needed for the 'all' variant.
history:
SUPERSEDED 2026-09-15: ai.regenerate_agent_type_layer0 regenerates with no dialog at all (see nav-regen-no-modal, MCP regenerate_navigation). This dialog-clicking helper is only needed for the 'all' variant.

<engine source checkout> <outfile>

Regenerates the navmesh AND clicks through the modal dialog that blocks on it. It:
  1. sends "bridge.execute_command ai.regenerate_agent_type_all" on a worker thread
     (this call blocks until the dialog is dismissed)
  2. polls bridge.window.list every 0.5 s for a window whose title contains "MNM" or
     "Navigation"
  3. computes the Yes button from that window's rect
     (x = left + 0.64*width, y = top + 0.79*height)
  4. converts to MAIN-WINDOW-RELATIVE coordinates (bridge.input.click wants those:
     rel = abs - mainRect.topLeft) and clicks
  5. waits for the modal to disappear

USE THIS rather than a hard-coded click position. A hard-coded click worked until the user
moved the Sandbox window to a different monitor, after which it silently missed and the
navmesh was never rebuilt - which showed up much later as "0 of 4 waypoints usable".

title: Helper: claude_grep.py - search the engine source without freezing the editor
content:
<engine source checkout> <root> <regex> <outfile>

Detached recursive regex search over .cpp/.h/.cs/.lua/.xml, writing "path:line: text"
(truncated to 300 chars), capped at 400 hits, ending with "DONE <n>".

Use this instead of os.walk from inside execute_python, which blocks the editor's main
thread. Typical use - answering an engine behaviour question from the real source at
<engine source checkout> That source has been a far more reliable
reference than the online documentation.

title: Helper: bridge_shoot.py and the stale-frame rule
content:
<project>\bridge_shoot.py <shots.txt>

Each line: <output path>|<eye x y z>|<target x y z>
Example:  <engine source checkout>|492 318 58|524 352 36

The non-obvious rule it encodes, from its own docstring: a STALE viewport CONVERGES
(successive captures are byte-identical because the editor never redrew), while a LIVE 3D
viewport never converges (time of day, fog, water and terrain LOD keep moving). So
"keep shooting until two frames match" is exactly backwards - it stops on the bad case and
never terminates on the good one. The rule that works: a capture whose checksum DIFFERS
from the one before it came from a viewport that is actually drawing.

It also parks the mouse pointer over the viewport with an ABSOLUTE move before capturing:
the settle jitter is a relative one-pixel nudge, so it only wakes Sandbox if the pointer is
already over it. That is why the same run produced three good captures and three grey ones
with no pattern in the camera positions.

Output is a full-window BMP (1119x1021 or 959x1032 depending on window size). The 3D
viewport is roughly the crop box (286,140,1007,576) on the 1119-wide layout.

title: Engine primitive dimensions (measured, not assumed)
content:
Parsed out of the CGF AABBs because assuming they were unit cubes was wrong and caused a
rebuild of the whole farmstead:

  primitive_box       1 x 1 x 0.25     <- a SLAB, not a cube
  primitive_cube      1 x 1 x 1
  primitive_cylinder  1 x 1 x 1
  primitive_sphere    1 x 1 x 1
  primitive_pyramid   1 x 1 x 0.7071

All are centred on the origin, so a wall of height H placed with its base at z0 needs its
origin at z0 + H/2.

Use primitive_cube for walls. For a pyramid roof of height H, z-scale = H / 0.7071.

They live at %ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Objects/primitive_*.cgf.

title: Heightmap axis convention: world (x,y) -> h[x][y]
content:
For the terrain heightmap arrays used with bridge.terrain.get_heights_raw /
set_heights_raw: world (x, y) maps to h[x][y] - the FIRST index is world X.

This was established empirically with a buried-vs-visible box test (write a flat pad at a
known world position, place a box there, see whether it is buried or standing proud).

The working heightmap is 1024x1024 float32. A flattened building pad was produced with a
smoothstep falloff: R_FLAT=26, R_BLEND=30 around world (520,348), target height 33.365 m.
Round-trip was verified by MD5 on both sides.

title: The farmstead: what is in the level
content:
About 50 objects built from engine primitives, centred near world (520, 348) on a
flattened pad at terrain height 33.365 m: a farmhouse, a barn, a shed, a perimeter fence,
a gate, a well, a chimney and crates.

Entities in the level: Player0 (spawns at the farm gate 516,334), Villager1 (544,352),
Villager2 (520,374), FarmProbe (520,348,45 - the environment probe).

They were built from a command file of the form, three lines per object:
    bridge.object.create Brush <x> <y> <z> <name> <cgf>
    bridge.object.transform <name> x y z rx ry rz sx sy sz
    bridge.object.material <name> materials/<mat>

Everything is saved in Assets/levels/example/layers/main.lyr, which is plain XML and can
be hand-edited (with Sandbox closed, or the editor will overwrite you on its next save).

title: Material file template and the surface-type warnings
content:
Materials live in <project>\Assets\materials\ (wood_dark, wood_light, thatch, stone,
roof_dark, render_white), each a .mtl plus a sibling .cryasset. Template:

  <Material MtlFlags="524288" Shader="Illum" GenMask="0" StringGenMask="" SurfaceType=""
            MatTemplate="" Diffuse="0.107,0.051,0.023" Specular="0.02,0.02,0.02"
            Opacity="1" Shininess="8" vertModifType="0" LayerAct="1">
   <Textures><Texture Map="Diffuse" File="%engine%/EngineAssets/TextureMsg/color_white.dds">
     <TexMod .../></Texture></Textures>
   <PublicParams EmittanceMapGamma="1" SSSIndex="0"/>
  </Material>

MtlFlags 524288 = 0x80000 = MTL_64BIT_SHADERGENMASK. It is NOT MTL_FLAG_UIMATERIAL
(that is 0x40000) - this was checked because a UI-material flag would have explained the
flat lighting. It did not; see light-two-causes.

The level-load warnings "'mat_wood' undefined surface type, using mat_default" and
"Physicalized object has material (...) with invalid surface type" are COSMETIC. The
custom materials name surface types that do not exist in SurfaceTypes.xml. Adding entries
there would silence them.

title: Lighting: why the walls were flat (two independent causes)
content:
"No light or shadow on the house walls, but shadows on the ground are fine" turned out to
be TWO independent problems. Fixing either alone leaves it looking wrong.

CAUSE 1 - no ambient at all. In CRYENGINE's deferred path with SVOGI off, outdoor ambient
comes ONLY from environment probes. The probe in the level had AffectsOnlyThisArea="true"
(meaningless outdoors, where there is no VisArea, so it lit nothing) and an empty Cubemap.
Fixing that took a shaded wall from 5.7 to 95.3 luma.

CAUSE 2 - the sun was overhead. Time of day was 11.5, so the sun sat near zenith and
VERTICAL faces got almost no N.L. Meanwhile DiffuseMultiplier="4" flooded them with
uniform white ambient, erasing what little shading was left. Result: correctly lit ground
with real shadows, and walls that looked like flat paper.

FIX: time of day 15.0 (raking light) and DiffuseMultiplier 1.5.

title: Current lighting settings
content:
Time of day: 15.0. Set with e_TimeOfDay 15.0 (or bridge.env.time 15.0), then
general.save_level to persist it. The watchdog's ENV_AFTER_RELOAD also sets 15.0 - keep
the two in sync.

FarmProbe, in main.lyr (component typeId 0d3d1840-d239-411e-8738-14c56cccee2c):
  AffectsOnlyThisArea="false"      <- must be false outdoors
  LinkToSkyColor="false"
  DiffuseMultiplier="1.5"
  SpecularMultiplier="0.3"
  Cubemap="%ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Textures/white_cm.dds"
  BoxSize 160 x 160 x 100, Color r0.55 g0.68 b0.9

The probe's properties are NOT reachable through general.set_entity_property
("DiffuseMultiplier is an invalid property"), so they are edited in main.lyr directly.
Do that with Sandbox closed (e.g. during a build) or the editor's next save overwrites it.

title: TRAP: object.generate_all_cubemaps is a silent-success failure
content:
object.generate_all_cubemaps() returns ok after about 9 ms and writes ZERO files. It
reports success and does nothing.

Workaround in use: point the probe at a stock white cubemap and scale it with
DiffuseMultiplier instead of generating one:
  Cubemap="%ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Textures/white_cm.dds"

This is one of several silent-success failures in this toolchain. Others found:
- an environment probe with AffectsOnlyThisArea=true outdoors (no VisArea, lights nothing)
- general.nav_insert_point accepting absolute coordinates and storing garbage
Always verify an effect by measuring it, not by the absence of an error.

title: How to measure lighting objectively
content:
Do not judge lighting by eye from a screenshot - judge it by pixel luminance, and always
compare against a control.

Method used:
1. Capture the same camera position twice, changing one thing (bridge_shoot.py or
   bridge.viewport.screenshot with an identical bridge.camera.look_at).
2. Stage the BMPs, crop the viewport, convert to L, average a small box on a known
   surface.
3. Compare. Also compare a box that should NOT change, as a control.

Real numbers from this project:
- probe fix: shaded wall 5.7 -> 95.3 luma (and 50,277 other pixels changed, confirming the
  earlier null result had been real rather than a stale frame)
- at TOD 16.5 with probes off vs on: front wall 128.9 -> 154.7, roof 207.8 -> 225.7,
  ground 50.8 -> 76.0

To see PURE sun shading with no ambient, set r_DeferredShadingEnvProbes 0 and sweep the
time of day. At 9:00 and 11:00 every camera-facing wall is pure black; at 15:00 the front
wall is lit and the gable end is not (good contrast); at 17:00 both are lit and it flattens
out again.

title: Player component overview
content:
Code/Components/Player.{h,cpp}. CPlayerComponent, GUID {63F4C0C6-32AF-4ACB-8FB0-57D45DD14725}.

A physical first-person character on Cry::DefaultComponents::CCharacterControllerComponent
(PE_LIVING). The original Blank-template player wrote the entity transform directly every
frame, which meant it flew, passed through walls and ignored the ground.

- Yaw is applied to the ENTITY (SetRotation(Quat::CreateRotationZ(m_lookYaw))); pitch is
  applied to the CAMERA ONLY (camera transform = rotation X by m_lookPitch, translation
  (0,0,1.68)). Pitching the entity would tilt the physics capsule and the controller would
  try to walk into the ground.
- kWalkSpeed 4.0, kSprintSpeed 7.5, kJumpSpeed 5.0, kEyeHeight 1.68, kMaxPitch 1.4 rad.
- WASD + LShift sprint + Space jump (jump uses AddVelocity and checks IsOnGround()).
- Movement is expressed as a target VELOCITY via ChangeVelocity(v, SetAsTarget); the
  living-entity solver resolves it against the ground. The vertical component is left at
  zero - gravity and jumping are the solver's job.
- Spawns at the farm gate (516, 334) at terrain height + 2 m. Revive() re-applies the
  controller config and calls Physicalize(), because leaving game mode tears the physical
  entity down.

title: Player fix: kInertia == 0 is a special case meaning 'exact velocity'
content:
Symptoms reported: "if the player is on a slope he starts sliding down" and "when I let go
of W it still slides for a few milliseconds".

Root cause, in the engine source at
<engine source checkout>:1359:

    if (kInertia==0 && !bFlying && !m_bJumpRequested || m_pWorld->m_vars.bFlyMode) {
        vel = m_velRequested;
        vel -= m_nslope*(m_nslope*vel);     // projected onto the ground plane
    }

kInertia == 0 is a SPECIAL CASE meaning "velocity becomes exactly what was requested,
projected onto the slope". With the component default of 8, the solver only EASES toward
the request (line 1962: last_force = (velReq-vel)*kInertia), so:
  - on release, velocity decays exponentially instead of stopping -> the slide
  - standing still on a slope, gravity along the slope is only asymptotically opposed
    -> the downhill creep

FIX applied in ConfigureCharacterController():
    movement.m_inertia             = 0.0f;
    movement.m_inertiaAcceleration = 0.0f;

Note the SMovement C++ member defaults differ from the reflected Schematyc defaults - the
member initialisers are what apply when the component is added from C++ with
GetOrCreateComponent (m_airControlRatio is 0.f in the member, 1.f in the reflection).

STATUS: built, NOT yet verified in game.
verified_note: The text itself says 'built, NOT yet verified in game'.

title: Player fix: heightCollider defaults to zero, burying half the capsule
content: CCharacterControllerComponent::Physicalize computes heightCollider from the component's transform translation z; a component added from C++ has a transform of ZERO, so the capsule is centred on the entity pivot (the feet) and its lower half sits in the terrain. The component also rescales its parameters: real radius = Radius/2, cylinder half-height = Height/4 (z*0.5 again when a capsule). The 'fix' written here (capsule bottom exactly at the feet) gives 0 m step-up and was WRONG: see player-capsule-correction, living-step-up-gap and my-project-physics-measured (Radius 0.7, Height 1.4, transform z 1.1 gives 0.4 m step-up, measured).
history:
CORRECTED 2026-09-15 - read player-capsule-correction first. Placing the capsule bottom at the feet gives 0 m step-up height in CLivingEntity::Step; the reasoning below that this fixes the stutter is probably wrong (source analysis, not yet measured).

Symptom reported: "every second I get stuck and continue to move".

Root cause: CCharacterControllerComponent::Physicalize() computes
    playerDimensions.heightCollider = m_pTransform != nullptr ? m_pTransform->GetTranslation().z : 0.f
and a component added from C++ has a transform of ZERO. So the capsule is centred on the
entity pivot - the character's FEET - and its lower half sits inside the terrain, with the
living-entity solver resolving that penetration every frame.

The component also rescales its exposed parameters on the way to physics:
    sizeCollider = (Radius * 0.5, 1, Height * 0.5); if (capsule) sizeCollider.z *= 0.5;
so the real capsule radius is Radius/2 and the real cylinder half-height is Height/4, and
the capsule spans heightCollider +/- (sizeCollider.z + sizeCollider.x).

FIX applied - a capsule of radius 0.35 m spanning exactly 0 -> 1.8 m above the pivot:
    physics.m_radius = 0.7f;    // -> real radius 0.35
    physics.m_height = 2.2f;    // -> real cylinder half-height 0.55
    physics.m_bCapsule = true;
    m_pCharacterController->SetTransformMatrix(
        Matrix34::Create(Vec3(1.f), IDENTITY, Vec3(0,0, 0.7f*0.5f + 2.2f*0.25f)));  // 0.9

Must be set BEFORE Physicalize(), and re-applied in Revive() because leaving game mode
tears the physical entity down.

STATUS: built, NOT yet verified in game. This is the leading candidate for the stutter but
it has not been confirmed - run claude_player_walk and read the trace.

title: Diagnostic: claude_player_walk console command
content:
Console command shipped in the current Game.dll:

    claude_player_walk <seconds>        (default 4)

Walks the player forward under its own steam and writes a per-frame trace to
<engine source checkout>, tab-separated:

    elapsed  frameTime  x  y  z  speed2d  vz  onGround  stepped

"stepped" is the 2D distance moved since the previous sample. Samples are buffered in
memory (up to 8192) and written once when the walk ends, so the logging is not itself a
source of hitching.

How to read it: the "stuck then continue" signature is `stepped` collapsing to ~0 for a
run of frames while `speed2d` stays high. A rendering/CPU hitch instead shows as a spike
in `frameTime`. Those are different problems with different fixes, and this trace tells
them apart - which a screenshot cannot.

Separate test for the slope slide: put the player on a slope, send no input for 5 s, and
sample entity positions via cryengine__list_entities. Any drift means it is not fixed.

title: Registering a component as a spawnable entity class
content:
To make a component spawnable BY NAME (from the editor's object list and from the bridge)
rather than something a user must add by hand to an empty entity:

    // in Npc.cpp
    void RegisterNpcEntityClass()
    {
        RegisterEntityClassWithDefaultComponent<CNpcComponent>(
            "Villager",
            "{2C7F6A19-8D34-4E51-B0A2-6F1D9C3E77B4}"_cry_guid,   // entity class GUID
            "{5A1E4B73-19CF-4D28-8E66-C4B70F2A9D15}"_cry_guid);  // component instance GUID
    }

The helper is declared in CryEntitySystem/IEntitySystem.h. Call it from GamePlugin.cpp in
ESYSTEM_EVENT_GAME_POST_INIT (this project calls it right after
AddNetworkedClientListener). Then spawn with:

    general.new_object("Entity", "Villager", "Villager1", 544, 352, 33.37)

Remember to add the new .cpp and .h to Code/CMakeLists.txt (they go into
Components_uber.cpp).

title: Navigation.xml agent type - sizes are in VOXELS
content:
<project>\Assets\scripts\AI\Navigation.xml defines agent type "Villager":

    radius 4, height 16, climbableHeight 4, climbableStepRatio 0.75,
    maxWaterDepth 2, voxelSize 0.125

THE SIZES ARE IN VOXELS, not metres. With voxelSize 0.125 that is:
    radius = 4  * 0.125 = 0.5 m
    height = 16 * 0.125 = 2.0 m

The agent type name must match what the component is given:
    m_pNav->SetNavigationAgentType("Villager");

title: TRAP: a Navigation Area is a prism extending UPWARD from its own Z
content:
A Navigation Area is a prism that extends UPWARD from its own Z position by its Height
property. Its floor must be BELOW the terrain or nothing is voxelised and the mesh comes
out empty.

This cost real time: the area sat at z 33.4 with terrain at 33.365, i.e. 3.5 cm above the
ground, and produced no navmesh at all while looking perfectly reasonable in the editor.

Current working values in main.lyr:
    FarmNavArea  Pos="520,348,28"  Height="24"
    relative points: (-32,-26,0) (32,-26,0) (32,34,0) (-32,34,0)

That covers world x 488..552, y 322..382 - which is why a waypoint at (556,352) reports
unreachable. That is correct behaviour, not a bug.

title: TRAP: nav_insert_point takes OBJECT-RELATIVE coordinates
content:
UPDATE 2026-09-15: relative coordinates confirmed as the contract (ShapeObject.cpp PyInsertPoint). Passing relative points to an area that already had a position did NOT move it; the 'first call folds into the position' effect below was seen with absolute coordinates only. MCP create_navigation_area converts world points for you.

general.nav_insert_point(name, index, x, y, z) takes OBJECT-RELATIVE coordinates, not
world coordinates.

Passing absolute world coords is accepted without error and stores garbage - and the FIRST
call folds the value into the object's position, so the area teleports. In this project it
ended up at (1008, 670) instead of (520, 348).

Another silent-success failure. Verify the area's Pos and points in main.lyr afterwards
rather than trusting the call.

title: The navmesh of a level that was never exported is lost on every editor restart (export it once)
content:
A navmesh that was only GENERATED lives in memory and dies with the editor. One that was EXPORTED (exporter.export_to_engine writes <level>/mnmnav<mission>.bai and packs it into level.pak, see nav-export-persists; every GameSDK level ships one) loads back with the level. My Project's first level had never been exported, so its mesh was lost on every restart. Export once and regeneration after a restart should no longer be needed (not yet tested on My Project).

Consequence for a level that was never exported: after EVERY Sandbox restart - including the ones the build task and the
watchdog perform - you must regenerate it before testing anything that navigates.

The symptom of forgetting is that every destination reports unreachable, e.g. the NPC log
line "route built, 0 of 4 waypoints usable (4 off the navmesh)". If you see that, the
navmesh is missing, not broken.

Regenerate with <engine source checkout> (superseded helper tool-nav-regen; use nav-regen-no-modal / MCP regenerate_navigation), then allow
20-30 s before entering game mode. A healthy result is "3 of 4 waypoints usable".

title: The navigation world monitor is STOPPED in game mode
content:
Entering game mode prints:
    CAIManager: navigation world monitor state: Started -> Stopped
and leaving prints the reverse.

So continuous navmesh regeneration (the world monitor re-voxelising tiles as physics
objects move) does NOT run in game mode, and is therefore NOT a candidate for in-game

title: OPEN PROBLEM: NPCs get exactly 0.0000 requested velocity
content: SOLVED 2026-09-15 - read npc-duplicate-components. The symptom was: the two villagers did not move; IEntityNavigationComponent::GetRequestedVelocity() returned EXACTLY 0.0000 on every frame (88,711 frames in one run) while ai_DebugMovementSystem showed the plan 'Executing | Plan: [FollowPath]'. title: What has been RULED OUT for the NPC zero-velocity bug, with evidence
content: Obsolete: every theory listed here was wrong (the cause was duplicate navigation components, npc-duplicate-components). Kept as history: missing navmesh, the villagers' own colliders carving holes, an unreachable destination, ORCA, the path follower's reach tests, UpdateTransformation zeroing the velocity and a plan not running were all measured and eliminated. The decisive measurement was that with collision avoidance EType::None the state-updated callback fired ZERO times in 20 s, so NewStateComputed was never called on the component the code held.
history:
Each of these was tested and eliminated - do not re-litigate them without new evidence:

- Navmesh missing or agent off-mesh. NO: ai_DebugDrawNavigation 1 shows solid blue mesh
  directly under both villagers.
- The villagers' own box colliders carving navmesh holes around themselves. NO: same
  screenshot, no hole. (This was a plausible theory - the mesh component is
  RenderAndCollider - and it was wrong.)
- Destination unreachable. NO: IsDestinationReachable returns true and 3 of 4 waypoints
  are accepted at route-build time.
- ORCA collision avoidance overwriting the velocity with zero. NO: ai_EnableORCA 0 changed
  nothing.
- The path follower failing its reach tests. NO: with ai_DrawPathFollower 2 the label
  "Failed PathFollower!" is never drawn.
- CEntityAINavigationComponent::UpdateTransformation() zeroing m_requestedVelocity at the
  end of its update. NO: that handler is only subscribed when m_bUpdateTransformation is
  true, and main.lyr has updateTransf="false".
- The movement plan not running at all. NO: ai_DebugMovementSystem 1 shows it executing.
- The velocity being tiny rather than zero (the acceleration ramp). NO: measured 0.0000
  against a 0.0005 threshold.

DECISIVE MEASUREMENT: with collision avoidance set to EType::None - which removes the
early return in NewStateComputed that withholds the callback when avoidance is Active -
the state-updated callback fired ZERO times in 20 s. Since
Movement::Helpers::UpdatePathFollowing calls EITHER SetMovementOutputValue OR
ClearMovementState, and both route into NewStateComputed, zero callbacks means
NewStateComputed is never called AT ALL on the component this code holds a pointer to.

title: LEADING HYPOTHESIS: two navigation components per villager
content: CONFIRMED and SOLVED - see npc-duplicate-components. The hypothesis 'each villager has TWO CEntityAINavigationComponent instances and the movement system drives the one the code does not hold' was true (in fact four: three serialized into main.lyr over successive saves plus one made by GetOrCreateComponent). Fix: rebuild the owned components on entering game mode and flag them NoSave.
history:
NOT YET VERIFIED. Test this first.

Hypothesis: each villager has TWO CEntityAINavigationComponent instances, and the movement
system is driving the one this code does not hold.

Supporting facts:
- main.lyr ALREADY CONTAINS a serialized navigation component per villager:
  TypeGUID="1b988fa3-2cc8-4dfa-9107-a63aded77e91" TypeName="CEntityAINavigationComponent",
  with properties agent="Villager" updateTransf="false" and movement / colavoid /
  queryFilter blocks.
- CNpcComponent::Initialize() calls
  m_pEntity->GetOrCreateComponent<IEntityNavigationComponent>(). For a component loaded
  from a layer file, Initialize() runs DURING load - plausibly BEFORE the navigation
  component is deserialized. GetComponent finds nothing, so it CREATES one, and the
  serializer then adds the second.
- Both instances call Start() -> MovementSystem::RegisterEntity(entityId, callbacks,
  adapter). If the first registration wins, the plan runs against instance #1's adapter
  and writes instance #1's m_requestedVelocity, while this code reads instance #2's -
  permanently zero, with no callback, forever.

It fits every observation, including why IsDestinationReachable still works (it is a pure
query against the agent type and navmesh, correct on any instance) and why NavigateTo
visibly queues a MoveTo for the right entity id.

HOW TO TEST (one build):
1. In Initialize(), call GetComponent<IEntityNavigationComponent>() (not GetOrCreate) and
   log whether it returned null, plus the pointer value.
2. Acquire the component LAZILY in GameplayStarted / Reset(entering game mode), by which
   time deserialization is complete, and log that pointer too.
3. If the two pointers differ, the hypothesis is confirmed; keep the lazily acquired one.

title: Engine source oddities in the NPC movement path (CSmartPathFollower early return, MovementSystem frame time, inverted condition)
content:
Engine source oddities in the NPC movement path, found while debugging the zero-velocity bug (read from source, none was the cause - npc-duplicate-components was):
1. CSmartPathFollower::ProcessPath() returns early when pathPts.size() < 2, leaving m_path EMPTY. Update() then hits the early return at the top: if (m_path.empty() || m_path.TotalDistance() < FLT_EPSILON) { result.reachedEnd = true; return true; } with velocityOut already zeroed - exactly zero velocity with no failure label. CMovementActorAdapter::GetMoveDirection() is a STUB returning ZERO, so the 'stopped' test speed = groundVelocity.Dot(moveDir) is always 0 < 0.01 and always true.
2. MovementSystem::Update contains a genuine engine bug: m_frameStartTime = frameDeltaTime; (assigns a DELTA to a START TIME). Harmless for velocity as far as could be determined; context.updateTime comes from m_frameDeltaTime, which is set correctly.
3. SmartPathFollower.cpp:630 has an inverted condition - the comment says 'Couldn't find a triangle for the end position' but the test is `if (triangleEndID.IsValid())`, so it re-queries the closest triangle precisely when it already has a valid one.
Measured frame time in the editor during these tests was about 0.00127 s (790 fps), which matters because the path follower's speed ramp is maxOutputSpeed = m_lastOutputSpeed + dt * maxAccel: at that dt the per-frame increment is only 0.0038 m/s.

title: POLICY: the straight-line fallback was removed deliberately
content:
An earlier version of CNpcComponent had a fallback: if the navigation component produced
no velocity for 1 second, steer the character controller straight at the waypoint.

That made the villagers appear to patrol, and it was reported to the user as working. It
has been REMOVED, deliberately, because calling it "CRYENGINE's built-in AI" would be
false - the villagers would walk through walls, using the navmesh only for a reachability
check, and the user explicitly asked for the real thing.

Do not reinstate it as a fix. If it is reinstated as a temporary stopgap so the level is
demoable, say so plainly and in the same breath as the demo.

What replaced it: if there is no velocity for 4 seconds the component re-issues
NavigateTo and counts the re-issue, which is visible in the trace log.

title: CEntityAINavigationComponent internals worth knowing
content:
Source: <engine source checkout>\
NavigationComponent.{h,cpp}. Public interface:
Code\CryEngine\CryCommon\CryAISystem\Components\IEntityNavigationComponent.h

Key behaviours:

- GetEventMask(): the default mask is only START_GAME | RESET |
  COMPONENT_PROPERTY_CHANGED. ENTITY_EVENT_UPDATE is added ONLY if m_bUpdateTransformation
  is true; ENTITY_EVENT_PREPHYSICSUPDATE only if the entity has NO physics.

- UpdateTransformation() (the ENTITY_EVENT_UPDATE handler) is what moves the entity itself
  when "Update Transformation" is enabled - for PE_LIVING it issues pe_action_move plus
  pe_action_set_velocity - and it ZEROES m_requestedVelocity at the end. With
  updateTransf=false it never runs, so it is not a source of zeroed velocity.

- NewStateComputed(result, pSender) sets m_requestedVelocity = result.velocityOut FIRST,
  then, if collision avoidance is Active and the velocity is non-zero and the sender is
  not the collision agent, RETURNS EARLY WITHOUT FIRING THE CALLBACK. That is why the
  state-updated callback appears never to fire with Active avoidance - the design expects
  the ORCA pass to deliver the final velocity via ApplyComputedVelocity. Set avoidance to
  None to get the callback straight from the path follower.

- Initialize() calls Start() immediately ("temporary solution" per the engine comment), and
  START_GAME / RESET each do a full Stop(); Start(); cycle, re-registering with the
  movement system.

- SetNavigationAgentType() also does Stop(); Start(); if the type id changed.

title: The path-following call chain (where velocity comes from)
content:
The chain that produces an NPC's velocity, with file references under
<engine source checkout>\:

  CAISystem::Update (CAISystem.cpp:2587)
    -> InitUpdate() gate: returns false if !m_bInitialized || !IsEnabled() || !ai_SystemUpdate
    -> TrySubsystemUpdateMovementSystem (CAISystemUpdate.cpp:345)
      -> MovementSystem::Update (Movement/MovementSystem.cpp:227)
        -> UpdateActors -> UpdateActor
          -> IsActorValidForMovementUpdateContextCreation (needs a non-null path follower)
          -> StartWorkingOnNewRequestIfPossible
          -> if (planner.IsUpdateNeeded()) UpdatePlannerAndDealWithResult
            -> GenericPlanner::Update (Movement/MovementPlanner.cpp:109)
              -> ExecuteCurrentPlan -> Plan::Execute -> FollowPath::Update
                -> Movement::Helpers::UpdatePathFollowing (Movement/MovementHelpers.cpp)
                  -> pathFollower.Update(result, position, velocity, dt)
                  -> if (targetReachable) adapter.SetMovementOutputValue(result)
                     else                 adapter.ClearMovementState()      // zero
                    -> CEntityAINavigationComponent::NewStateComputed

Then, later in the same AI update, SubsystemUpdateCollisionAvoidanceSystem ->
CCollisionAvoidanceSystem::Update -> ApplyResults -> ApplyComputedVelocity ->
NewStateComputed again, with the ORCA-adjusted velocity.

Because BOTH branches of UpdatePathFollowing end in NewStateComputed, a callback count of
zero proves the chain is broken above that point.

title: How CSmartPathFollower computes the output velocity
content:
<engine source checkout>, around line 1104:

    velocity = (followTargetPos - curPos); velocity.z = 0 (use2D); NormalizeSafe()
    speed = m_params.normalSpeed
    if (stopAtEnd) {
        if (distToEnd < m_params.endAccuracy) { result.reachedEnd = true; speed = 0; }
        else speed = min(speed, decelerationMultiplier * distToEnd / 1.2f);
    }
    if (bPathHasChanged) m_lastOutputSpeed = curSpeed * dot(velDir, moveDir);
    Limit(m_lastOutputSpeed, minSpeed, maxSpeed);
    maxOutputSpeed = min(m_lastOutputSpeed + dt * maxAccel, maxSpeed);
    minOutputSpeed = stopAtEnd ? 0 : max(m_lastOutputSpeed - dt*maxDecel, minSpeed);
    Limit(speed, minOutputSpeed, maxOutputSpeed);
    m_lastOutputSpeed = speed;
    result.velocityOut = velocity * speed;

Consequences worth knowing:
- The speed RAMPS from zero at maxAccel, so the first frames of a leg are legitimately
  tiny. Do not use a large "is it moving" threshold (see npc-duplicate-components: threshold no higher than 0.0005, print %.4f).
- If bPathHasChanged is true every frame, m_lastOutputSpeed is reset to the actor's
  current speed each frame, so a stationary actor can never ramp past dt*maxAccel.
- Early in Update(): if m_path is empty or has zero total distance, it sets
  reachedEnd = true and returns TRUE with a ZEROED velocityOut.

PathFollowerParams defaults (CryCommon/CryAISystem/IPathfinder.h:83): pathRadius 0.0,
endAccuracy 0.2, passRadius 0.5, isAllowedToShortcut true. FillPathFollowerParams in the
navigation component sets only use2D, snapEndPointToGround, the speeds, endDistance 0,
maxAccel/maxDecel, stopAtEnd and pQueryFilter - the rest keep those defaults.

title: Assorted engine facts collected while debugging
content:
- CGF format: magic "CrChF" (8-byte signature block) + uint32 chunkCount + uint32
  chunkTableOffset; 16-byte table entries {uint16 type; uint16 version; uint32 id;
  uint32 size; uint32 offset}. Mesh chunk type 0x1000 ends with the AABB - that is how the
  primitive dimensions in content-primitives were measured.

- Reading engine.pak with Python's zipfile throws
  "BadZipFile: File name in directory ... and header ... differ" because CryPak stores
  BACKSLASHES in entry names. Read the local headers manually and
  zlib.decompress(raw, -15).

- Material flags (Cry3DEngine/IMaterial.h): MTL_FLAG_LIGHTING 0x0010,
  MTL_FLAG_NOSHADOW 0x0020, MTL_FLAG_UIMATERIAL 0x40000,
  MTL_64BIT_SHADERGENMASK 0x80000. The project's materials use 524288 = 0x80000, which is
  the harmless shadergen-remap flag, NOT the UI flag.

- general.get_root_path DOES NOT EXIST in any registry. An earlier report that it crashed
  Sandbox was investigated and disproved.

- general.get_game_folder() returns the ENGINE assets directory
  (...\5.7.1/assets), while os.getcwd() in Sandbox's Python returns the PROJECT root.

- IRenderer::ScreenShot (the cryengine__take_screenshot MCP tool) returns false in this
  setup, in both editor and game mode. r_GetScreenShot 1 also produced nothing findable.
  Use bridge.viewport.screenshot.

- The "ZipDir::Cache::ReadFile mismatch detected for file tileN_N.raw" errors at level
  load are pre-existing terrain surface-texture CRC errors, unrelated to any of this work.

title: Method: verify by measurement, because this stack fails silently
content:
The recurring theme of this project is SILENT-SUCCESS FAILURE: a call returns ok and does
nothing. Confirmed instances:

- object.generate_all_cubemaps() - returned in 9 ms, wrote zero files
- an environment probe with AffectsOnlyThisArea=true outdoors - lights nothing
- general.nav_insert_point with absolute coordinates - stores garbage
- execute_editor_command with an unknown typeName - logs a warning, no-ops, returns ok
- device_commit_files re-committing from a reused staged path - wrote stale bytes
- a hard-coded modal click after the window moved - clicked nothing, navmesh never rebuilt
- the build batch relaunching Sandbox after a FAILED build

So: prove effects, do not infer them.
- Lighting: measure pixel luminance against a control (see light-measure-method).
- Code reaching the machine: read the file size and grep for a marker on the device.
- Builds: read the exit code in claude_game_build.log.
- Navmesh: look for "3 of 4 waypoints usable", or draw it with ai_DebugDrawNavigation.
- NPC movement: count frames and print %.4f, do not eyeball it.
- A one-shot log line proves a condition happened ONCE, not that it persists. A one-shot
  "no velocity" message was read as a permanent state for an afternoon; replacing it with
  per-3-second counters is what actually settled the question.

REMEMBER on every restart: reopen the level (asset.edit levels/example/example.level) and
REGENERATE THE NAVMESH before testing navigation.

title: GameSDK sample project: where its AI actually is
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
Project: <projects>\CRYENGINE GameSDK Sample Project
(asset folder "gamesdk", engine-5.7, game DLL CryGameSDK).

- levels/multiplayer/airfield is the ONLY level with AI characters: layer Multiplayer_AI
  (DefaultLoaded=0) holds 12 x Characters.Enemy.Easy_Rifle archetype instances and one
  4-point NavigationArea (height 8, agent MediumSizedCharacters). No seeds, no cover.
- levels/singleplayer/woodland has the complete navigation + cover setup but NO
  characters: 5 inclusion NavigationAreas, 28 exclusion volumes, 5 NavigationSeedPoints,
  345 CoverSurfaces, 17 SmartObjects (jump_v150/300/450_human, repeldown_v900), and a
  baked mnmnavmission0.bai (486 KB) + covermission0.bai inside level.pak.
- list_entities caps at 200 and misses non-entity objects, so it shows none of this.
  Use inspect_level / level_inventory.py (reads the .lyr XML directly, no cap).

Full write-up: GAMESDK_AI_GUIDE.md

title: GameSDK assets are packed: read them with crypak.py / read_asset_file
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
Only levels/*/layers/*.lyr are loose in GameSDK. Scripts and libraries are inside paks:
- scripts.pak: Scripts/AI/{Navigation.xml, Factions.xml, BehaviorTrees/SDK_Grunt_01..07.xml,
  TPS/, GoalPipes/, Communication/}, Scripts/Entities/AI/{Characters/Human_x.lua, AISpawner,
  AITerritory, AIWave, NavigationSeedPoint, SmartObject}.
- gamedata.pak: Libs/EntityArchetypes/Characters.xml (27 archetypes), Libs/EquipmentPacks/AI_*.xml,
  Libs/SmartObjects*, Libs/AITargetStimulusConfig.xml, MovementTransitions_Human.xml.

Python's zipfile fails on CryPak archives (backslash names). packaging/crypak.py parses the
central directory itself:
  crypak.py grep <asset dir> "Scripts/AI/"
  crypak.py cat  <asset dir> Scripts/AI/Factions.xml
  crypak.py extract <pak|dir> <regex> <outdir>
MCP tool read_asset_file("Scripts/AI/Navigation.xml") does the same for the loaded project
(loose file first, then any pak).

title: An AI character is one entity archetype (Characters.Enemy.Easy_Rifle)
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
Characters.Enemy.Easy_Rifle = {E2A39ED7-6C21-4819-A245-CA9241530D32}, class Human. Properties:
esFaction=Grunts, esModularBehaviorTree=sdk_grunt_07, esBehaviorSelection=HumanGrunt,
equip_EquipmentPack=AI_Rifle, esNavigationType=MediumSizedCharacters,
fileModel=objects/characters/human/sdk_player/sdk_player_red.cdf, health 250, sightrange 30,
FOV 40/80, attackrange 70. Variants Enemy./Friendly. x Easy_/Norm_/Hard_ x Rifle/Pistol/
Shotgun/RPG; Friendly.* use faction Players.

Place one (TESTED 2026-09-15 in woodland):
  general.new_object("EntityArchetype", "{GUID}", name, x, y, z)
The second argument must be the GUID (CProtEntityObject::Init -> CryGUID::FromString), not
the name. MCP: spawn_archetype("Characters.Enemy.Easy_Rifle", x, y, z) resolves the name.

Archetype properties are NOT instance properties: general.get_entity_property(n, "esFaction")
raises '"esFaction" is an invalid property'. Read them with list_archetypes.

esNavigationType must name an agent type the navmesh was generated for, or the AI never
moves. Needs the GameSDK game DLL + scripts; a Blank-template project has no Human class.

title: How woodland lays out navigation: big inclusion areas, many exclusion holes, one seed each
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
Woodland's navigation, from main.lyr:
1. 5 large inclusion NavigationAreas (12-28 points) following the playable ground; floor a
   few metres below terrain, Height 8-18 m.
2. 28 small exclusion volumes (Exclusion="1", 4-22 points, Height 4-20) around rocks, water
   edges and props that must not be walkable.
3. 5 NavigationSeedPoints, one per inclusion area, on walkable ground.
4. 345 CoverSurface objects (ai.generate_cover_surfaces generates AND exports them).
5. SmartObjects jump_v150/jump_v300/jump_v450_human/repeldown_v900 as off-mesh links.
6. Exported: mnmnavmission0.bai + covermission0.bai live in level.pak.

Agent types (Scripts/AI/Navigation.xml): MediumSizedCharacters voxel 0.125 radius 4 height 16
climbableHeight 3 maxWaterDepth 8, SmartObjectUserClasses Human; VehicleMedium voxel 0.2
radius 14 height 10. Sizes in voxels (0.5 m radius, 2 m tall). File order = agent type index.

MCP: create_navigation_area(points, floor_z, height, exclusion), create_nav_seed_point,
regenerate_navigation(0), set_ai_debug(navigation=1), export_level.

title: Regenerate the navmesh WITHOUT the modal: ai.regenerate_agent_type_layer0
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
TESTED 2026-09-15: execute_editor_command("ai.regenerate_agent_type_layer0") returned in
0.0 s, no dialog appeared (bridge.window.list showed no extra window), editor stayed
responsive. It calls INavigationUpdatesManager::RequestGlobalUpdateForAgentType directly
(Sandbox/EditorQt/AI/EditorCommands_AI.cpp). Commands exist for indices 0-5; the index is the
agent type's order in Scripts/AI/Navigation.xml. MCP: regenerate_navigation(0).

MODAL, avoid unattended: ai.regenerate_agent_type_all AND ai.regenerate_mnm_type('all') both
reach CAIManager::RegenerateNavigationByTypeName("all") -> CQuestionDialog "MNM Navigation
Rebuilding request". ai.regenerate_mnm_type('<AgentTypeName>') is modal-free but Python-only,
and Sandbox's Python has no `ai` module in globals (NameError / ImportError), so it cannot be
called. ai.regenerate_ignored applies pending (buffered) changes.

This supersedes the need for claude_nav_regen.py's dialog-clicking (tool-nav-regen), which
still works but depends on window geometry. (tool-nav-regen, the dialog-clicking helper this replaced, is superseded.)

title: exporter.export_to_engine writes the navmesh to disk (mnmnav<mission>.bai)
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
SOURCE-VERIFIED, not yet run on My Project: exporter.export_to_engine (File > Export to Engine,
Ctrl+E/F7, ICommandManager) -> CGameExporter::Export(eExp_AI_All) ->
CGameEngine::GenerateAINavigationMesh -> NavigationSystem::SaveToFile("<level>/mnmnav<mission>.bai"),
then packs it into level.pak with cover<mission>.bai. Loading the level reads it back
(IAISystem::LoadNavigationData(levelPath, missionName)). Evidence it works: every shipped
GameSDK level has mnmnavmission0.bai in level.pak.

general.save_level does NOT write it. So "the navmesh is in-memory only" (nav-inmemory) is
only true until the level is exported once.

Export refuses with a MODAL "Navigation System Warning" while tile updates are buffered or
still generating (CAIManager::IsReadyToGameExport). Wait for "Navigation System Idle" in the
ai_DebugDrawNavigation overlay first. MCP export_level() runs the export on a thread and
reports any dialog it sees via the out-of-band window list instead of hanging.
Also: ai.generate_cover_surfaces generates cover and exports it (eExp_AI_CoverSurfaces).

title: Seed points prune only when present; RemoveInaccessibleTriangles defaults on
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
NavigationSystem::ComputeMeshesAccessibility (CryAISystem/Navigation/NavigationSystem/
NavigationSystem.cpp ~1809): for each mesh it collects the seed points inside its volume. If
there are NONE, every island is marked Accessible - nothing is removed. If there are some,
islands not connected to a seed become inaccessible and are removed when the area's
RemoveInaccessibleTriangles is on (editor default true, CNavigationAreaObject::InitVariables).

Consequence: adding a seed in the wrong place (a rooftop, inside a rock) can make most of an
area's mesh disappear. Put seeds on the main walkable ground. In the launcher (not the
editor) inaccessible triangles are also stripped at load when
ai_MNMRemoveInaccessibleTrianglesOnLoad is set.

title: NavigationArea object variables and how to set them from Python
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
CNavigationAreaObject::InitVariables (Sandbox/EditorQt/Objects/ShapeObject.cpp ~4364):
Height=16, Exclusion=false, RemoveInaccessibleTriangles=true, DisplayFilled=false, and one bool
per agent type (named after the agent type) under AffectedAgentTypes - ALL default to true.

TESTED: general.new_object("NavigationArea", "", name, x, y, z) creates it;
general.get_entity_param(n, "Height") / set_entity_param(n, "Height", 24.0) work;
get_entity_param(n, "Exclusion") returns False. BUT set_entity_param(n,
"RemoveInaccessibleTriangles", ...) raises '"RemoveInaccessibleTriangles" is an invalid
parameter' although the variable exists - change it in the Properties panel instead. general.new_object("NavigationSeedPoint",
"", name, x, y, z) creates a seed (object type "NavigationSeedPoint").

nav_insert_point(name, index, x, y, z) is OBJECT-RELATIVE (see nav-insert-point-relative). In
the 2026-09-15 test, four relative points on an already-positioned area did not move the
object, and with ai_DebugDrawNavigation 1 a navmesh with a straight area edge appeared at
exactly that spot (outside every existing woodland area) once the floor was put below the
ground (terrain 53-59 m, floor 38, Height 24) - so the geometry is right.
Terrain height at a point: bridge.terrain.get_heights_raw <file> dumps float32 metres,
index [x * width + y] (world X first), 1 m cells on woodland's 2048 map. PyInsertPoint does SetPoint(idx) then InsertPoint(-1), so always pass
idx == current point count or a point is overwritten AND duplicated.

title: SDK_Grunt_01..07 behaviour trees are a step-by-step tutorial
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
Scripts/AI/BehaviorTrees/SDK_Grunt_0N.xml (scripts.pak) - each builds on the previous:
01 Idle only; 02 Idle<->Combat on OnNewAttentionTarget; 03 lose target -> run to last known
position, search 10 s, back to Idle; 04-06 alertness, cover (QueryTPS, ShootFromCover,
AdjustCoverStance), group scope; 07 (used by every Characters archetype) states Idle, Guard,
Disturbance, UnknownEnemyAround, FlinchAndGoToCombat, Combat,
ApproachAndInspectLastKnownPlayerPosition, Search, FoundEnemy, plus Flow Graph
AIAssignments DefendArea/HoldPosition.

File layout: <Variables>, <Events><GameEvents>, <SignalVariables> (perception signal ->
variable, e.g. OnNewAttentionTarget -> HasTarget=true), <Timestamps>, <Root><StateMachine>
<State><Transitions/><BehaviorTree>. Common nodes: Sequence, Selector, Parallel,
SuppressFailure, Loop, Wait, Move to="Target" speed="Run" stopWithinDistance=, Shoot
at="Target" fireMode="Burst", Animate, ExecuteLua code="entity:SelectPrimaryWeapon()",
SendTransitionSignal, IfTime, LuaGate, QueryTPS.

Factions.xml: Players hostile to Grunts/Assassins, friendly to Civilians; Grunts hostile to
Players/Assassins; WildLife and Civilians neutral.

These drive Lua Human actors. A C++ component NPC (My Project's CNpcComponent) gets none of
it and must drive IEntityNavigationComponent itself.

title: TRAP: Sandbox Python functions that are broken under Python 3
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
Found 2026-09-15 (Sandbox embedded Python 3.7):
- object.get_all_objects(type, layer) -> TypeError('expected bytes, str found') for any
  str args; bytes args -> ArgumentError. It returns std::vector<std::string> and the
  converter is broken. Use bridge.object.list (MCP list_objects, 500 cap, has type) or
  inspect_level (offline, uncapped).
- object.get_object_layer(name) -> SystemError('... returned a result with an error set').
- general.get_current_level_path() returns a PROJECT-RELATIVE path
  ("gamesdk/levels/singleplayer/woodland"); join with os.getcwd().
- There is no `ai` name in the Python globals (the reference lists ai.* functions);
  `from sandbox import ai` -> ImportError. Call ai.* commands via execute_editor_command.
- general.get_all_objects does not exist (it is in the `object` module).

title: Multi-line Python in Sandbox: execute_python_script / bridge_py.py
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
execute_python (MCP) collapses runs of whitespace, so any indented code fails with
IndentationError. Fixed routes, both using bridge.execute_python.b64 (source moved through a
temp file, stdout captured, no CryLog format-string hazard, no ~1000 char truncation):
- MCP tool execute_python_script(code) - send a normal multi-line script.
- bridge/bridge_py.py script.py [--engine-log] - from PowerShell with the real python.exe.
Scripts that must return data: print("@@JSON " + json.dumps(value)); server._python_json
parses that line.

Still true: the script runs on the editor main thread. Keep it to a couple of seconds.
From PowerShell 5.1 do not pass Python via python -c with quotes (they are stripped) and do
not write helper files with Set-Content -Encoding utf8 (adds a BOM that breaks path parsing
in bridge_shoot.py); use [IO.File]::WriteAllText.

title: Tools: level_inventory.py / inspect_level, crypak.py, bmp2png.py
source: GameSDK sample project study, 2026-09-15
content:
level/level_inventory.py <level dir> [--json] [--nav-points]  (MCP: inspect_level)
Reads layers/*.lyr + level.pak with Sandbox closed or open: object types per layer, entity
classes, AI characters with archetype faction/BT/equipment (GUIDs resolved through
Libs/EntityArchetypes in loose files or paks), NavigationAreas (inclusion/exclusion, floor z,
height, agents, world-space bbox, optional world points with rotation applied), seed points,
cover count, smart-object classes, and which .bai files were exported.

packaging/crypak.py list|grep|cat|extract - read CryPak archives (see gamesdk-paks).

assets/bmp2png.py in.bmp [out.png] [--scale N] - bridge.viewport.screenshot writes BMP of
the WHOLE Sandbox window; convert to view it. Prints mean luma and saturation.
Note: a saturation of ~5 (below bridge_shoot.py's blank threshold of 8) was a REAL frame of
dark forest canopy, not a blank one - look at the image before rejecting it.

title: Layer streaming: tall AreaShape -> AreaTrigger -> Engine:LayerSwitch
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Woodland splits into 6 zones AB01..AB06; each is a parent layer with _Objects, _PFX,
_Gameplay children plus ABnn_Lighting under a Lighting parent. Only Main, Audio and
Player_Collisions have DefaultLoaded="1". Editor-only layers use Exportable="0"
(Level_Occ_Mesh, Lighting_Helpers, GDC_Demo_Materials).

Switching: ABnn_LS_Shape (closed AreaShape in Main, Height=100, floor z=0) lists
ABnn_LS_trig in its <Entities> (the shape's target) -> AreaTrigger (bOnlyPlayers=1,
entity itself parked at z~129 - its position is irrelevant) -> Start_FG:
entity:AreaTrigger.Enter -> Engine:LayerSwitch nodes. Entering AB01 unhides AB01, AB02,
their lighting, Background, Cinematics and hides AB03-AB06 + lighting.

Tool: level_study.py <level> streaming (or MCP study_level("streaming")) prints
trigger.Enter -> Layer(Hide|Unhide). Linking shape -> trigger has no Python command
(general.add_entity_link is a different link type); do it in the shape's Properties.

title: Sound: AudioAreaAmbience + linked shape + area_fade_distance RTPC
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Woodland ambience beds (19): an AudioAreaAmbience entity with
audioTriggerPlayTrigger="Play_l_woodland_amb_<area>_<thing>", audioRTPCRtpc="area_fade_distance",
fRtpcDistance=15, eiOcclusionType=1, is the TARGET of an AreaShape (e.g. 8 points,
Height=70, Priority=30, GroupId=1, per-side ObstructSound) or AreaSphere (Radius 10) /
AreaBox in the always-loaded Audio layer. The RTPC runs 0..fRtpcDistance as the listener
approaches, fading the bed across the border; Priority picks the winner of overlaps.

Reverb: AudioAreaEntity (3) with fEnvironmentDistance/fFadeDistance 5 on shapes like an
AreaBox 9x10x15 m priority 90; environments forest, open_ground, cave, tower.
One-shots: AudioTriggerSpot (21) audioTriggerPlayTriggerName=Play_l_woodland_sfx_*, PlayMode
eiBehaviour + fMinDelay/fMaxDelay 1-2 s + vectorRandomizationArea for random repeats.
FG_Audio flowgraph: AudioAreaEntity OnFarToNear/OnNearToFar -> Audio:Trigger play/stop,
FadeValue -> Audio:Rtpc; Audio:Switch l_woodland_mixing states cave/ravine/riverbed/none;
ProximityTrigger -> bird fly-off one-shot. Cinematic music = Audio:Trigger in Start_FG.

Middleware: GameSDK audio.pak ships audio/fmod, audio/wwise, audio/sdlmixer (each ace/ +
assets/). Level objects only reference trigger names defined in the ACE project.

title: Invisible walls = any mesh whose material has MTL_FLAG_COLLISION_PROXY (0x2000)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Woodland layer Player_Collisions (DefaultLoaded=1): 147 Designer meshes along the playable
edge using materials/special/collision_proxy_entitiesonly.mtl:
  <Material MtlFlags="532512" Shader="Illum" SurfaceType="mat_nodraw" Diffuse="1,0,0" Opacity="0.05">
532512 = 0x82020 includes MTL_FLAG_COLLISION_PROXY 0x2000 (Cry3DEngine/IMaterial.h).
CBrush::SetMaterial (Cry3DEngine/Brush.cpp ~618) and CEntitySlot set ERF_COLLISION_PROXY
(RndFlags bit 22) automatically; render, shadows, SVO/GI and culling skip such nodes,
physics keeps them. MTL_FLAG_RAYCAST_PROXY 0x100000 -> ERF_RAYCAST_PROXY blocks raycasts only.

MCP create_collision_wall(x, y, z, length, height, thickness, yaw_deg, material): scaled
objects/default/primitive_cube.cgf Brush + object.set_custom_material; writes
<assets>/materials/special/collision_proxy.mtl with those flags if the material is missing.
TESTED in editor 2026-09-15 (pos, 30 deg yaw via object.set_rotation degrees, scale
10x0.5x4, material applied). NOT yet tested that it blocks the player in game mode.
verified_note: The text says it was not tested that the wall blocks the player in game mode. Listed by the 2026-10-23 audit (K-14): the text holds a claim that was read or planned but never run or seen working (look for 'untested', 'NOT SEEN', 'not yet'); treat it as a hypothesis until shown.

title: Kill zones, visual borders and occluder meshes in woodland
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Kill zone: AB06_river_kill_shape (AreaShape, 6 points, Height 8) -> AB06_river_kill_Atrig
(AreaTrigger, bOnlyPlayers) -> AB06_FG: Enter -> Actor:KillPlayer.

Visual border: vegetation group sprucetree_border (spruce_border_d.cgf, 394 instances,

title: Woodland terrain: painted 4-layer Terrain.Layer materials, vegetation, roads, water
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Heightmap 2048 m, 1 m cells (bridge.terrain.info; leveldata.xml LevelInfo HeightmapSize=800 is
stale - trust the live value), elevation 18-245, no ocean (WaterLevel -1000000).
Terrain layers Ground/Rock/RiverBed/Moss all altitude 0-1024 with meaningless slope bands

title: Woodland probe scheme: one global probe + root/child probes per location
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
47 EnvironmentProbes (the ambient in deferred shading without SVOGI):
- l_probe_global: box 5000^3, SortPriority 1, diffuse 1, 256 cubemap - the fallback.
- 33 root probes l_probe_AB<n>_<place>_root: boxes 10-120 m, SortPriority 10-20, diffuse 1-2,
  fAttenuationFalloffMax 0.1-0.5, cubemap_resolution 256, texture Textures/cubemaps/woodland/<name>_cm.tif.
  Some roots are 1x1x1 boxes that only capture.
- 11 child probes: cubemap_resolution 0 and the ROOT's cubemap path, larger/offset boxes.
- all bAffectsThisAreaOnly=1, bVolumetricFog=1; live in ABnn_Lighting layers that stream with the zone.
- interior probe priority 99 for the cinematic room; l_probe_global_night bActive=0 diffuse 6
  priority 100 in Lighting_Night (switchable).
Cubemaps are shipped pre-generated (222 files in textures.pak). Only 5 point lights exist,
all in the cinematic room; outdoors is sun + probes only.
Look-dev: layer Lighting_Helpers (not exported) has 98 hidden primitive_sphere_noproxy with
Materials/references/black_reflective to judge probe transitions.

title: Woodland cinematic: TrackView sequence GDC_Flythrough_01 and how it is started
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:

room (primitive_sphere x5 black_matte_2_sided + VisArea + 5 lights + probe priority 99),
staged GeomEntities, and SequenceObject GDC_Flythrough_01 (also moviedata.xml in level.pak).

(0.25-1.25) and Goto tracks; Event node TrackEvent keys Heads_Track_Layers 0, Toad_Track_Layers
53, Flythrough_Layers_A 68, Flythrough_Layers_B 239 which Start_FG's TrackEvent nodes turn into
LayerSwitches; ScreenFader keys (black, 1.5-2 s); DepthOfField keys; Camera node FOV 35-50 +
Position/Rotation 50+ keys + ShakeMultiplier; 11 Entity nodes (Visibility/Animation/Event,
particles via ByString, two AudioTrigger tracks); a GeomCache node.

Start: Start_FG Cutscene_Menu_ATrig (AreaTrigger on a 4-point shape H30) / action listeners ->
Engine:LayerSwitch Cinematics -> Animations:PlaySequence seq_Sequence_File=GDC_Flythrough_01 +
Image:ScreenFader fade-in 2 s + Audio:Trigger Play_l_woodland_mus_trackview. Triggers also have
a PlaySequence property. Python `trackview` module has 87 functions (new_sequence_by_name,
add_node, set_time...) - untested.

title: Woodland gameplay glue: objectives, waterfall spray, spawn points
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
- Objectives: leveldata/objectives.xml texts; 7 MissionObjective entities; AB05_FG (154 nodes)
  drives them with ProximityTriggers, Mission:GameTokenSet/Check, Logic:Gate, RandomSelect.

title: Tools: level_study.py / study_level, layer_probe.py, create_collision_wall
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
level/level_study.py <level dir> [overview streaming audio borders terrain lighting
cinematics logic] [--json] - offline explanation of how a level is built (reads .lyr,
leveldata/, <level>.level, level.pak through crypak). MCP study_level(section, level_dir="").

title: CRITICAL: a living entity's collider must float above the feet - the gap is the step-up height
source: GameSDK player study, 2026-09-15 (PLAYER_GUIDE.md)
content:
CLivingEntity::Step (CryPhysics/livingentity.cpp):
  maxUpStep = heightCollider - size.z - size.x*bUseCapsule            (~1414)
  ground ray from heightCollider - size.z, length 1.5*(heightCollider - size.z)   (~1016)
  snap onto ground found within (heightCollider - size.z) below the feet if slope < minFallAngle (~1681)
The capsule is meant to touch only walls/obstacles taller than the gap; the ray carries the
character over lower bumps. A collider whose bottom is at the pivot has ZERO step-up height
and collides with every terrain bump.

GameSDK standing player: size (0.41, 0.41, 0.3) capsule, heightCollider 1.25 -> bottom 0.54 m,
top 1.96 m, step-up 0.54 m. Crouch: heightCollider 0.7, size.z 0.1 -> step 0.19 m.
Tool: character_collider.py / MCP plan_character_collider (design or check parameters).

title: CORRECTION: My Project's capsule 'fix' (bottom at the feet) gives 0 m step-up
source: GameSDK player study, 2026-09-15 (PLAYER_GUIDE.md)
content:
Earlier the capsule was set with
CCharacterControllerComponent Radius 0.7, Height 2.2 and transform z = 0.7*0.5 + 2.2*0.25 = 0.9,
i.e. radius 0.35, cylinder half-height 0.55, spanning exactly 0 -> 1.8 m, and this was called
the "best candidate for the stutter". By the engine code (see living-step-up-gap) that layout has
stepUpHeight = 0.9 - 0.55 - 0.35 = 0: the capsule hits every bump, which can itself produce
"stuck every second". This is source analysis, NOT a measurement.

Suggested test (one build): Radius 0.7, Height 1.4, transform z 1.1 -> capsule 0.4..1.8 m with
0.4 m step-up (character_collider.py design --height 1.8 --radius 0.35 --step 0.4). Measure with
claude_player_walk 6 and, once deployed, sample_entity_physics (bStuck/bFlying/velocity).

title: pe_player_dynamics angles are DEGREES (header says radians); engine and component defaults
source: GameSDK player study, 2026-09-15 (PLAYER_GUIDE.md)
content:
physinterface.h documents minSlideAngle/maxClimbAngle/maxJumpAngle/minFallAngle as radians, but
CLivingEntity::SetParams does cos(angle*pi/180) and GetParams returns acos(...)*180/pi
(livingentity.cpp ~440 and ~493): they are DEGREES. CCharacterControllerComponent passes .ToDegrees().
Engine defaults: kInertia 8, kInertiaAccel 0, hCyl 1.1, size (0.4,0.4,0.6), cylinder, slide 36 deg,
climb 54, jump 54, fall 70.2, nodSpeed 60, groundContactEps max(0.01*size.z, 0.004).
kInertia == 0 is a special case: velocity = requested velocity projected on the ground.

CCharacterControllerComponent::Physicalize: sizeCollider = (Radius*0.5, 1, Height*0.5), capsule
halves size.z again; heightCollider = component transform z (0 if never set). Defaults Radius 0.45,
Height 0.935, inertia 8/8, climb 50, jump 50, slide 70, fall 80; the editor default of
MaxGroundVelocity is DEG2RAD(50)=0.87 while the member init is 16 (effect not checked).

title: GameSDK player movement pipeline, slope handling and jump
source: GameSDK player study, 2026-09-15 (PLAYER_GUIDE.md)
content:
Input actionmap "player" (Libs/Config/defaultProfile.xml: WASD, space jump, c crouch, lshift sprint,
maxis_x/y rotate, q/e lean, f use) -> CPlayerInput -> CPlayerMovementController -> state machine.
CPlayerStateUtil::CalculateGroundOrJumpMovement: stance maxSpeed x sprint/backward/strafe multipliers x
cvars pl_movement.speedScale 1.2, sprint_SpeedScale 1.8, strafe_SpeedScale 0.9, crouch_SpeedScale 1.0.
CPlayerStateGround::OnPrePhysicsUpdate: shallow-water slowdown; SP desiredVel *= groundNormal.z (slower
on slopes); between 10 and 50 deg (cubic ramp) removes the velocity component into the slope; flattens
to base orientation; request goes through AnimatedCharacter (inertia in SAnimatedCharacterParams).
UpdatePlayerPhysicsStats reads pe_status_living: vel - velGround, groundNormal lerp frameTime*6.666,
flying/stuck; pl_movement.ground_timeInAirToFall 0.3, pl_fallHeight 0.3.
Jump (CPlayerStateJump::StartJump): speed sqrt(2*jumpHeight*g), allowed after onGround > 0.2 s, jump-lock
timer damps repeats, in air kAirControl x pl_jump_control.air_control_scale 1.0 and inertia x
air_inertia_scale 0.3; landing height accounts for collider bottom.

title: SOLVED: NPC requested velocity 0.0000 - duplicate navigation components serialized into the layer
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Symptom: IEntityNavigationComponent::GetRequestedVelocity() 0.0000 every frame and 0 state-updated
callbacks, while ai_DebugMovementSystem showed the plan executing [FollowPath].
Cause (measured): each villager had 4 CEntityAINavigationComponent, 4 CCharacterControllerComponent and
4 CStaticMeshComponent - 3 serialized into main.lyr over successive saves plus the one Initialize()
created with GetOrCreateComponent. CEntityAINavigationComponent::ProcessEvent(START_GAME) does Stop()
(MovementSystem::UnregisterEntity(entityId)) then Start() (RegisterEntity with ITS adapter), so the last
instance to process the event owns the movement plan; the pointer the game code held never got callbacks.
Fix (My Project Npc.cpp RebuildOwnedComponents): on Reset(entering game)/GameplayStarted remove EVERY
instance (IEntity::GetAllComponents<T> + RemoveComponent), create one fresh set, flag each
GetComponentFlags().Add(EEntityComponentFlags::NoSave), then m_pEntity->UpdateComponentEventMask(nav).
Keeping one old copy does not work: removing any nav component unregisters the entity id for all.
Facts: RemoveComponent destroys the record immediately (~SEntityComponentRecord -> ShutDownComponent ->
OnShutDown -> Stop), so the old Stop() runs before the new Initialize()->Start(); entity events go through
per-event listener sets that tolerate add/remove mid-dispatch; IEntityComponent::ProcessEvent is protected
(calling it on another component does not compile). Result: 14,439 callbacks at 2.2 m/s, waypoint reached,
and after one save main.lyr holds only CNpcComponent per villager. HOW IT WAS FOUND, and the instrument lesson: the investigation (history in the superseded chunks npc-open-problem, npc-hypothesis, npc-ruled-out, read with include_superseded) measured GetRequestedVelocity() as EXACTLY 0.0000 on every frame and, with collision avoidance set to EType::None, the state-updated callback fired ZERO times in 20 s, which showed NewStateComputed was never called on the component the code held. Instrument with a threshold no higher than 0.0005 and print %.4f: an earlier 0.1 m/s threshold produced a false 'no velocity' reading (the path follower ramps up from zero at maxAcceleration) and misled the investigation for an afternoon.
