title: Character stalls on small inclines / goes bFlying: groundContactEps 0.004 and air control 0 (component defaults)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Measured 2026-09-15: villagers requested 2.2 m/s but moved ~0.77 m/s and stalled on small inclines;
bridge.entities.physics showed bFlying 1 while 0.009 m above groundHeight, and bStuck on a ~7 deg climb.
Source: CLivingEntity::Step (livingentity.cpp) ground contact = feet within groundContactEps of the ground
ray hit (~1946); bFlying = !(groundContact|stuck) (~1950); the snap back down while above ground needs the
drop to be smaller than this frame's move (~1682), and at ~750 fps a frame moves < 3 mm. While flying the
requested velocity is applied only if kAirControl > 0 (~1363). CCharacterControllerComponent defaults:
GroundContactEps 0.004, AirControl 0 (CharacterControllerComponent.h). GameSDK characters: groundContactEps
0.025 (ActorDefinitions.h), k_air_control 0.9 (BasicActor.lua).
CORRECTION after building and measuring: eps 0.025 (GameSDK's value) was NOT enough. On 5-15 deg slopes the feet
sit 0.028-0.042 m above the ray hit and bFlying toggles exactly at the tolerance; villagers stalled ~10 s pushing at
2.2 m/s, then "path failed" and the patrol moved to the next waypoint (the user's "turns away"). Live A/B via
bridge.component.properties, speed from position change: eps 0.025 downhill 94% flying, 50% windows < 1.5 m/s;
eps 0.10 level 2.15 / uphill 2.16 / downhill 2.15 m/s, 0-2% flying. GameSDK inertia 10/11 made level walking worse.
Npc.h kGroundContactEps is now 0.10 (air control 0.9 kept). VERIFIED after rebuild, 150 s: Villager1 on AI Path
VillagerRoute (33.7->40 m) level 2.18 / uphill 2.13 / downhill 2.14 m/s, Villager2 2.19 / 2.18 / 2.16, 0% flying,
106 waypoints reached, 0 path failed, 0 re-issues -- solved. Player still has eps 0.004 (untested on slopes). Exact cause of the few-cm hover not fully explained;
"footprint max" was wrong (ShootRayDown casts one centre ray). Measure speed from displacement: physics vel keeps its
requested value while crawling; NPC-log distance-to-waypoint is invalid (paths detour). Ruled out: navigation velocity z = 0 (with kInertia 0 and contact it is projected on the
slope, ~1359); per-frame SetRotation (rotation-only xform sends only q, PhysicsProxy.cpp ~631, so the
pe_params_pos teleport check at ~316 that zeroes velocity is not hit). The player has the same eps default.

title: Homebound (GGJ19) crowd pathing = Entity Link waypoint chains, not the navmesh
source: Homebound GGJ19 study, 2026-09-15 (HOMEBOUND_STUDY.md)
content:
Homebound (Launcher asset crytek/homebound-project-ggj19, engine-5.5) has no NavigationArea/AIPath; level.pak's
mnmnavmission0.bai is 30 bytes (empty). Crowd NPCs (schematyc::crowd, CPersonComponent) walk the entity's Entity Links in
order: layer <EntityLinks><Link TargetId Name/></EntityLinks> to empty entities used as waypoints; repeating a link makes
it turn back (crowd-20: 102,101,98,101,102,103,104,103), Loop restarts at the first link. Update: face the flattened
direction, step to link->next within sqrt(0.5) m, pe_action_impulse(dir*MoveSpeed*dt) while speed^2 < MaxVelocity, zero
angular velocity each frame. Body: rigid body + Plane Constraint (Z axis) to stay upright. Level is flat (z=32), no
obstacle avoidance. Reusable idea for My Project: Entity Links as quick designer waypoints feeding NavigateTo
(IEntity::GetEntityLinks / IEntityLink::next exist in 5.7); AI Path is the engine-native equivalent already implemented.

title: Homebound traffic: CarSpawner linked to one target, straight-line impulse cars with ray queueing
source: Homebound GGJ19 study, 2026-09-15 (HOMEBOUND_STUDY.md)
content:
CCarSpawner (14 in logic.lyr, MinDelay 2 MaxDelay 4) links to one Car_Spawner_Target-N; START_GAME stores the target
position; when activated from Flow Graph (EntityFlowNode "Activate") it spawns schematyc::car every random delay facing the
target with a random mesh/material from Objects/Vehicles/TrafficCars. CCarComponent: impulse along the direction under
MaxVelocity, zero angular velocity, three forward RayWorldIntersection casts; if another car going the same way (or
crossing) is hit it sets velocity 0 (queues). Deletes itself at the destination (<1 m, z ignored), after MaxLifeTime 20 s,
or on RESET. car.schematyc_ent: RigidBody, Car (MoveSpeed 100, MaxVelocity 40), mesh, Plane Constraint, Damage,
Projector Light, Trigger. Player is also a rigid body moved by impulses (no character controller).

function); objectGUID ties a node to a component instance; <links> use srcOutputId/dstInputId FourCC ids.

title: Off-screen characters don't animate; don't queue Mannequin fragments for them (queue piles up)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
CCharInstance::PerFrameUpdate (CryAnimation/CharacterInstance.cpp:957) advances a character only with
CS_FLAG_UPDATE_ALWAYS or CS_FLAG_RENDER_NODE_VISIBLE (set by 3DEngine when the render node is potentially visible). Measured:
an out-of-view villager's walk stayed at normalized time 0.05 while Idle/Walk fragments queued behind it (11 entries);
moving the player so it was in view drained the queue to 1 and the walk resumed, MoveSpeed = ground speed. Expected engine
optimisation. Fix in Npc.cpp UpdateAnimation: if !(pCharacter->GetFlags() & (CS_FLAG_RENDER_NODE_VISIBLE |
CS_FLAG_UPDATE_ALWAYS)) forget the active fragment and don't queue; it re-queues once visible. Verified: hidden villager held queue 1
for 45 s; brought into view it played Walk within one 3 s dump, MoveSpeed 2.20/1.30 = ground speed. Set CS_FLAG_UPDATE_ALWAYS only if hidden characters need poses (anim events, attachments). In editor game mode
the player spawns at the viewport camera, so which NPCs animate depends on where the camera was.

title: Debugging animation playback: dump the skeleton FIFO; GetDesiredMotionParam misleads
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
SetDesiredMotionParam writes only the newest (unlocked, not blending-out) queue entry's SParametricSampler;
GetDesiredMotionParam returns the value of an older activated sampler, so a "0.00" readout does not mean the blend gets 0.
Dump layer 0 instead: for i < GetNumAnimsInFIFO(0): GetAnimFromFIFO(0,i) -> GetIAnimationSet()->GetNameByAnimID(GetAnimationId()),
IsActivated(), GetTransitionWeight(), GetCurrentSegmentNormalizedTime(), and for parametric entries
m_MotionParameter[d] where m_MotionParameterID[d] == eMotionParamID_TravelSpeed. A normalized time that never changes =
the skeleton is not being updated (see anim-offscreen-no-update). Check what the game camera sees with
bridge.viewport.screenshot (no camera move) before concluding a character is visible.

title: FBX animation -> .caf with rc.exe, no Sandbox: flat JSON request + proxy skin for animation-only FBX
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
animation/fbx_to_caf.py <clip.FBX> <out folder> converts a clip (tested: crysis-animation-assets, Bip01 rig).
Measured traps (RC 1.1.8.7): (1) rc.exe rejects a raw .fbx -- it takes an import-request JSON plus /overwriteextension=fbx.
The JSON is FLAT {"source_filename","output_ext":"caf","unit_size":"file","scale":1,"animation":{"name":"",
"motionNodePath":["Locator_Locomotion"],"startFrame":-1,"endFrame":-1}}; a {"metadata":..} or {"request":..} wrapper is
silently ignored and RC writes a static .cgf. (2) RC's FBX SDK refuses files without a skinned mesh
("FBX Scene does not have any skinned mesh", CryFbxScene.cpp PrepareBones) and these clips have none:
fbx_binary.add_proxy_skin binds one mesh to Bip01 Pelvis (Skin Deformer + Cluster + 3 OO connections + Definitions).
(3) Rewriting a binary FBX must keep the original 16-byte footer id (tied to FileId/CreationTime) or the SDK says
"File is corrupted"; footer = pad to 16 (full 16 if aligned) + 4 zeros + version + 120 zeros + magic.
(4) Git Bash rewrites /options into paths: call rc.exe from Python or MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1.

Animations.img + *.dba bytes (crypak extract) before converting. Used: melee_killingblow_rightkick_1p_01 (4.97 s).

title: Simple NPC reactions in C++: sight cone + line of sight, hearing, watch, startle, hurry (CNpcComponent)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Every 0.2 s SensePlayer: CGamePlugin::IterateOverPlayers; seen = distance < SightRange (10) and inside SightFov
(120 deg) or within PersonalSpace, and RayWorldIntersection(eye 1.6 m -> player eye, ent_static|ent_terrain,
skip both physical entities) hits nothing; heard = within HearingRange (16) and player pe_status_dynamics speed > 5
(sprint 7.5, walk 4.0). Sensed -> BeginWatching: m_bNavigating=false BEFORE IEntityNavigationComponent::StopMovement
(its completion callback must not advance the patrol), Drive(0), ignore the nav velocity callback, slerp to face the
player; 2.5 s after losing the player -> GoToWaypoint(current). Closer than PersonalSpace (2.5) -> Startle fragment
(clamped 1.6 s) then SetMovementProperties normalSpeed=RunSpeed for 5 s (Run fragment above 2.8 m/s). Measured:
"sees the player at 9.7 m", startle at 1.6 m, legs at 4.5 m/s then "calmed down". Sight range needs hysteresis
(+2 m while watching): without it a player at ~10 m flipped sees/lost every few seconds. Not separately tested yet:
hearing (the scripted walk is below the audible speed) and the hysteresis itself.

title: Match an NPC's movement speed to its clip's root speed (read it from GetCurrentVelocity)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
With animation-driven motion ON, ISkeletonAnim::GetCurrentVelocity reports the clip's locator speed, so the NPC
trace shows it next to the body's ground speed. Measured: GameSDK relaxed_tac_run_nw_fwd_fast_3p_01 ~3.5 m/s root
while the villager moved at 4.45 -> RunSpeed default 3.5; walk blend-space tops out at 2.0 while villagers walked 2.2 ->
WalkSpeed 2.0. Re-measured after the change: run body 3.33 / root 3.39, walk 1.97 / 1.97. Values saved in main.lyr override the C++ defaults: WalkSpeed was
written as 2.2 in the layer and had to be changed there too (bridge.component.properties + save_level did not rewrite
the unmodified layer; editing main.lyr before an editor restart did).

Correction 2026-09-24: GetCurrentVelocity is the clip's LOCATOR speed per animation second; the blend space is driven by TravelSpeed = body speed, so it matches the body by construction. The feet do not: see foot-slide-stance-probe (feet 1.90 vs locator 2.00).

title: Player on slopes: groundContactEps 0.004 is fine up to 23 degrees (villager needed 0.10)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository

claude_player_walk <seconds> <yawDeg> (yaw 0 = +Y, world direction angle theta -> yaw = theta - 90) walks the
player and writes claude_player_walk.log. Segments found from heights.r32 (index [x*1024+y]). eps 0.004: up/down 12 deg

title: exporter.export_to_engine can block on 'Navigation System Warning' -- Enter is the safe default

source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
packaging/package_project.py <Game.cryproject> --out <dir> imports the engine's
Tools/CryVersionSelector/release_project.py, replaces release_project_gui.configure_build (Tk dialog) with
(out, "win_x64:Profile", "bin/win_x64", symbols) and input() with a no-op, then runs the same task list: engine paks,

(/TargetHasEditor=0 /stripMetadata -> Animations/Data/GameData/Objects/Textures.pak), config.pak + system.cfg.
Found: RC's TexturesJob re-converts every .dds and fails on GameSDK's already-compiled, split textures
("Cannot load texture, file content too small") so they were absent; the script packs every loose .dds/.dds.N that no
packaged pak contains into Assets/PrecompiledTextures.pak (289 files, 80 MB). Verified: GameLauncher.exe
+r_Fullscreen 0 +map example loads the level, villagers route over the exported navmesh and arrive, textures load.
Editor leftovers terraintexture.pak$* in the level folder get packed too (clean them first). 607 MB build.

title: Seeing with IVisionMap from C++: register observer/observable yourself, fovCos is the half angle
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
CEntityAIObserverComponent / CEntityAIObservableComponent register with the vision map only on
ENTITY_EVENT_START_GAME, so components created by code at game start never register. Registering directly works and
uses CryCommon only: pVisionMap->CreateVisionID("name.Observer") then RegisterObserver(id, ObserverParams{callback,
entityId, faction, typeMask, typesToObserveMask=VisionMapTypes::Player, factionsToObserveMask=1<<playersFaction,
sightRange, fovCos, eyePosition, eyeDirection, updatePeriod, raycastFlags=AI_VISION_RAY_CAST_FLAG_BLOCKED_BY_SOLID_COVER,
skipList=own physical entity}); each frame SyncEye + ObserverChanged(id, params, eChangedPosition|eChangedOrientation|
eChangedSightRange). The observed entity needs RegisterObservable with typeMask Player, a valid faction and its own
physical entity in the skip list (otherwise the ray ends in its own capsule). CVisionMap::ShouldObserve = typesToObserve
& typeMask, factionsToObserve & (1<<faction), range, FOV, user condition; rays are queued, results arrive in the callback.
TRAP: IsInFoV compares dot(eyeDir,toTarget) with fovCos directly -> fovCos = cos(fov/2); the stock observer component
passes cos(full fov), so its "60 degrees" is a 120 degree cone. Measured: engine sight matched a hand-written
cone+raycast on 96 of 98 ticks (the 2 differences were the queued ray lagging/leading).

title: Hearing with IAuditionMap: listener ears, sound stimuli, and the faction requirement
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Listener: pAuditionMap->RegisterListener(entityId, SListenerParams{listeningDistanceScale,
factionsToListenMask, ears (SListenerEarParams world positions), onSoundHeardCallback}) and ListenerChanged(entityId,
params, ListenerParamsChangeOptions::ChangedEars) as it moves -- a listener with NO ears never hears anything, and the
stock AI Listener component starts with an empty ear list. Sound: pAuditionMap->OnSoundEvent(SSoundStimulusParams{
position, radius, sourceEntityId, faction, obstructionHandling}, "debug text"). CAuditionMap::ShouldListenerAcknowledgeSound
DROPS any stimulus whose faction is IFactionMap::InvalidFactionID (0xff) and then tests factionsToListenMask &
(1<<faction), so Scripts/AI/Factions.xml must define the factions (this project: Players, Villagers) and the emitter must
set one. Measured in My Project: the player emits a stimulus every 0.4 s while moving, radius 5 m walking and 16 m
sprinting; a villager 15.1 m away heard the sprint and reacted.

title: A behaviour tree on a component entity: core nodes + Basic_MoveToPosition only, C++ as the senses
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Start it from C++: gEnv->pAISystem->GetIBehaviorTreeManager()->StartModularBehaviorTree(entityId,
"Villager_Patrol") (Scripts/AI/BehaviorTrees/<name>.xml, no extension); the AI Behavior Tree component cannot be given a
tree name through its interface. Send events with HandleEvent(entityId, BehaviorTree::Event("PlayerSeen")) and write the
blackboard with GetBehaviorTreeBlackboard(entityId)->SetVariable<Vec3>(BlackboardVariableId("Waypoint"), pos).
Node availability: BehaviorTreeNodes_Core.cpp (Sequence, Selector, Priority, Parallel, Loop, StateMachine + Transitions,
Wait, Timeout, IfCondition, AssertCondition, MonitorCondition, WaitForEvent, SendEvent, SendTransitionEvent,
SuppressFailure, Log, Halt, RandomGate) and the component-safe BehaviorTreeNodes_Basic.cpp (Basic_MoveToPosition,
Basic_MoveToCover) work without an AI actor; everything in BehaviorTreeNodes_AI.cpp (Move, Shoot, Stance, Animate,
ExecuteLua, SetAlertness, ...) needs GameSDK's Lua CAIActor. Basic_MoveToPosition requires a 'speed' attribute
(Walk|Run|Sprint) plus bbDestination and queues a MovementRequest for the entity -- the navigation component's movement
adapter serves it, so the velocity arrives through the same callback as an ordinary NavigateTo. Leaving a state destroys
the node's runtime data, which calls UnsuscribeFromRequestCallback -> the planner cancels that request, so movement stops.
Measured: villager walked its ring under the tree, stopped on PlayerHeard, resumed on PlayerLost.

title: Exclusion areas cut the navmesh in ~5 s; measure with claude_nav_probe / claude_nav_ray
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
A NavigationArea with Exclusion=true (general.new_object('NavigationArea'), set Height, set Exclusion,
nav_insert_point in OBJECT-RELATIVE coords) cuts a hole in every overlapping mesh. Two console commands added to
My Project's Game.dll make this measurable instead of visual: claude_nav_probe x y z [agentType] prints
IsLocationValidInNavigationMesh + GetClosestPointInNavigationMesh + GetEnclosingMeshID, and claude_nav_ray x1 y1 z1
x2 y2 z2 [agentType] prints INavigationSystem::NavMeshRayCast's result (0 NoHit, 1 Hit, 2 RayTooLong,
3 DisconnectedLocations, 4 InvalidStart, 5 InvalidEnd); both write to claude_npc.log. Measured: a 6x4 m exclusion prism
(floor 25 m, height 20 m) over the patrol route turned "on mesh 1" into "on mesh 0, closest 2.5 m away" and the route ray
from NoHit into Hit about 5 s after creation, with no manual regeneration; deleting the area restored both. The villager's
AI path then reported "30 waypoints usable (2 off the navmesh)" and it kept patrolling without a path failure.

title: Runtime navmesh updates come from WorldMonitor -- and it only runs in the editor
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
NavigationSystem hooks WorldMonitor to EventPhysBBoxChange and EventPhysEntityDeleted and forwards the
old and new AABBs to CMNMUpdatesManager::EntityChanged, which queues tile updates. WorldMonitor sets
m_enabled = gEnv->IsEditor() in its constructor, so in a packaged game nothing regenerates when the world moves: the game
must call gEnv->pAISystem->GetNavigationSystem()->GetUpdateManager()->WorldChanged(aabb) itself (that is exactly what the
Flow Graph node at FlowNodeAI.cpp:2519 does). Only static entities and rigid bodies with mass 0 are considered
(NavigationSystemUtils::IsDynamicObjectPartOfTheMNMGenerationProcess). Update modes (INavigationUpdatesManager::EUpdateMode):
Continuous (default), AfterStabilization (waits ai_NavmeshStabilizationTimeToUpdate = 0.3 s of quiet), Disabled,
DisabledDuringLoad; the editor also has ai_MNMEditorBackgroundUpdate=1.

title: Collision avoidance (ORCA) on IEntityNavigationComponent: small but real, and it gates the velocity
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
SCollisionAvoidanceProperties{radius 0.3, height 2.0, type None|Passive|Active} on the navigation
component; the agent registers with gEnv->pAISystem->GetCollisionAvoidanceSystem() and reports maxSpeed from the movement
properties and radius from these. With type Active, CEntityAINavigationComponent::NewStateComputed IGNORES the path
follower's velocity (returns early) until the avoidance agent delivers its adjusted one -- so a game that reads
GetRequestedVelocity sees ORCA's output, and a game that relies on the state callback firing every frame sees fewer calls.
Measured with two villagers walking the same AI path in opposite directions (0.35 m capsules, 2 m/s): closest approach
0.70 m with None (capsules touching) vs 0.90 m with Active. Live A/B is possible with bridge.component.properties
{"colavoid": {"type": "Active"}} on CEntityAINavigationComponent.

title: Custom off-mesh links (jump/ladder) in a component project: pathfinding yes, traversal no
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full pipeline in Code/Components/JumpLink.{h,cpp} (CryCommon only): subclass MNM::IOffMeshLink (own
CryGUID, GetStartPosition/GetEndPosition/CanUse) -> IOffMeshNavigationManager::RequestLinkAddition(MNM::OffMeshLinkID(),
agentTypeId, link, SOffMeshLinkCallbacks{acquireDataCallback, additionCompletedCallback, removedCallback}); the acquire
callback fills SNavigationData with GetEnclosingMeshID + GetTriangleIDWhereLocationIsAtForMesh (both ends must be on the
SAME mesh) -> register a Movement::Block factory via
IMovementSystem::RegisterFunctionToConstructMovementBlockForCustomNavigationType (re-register per game session).
MEASURED: addition returns Success with both triangle ids; with an exclusion wall cutting a corridor end to end,
INavigationSystem::IsPointReachableFromPosition went 0 -> 1 after adding the link, and the agent paths to the link's start
point. But the agent does NOT cross: GenericPlanner splits the path into FollowPath (endDistance 2.5 m before a custom
block) + the custom block; the creator IS called (4 times = s_maxAllowedReplanning) yet the block's Begin never runs
because FollowPath::Update returns CantBeFinished after the path follower reports the target unreachable for >3 s
(MovementBlock_FollowPath.cpp:100), and the request fails. CPathFollower has NAV_CUSTOM_NAVIGATION special cases
(GetDistToCustomNav) that the smart-object flow uses together with GameSDK's actor adapter and its exact-positioning
phases; the component adapter (CEntityAINavigationComponent, endDistance 0, use2D) does not provide them. So in a
component project use custom links for pathfinding/reachability and carry the character across in game code.

title: Day/night and rain from code: ITimeOfDay::SetTime and I3DEngine::SetRainParams
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Time of day: gEnv->p3DEngine->GetTimeOfDay()->SetTime(hour, true) applies immediately; the cvar
e_TimeOfDaySpeed then advances it by itself (0 = frozen). It is a level/preset setting, so it survives game-mode toggles
and is stored in the time-of-day preset, not per session. Rain: fill SRainParams (vWorldPos + fRadius define the volume,
fAmount/fCurrentAmount the strength, then the look: fRainDropsAmount/Speed/Lighting, fMistAmount/fMistHeight,
fPuddlesAmount/MaskAmount/RippleAmount, fSplashesAmount, fFakeGlossiness, fFakeReflectionAmount) and call
gEnv->p3DEngine->SetRainParams(params); also set r_Rain (2 on, 0 off). CRYENGINE 5.7 has NO rain default-component --
GameSDK's Rain entity (GameDll/Environment/Rain.cpp) just calls SetRainParams every frame with the entity's position.
My Project wraps both as console commands claude_tod <hour> [speed] and claude_rain <amount> [radius]; measured viewport
saturation noon 15.9 vs 21:30 12.0.

title: Jumping a living entity: AddVelocity while IsOnGround, measured 1.19 m
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Every C++ template jumps the same way: if the character controller reports IsOnGround(), call
AddVelocity(Vec3(0,0,jumpSpeed)) -- the living-entity solver then handles the arc and the landing (RollingBall adds a
downward ray test of its own before allowing it). My Project's player uses 5 m/s; measured from the per-frame trace
(claude_player_jump writes it through the existing walk trace): rise 1.19 m over 825 airborne samples of 1867, which
matches v^2/2g = 1.27 m. IsOnGround goes false for the whole arc, so it doubles as an "in air" test for animation.

title: A cutscene camera from code; TrackView's Python surface cannot add keys
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Simplest working cutscene in a component project: spawn an entity, give it a
Cry::DefaultComponents::CCameraComponent, call Activate() (which takes the view from the player's camera), move the
entity each frame (orbit/follow a target), then re-activate the player's camera and remove the entity.
CCutsceneCameraComponent in Components/WorldTools.cpp does this; console: claude_cutscene <entity> <seconds>. Measured:
"following entity 3 for 10.0 s" then "finished ... camera returned to the player". TrackView is scriptable through the
bridge (trackview.new_sequence_by_name / add_node / add_track / set_sequence_time_range / set_time / play), but its 87
exposed functions include NO key-adding call (only get_key_value / get_num_track_keys), so a keyframed sequence cannot be
authored from outside the editor UI -- drive a camera entity from code instead.

title: A usable prop (ray + E) and an in-game menu drawn with IRenderAuxText
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Interactable prop: a component with a CStaticMeshComponent + CPointLightComponent; the player casts a ray
from the eye along its look direction (rwi_stop_at_pierceable|rwi_colltype_any, skipping its own physics), resolves the
entity with gEnv->pEntitySystem->GetEntityFromPhysics(hit.pCollider), checks the component's use range and toggles.
Traps: (1) the default light component keeps m_radius/m_color PROTECTED -- code may only call Enable(bool) /
GetColorParameters(); (2) engine primitives live under %ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Objects/primitive_*.cgf, a project-relative
path loads nothing and the ray then passes through; (3) a mesh loaded at runtime is NOT physicalized -- add
SEntityPhysicalizeParams{PE_STATIC, mass 0} + IEntity::Physicalize or every ray misses (measured physType None);
(4) the aim test must be HORIZONTAL: standing next to a low prop puts it far below eye height (measured eye 2.0 m
above the lamp base at 1.2 m range -- 3D dot 0.77 aiming at +1 m, 0.61 at +0.5 m), so any 3D cone rejects an object the
player is plainly facing; compare headings on the XY plane (60 degrees) and let the range check handle height --
verified "switched ON by the player" only after that change; (5) general.new_object('<class>') needs an EDITOR object class --
a game entity class registered with RegisterEntityClassWithDefaultComponent reports "RuntimeClass ... not registered",
so spawn from game code with SEntitySpawnParams + GetOrCreateComponent. In-game menu without Flash: draw with
IRenderAuxText::Draw2dLabel from the player's update and drive it with CInputComponent actions (F1 toggles, arrows move,
Enter runs the item, which just calls gEnv->pConsole->ExecuteString).

title: Placing trees and bushes: CVegetationMap through new bridge verbs (editor-only, level-owned)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Vegetation is an EDITOR feature: CVegetationMap owns one object type per .cgf and all its instances, and
Sandbox's Python surface only exposes the paint/erase TOOLS, not object creation. The ClaudeBridge plugin now has
bridge.vegetation.list / add <cgf> [density] [castShadow] / place <objectIndex> <x> <y> <z>, implemented against
CVegetationMap (SANDBOX_API) via GetIEditor()'s concrete CEditorImpl -- GetVegetationMap() is NOT on the abstract IEditor,
and CVegetationObject::SetEngineParams is protected (use the map's public SetEngineObjectsParams). Measured: 30 aspen +
60 bush instances placed around the farm, then general.save_level to keep them -- vegetation objects live in the level,
so an editor restart without saving loses them (a rebuild between test passes wiped them once). Meshes and materials can
be copied from GameSDK (objects/natural/trees|bushes) but their textures must be copied too or the engine logs
"Texture does not exist" and renders them untextured.

title: Crossing a custom off-mesh link from game code (the engine plans it but will not carry you)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Because the component movement stack never runs the custom traversal block (guide section 10), the game
does it: JumpLink.cpp exposes FindJumpLinkNear(position, radius, outStart, outEnd), and CNpcComponent, when a movement
request fails, checks whether a link starts where it is standing; if so it drives straight to the link's end with the
character controller and then resumes navigation. Measured with an exclusion wall cutting the corridor: "stalled at an
off-mesh link -- crossing ... by hand" and the villager reached the far side (x 550 -> 558) in about 16 s. Two details
that cost a run each: the crossing update must sit BEFORE the "no patrol route" early-out in the entity update (a one-off
goto clears the route), and the arrival tolerance has to be ~1.2 m because the link's end point is a navmesh point, not
necessarily a spot the capsule can stand on (0.5 m timed out with the villager already across).

title: A real UQS query: blueprint XML, runtime parameters, and running it from C++
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
A working query needs three things and no plugin beyond CryUQS_Core (StdLib and the XML datasource are
linked INTO that DLL: CHub instantiates the StdLib factories and installs the datasource at "libs/ai/uqs" itself).
1. The blueprint is data: Assets/libs/ai/uqs/<Name>.uqs, root <Query factory="Regular" maxItemsToKeepInResultSet="N">,
then <GlobalParams> with <RuntimeParam name= type=>, one <Generator name="std::...">, and <InstantEvaluator name="std::..."
weight= scoreTransform="Linear" negateDiscard="0">. Every parameter is an <Input name= paramID="XXXX"> holding one
<Function>. The paramID is the 4-character id from the factory's UQS_EXPOSE_PARAM (center CENT, size SIZE, spacing SPAC,
navigationAgentTypeID AGEN, verticalTolerance VTOL, pos1 POS1, pos2 POS2, minRequiredDistance MIND, maxAllowedDistance
and distanceThreshold MAXD).
2. Leaf functions are named by convention: _builtin_Func_Literal_std::float, _builtin_Func_GlobalParam_std::Pos3,
_builtin_Func_IteratedItem_std::Pos3 -- the "returnValue" attribute is the literal for a literal and the PARAMETER NAME
for a global param.
3. The game side is Client::CQueryHost (header-only): SetQueryBlueprint("Name"), SetExpectedOutputType,
SetCallback(functor(...)), fill GetRuntimeParamsStorage(), StartQuery(). The host must outlive the call that starts it --
a host on the stack cancels its own query in the destructor. My Project: Assets/libs/ai/uqs/BestSpotToStand.uqs plus
Code/Components/UqsSpot.cpp, console command claude_uqs_best_spot <villager>; measured result "best spot is 560.1 354.6
36.2 (score 4.736)" and the villager walked to 559.9 354.5.
Iterating on a blueprint does not need a restart: UQS_XML_LoadQueryBlueprintLibrary reloads every .uqs from disk and
prints the syntax errors. uqs_logQueryHistory 1 plus UQS_DumpQueryHistory writes an XML with the generated items, the
per-evaluator runs and the final statistics -- that dump is how a query that "succeeds with 0 items" gets diagnosed.

title: UQS_SCHEMATYC_SUPPORT must match the engine's, or every UQS item value is garbage
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
CORRECTION/TRAP, cost a whole debugging round: UQS's interfaces are compiled differently depending on the
UQS_SCHEMATYC_SUPPORT define -- IItemFactory declares two extra virtuals (GetFromForeignTypeConverters /
GetToForeignTypeConverters) when it is 1. The shipped CryUQS_Core.dll was built as part of the engine, where
Tools/CMake/CommonOptions.cmake defaults OPTION_UQS_SCHEMATYC_SUPPORT to ON; a PROJECT-ONLY build (OPTION_ENGINE off)
defaults it to OFF. The vtables then disagree, so calls through IItemFactory land on the wrong function: runtime
parameters arrived as garbage (a Pos3 read back as -0.0 0.0 43710144.0 while its source was 556.2 352.6 34.9), the query
generated its grid around the origin and returned nothing, and GetItemSize() took the editor down. Fix in the project's
Code/CMakeLists.txt, BEFORE including CommonOptions.cmake:
  set(OPTION_UQS_SCHEMATYC_SUPPORT ON CACHE BOOL "Enable UQS functions in Schematyc" FORCE)
Also add "${CRYENGINE_DIR}/Code/CryPlugins" to target_include_directories so <CryUQS/...> resolves. The general lesson:
any engine header behind a compile-time switch has to be compiled in the game module with the SAME switch value the
shipped DLL used.

title: UQS literals in a blueprint are bare values, not JSON objects
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
A literal's textual value goes through yasli's JSONIArchive opened at its ROOT, and at the root level
JSONIArchive::findName ignores the member name and takes the next token as the value. So returnValue="40" is right and
returnValue="{ "value": 40 }" parses as 0 -- which surfaces as the generator rejecting its own parameter
("Bad 'size' param: 0.000000"). Positions are easier to pass as runtime parameters than as literals anyway. And keep XML
comments free of "--": CryXML rejects the file ("not well-formed (invalid token)") and the blueprint silently disappears
from the library.

title: The green checkerboard under your feet is a terrain layer with no detail material
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
A terrain layer has TWO appearances: the baked surface texture (what you see from a distance, generated
from the layer's .bmp) and a detail MATERIAL (what you see close up). Layers created from script start on
%ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Materials/material_terrain_default, which renders as a green-and-black checkerboard -- so a level
can look finished from the air and be a checkerboard around the player. There is no Python or ICommandManager command for
it; the plugin verb bridge.terrain.set_layer_material <index-or-name> <material> calls CLayer::AssignMaterial followed by
CTerrainManager::ReloadSurfaceTypes. Usable materials can be copied from GameSDK (Materials/terrain/grass_3, mud_1,
forest_terrain -- shader "Terrain.Layer") together with their Textures/terrain/detail/* files. Each of those materials
names a SurfaceType (mat_grass, mat_soil); add the missing entries to Assets/libs/MaterialEffects/SurfaceTypes.xml from
GameSDK's copy or the log fills with "undefined surface type, using mat_default".

title: Vegetation that reports instances but renders nothing: instance scale 0
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
bridge.vegetation.list happily reports "instances: 60" for a brush nobody can see. Each instance stores its
own scale, taken from the OBJECT's Size when it was placed (CVegetationObject::CalcVariableSize), so a brush whose Size
ended up 0 produces instances with scale 0 and no render node at all -- and changing the object's Size afterwards does
NOT fix the instances that already exist. Diagnose with bridge.vegetation.instances [objectIndex] [max], which reports
each instance's position, scale and whether it has a render node (measured: 30 trees at scale 1 rendered, 60 bushes at
scale 0 not rendered). Fix by setting the brush up (bridge.vegetation.params <index> size 1.1 sizevar 0.3 elevmin 0
elevmax 4096 slopemin 0 slopemax 60), clearing the dead instances (bridge.vegetation.clear <index> x1 y1 x2 y2) and
painting again. Two more notes: CVegetationObject::GetIndex() is not maintained by CreateObject, so instances all report
object 0 -- to tell brushes apart, hide one (bridge.vegetation.params <i> hidden 1) and look at which instances lose
their render node. And vegetation does not cut the navmesh unless the .cgf has collision: measured, aspen trunks leave a
0.69 m hole in the mesh while 2600 grass and bush instances leave it untouched.

title: Drawing a menu: aux geometry and Draw2dLabel share the same pixel space
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
A panel behind the text needs IRenderAuxGeom: gEnv->pAuxGeomRenderer, SetRenderFlags(e_Mode2D |
e_AlphaBlended | e_DepthTestOff | e_DepthWriteOff | e_CullModeNone), then DrawQuad with Vec3(x, y, 0) corners, and put the
previous flags back afterwards. The coordinates are viewport PIXELS (the renderer builds an ortho matrix over the view
surface), and although IRenderAuxText::Draw2dLabel passes eDrawText_800x600 it lands in the same pixels in practice --
measured: a 32-unit row step came out as 32 pixels. Scaling the boxes into an 800x600 space while leaving the text alone
is what put the highlight bar two rows away from the selected item. Centre the panel on
gEnv->pRenderer->GetOverlayWidth()/GetOverlayHeight() and use one space for both. Also: Sandbox keeps F1 for its own help
even in game mode, so bind a second key (M) for use inside the editor; and injected key events (the bridge's
bridge.input.key) do NOT reach the engine's action maps, so a menu's keyboard navigation cannot be verified from here --
drive its actions through console commands instead and check the drawing in a screenshot.

title: Creating a C++ component entity in the editor from Python
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
general.new_object takes (TYPE, FILE, NAME, x, y, z). For an entity class registered by game code with
RegisterEntityClassWithDefaultComponent the TYPE is "Entity" and the class name goes in FILE:
general.new_object("Entity", "Interactable", "ClaudeLamp", 516, 330, 33.4). Passing the class as the object TYPE is what
produces "RuntimeClass ... not registered" -- the earlier conclusion that such entities could only be spawned from a
console command was wrong. The object is a normal level object afterwards: bridge.object.transform moves it,
bridge.component.properties sets its component members (send the COMPLETE property set), and general.save_level keeps it.
A component that builds its parts in Initialize() picks up a property change on the next game-mode Reset.

title: Particles: the legacy XML libraries are where GameSDK's content is
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
CRYENGINE 5.7 runs two particle systems side by side and both work. The modern one is
.pfx files (pfx2); the legacy one is XML libraries in Libs/Particles/*.xml, loaded on demand by a
three-part name "library.group.effect" -- and that is where GameSDK's usable content lives
(smoke_and_fire.campfire.small for a campfire, smoke_and_fire.black_smoke.white_cont for chimney smoke,
collisions.footsteps.dirt for a footstep puff, weather.rain.space_loop for rain). Copy the library XML
plus only the textures those effects name (textures/sprites/...): a MISSING texture renders as magenta
quads, so a broken effect is loud, while an effect that draws nothing is usually a scale problem.
Three ways to emit: Cry::DefaultComponents::CParticleComponent attached to an entity; a placeable
emitter entity (My Project's ParticleProp, with Effect/Scale/CountScale/FollowCamera, saved in the
level); and IParticleEffect::Spawn(ParticleLoc(pos, up, scale)) for a free-standing one-shot -- which
is what footstep dust wants, because an ATTACHED emitter drags its particles along with the walker.

title: Changing a particle effect needs LoadEffect, not Activate
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
TRAP: CParticleComponent::Activate(true) returns immediately if the emitter is already
active, so SetEffectName() followed by Activate(true) leaves the OLD effect playing. LoadEffect(true) is
the call that frees the slot and loads the new effect. Measured: a rain emitter kept emitting the smoke
it had been created with, while the log happily reported the new effect name. Related: rain particles at
1:1 are nearly invisible in a bright level (size scale 1.8 and count scale 3.0 read as light rain), and
I3DEngine::SetRainParams is a per-frame REQUEST, not a setting -- GameSDK's Rain entity re-applies it
every frame and so must you (My Project does it in CGamePlugin::OnPostUpdate), or the wet look fades.

title: Smart objects: the navigation link is real, but the object must be a Lua entity
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
A navigational smart object needs: rules in Libs/SmartObjects.xml (<Helper className= name=
pos= rot=> for the helper points, and <SmartObject ... iRuleType="1" sUserClass= sObjectClass=
sEntranceHelper= sExitHelper=>); the agent type listing that user class in
Scripts/AI/Navigation.xml (SmartObjectUserClasses); and an ENTITY WITH A SCRIPT TABLE --
CSmartObjectManager::ParseClassesFromProperties reads Properties.soclasses_SmartObjectClass off the Lua
table, so a C++ component entity can never be a smart object. A minimal Lua entity (entities.xml entry
plus a .lua with one Properties string) is enough. Measured in My Project: class and helpers registered,
entity registered, and the link is genuinely in the navmesh -- with a 200 m wall across the level,
reachability through the gate was 1 with the gate in place and 0 with it moved 60 m away. What does NOT
work is using it from a component-driven agent: asking with the villager as the requester returns 0,
because traversal goes through CSmartObjectManager::UseSmartObject and the GameSDK actor/AnimationGraph
stack -- the same wall as the AI behaviour-tree nodes and custom off-mesh links.

title: Dynamic Response System: the game sends signals, the data decides the line
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
DRS data lives under the drs_dataPath cvar (default Libs/DynamicResponseSystem):
DialogLines/dialoglines.dialog holds line sets whose variations carry "text", "audioStartTrigger" and
"pauseLength"; Responses/<signal>.response is one file PER SIGNAL (the file name is the signal name),
holding a tree of segments with conditions ("Variable equal to ", "Variable greater than ") and actions
(ChangeVariable, SpeakLine, SendSignal, Wait). The collection name "Local" means the actor's own
variables. Game code only reports what happened:
  gEnv->pDynamicResponseSystem->CreateResponseActor(name, entityId) once, then
  pActor->QueueSignal("sg_villager_sees_player").
Measured: the same signal produced a greeting on the first sighting and a wary line on the third,
without any game code change. Subtitles are the GAME's job -- implement ISpeakerManager::IListener and
read IDialogLine::GetText() on eLineEvent_Started (a line skipped for priority arrives as event 0x20).
Console: claude_say <entity> <signal>, claude_drs_reload.

title: UDR: recording what an AI was doing, and what it costs
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
The Universal Debug Recorder is header-only through gEnv->pUDR, so a game module needs no
linking: Cry::UDR::CScope_FixedString scope("Villagers") opens (or re-enters) a named node and
scope->AddSphere/AddLine/AddText/LogInformation hang primitives and messages off it, building a tree that
can be drawn live or dumped and replayed. Primitives default to a single frame, so udr_debugDrawDuration 2
is what makes a live recording visible; UDR_PrintStatistics reports the tree and UDR_DumpRecordings writes
XML. Recording every frame is expensive: measured 335,958 primitives and 21 MB after a few minutes of two
villagers, so throttle it (5 Hz is plenty).

title: Flow Graph: game nodes register per module, and a graph can be hand-written XML
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Flow node auto-registration is PER MODULE: REGISTER_FLOW_NODE puts the factory in that DLL's
own static list, and the game has to hand it to the flow system itself with CryRegisterFlowNodes() (the
statics it needs are defined by platform_impl.inl, already included by the template's GamePlugin.cpp).
A node derives from CFlowBaseNode<eNCT_Singleton> and needs an explicit constructor taking
SActivationInfo* -- the factory constructs even singletons with it. A graph is just data:
IFlowSystem::CreateFlowGraph() + SerializeXML(root, true) reads a hand-written file
(<Graph><Nodes><Node ID= Class=><Inputs port="value"/></Node></Nodes><Edges><Edge nodeOut= portOut=
nodeIn= portIn=/></Edges></Graph>), then SetEnabled(true) + InitializeValues(), and something must keep
a reference or the graph stops running. Port names matter (Debug:Log's input is "input", not "in"), and a
wrong port shows up as "[flow] Attempt to link an output node to an output node". Measured in My Project:
Time:Timer -> Claude:Lamp (toggles the campfire) -> Claude:VillagerSays (a DRS signal), all from
Assets/libs/FlowGraphs/claude_farm.xml loaded with claude_flowgraph.

title: One blend space from idle to run, and the three traps that hide it
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
A 1D blend space over MoveSpeed (Dimensions/ExampleList/ExamplePseudo/Blendable, shaped like
the shipped animals/deer/*.bspace) lets one Mannequin fragment cover walking AND running: measured ground
speed 2.00 with animation root speed 2.00, and 3.20 with 3.19, where GameSDK's relaxed_tac_walk_nw_3p_01
space capped at 2.0 and forced a separate run clip. Three traps, each of which costs a run:
(1) an animation only exists for a character if its chrparams lists it, and paths listed there resolve
against the DEFAULT ANIMATION DIRECTORY -- three folders above the .chr plus "/animations"
(CDefaultSkeleton::GetDefaultAnimDir) -- not the assets root; "#filepath" resets that directory for the
entries after it. The easier route is to drop the file where an existing wildcard already looks (GameSDK's
player.chrparams collects */*.bspace under Animations/human/male).
(2) NO "--" INSIDE XML COMMENTS: CryXML rejects the whole file, and a rejected chrparams shows up as a
character with 0 animations rather than as a comment error. The same trap killed a UQS blueprint and the
smart objects library in the same session.
(3) the skeleton and its animation set are cached for the process, so a chrparams change needs an editor
restart, not just a level reload.

title: Merged-mesh grass: one checkbox, 58% fewer draw calls (measured)
source: Merged-mesh grass, measured 2026-09-17 (manual: Vegetation 02 Grass (Merged Meshes) CRYENGINE, page 24285892)
content:
Vegetation painted as ordinary instances is one render node each. Turning ON the
vegetation object's AutoMerged flag hands those instances to the merged-mesh system instead, which
batches them. That is the whole engine-side procedure -- the manual's DCC tutorials are about
authoring the asset; for an asset that already exists it is one flag.

Measured on this project's farm, same camera, 2484 grass instances across three brushes
(small_grass_a, small_grass_b, tall_grass_a):

                     before      after
  draw calls (DP)      2363        988      -58%
  total incl. shadows  3664       1470      -60%
  shadow gen           1301        482
  polygons          641,781    641,610      unchanged
  FPS                   422        481      (noisy at this framerate; draw calls are the real number)

e_MergedMeshesDebug 1 confirms the system took over: 1999 instances managed, 981 visible, dynamic
merged rendermeshes 6.4 MB VRAM, no pool overflow (e_MergedMeshesPool is 8192 kb here). The count is
lower than the 2484 painted because merged meshes have their own view distance
(e_MergedMeshesViewDistRatio, 30 by default).

How to set it: the flag has a getter (CVegetationObject::IsAutoMerged) but NO setter, and the
merged-mesh behaviour parameters (Stiffness, Damping, Variance, AirResistance) have neither. They are
CVarObject variables, so the bridge now reaches any of them by name --
`bridge.vegetation.params <index> automerged 1` -- falling back to
GetVarObject()->GetVariable(i)->Set() for keys with no explicit setter. The flag is level data: it
survives save + reload (verified), and the appearance is unchanged.

The material matters: merged meshes want the Vegetation shader. GameSDK's field_grass.mtl already
uses it, but with %LEAVES% (the higher-quality path) where the manual's tutorial picks the Grass
shader-gen flag as the cheaper one -- untested here, so the numbers above are for LEAVES.
verified_note: Measured on LEAVES in an editor/profile run; the Grass shader-gen flag and the packaged effect are untested. Listed by the 2026-10-23 audit (K-14): the text holds a claim that was read or planned but never run or seen working (look for 'untested', 'NOT SEEN', 'not yet'); treat it as a hypothesis until shown.

title: Component agents CAN traverse off-mesh links: SetActorPath is an empty stub in 5.7.1
source: Off-mesh link A/B measured 2026-09-17 (stock vs patched CryAISystem.dll, same level and link)
content:
UPDATED 2026-09-25: the diagnosis stands, but the fix is now in the game on a stock engine (offmesh-link-follow-game-side), not an engine patch.

Three separate investigations concluded "component entities need GameSDK's actor
for off-mesh traversal". That was wrong. The cause is one empty override in the engine:

    // Code/CryEngine/CryAISystem/Components/Navigation/MovementActorAdapter.h, 5.7.1 as shipped
    virtual void SetActorPath(const MovementStyle& style, const INavPath& navPath) override {}

FollowPath::Begin -> Movement::Helpers::BeginPathFollowing -> adapter.SetActorPath(style, blockPath) is how a
movement block tells the path follower "follow only this piece of the path". GameSDK's adapter implements it
(PipeUserMovementActorAdapter copies the block path into CPipeUser::m_Path, which its follower is attached to);
the component's adapter discards it, and CEntityAINavigationComponent::OnMNMPathfinderResult has already
attached the follower to the WHOLE path. The follower therefore keeps trying to walk the link's own segment --
the one piece that is deliberately off the navmesh -- CSmartPathFollower::Update cannot find a reachable
target, and MovementBlock_FollowPath.cpp:100 returns CantBeFinished after 3 s. The custom block's Begin is
never reached, and the request fails after 4 replans.

The fix is to implement that method: keep a CNavPath member, SetParams + SetPathPoints from the block's path,
and m_pPathfollower->AttachToPath(&member).

MEASURED A/B, same level, same link, villager crossing a 4 m navmesh exclusion strip (claude_nav_reach 0
without the link, 1 with it):

                          stock CryAISystem.dll      patched
  link registered         yes (result 0)             yes
  planner uses it         yes                        yes
  block creator called    4 times (replans)          once
  block Begin             NEVER                      yes
  crossing                stops dead at the entry    1593 updates / 2.73 s, "finished crossing"
  outcome                 "path failed"              walks on to the destination

Two limits that are real and stay real:
  * Smart objects genuinely do need GameSDK: CSmartObjectManager::PrepareNavigateSmartObject takes a
    CPipeUser*, and the component adapter's IsClosestToUseTheSmartObject / PrepareNavigateSmartObject are
    `return false` by construction. Use a custom MNM::IOffMeshLink instead -- OffMeshLink.h,
    IOffMeshNavigationManager.h and MovementBlock.h are all in CryCommon, so the whole pipeline is game-side.
  * A movement block that writes a velocity (SetMovementOutputValue) cannot push a character through solid
    geometry: the same link aimed through a barn wall ran the block correctly and the villager stood against
    the wall. A ladder/vault block moves the entity itself -- root-motion animation or transform.

title: SUPERSEDED: The installed engine's CryAISystem.dll is patched (and how to swap it back)
source: Off-mesh link A/B measured 2026-09-17 (stock vs patched CryAISystem.dll, same level and link)
content: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-25: the installed CryAISystem.dll is Crytek's signed original again; the link fix is game-side (see offmesh-link-follow-game-side). Do not swap the patched DLL back in.
history:
SUPERSEDED 2026-09-25: the installed CryAISystem.dll is Crytek's signed original again; the link fix is game-side (see offmesh-link-follow-game-side). Do not swap the patched DLL back in.

This project runs Sandbox from the Launcher engine (5.7.1) but builds from
<engine source checkout>. Since 2026-09-17 one engine DLL is NOT Crytek's:

  <engine>\bin\win_x64\CryAISystem.dll           patched (off-mesh link fix)
  <engine>\bin\win_x64\CryAISystem.dll.orig571   Crytek's original, dated 2022-05-18
  <engine>\bin\win_x64\CryAISystem.dll.patched   copy of the patched one, for swapping back

The source tree's HEAD is 2022-05-13 and the shipped DLL 2022-05-18 -- the same release -- and the editor has
been started healthy on both. Build with msbuild on
solutions_cmake/win64/Code/CryEngine/CryAISystem/CryAISystem.vcxproj, Configuration=Profile (about a minute,
output goes to <engine source checkout>).

To swap: write <engine source checkout> (the watchdog stands down while it exists),
Stop-Process -Name Sandbox, copy the DLL, Start-Process Sandbox, delete the marker. Sandbox holds the DLL open,
so it must be closed first; the level is lost if it was not saved. msbuild flags must be passed from PowerShell,
not Git Bash, which rewrites /t:Build into a path.

Consequence for shipping: a packaged build loads the ENGINE's DLLs, so the packaged game does not have the fix
unless the patched CryAISystem.dll is packaged with it.

title: A gate as level data: CNavLinkComponent, and the two traps registering a component
source: Gate built and measured 2026-09-17 (ClaudeNorthGate on the farm's north fence)
content:
Code/Components/NavLink.{h,cpp} (entity class "NavLink") turns an off-mesh link into
something a designer places. Entry and exit are offsets in the ENTITY's space -- rotating the gate rotates the
crossing -- plus AgentType, BothWays, Cost, Speed, Arc Height, Enabled, all in the Inspector and all reachable
live through bridge.component.properties.

Off-mesh links are runtime state: IOffMeshNavigationManager holds them and the navigation system is reset
between game sessions, so the component registers them on entering game mode (GameplayStarted / Reset with
nParam[0] != 0) and removes them on leaving. That is what makes the gate level data -- verified across a save
and an editor restart. BothWays registers the reverse link too, because an off-mesh link is one-way.

Two traps, each one build cycle:

  * general.new_object('NavLink', ...) fails with "RuntimeClass NavLink (as well as NavLink::) not
    registered". That first argument is the EDITOR class, not the entity class:
    general.new_object('Entity', 'NavLink', name, x, y, z).
  * RegisterEntityClassWithDefaultComponent<T>() alone is NOT enough. Without
    CRY_STATIC_AUTO_REGISTER_FUNCTION(&RegisterTComponent) wrapping SCHEMATYC_MAKE_ENV_COMPONENT(T), the
    entity is created EMPTY: it is in the level, it receives no events, and it registers nothing. The symptom
    is silence -- no error, just a component that never runs.

title: Crossing a link is scripted, not walked: transform interpolation + walk animation
source: Gate built and measured 2026-09-17 (ClaudeNorthGate on the farm's north fence)
content:
A movement block that writes a velocity makes the agent WALK the link, so it is stopped by
exactly the thing the link exists to bypass (measured: aimed through a barn wall, the block ran perfectly and
the villager stood against the wall pushing). CNavLinkBlock therefore drives the entity itself:

  * Begin: start from the agent's current position (FollowPath hands over within its 2.5 m end distance, so
    the agent is near the entry, rarely on it); duration = length / speed.
  * Update: SetPosRotScale along a lerp from there to the link's exit, z raised by arcHeight*sin(pi*u) for a
    vault or a jump down, facing along the way; SetMovementOutputValue with velocity ZERO so the path
    follower and the character controller do not fight the interpolation.
  * InterruptibleNow() returns false -- a scripted traversal must not be abandoned half way over a fence.

The NPC stands down meanwhile: CNpcComponent::BeginScriptedTraversal sets a flag that skips its own driving
and freezes its idle/re-issue detector (4 s of "no velocity" would otherwise re-request the path mid-crossing),
and queues the Walk fragment so the legs move. EndScriptedTraversal releases it -- from the block's End() as
well as the success path, so an interrupted plan cannot leave the villager frozen.

MEASURED on the farm's north fence (1.4 m high, arc 1.9 m, speed 2 m/s, both directions through one gate
entity): 3.05 s northbound over 6.1 m, 3.25 s southbound over 6.5 m, ~1550 block updates each, and the patrol
route now crosses the fence on every lap with no path failures.

title: Autonomous villagers: a utility brain over component bodies (no behaviour tree, no GameSDK actor)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
CVillagerBrain (Code/Components/VillagerBrain.*) runs on any Villager with Autonomous set. While
patrolling it re-scores every 1.5 s: TendFire 0.9 (dark and the home fire out, or light and still
burning), HaulWood 0.6 (a PickupItem lying near home, away from the woodpile), Visit 0.5 (not been to
the other village for VisitInterval seconds), Patrol 0.2. The winner becomes a list of steps -- MoveTo,
Face, Action (a Mannequin fragment, waited for by its clip length), Wait, Call (act on the world) --
built from what is in the level now, and runs to the end. Places and things are found by component
(VillagePoint Village/Woodpile, PickupItem, CInteractableComponent fires), so nothing names a place.
Claims (ClaimTarget) stop two villagers taking the same log or fire.

It does not plan routes: 'go to the hamlet' is one MoveTo, and the pathfinder picks the road (area
cost), the gate (carrying forbids vaults) or a vault (when the gate is far).

Measured in a 7-minute soak with two autonomous villagers: 12 decisions, 7 tasks finished, 3 logs
delivered, 4 village-to-village walks (~205 m in ~100 s), 7 gate crossings (mean 10.9 s), 5 vaults
(mean 4.2 s), 0 failures. Both villagers lit their fire at 20:30 and put it out at 07:00-07:30. Tasks
are not interrupted: a villager away on a visit at dusk leaves its fire dark until it returns.
Commands: claude_villager_status, claude_villager_do <villager> fire|haul|visit|patrol.

title: Vaultable fences found automatically: AutoVault generates off-mesh links from the world
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
The engine has no system that notices a fence and decides to jump it; traversability is data.
CAutoVaultComponent (entity class AutoVault) generates that data: on a grid of navmesh points it looks
1.3-3.3 m out in eight directions for a navmesh point that the mesh does not connect in a straight line
(NavMeshRayCast != NoHit), at about the same height, with static geometry at knee height and none at
vault height between them (two physics rays). Each pair becomes a Vault link whose arc clears the
obstacle top measured by a downward ray; links are thinned to one per 4 m per direction and kept 5 m
from any gate. Measured on the farm: 2121 points (1681 on the mesh) scanned in 53 ms, 747 vaultable
spots, 48 near the gate dropped, 64 links.

Vault links set forbidWhenEncumbered: CJumpLink::CanUse returns false for an agent in the encumbrance
registry. CanUse is called by the pathfinder, possibly off the main thread, so the registry is a
mutex-protected set, not an entity lookup. Measured: a villager fetching a log outside the west fence
vaulted out (4.3 s) and, carrying it, walked round through the gate.

Links in a regenerated tile are removed (EOffMeshLinkRemovalReason::MeshUpdated) and never restored;
AutoVault rescans when more than 10% of its links have gone.

title: A gate villagers open, walk through and shut: keep the leaf out of the navmesh
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
CFarmGateComponent (entity class FarmGate): a hinged leaf that is a physical obstacle for the player
but carries ENTITY_FLAG_EXTENDED_IGNORED_IN_NAVMESH_GENERATION, with the gateway cut from the navmesh by a
small exclusion NavigationArea. So opening and shutting never changes the mesh -- which matters because a
tile regeneration deletes the off-mesh links in it. Navigation sees the gate only as two links of kind
Gate; the crossing block walks up, plays OpenGate (GameSDK stand_tac_opendoor_nw_1p_01, 1.5 s), asks the
gate to open a third of the way in, waits until it is open, walks through via the opening's centre,
turns and pushes it shut -- only if it opened it (a player-opened gate, via E, stays open; a gate held
by another villager is not shut in its face). On the swing side the villager waits beside the leaf's
tip: the 3.1 m leaf sweeps everything within that of the hinge.

Trap measured on the way: during a scripted crossing the character controller keeps its last velocity
between the block's moves -- a villager that reached the gate along the fence drifted west at ~2 m/s
while opening it. Zero the controller (and pe_action_set_velocity) when a traversal begins and every
frame during it.

title: A road the pathfinder prefers: Road area type + markup volumes + filter costs >= 1
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Scripts/AI/Navigation.xml gains <AreaTypes><AreaType id="1" name="Road"><Flag>Walkable</Flag></AreaType>
(bump the Navigation version, regenerate, export). CNavRoadComponent (entity class NavRoad) reads an AI
Path as the centreline and lays one markup volume per segment (RegisterEntityMarkups + SetMarkupVolume,
annotation = GetAreaTypeAnnotation(GetAnnotationLibrary().GetAreaTypeID("Road"))); SetMarkupVolume
requests the tile updates itself. claude_nav_area x y z confirms: road triangles report area type 1 'Road'.

Each villager's filter (SNavMeshQueryFilterDefaultWithCosts, set with IEntityNavigationComponent::
SetNavigationQueryFilter) carries the preference. Write it with every multiplier >= 1: CNavMesh::FindWay's
A* heuristic is plain straight-line distance (NavMesh.cpp ~870), so a cost below 1 makes it overestimate
and the search is no longer guaranteed optimal. RoadCost 0.35 becomes ground 2.86, road 1.0 -- a
precaution from the source; the walk looked much the same either way.

Measured A/B, same visit, tracked positions: with the preference the villager's median distance from
the road centreline was 2.7 m (max 9.7); with RoadCost 1.0 it was 18.9 m (max 42.3, 0% within 2 m).
The road is 201 m, the straight line 165 m. The brain's own on-road percentage (~30%) understates it:
the path follower cuts bends across open ground.

title: Ashvale: the whole game, and where each piece lives
source: Ashvale build, 2026-09-22 (Design/ASHVALE_SCRIPT.md, examples/ashvale/build_ashvale.py)
content:
A playable medieval game in the level `ashvale`, built from a written script first
(Design/ASHVALE_SCRIPT.md: premise, map, characters, quests, combat numbers) and then
generated from it.

- Level build: examples/ashvale/build_ashvale.py, phases `buildings village camp people nav
  vegetation` (and `clear <prefix>`), each run separately and SAVED after (a crash
  between phases costs everything since the last save).
- Terrain: ashvale_heightmap.py writes a 1024x1024 float32 valley
  (shrine y~165 -> Ashford y~362 -> river y~470 -> clearing y~592 -> ridge tower y~772),
  installed with bridge.terrain.set_heights_raw <file> 200.
- Layer textures: ashvale_layer_textures.py (numpy only, writes BMPs).
- Game code: Code/Components/{AshvaleGame,AshvaleObjects,BanditBrain,Health}.{h,cpp}
  plus Npc/Player/VillagerBrain changes. Dialogue: Assets/libs/ashvale/dialogue.xml.
- Playtest: examples/ashvale/ashvale_playtest.py drives the whole story from the console and
  checks 12 assertions (menu, each conversation and flag, locked chest, bandits noticing
  the player, five kills, the tithe, the ending). Export: export_level.py.

The launcher boots into it: GamePlugin.cpp runs `map ashvale s` outside the editor, and
the game's own main menu is the front end.

title: Black terrain: export_to_engine does NOT compile the terrain texture
source: Ashvale build, 2026-09-22 (Design/ASHVALE_SCRIPT.md, examples/ashvale/build_ashvale.py)
content:
A level made with general.create_level renders its terrain almost black however bright
the layers are, because terrain/cover.ctc is a stub compiled at colour multiplier 0.
`exporter.export_to_engine` never fixes this: it exports with eExp_AI_All only, and
CGameExporter::ExportMap compiles the surface texture only for eExp_SurfaceTexture
(GameExporter.cpp:338-381). Only the terrain dialog's "Export Terrain Texture" does it.

Measure it at load: the log line `RGB multiplier: N, Texture indices: M` (terrain_load.cpp
:328). A good level reads `8 / 341`; the broken one read `0 / 5`, and cover.ctc was 131 KB
against the farm's 11 MB.

Fixed with a bridge verb: `bridge.terrain.export_texture [resolution=4096]
[colorMultiplier=8]`, which runs CGameExporter with eExp_SurfaceTexture|eExp_ReloadTerrain
and no dialog. Note SGameExporterSettings is NOT SANDBOX_API (its constructor lives in
Sandbox.exe), so the verb fills the struct field by field in raw storage instead of
constructing it. Brightening the baked layer colours first changed almost nothing --
always check cover.ctc before touching albedo.

title: NPCs cannot path indoors when waypoints are dropped on the terrain
source: Ashvale build, 2026-09-22 (Design/ASHVALE_SCRIPT.md, examples/ashvale/build_ashvale.py)
content:
Patrol points were placed with GetTerrainElevation, which is UNDER a house floor
(planks 0.25 m thick): every waypoint inside the tavern and chapel failed with
"Navigation system couldn't find NavMesh triangle at path destination point".

Fix: `float WalkableHeightAt(float x, float y, float zHint)` in Npc.cpp -- a downward ray
from zHint+1.2 against ent_static|ent_terrain, falling back to terrain elevation -- used
for patrol rings and for put-down points in VillagerBrain. After it, every villager
arrival logged `(ok)` and the warnings stopped.

Probe it directly with `claude_nav_probe x y z [agentType]` (Npc.cpp): it prints on-mesh,
the closest mesh point and the distance. Note the navmesh inside a house sits ~0.4 m above
the floor, and a probe at the room centre can read "off mesh" simply because furniture
occupies that spot -- probe where an NPC would actually stand.

title: A held mesh with a collider wedges its own character in place
source: Ashvale build, 2026-09-22 (Design/ASHVALE_SCRIPT.md, examples/ashvale/build_ashvale.py)
content:
Bandits were driven at 2.0 m/s and measured 0 m of movement: the club was a
CStaticMeshComponent left at its default EMeshType::RenderAndCollider, so its geometry
became a part of the bandit's own living entity and jammed the controller. Villagers
(no weapon) walked fine, which is what isolated it.

Anything held in or near a character -- a weapon, the first-person sword held in front of
the camera -- must be `SetType(Cry::DefaultComponents::EMeshType::Render)`.

title: A slot material never reaches a .cdf character's clothes
source: Ashvale build, 2026-09-22 (Design/ASHVALE_SCRIPT.md, examples/ashvale/build_ashvale.py)
content:
sdk_player is a .cdf: the clothes are CA_SKIN attachments, each drawn with its own skin's
material, so SetSlotMaterial on the character slot changes nothing (every NPC kept the
yellow varsity jacket, including the older sdk_player_red override that appeared to work).

Replace it per attachment instead: walk IAttachmentManager, and for each CA_SKIN whose
GetBaseMaterial(0) is the clothing material, call SetReplacementMaterial(pMaterial, lod)
for lods 0..5. Match on the material's FILE NAME (PathUtil::GetFile(...) == "sdk_player*")
and not on the path -- head_a.mtl lives in the same sdk_player folder, and matching the
folder gave every NPC a red cap and a wrong-coloured face.

The medieval outfits are copies of sdk_player.mtl with the jacket/jeans/buttons diffuse
maps swapped for %engine%/EngineAssets/TextureMsg/color_white.dds and a wool colour:
Assets/materials/ashvale/people/*.mtl.

title: A cached IParticleEffect* crashes the editor after a level reload
source: Ashvale build, 2026-09-22 (Design/ASHVALE_SCRIPT.md, examples/ashvale/build_ashvale.py)
content:
Sandbox died with EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION reading 0x38 in Game.dll. Resolving the
frame against Game.pdb (bridge/symbolize.py, dbghelp, no debugger needed) named
CNpcComponent::UpdateFootstepDust+0x1b5: the footstep effect was held in a function-level
`static IParticleEffect*`, and reloading the level unloads the particle library under it.

Look the effect up per use instead (footsteps are ~0.7 m apart, so the cost is nothing).
Any pointer to an engine resource cached in a static outlives the level it came from.

`python bridge/symbolize.py <dll> 0x19ee55 ...` turns the Module+0xOFFSET frames in
error.log into function names and source lines.

title: Gate the game's HUD and menus on !gEnv->IsEditing()
source: Ashvale build, 2026-09-22 (Design/ASHVALE_SCRIPT.md, examples/ashvale/build_ashvale.py)
content:
Sandbox keeps the local player alive while editing, so the game's Update/Draw ran in the
editor viewport: the main menu and HUD were drawn over the level while building it.

Gate them with `const bool bPlaying = !gEnv->IsEditing();` in the player's Update.

Related, for testing: injected keys never reach the game's action maps, so the story is
driven by console commands -- ash_newgame, ash_pause, ash_select, ash_choose n,
ash_respawn, ash_mainmenu, ash_flag, ash_status, plus the test hooks ash_attack,
ash_block, ash_use and `ash_goto <entity> [distance]` (stand facing an entity).

title: Time-of-day settings live in the preset, so the game applies its own
source: Ashvale build, 2026-09-22 (Design/ASHVALE_SCRIPT.md, examples/ashvale/build_ashvale.py)
content:
Fog and exposure edits go into %ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Shading/default.env, not the level:
they survive a level reload and are lost on an editor restart, and a packaged game would
never see them. CAshvaleGame::ApplyValleyAtmosphere writes them itself when the game
activates (volumetric fog 0.35, volumetric fog 2 density 0.03, fog colour multiplier 2.0,
radial size 0.6, layer density 0.02, EV auto compensation 0).

Two measured lighting notes for this valley:
- The only ambient in the deferred path is an EnvironmentProbe. At DiffuseMultiplier 1.5
  with a white cubemap, shadowed faces were as bright as lit ones and everything read as
  flat white; 0.7 restored the shading.
- "EV Auto compensation" 1.5 -> 0 took a village view's mean luminance from 137 to 123.
  Nothing was actually clipping (0.1% of pixels), so the washed-out look was ambient and
  exposure, not the materials.

title: Four Ashvale gameplay bugs and the measurement that refuted a fifth
source: Ashvale playtest fixes, 2026-09-22 evening
content:
Found by playing the build:

1. Villagers appeared to attack: kStartleClip was melee_killingblow_rightkick_1p_01, so the
   startle reaction played a KICK. It now stops and stands (no fragment queued at all --
   queueing one from that path crashed CryAnimation, with either the Startle or the Idle
   fragment; the locomotion updater picks Idle by itself when the body stops).
2. The first-person sword lagged and jittered: UpdateSword wrote its WORLD matrix from the
   camera's world matrix, one frame behind the body. It is now a child entity placed with
   SetLocalTM(cameraLocal * offset) -- measured offset spread 0.000 m standing, walking,
   sprinting and strafing.
3. The editor crashed on the SECOND entry into game mode: RebuildOwnedComponents removes every
   CStaticMeshComponent (the bandit's club among them) but did not null m_pWeapon. Any pointer
   to a component that a rebuild can delete must be nulled with the others. The player's sword
   entity is NO_SAVE and removed with the session, so it is held by EntityId and rebuilt.
4. After dying, the player walked around at 0 health and could not be killed or healed: the
   sample's revive flow only runs for the first session, so CAshvaleGame::m_pPlayer was null
   from the second one and Respawn placed nobody. Bind lazily via CPlayerComponent::GetLocal()
   and treat zero health while Playing as death. Do NOT bind from the player's Reset event --
   it fires again mid-session and re-ran the game setup during NewGame.

Refuted by measurement: "W+A gives a speed boost". On flat open ground W 3.98, A 4.00, S 4.00,
W+A 3.98, W+D 3.97 m/s, and 3.99 when A is added while already walking. Use ash_hold <keys>
<seconds> (w/a/s/d, + for sprint); it writes distance and speed to claude_npc.log.

Test-harness note: ash_status prints a tick counter that only advances while the game runs, so
a script can tell game mode from edit mode instead of blindly toggling (a run that left the
editor in game mode made the next run toggle it OFF and fail ten checks against a dead game).

5. Two swords in view: hiding the per-session sword and dropping its id left the entity in
   the world, parented to the player, and the next session built a second one beside it.
   Remove a per-session entity outright on leaving game mode, sweep by name before
   spawning, and rebuild it on demand. Verified: one sword entity, four parts, three
   consecutive sessions.

title: "IRenderNode::SetMatrix: Invalid matrix ignored" -- what it means and how to find the node
source: Ashvale log-spam investigation, 2026-09-23
content:
CBrush::IsMatrixValid (Cry3DEngine/Brush.cpp:596) rejects a render-node matrix whose Z column
is shorter than 0.01 or longer than 1000, is non-finite, or sits further than 256 km from the
origin. The node keeps its old matrix and the engine logs a warning PER NODE PER FRAME, which
is what makes the game stutter -- the spam is the cost, not the rejection.

The name in the message is mangled ("0.000000E+00NGINE/EngineAssets/...") because the message
is built with Format and a name containing %ENGINE% is eaten as a printf conversion.

Finding the node: entity component slots render as movable brushes, so a held or attached
primitive is a candidate even though the name is a .cgf path. `ash_nodes <x> <y> <z> [radius]`
(Game.dll) lists render nodes near a point with type, name, position and size. Compare the
reported position against local part offsets too -- a reported [0.00,0.52,0.00] matched the
sword blade's local offset exactly and identified it.

MEASUREMENT TRAP: the engine flushes editor.log with a delay. Counting the warning in
editor.log straight after a test run returned 0 twice while the same session's rotated copy
under logbackups/ held hundreds. Count after ~20 seconds, or from the backup file. Measuring
too early produced a confident wrong diagnosis that a later A/B refuted.

title: The project's most repeated bug: a handle outliving what it points to
source: Project retrospective, 2026-09-23 (farm level -> autonomous villagers -> Ashvale)
content:
Nearly every hard bug in this project had the same shape -- something kept a reference
across a boundary the engine had already crossed. The boundaries are: entering/leaving game
mode, a level reload, a navmesh tile regeneration, and an editor restart.

Instances, all separately debugged before the pattern was named:
  * components deserialized from main.lyr duplicated the ones Initialize created, and the
    LAST one to process START_GAME owned the movement plan (NPC patrol, 2026-09-15);
  * off-mesh links vanish when their tile regenerates -- every owner re-registers on
    MeshUpdated (2026-09-17);
  * a function-level `static IParticleEffect*` survived a level reload and crashed the editor
    in the animation update (footstep dust, 2026-09-22);
  * `RebuildOwnedComponents` deletes every CStaticMeshComponent, which includes the bandit's
    club, but only nulled three of the four pointers -- the second entry into game mode wrote
    through freed memory (2026-09-22);
  * the player's sword entity is NO_SAVE: hiding it and dropping the id left an orphan
    parented to the player, and the next session built a second sword beside it;
  * CAshvaleGame::m_pPlayer was bound by the sample's revive flow, which only runs for the
    FIRST session, so from the second one respawn placed nobody.

The rule that would have prevented all six: **own the rebuild.** At a boundary, drop every
handle and recreate what you need on demand -- hold entities by EntityId and resolve them, null
component pointers wherever components are removed, re-register anything the engine owns, and
rebuild rather than reuse. And when a fix must survive a boundary, TEST the second iteration:
enter game mode twice, reload the level, regenerate the navmesh. The first iteration passing
means nothing here.

title: Write traces that report the measured effect, never the intention
source: Project retrospective, 2026-09-23 (farm level -> autonomous villagers -> Ashvale)
content:
This stack reports success while doing nothing -- terrain.flood_layer, device_commit_files,
general.take_screenshot, bridge.env.set (once), set_layer_texture, a screenshot that returns
a stale frame, exporter.export_to_engine "succeeding" without compiling the terrain texture.
The habit that survives this is to log what was measured afterwards, not what was attempted.

The sharpest lesson is that OUR OWN code made the same mistake. CAshvaleGame::Respawn logged
"respawned at the well" and then called PlacePlayerAt, which returned silently when the player
pointer was null: the message was true about the intention and false about the world, and it
hid a player walking around at 0 health for an entire playtest. The bridge verbs that were
worth writing all do the opposite -- generate_surface_texture reports measured coveragePercent
per layer, bridge.env.set reads the value back rather than echoing the request, the screenshot
verb reports saturation and a checksum so a blank or stale frame is visible.

Applied to traces: log positions and distances after the move, health after the damage, the
count of objects actually created, "n of m applied". A trace that only proves the code path ran
is the same lie the engine tells.

Corollary (2026-09-23): a "0 problems" result is not evidence until the instrument has shown a
non-zero on a known-bad case -- editor.log is flushed with a delay, and counting immediately
after a run returned 0 while the rotated copy in logbackups/ held hundreds.

title: The engine narrates more than it seems: grep its log strings in the source
source: Project retrospective, 2026-09-23 (farm level -> autonomous villagers -> Ashvale)
content:
Three separate diagnoses in this project came from one grep of a log message in
<engine source checkout>, after hours of plausible theorising:

  * `RGB multiplier: 0, Texture indices: 5` at level load (terrain_load.cpp:328) said the
    terrain texture had never been compiled -- the "black terrain" was not albedo, lighting or
