    fog, and brightening layer colours 2x had changed nothing;
  * `IRenderNode::SetMatrix: Invalid matrix ignored` (Brush.cpp:194) gave the exact rule
    (Z column < 0.01 or > 1000, non-finite, or > 256 km out) and explained the mangled name in
    the same message (the text is built with Format, so %ENGINE% is eaten as a conversion);
  * `CGameExporter::ExportMap` showed that the surface texture is compiled only under
    eExp_SurfaceTexture, which is why export_to_engine never fixed the terrain.

Order of authority, learned the hard way: the engine source, then a measurement, then the
offline manual (the notes folder/docs, docs_search.py), then the tool's own success report -- which
is worth nothing on its own. Before theorising about a symptom, find the code that prints it.

The same applies to the editor: `CBrush::IsMatrixValid`, `CHeightmap`, `CGameExporter` and the
navigation system are all readable, and most of Sandbox's own dialogs turn out to be thin
wrappers around a call a plugin verb can make directly without the dialog.

title: Iteration economics here: console hooks beat rebuilds, instrument once
source: Project retrospective, 2026-09-23 (farm level -> autonomous villagers -> Ashvale)
content:
A Game.dll change costs ~3 minutes and restarts the editor, which also loses any
unexported navmesh and any time-of-day edit. That price shapes the right workflow:

  * Put test hooks in the game rather than rebuilding to probe: ash_goto/ash_attack/ash_use/
    ash_hold/ash_status/ash_nodes/claude_nav_probe each answered a class of question forever
    after. Injected keys never reach the action maps, so a console hook is the ONLY way to
    drive gameplay from a script anyway.
  * Make the state observable before debugging it: ash_status prints a tick counter, which is
    how a script tells game mode from edit mode -- one run left the editor in game mode and the
    next blindly toggled it OFF, failing ten checks against a dead game.
  * Batch code changes into one build. Several one-line fixes discovered separately should
    still be a single cycle.
  * Save the level between every build step and every content phase: an editor crash (one was
    inside the AMD driver) costs everything since the last save, and once cost five build
    phases of the Ashvale level.
  * Check what the watchdog will reopen. bridge_watchdog.py's LEVEL_ASSET decides which level
    comes back after a crash; it was still pointed at the farm, so a whole build phase was
    created in the wrong level and the save prompt wrote it in.

The general principle: spend a build on making the system answer questions, not on guessing
one answer.

title: CRYENGINE 5.7 logs content as a printf format (3 sites): mangled names and a crash
source: Engine source audit, 2026-09-23
content:
Three engine call sites pass already-formatted, CONTENT-controlled text to a printf-style
logger as the FORMAT argument:

  Cry3DEngine/Brush.cpp:199                       Warning(message.c_str());
  Cry3DEngine/RenderNodes/CharacterRenderNode.cpp:129   Warning(message.c_str());
  CryEntitySystem/AreaManager.cpp:37              CryLog(outputBuf.c_str());   (already FormatV'd)

The text contains asset paths and entity/area names, so the '%' comes from level content. This
is what turns the invalid-matrix warning's name into "0.000000E+00NGINE/EngineAssets/..." --
"%E" is consumed as a float conversion.

Measured with a standalone reproduction of the same code shape (scratchpad/formatbug):
  * name "%ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Objects/primitive_cube.cgf"
      unpatched -> name="9.802791E-313NGINE/EngineAssets/..." (stack garbage)
      patched   -> name="%ENGINE%/EngineAssets/..."           (correct)
  * name "BanditCamp_%s_%s_%x" (a name a level author can type)
      unpatched -> process dies with 0xC0000005 ACCESS_VIOLATION
      patched   -> prints the name

Fix is `Warning("%s", message.c_str())` / `CryLog("%s", outputBuf.c_str())`. A wider scan of
the engine (log calls whose first argument is not a literal) found 26 candidates, of which
about 14 are real code rather than comments or macro definitions -- CGFLoader, EntityContainer,
BehaviorTreeManager and LiveCreate are the other content-fed ones worth auditing.

Engine modules CAN be rebuilt from <engine source checkout> and deployed like the CryAISystem patch:
  msbuild solutions_cmake/win64/Code/CryEngine/<Module>/<Module>.vcxproj -t:Build
          -p:Configuration=Profile -p:Platform=x64
CryEntitySystem and Cry3DEngine both build in a few minutes and land in
<engine source checkout> Deploying means copying into the installed engine's
bin/win_x64 while Sandbox is closed (claude_engine_deploy.bat + the ClaudeEngineDeploy task,
which backs the originals up as *.orig571 first). The source tree's bin holds only the modules
that were built, so running Sandbox from there is not an option without building the whole
engine.

title: Save/load with a component player: the engine's SaveGame refuses, its serializer does not
source: Ashvale save/load, 2026-09-23
content:
CryAction's own save game cannot be used by a project built on the C++ component template.
CCryAction::SaveGame (CryAction.cpp ~3254) returns false at `if (!pClientActor)` -- it needs a
legacy IActor player, and a player made of IEntityComponents is not one. Measured: CanSave()
returns 1 and SaveGame() still returns 0, silently, with nothing in the log.

What DOES work is the engine's serializer on its own:

    IXmlSerializer* pSer = gEnv->pSystem->GetXmlUtils()->CreateXmlSerializer();
    pComponent->GameSerialize(TSerialize(pSer->GetWriter(node)));   // or GetReader(node)
    pSer->Release();

so every component's `GameSerialize(TSerialize)` / `NeedGameSerialize()` is written exactly as
the engine expects and reused by a hand-rolled save file. Ashvale's save (CAshvaleGame::
SaveToFile / LoadFromFile, ash_savegame / ash_loadgame, F5 / F9) writes %USER%/ashvale_<name>.xml:
the run's phase, flags, coins and bread from a singleton that is not an entity (carried by the
PlayerStart marker's GameSerialize), plus per-entity transform, CHealthComponent and
CChestComponent state. One serializer per node -- GetWriter/GetReader bind to the node given.

Three things the implementation had to get right:
  * The XML writer OMITS values it considers default: a closed chest writes `<Chest />` with no
    attribute, and the reader leaves the variable untouched. So a load must start from a known
    baseline (ResetWorld) and then apply the file over it.
  * Death is derived state. Health comes back at 0 but the body is standing and the brain is
    running, so the NPC checks `IsDead() && !m_bCorpse` in Update and applies the corpse
    presentation there -- not in the serializer (component order is not guaranteed) and not via
    OnDied (which would count the kill a second time, since the kill flags are in the save).
  * Restoring the player through ResetForGame re-fills health, so health is deserialized AFTER
    the transform, and regeneration then heals visibly within seconds (measured: saved at 88,
    read back 90 half a second later, 100 after four).

Verified: fresh game -> Tom's chest gives "Found 2 bread"; load a save where it was looted ->
"It is empty."; flags, purse, player position and a dead bandit (restored as a corpse) all come
back, and the full 13-check playtest still passes.

title: Measuring a level's performance here: two instruments that lie, and the numbers
source: Ashvale performance pass, 2026-09-23
content:
Instrument: `ash_perf <seconds> [label]` (Game.dll) samples gEnv->pTimer->GetRealFrameTime()
every frame and logs mean/median/p95/worst. The engine's r_DisplayInfo overlay cannot be read
from a script, and a screenshot of an fps counter is not a measurement. Attribution without the
engine profiler: switch one subsystem off (e_Vegetation, e_Shadows, e_Terrain, e_Brushes,
e_Particles), measure the delta, switch it back.

TWO WAYS THE MEASUREMENT LIED, both caught by checking that a known change moves the number:

  * The EDITOR VIEWPORT is not the game. It renders into a ~700x850 panel and measured
    ~2 ms/frame -- useless as a proxy. Measure in the launcher (launcher_perf.py), whose Game.dll
    carries the same bridge on port 37777; Sandbox must be closed first because the editor's
    Game.dll owns that port.
  * VSYNC pinned every sample to 179-180 fps (5.57 ms) and made every A/B delta zero. r_VSync 0
    first, or the whole run is noise. sys_MaxFPS was already -1; vsync was the cap.

Measured for Ashvale at 1704x959 on this machine (AMD), after r_VSync 0:

  viewpoint   frame time   fps
  tavern       1.86 ms     539     (interior, little in view)
  camp         1.87 ms     536
  village      2.53 ms     395
  clearing     2.83-2.95   ~345    (worst: forest, most vegetation)

  attribution at the clearing: vegetation 13%, shadows 9%, terrain 8.5%, brushes 2%,
  particles ~0. Everything renderable off: 1.99 ms, so the whole scene is 1.15 ms (37%) and
  ~2 ms is fixed cost -- engine update, game logic, present.

CONCLUSION: there is nothing to optimise. 345-540 fps with 37% of the frame spent on the scene
means the level is nowhere near a limit on this hardware, and "optimising" it would be inventing
work. The useful output of a performance pass can be a number that says stop.

title: ashvale_ci.py: one command that says whether the game still works
source: Ashvale regression harness, 2026-09-23
content:
python examples/ashvale/ashvale_ci.py            # play it through, compare against the baseline (exit 1 on a regression)
    python examples/ashvale/ashvale_ci.py --build    # rebuild Game.dll first
    python examples/ashvale/ashvale_ci.py --accept   # store this run as the new baseline
    python examples/ashvale/ashvale_ci.py --inject-fault   # positive control: break the story, expect a REGRESSION

A run takes 70-110 s and produces ci_runs/<timestamp>/ with run.json, the playtest output, its
trace and screenshots. It compares three things against ashvale_baseline.json: every gameplay
check (a check that passed before must still pass, and a check that vanishes counts as a
failure), the number of player deaths, and counts of WATCHED log lines -- "Invalid matrix
ignored", "couldn't find NavMesh triangle", "(path failed)", the collision-avoidance unregister,
the animation processing-context warning, and crash dumps. A new warning fails the run even when
every gameplay check still passes.

Three things this cost, each worth keeping:

  * `game.toggle_game_mode` can return ok and do NOTHING: measured 2026-09-23, ticks stayed at 0
    through three toggles while Ctrl+G (`bridge.input.key g ctrl`) entered immediately. The
    playtest now alternates both and trusts only the tick counter.
  * A harness that has never failed is not evidence. The first --inject-fault set a story flag
    before the run, the playtest's own ash_newgame wiped it, and the harness cheerfully reported
    OK. The fault has to be LEVEL state to survive: renaming BlackWat out of the way makes the
    kill sequence impossible, and it is renamed back afterwards.
  * Parse a machine-readable line, not the human one. The playtest prints both -- "PASS <label>
    <detail>" for reading and "CHECK|PASS|<label>" for the harness -- because detail text in the
    name made every check look MISSING between runs.

title: Combat that reads: a parry window, stagger, a camera kick and a lunge
source: Ashvale combat pass, 2026-09-23
content:
Ashvale's fight was one swing and one guard, with no reason to time anything. Four changes,
none of which needed new animation:

  * PARRY. CHealthComponent gained `onFilterDamage`, which runs BEFORE damage is applied and
    returns the amount that should land -- a reaction after the fact cannot cancel a blow. The
    player installs a filter: guard raised within kParryWindow (0.45 s) of the hit lands zero
    damage and staggers the attacker; a guard merely held still blocks through the damage scale.
  * STAGGER (CBanditBrain::Stagger): cancels the swing in progress, delays the next one, pushes
    the body back 0.35 m, and blocks the Attack state while it runs. A landed player hit gives
    0.45 s; a parry gives 1.1 s.
  * CAMERA KICK on taking damage -- a pitch offset plus a random roll that decays over ~0.3 s.
    A hit should move the view, not only tint it.
  * LUNGE: the bandit steps 0.25 m toward the player at the exact hit moment, which is the only
    cue available without an animation that the blow is landing NOW.

Measured against a bandit (12 damage, 1.7 s interval), 11 s per trial:
    no guard      7 hits   -88 health  (~12.6 per hit)
    guard held   20 hits   -77 health  (~3.9 per hit -- the 0.3 damage scale)
    guard timed  14 hits, 7 parried, -88 -- zero on every parried blow, full on every missed one

so holding the guard is safe and dull, and timing it is strictly better only if the timing is
good. The scripted test alternates blindly and catches about half.

Watch the logs, not the impression: the parry line goes through CryLogAlways (console/editor.log)
while BanditTrace goes to claude_npc.log, and counting "parry" in the wrong file reported zero
parries while seven staggers were sitting in the other one.

title: Packaging Ashvale as a standalone build, and what ends up inside it
source: Ashvale standalone build, 2026-09-23
content:
python packaging/package_project.py <project.cryproject> --out <folder>

Runs the engine's own release_project.py task list with the Tk dialog answered in code. Takes a
few minutes, spawns rc.exe, and must run with Sandbox CLOSED (the packaged game also wants the
game bridge on port 37777, which the editor's Game.dll owns).

Result for Ashvale: 1.1 GB -- Assets as paks (PrecompiledTextures.pak alone is 498 MB of the
GameSDK art that was imported), engine binaries under bin/win_x64, levels/ashvale, config.pak and
system.cfg. Start it with bin/win_x64/GameLauncher.exe from the build's own folder.

VERIFIED IN THE PACKAGE, not just in the editor (driven through the same ash_* console commands
over the game bridge): boots to the main menu, new game, dialogue sets a quest flag, combat kills
a bandit, save and load restore the run -- 5 of 5.

Two things worth knowing about what lands in the folder:

  * The packager copies the engine's bin folder as it stands, so ANY locally patched engine DLL
    goes with it -- the package carries the patched CryAISystem.dll (md5 matches the .patched
    copy, differs from .orig571), which means the off-mesh link fix travels with the build and
    the package does NOT depend on the machine's engine install. An older note in the project notes saying
    "a packaged build does not have the fix" was wrong.
  * It also copies whatever junk is in that folder: *.orig571 backups and the *UnitTest.exe
    binaries came along. Deleting them took bin/win_x64 from 509 MB to 400 MB, and the trimmed
    build still boots and plays.

title: Bandits as a faction: shouted alerts, a walked post, a night camp, and a hunt
source: Ashvale bandit faction, 2026-09-23
content:
Four behaviours turned five separate fights into a camp that behaves like one group. All of it
sits in CBanditBrain and needs no behaviour tree:

  * SHOUT. A bandit entering Chase because he SAW the player calls ShoutTo(playerPos), which
    iterates entities, keeps CNpcComponents whose GetRole() is Bandit and are alive, and Alerts
    everyone within kShoutRadius (28 m). An alerted bandit runs to the point without having seen
    anything himself (m_bAlerted, cleared the moment he does see the player).
    Measured: one sighting at the west gate brought THREE others -- "BanditGateW: shouts -- 3
    others coming", then three "Guard -> Chase (heard the shout)".
  * WALKED POST. Guard now steps between four points at kPatrolRadius (6 m) around home with a
    3.5 s pause, seeded by entity id so the camp does not move in lockstep. Measured: one bandit
    occupied 11 distinct positions in 18 s where he used to stand on one.
  * NIGHT. After 20:30 (ITimeOfDay::GetTime) they walk to the CampFire entity and stay there;
    before 05:30 they are still there; in the morning they go back on watch. Measured: mean
    distance from the fire 11.2 m at noon, 2.2 m at 22:30, with five "turning in" traces and
    five "back on watch" in the morning.
  * THE HUNT. Once the player has the tithe (flag has_tithe), CanSeePlayer multiplies combat
    sight by kTitheSightBonus (1.6, so 18 m -> 28.8 m). Measured at 30 m, beyond what patrol
    wandering can close: 1 sighting with the tithe safe, 5 once it is taken.

Measuring AI behaviour needs care: after patrol was added, a sighting test at 22 m was
meaningless because the patrol itself closes 6 m. Test beyond the range of every other motion
in the system, or the number measures the wrong thing.

title: Driving the renderer from game state: SetPostEffectParam, and the parameters that exist
source: Ashvale renderer pass, 2026-09-23
content:
`gEnv->p3DEngine->SetPostEffectParam(name, value)` / `GetPostEffectParam` reach the stock post
effects with no shader work and no CVars. The full name list is in
RenderDll/Common/PostProcess/PostProcess.cpp and PostEffects.cpp (grep AddParamFloat): the
Global_User_* grade (Saturation, Brightness, Contrast, ColorC/Y/M/K, ColorHue) is the set a game
may own, alongside FilterBlurring_Amount, FilterGrain_Amount, FilterSharpening_Amount,
FilterChromaShift_User_Amount, MotionBlur_*, ImageGhosting_Amount and the Flashbang/KillCamera
groups.

Ashvale drives them from the run's state in CAshvaleGame::UpdatePostEffects, eased per frame:
  * wounded (below half health): saturation down to 0.45, brightness down 25%, contrast up 10%,
    scaled by how hurt the player is;
  * dead: saturation 0, brightness 0.55, FilterBlurring_Amount 1.4;
  * ending: saturation 1.12, brightness 1.05, Global_User_ColorY 0.25 (firelight).

Verified as numbers with `ash_post`, which reads the values back out of the renderer:
healthy 1.00/1.00/1.00/0.00/0.0, wounded at 20 hp 0.607/0.821/1.071, dead 0.0/0.55/blur 1.4,
ending 1.12/1.05/warm 0.25 -- and visually, the death frame is fully grey, dark and blurred.

Two things to know: the post-effect manager KEEPS the last value, so leaving a state has to write
the neutral value back (ResetPostEffects on OnPlayerRemoved), and a screenshot is a poor witness
here -- three captures of the graded states came back as flat editor grey (the blank-frame trap),
so the parameter read-back is the measurement and the picture is the illustration.

title: The four boundaries: the model behind almost every hard bug in this project
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
the notes folder/docs/engine-lifetimes.md holds the model, not the trap list. CryEngine has four
lifetimes, and each destroys a different slice while leaving the rest looking intact:

  FRAME          destroys nothing; ordering still matters (read state after whatever writes it --
                 the first-person sword lagged because it used the camera's WORLD matrix, i.e.
                 last frame's; a child entity with a LOCAL transform fixed it structurally).
  GAME MODE      destroys NO_SAVE entities, runtime components, AI registrations and any binding
                 the game made to the player. This is the "works the first time" class: a freed
                 m_pWeapon, an orphaned sword entity, a null m_pPlayer from the second session on,
                 duplicated components where the LAST one to see START_GAME owns movement.
  LEVEL RELOAD   destroys every entity and every loaded resource. A cached IParticleEffect* in a
                 function-level static crashed the editor here. Also: the watchdog may reopen a
                 DIFFERENT level than the one being worked on.
  EDITOR RESTART destroys everything not on disk -- and several things are not files when you
                 assume they are: the navmesh until exported, time-of-day/fog (they live in the
                 engine preset), the compiled terrain texture, and loose assets cached by CryPak.

Three habits: own the rebuild (drop every handle at a boundary, hold entities by id, re-resolve);
make invalid states impossible or recoverable (a player at 0 health who can be neither damaged nor
healed has no exit); and test ACROSS the boundary -- enter game mode twice, reload, restart.

Closing rule from the same document: a result is not evidence until the instrument has shown it
can produce the opposite result.

title: Entering and leaving game mode (and how to know which you are in)
source: Session 2026-09-24: research agents over the manual + source, then live measurement
content:
`game.toggle_game_mode` (ICommandManager) is a TOGGLE and it is DEFERRED -- see
editor-game-mode-toggle-deferred. The editor's own state is `game.is_in_game_mode` (also
ICommandManager, GameEngine.cpp:1910); its answer is the 'Returned: true|false' line in the
reply's log text. There is no Python equivalent.

Use bridge/editor_state.py rather than toggling by hand:
  hold_active()      live 0->1 kick of ed_keepEditorActive, so the editor updates unfocused
  set_game_mode(b)   toggles at most once, then polls is_in_game_mode (returns seconds or None)
  release_active()   back to Crytek's default (idle when nobody looks at the editor)
Never toggle because a game-side counter stopped: in game mode but unfocused, everything
freezes and a toggle switches it OFF. Screenshots: use bridge.viewport.screenshot.

title: TRAP: game.toggle_game_mode only queues; ed_keepEditorActive in user.cfg never works
source: Session 2026-09-24: research agents over the manual + source, then live measurement
content:
ToggleGameMode -> EnterGameMode -> CGameEngine::RequestSetGameMode stores a pending
request; CGameEngine::Update carries it out, and CCryEditApp::IdleProcessing only calls Update
while a Sandbox window is ACTIVE or m_bKeepEditorActive is set (CryEdit.cpp:885-923). The bridge
answers from its own WM_TIMER pump, so `ok` means "queued". Measured 2026-09-24 on a fresh editor:
focused -> entered in 0.12 s; minimised -> nothing for 5 s, no warning; restored with NO new
command -> the queued entry ran within 0.02 s. In game mode and minimised, the game freezes
(is_in_game_mode stays true, ticks stop).

ed_keepEditorActive = 1 in user.cfg does NOT set the flag: user.cfg is applied before CGameEngine
registers the CVar, the stored value is applied before the change callback is attached, and
setting the same value again is a no-op. Matched test: CVar reads 1, set 1 again -> a minimised
toggle never entered; set 0 then 1 -> entered in 0.09 s and ticked while minimised. So: kick it
0 -> 1 live (editor_state.hold_active) for the length of a run, and release it after -- held
permanently the editor renders flat out in the background.

title: RETRACTED 2026-09-24: the speed-matching 'negative result' measured the wrong thing
source: Session 2026-09-24: research agents over the manual + source, then live measurement
content:
The 2026-09-23 conclusion ("0.50 vs 0.48 m/s, the body already follows the clip, nothing to
correct") was wrong three ways:
  * the body does NOT follow the clip: navigation moves it (ChangeVelocity SetAsTarget), and
    CAdvancedAnimationComponent writes TravelSpeed = |physics v| every frame
    (AdvancedAnimationComponent.cpp:113-137) -- the clip follows the body;
  * the matcher's error, locator speed minus body speed, is therefore zero BY CONSTRUCTION, so it
    could never move; GetCurrentVelocity = GetRelMovement().t / m_fDeltaTime is the locator speed
    per animation second and does not change with SetPlaybackScale;
  * 0.50 m/s was mostly ankle roll plus frozen off-screen poses: the per-frame min-of-two-ankles
    probe was never checked against a control.
The validated measurement and the working fix: foot-slide-stance-probe.

title: Measuring foot slide properly: heel/toe drift per ground contact, with a known-slide control
source: Session 2026-09-24: research agents over the manual + source, then live measurement
content:
Primary metric (CNpcComponent::UpdateFootSlideProbe): net world displacement of each heel and
toe joint (Bip01 L/R Heel, Toe0) from touch-down to lift-off, divided by the contact time. A
planted foot must end where it started; this is immune to the pose/WorldTM timing offset (the
pose read in an entity update is last frame's). Frames where the pose did not change bit for bit
(the renderer skipped the character) are counted and excluded. Contact = model-space height
within 3 cm of the joint's lowest (5 cm to leave).

Controls: `claude_slide_k <k>` forces the target's playback scale -- a KNOWN slide (k=0.5 must
read ~0.5*v). Idle must read 0. Driver: foot_slide_run.py <villager> k... (the
villager must be >10 m from the player or it stops to watch; legs are navmesh-checked).

Measured on Edmund at 2.00 m/s, steady and straight: k=1.00 -> 0.11/0.12 (heel/toe);
k=0.5 -> 1.05; k=1.5 -> 0.85; k=1.053 -> 0.04 (the floor); k=1.10 -> 0.09; idle 0.000. One
parameter fits all: the blended walk's FEET cover 1.90 m/s while its locator claims 2.00. The old
ankle metrics read 0.35-0.58 across the whole dip -- blind to it.

Fix: claude_stride_match 1 (default). Each stance's SIGNED drift along the facing (+ = foot crept
forward = body outran the clip) nudges a per-villager, per-gait playback scale, learned only on
steady straight locomotion. Same session: off -> 0.135/0.123, signed +0.126; on -> 0.054/0.068,
signed -0.004, scale 1.066. Still sliding: turning (~0.2-0.3 m/s at 50-60 deg/s; Drive snaps
yaw, no turn assets) and start/stop (0.3-0.6).

title: Custom shaders on the stock engine: Assets/GameShaders, hot reload, and the ZPass catch
source: Session 2026-09-24: research agents over the manual + source, then live measurement
content:
A project shader loads from <project>/Assets/GameShaders/HWScripts/CryFX/<Name>.cfx (+ optional
Assets/GameShaders/<Name>.ext); CShaderManBin::GetBinShader looks there before the engine
(ShaderFXParseBin.cpp:973-992). The manual's Assets/Shaders/HWScripts/CryFX does NOT load
("[SHADERS] Failed to load shader"). A material uses it by name: Shader="Name".

Check a load in code: `ash_shader <name>` (EF_LoadShader, flags logged to claude_npc.log). The
parse is async on the render thread: read the flags seconds later, the immediate read is
"found, flags 0" for everything. Controls: ReferenceImage found; a missing name NOT FOUND.

Measured: a ReferenceImage copy returning cyan drew 1,440 pixels of exactly (0,255,255); the
all-stock control (ReferenceImage + color_Magenta.dds) 1,371 exact magenta; swapping materials
moved the colour. HLSL errors appear in the editor console (error X3004 ... Couldn't compile HW
shader) and the object is not drawn. Saving the .cfx hot-reloads it with r_ShadersEditing 0
(the manual says it is needed): cyan -> yellow in 7.6 s.

The catch for real materials: the deferred G-buffer pass does not call the shader's
GatherMaterialAttribs -- CommonZPass.cfi (lines 415-449) builds the albedo itself; the Illum
function only feeds the forward path. Copy the include into GameShaders (AshZPass.cfi) and
#include it from your copy of Illum: it resolves, and gave lit, shadowed, depth-tested cyan (R/G
0.19 vs 1.02). AfterHDRPostProcess shaders have no depth test: through walls. Engine paks can be
read with packaging/pakread.py (their backslash local headers break zipfile).

title: Sound with no middleware: SDL mixer, a hand-written ACE file, and game-side distance gain
source: Session 2026-09-24: research agents over the manual + source, then live measurement
content:
s_ImplName defaults to CryAudioImplSDLMixer. Samples: Assets/audio/sdlmixer/assets/*.ogg (GameSDK's
audio.pak has 124 usable ones -- footsteps per surface, woodland ambience beds, impacts); controls:
Assets/audio/sdlmixer/ace/<lib>.xml, e.g.
<AudioSystemData name="x" version="5" triggers="N" parameters="M"><ImplData events="N" parameters="K"/>
<Triggers><Trigger name="t"><Event name="s.ogg" type="start" volume="-6" loop_count="1"/></Trigger>
</Triggers><Parameters><Parameter name="g"><Event name="s.ogg"/></Parameter></Parameters>...
loop_count 0 = forever; type="stop" stops a loop. A <Parameter> with <Event> children is a linear
0..1 volume multiplier for that sample on the object (applied at start and live).

Code: CryAudio::StringToId("t") (constexpr); pEntity->GetOrCreateComponent<IEntityAudioComponent>()
->SetParameter(g, gain) / ->ExecuteTrigger(t) for a sound AT an entity; gEnv->pAudioSystem->
ExecuteTrigger for 2D. Ashvale: AshvaleAudio::PlayAt / Play2D / GainAt, ash_audio_stats counts
what started and what was culled, ash_ambience 0/1. See sdl-mixer-71-no-attenuation before
trusting enable_dist_attenuation. Verify with audio_peakmeter.ps1 (real output), not
the debug overlay (an event can be 'playing' and inaudible).

title: TRAP: on a 7.1 output the SDL implementation never attenuates or pans
source: Session 2026-09-24: research agents over the manual + source, then live measurement
content:
Measured 2026-09-24: a positional footstep 540 m from the listener peaked 0.35 on the output;
game mode sat at 1.00 (clipping) from every villager's footsteps at any distance. Cause, from
source: Mix_OpenAudio(48000, S16, 2, 4096) allows a channel-count change, so on a 7.1 default
device (Core Audio: 8 channels) SDL opens 8; SDL_mixer 2.0.4's position effect supports only
1/2/4/6 channels (effect_position.c get_position_effect_func -> "Unsupported audio channels"), so
Mix_SetDistance / Mix_SetPosition fail silently. enable_dist_attenuation and enable_panning do
nothing on such a machine; the debug overlay still shows correct listener and distances.

Fix without the engine: compute the gain in game code from the camera distance and set it through
an ACE <Parameter> (per-sample volume multiplier) before the trigger; cull out-of-range sounds;
update loops' gain periodically; remove enable_dist_attenuation so a stereo machine does not
attenuate twice. Panning needs a non-7.1 output. Instrument: audio_peakmeter.ps1 reports the
endpoint and session channel counts.

title: Sandbox dies ~28 min into every session when left running with the display off
source: Session 2026-09-24: research agents over the manual + source, then live measurement
content:
2026-09-24 02:48-08:53: every watchdog-launched session crashed 27.8-30.1 minutes after start.
Always an access violation on an unnamed AMD driver thread (AMDXX64.DLL+0xd9998/+0xd99ca), then
0xc0000374 heap corruption; the render thread inside d3d11 -> AMDXX64, the main thread waiting.
Not a leak (memory, GPU memory, handles flat until the crash), not rendering load (display off,
3D utilisation 0%), not auto-backup (off). The 09-23 session ran 13 h while the user was at the
PC. Treat as an AMD driver fault with the editor unattended and the monitor asleep: update the
driver or don't leave Sandbox running overnight -- the watchdog restarts it into the same crash
every 35 minutes. Evidence lives in the Windows Application log (event 1000: Sandbox.exe, ntdll,
0xc0000374), <project>/editor.log (per-thread stack dumps) and error.log (last crash only).

Prediction tested 09:13: a session launched 08:41:33, used actively for its first minutes (game mode, audio tests, CI) then left idle, crashed at 31.8 min with the same AMDXX64 fault. The constant is time since launch (27.8-31.8 min across four crashes), not idleness.

title: TRAP: Windows PowerShell 5.1 Get-Content/Set-Content garbles UTF-8 docs
source: Session 2026-09-24: research agents over the manual + source, then live measurement
content:
On a BOM-less UTF-8 file, Windows PowerShell 5.1's Get-Content -Raw decodes as the ANSI code page
(Windows-1252), and Set-Content -Encoding utf8 writes it back with a BOM: every non-ASCII
character (em dash, arrows, section signs) becomes mojibake. It hit the project notes once (237
sequences); undone exactly by mapping each char back to its cp1252 byte and decoding as UTF-8.
Edit docs with the Edit tool or Python with explicit encoding, never PowerShell.

title: Why Sandbox.exe was rebuilt: the bridge imports exactly one non-stock symbol
source: Session 2026-09-24 afternoon: import-table analysis and turning-locomotion experiments
content:
UPDATED 2026-09-25: the static_cast is done; the plugin no longer imports GetIEditorImpl (bridge-plugin-dev-loop-2026-09-25).

The installed Sandbox.exe, EditorCommon.dll, CryQt.dll and MFCToolsPlugin.dll are unsigned local builds
(2026-09-10). The only editor-source edit is `SANDBOX_API CEditorImpl* GetIEditorImpl();`
(EditorQt/IEditorImpl.h) plus CMake guards for the missing proprietary FBX SDK. Reading the import
table (bridge/pe_imports.py, stdlib): ClaudeBridgePlugin.dll imports ONE symbol stock Sandbox does
not export, ?GetIEditorImpl@@YAPEAVCEditorImpl@@XZ, at 13 call sites (terrain manager, vegetation map,
lens flares). Everything else is a member of SANDBOX_API classes, exported by stock too
(`class SANDBOX_API CEditorImpl : public IEditor, ...`).

The way to drop it: REGISTER_PLUGIN defines the plugin's own GetIEditor() from
PLUGIN_INIT_PARAM::pIEditor, which is Sandbox's CEditorImpl; IEditor is its first base, so
static_cast<CEditorImpl*>(GetIEditor()) is exact. With that, the bridge would load in Crytek's stock
editor. The plugin source is in the read-only engine tree, so the change waits for the user. No FBX
capability was lost by the rebuild: FBXPlugin.dll (stock, signed) carries the SDK itself.

title: Turning locomotion: 2D MoveSpeed x TurnSpeed blend space, and why snapping/rate-limiting both slide
source: Session 2026-09-24 afternoon: import-table analysis and turning-locomotion experiments
content:
Measured on Ashvale's villagers (foot_slide_turns.py bins stance slide by turn rate):
turning was the dominant slide (0.31 m/s at 30-60 deg/s vs 0.06 straight).
  * A 2D blend space (MoveSpeed x TurnSpeed, faces counter-clockwise from above, TurnSpeed + = left)
    loads from project assets. GameSDK has relaxed_tac_walkturn_rifle_lft/rgt_slow/fast next to the
    relaxed_tac_walk clips. Verified with the clip locator's yaw rate (GetRelMovement().q).
  * CAdvancedAnimationComponent never writes TurnSpeed (only TravelSpeed/TravelAngle/TurnAngle): set
    it yourself every frame with SetMotionParameter(eMotionParamID_TurnSpeed, smoothed yaw rate).
  * A facing SNAPPED to the path direction turns in single frames at path corners; the blend sees
    ~0 and the planted foot is swept. RATE-LIMITING the facing alone makes it far worse: the body
    crab-walks (16-54 deg between travel and facing) and the feet drift sideways (0.66-1.5 m/s).
  * STEERING along the facing (velocity = speed * facing * cos(heading error), facing turns at a
    limited rate) removes the crab and halves turning slide, but slows walkers badly in corners.
  * RETRACTED: "the walkturn clips turn at only ~0.42 rad/s and the blend saturates". The clips turn
    at 0.81-1.43 rad/s and the blend delivers the fed TurnSpeed exactly; the 0.42/0.57 came from an
    instrument that summed idle and undrawn frames (chunk blendspace-turn-response). Keep the TurnSpeed
    axis narrow with enough cells (+-1.0 in 21 -- +-2.5 in 15 lost small turns in one cell).
Sharp corners need a different move (turn-in-place / Idle2Move starts) or wider path corners.
Trap: `--` in an XML comment makes a .bspace fail to load and the fragment silently plays nothing.

title: Ragdoll on death for a component character (CCharacterControllerComponent + CAdvancedAnimationComponent)
source: Session 2026-09-24: ragdoll experiments
content: Stock CRagdollComponent is incompatible with CCharacterControllerComponent (declared) and its Physicalize is protected; copy its mechanism instead. The entity system's living->ragdoll shortcut (PhysicsProxy.cpp:786, ConvertCharacterToRagdoll/RelinquishCharacterPhysics) needs skeleton physics created with the living entity, which the component controller never makes. Working recipe (Ashvale CNpcComponent::Ragdollize): Physicalize(PE_NONE); then SEntityPhysicalizeParams{type=PE_ARTICULATED, nSlot=animComponent->GetEntitySlotId(), nLod=1 (ragdoll LOD), mass=80, bCopyJointVelocities=true}; check GetType()==PE_ARTICULATED; StopAnimationsAllLayers; clear geom_colltype_player on every part (pe_status_nparts + pe_params_part); pe_action_impulse along the killing blow. Stop your own movement/rotation/animation code for the corpse. Undo: DestroyCharacterPhysics(0), SetDefaultPose, re-physicalize the controller. Measured: 17 parts, pelvis 0.87 -> 0.19 m in ~1 s, at rest by 1.5 s, peak 2.2 m/s; survives New Game and save/load (ragdoll_test.py).

title: A 2D blend space delivers the TurnSpeed it is fed -- measure over drawn Walk frames only
source: Session 2026-09-24: forced-TurnSpeed sweep in game mode; RC headers; FBX sources
content:
Measured on the villagers' villager_move.bspace (MoveSpeed x TurnSpeed, GameSDK
relaxed_tac_walk / walkturn clips), stock engine:

* The clips: walkturn lft slow/fast 0.807/1.426 rad/s, rgt slow/fast -0.857/-1.334 (69/87/-72/-82
  deg per cycle). animation/anim_img.py reads the RC's own per-clip header (CHUNK_GAHCAF_INFO,
  m_fTurnSpeed/m_fAssetTurn/m_fSpeed) from GameSDK Animations.img inside animations.pak;
  animation/fbx_root_motion.py evaluates the Crysis-pack FBX sources in world space. They agree to 3
  decimals; controls: straight clips 0 deg, walkStart clips their authored 89/-90/+-180 deg. The engine
  loads only times/start location from the .img (CharacterManager.cpp:3629) and re-extracts blend
  parameters from the root controller (GlobalAnimationHeaderLMG::Init_TurnSpeed: per-frame yaw of
  column 1, not scaled by playback; Init_MoveSpeed: per-frame arc length x m_fPlaybackScale).
* The blend: turn_response.py feeds every villager a constant TurnSpeed (claude_turn_force)
  and reads GetRelMovement over drawn Walk frames. Clip yaw rate = param x playback at 0.97-1.00 for
  +0.3/+0.6/+0.9/-0.6 rad/s; instrument control (locator travel vs MoveSpeed param x playback) 1.00 in
  every arm. Natural feed with a steered facing: clip/body 0.95.
* The trap: summing GetRelMovement every frame counts idle stops (body turns, idle clip does not) and
  undrawn frames (no pose update). Same windows: ungated 0.61; windows mostly outside drawn Walk 0.40,
  fully drawn Walk 0.91. Gate on the active fragment AND a pose that changed this frame.
* SetDesiredMotionParam writes straight through unless the dimension is locked="1"; the 2D sampler
  clamps to [min,max], bilinear-interpolates a precomputed virtual-example grid, and keeps at most 4
  examples per grid point (ParametricSampler.cpp:662).
* In a snap-facing controller the fed rate is ~0: a one-frame snap is a huge yaw rate and a clamp before
  smoothing discards nearly all of it -- the turn blend only helps with a rate-limited facing.
* FBX trap: the Crysis rig's Locator_Locomotion is a child of Bip01 (-90 deg PreRotation); its local
  curves read 0 turn. Compose world transforms, and pick the heading axis once (an upright locator has
  two flat axes).

title: TRAP: 'map <level> s' (Crytek's template default) never loads in a Release build
source: Session 2026-09-24: Release Ashvale stall, root-caused and fixed
content:
Crytek's C++ template boots with ExecuteString("map example s"). 's' makes a MULTIPLAYER listen server.
The Release engine's CryNetwork is PURE_CLIENT (game.log "[Network Version]: RELEASE PURE CLIENT"; Profile says
"PROFILE DEVELOPMENT BUILD"), and a pure client answers its own client's connection setup with ProcessDisconnect
when the process is multiplayer server AND client (CryNetwork/Protocol/NetNub.cpp:1070-1074, 1910-1914). The
failure is only a CryLog (ActionGame.cpp:1034-1038) -- compiled out in Release. Symptoms: "Loading level X" then
nothing, 0 entities forever, black screen, 3-20 s frames (the loading-screen render loop FlashUI started in
PrepareNextLevel is never stopped: it forces VSync and presents under m_rdldLock, which the render-loading thread
also needs), render thread parked in dxgi -> dwmapi!DwmpDxGetWindowSharedSurface, r_VSync 0 no help.
Fix for a single-player game: "map <level>" (local game). Measured on the same package: 37 entities in 8 s,
0.01 s frames. Diagnose Release hangs with launcher_diag.py (bridge latency, entity count, the game
code's own trace file) and stack_sample.py (debugger-free stacks).

title: TRAP: DwmGetCompositionTimingInfo cFrame/cRefresh are per-call counters here, not a composition meter
source: Session 2026-09-24: a wrong 'display is off' conclusion
content:
Tried as a 'is the desktop composing / is the display on' probe: cFrame and cRefresh advanced +1 per
second even while a game rendered and the user was at a lit monitor. Read three times in a row they were 2, 3, 4:
on this Windows 11 machine they increase by one per CALL. qpcVBlank was live (within 8 ms of now at the 180 Hz
period). The probe produced a confident, wrong 'the display is off' and was deleted. Lesson: an instrument with no
positive control that can reach a known-on state measures nothing; ask the user when a physical fact matters.

title: Packaging Ashvale with Crytek's own Package Build (no custom builder) -- what the project must provide
source: Session 2026-09-24 evening: stock packager + documented steps, measured 9/9 + 4/4 in both configs
content:
User rule: use the built-in packager (release_project.py = Launcher right-click > Package Build); fix the
project, not the output. packaging/package_project.py only runs it unattended (answers its dialog).
Before packaging: build Game.dll for the configuration (Release: cmake --build solutions/win64 --target Game
--config Release) and export the level (manual: Package Build does neither).
Project-side fixes (all measured):
* Shadows: "sys_spec": "2" in Game.cryproject console_variables (launchers default to sys_spec 0 = custom ->
  e_ObjShadowCastSpec 0 -> nothing casts). See trap-launcher-spec0-no-shadows.
* Textures: already-split GameSDK .dds (no .tif) are rejected by RC's PC texture job; ship them in
  Assets/GameSDKTextures.pak (engine Tools\7za.exe a -tzip -mx0, paths relative to Assets, no .cryasset).
  The packager copies Assets/*.pak as-is. Release guide: "a custom .pak file", "zipping ... changing the extension".
* Project shaders: Assets/GameShaders.pak (RC never copies .cfx/.cfi/.ext); rebuild when a shader changes.
* Release Game.dll: plugin "type": "EPluginType::Native" (engine alias, IProjectManager.h:41-49) makes the
  packager copy bin/win_x64_release/Game.dll; with "EType::Native" it silently ships the Profile DLL.
* Release shaders (source is never parsed in Release): the manual's procedure -- Remote Shader Compiler copied
  out of the engine (C:\ShaderCompiler), RSC CVars in Game.cryproject, play a FRESH package to fill
  Cache\Assets\ShaderList_PC.txt, packaging/shader_cache_gen.py (ShaderCacheGen with
  GenerateShaderCache.cryproject = Crytek's template: r_multithreaded 0, no plugins), Tools\PakShaders.bat
  D3D11 C:\ShaderPak (7za.exe + 7z.dll, stock paks seeded), remove the RSC CVars, Package Build, copy ONLY
  ShadersBin.pak over the build's engine\shadersbin.pak (see trap-pakshaders-merge-shadercache).

title: TRAP: a packaged game has NO shadows because the launcher runs sys_spec 0 ('custom')
source: Session 2026-09-24: user saw no shadows in packaged builds; measured and fixed
content:
The editor always applies a spec (saved configSpec, default Medium = 2). A GameLauncher registers sys_spec
as CONFIG_CUSTOM (0) (SystemInit.cpp:4916) and loads spec configs only for 1-4 (:631-664); auto-detection needs
-autodetect. So the sys_spec_Shadows group never runs and e_ObjShadowCastSpec keeps its code default 0
(cvars.cpp:1040): objects get the cast-shadow flag at LOAD only if their Cast Shadow Min Spec (default Low=1) <=
e_ObjShadowCastSpec (EntityLoadManager.cpp:276-283; vegetation/merged meshes likewise). Sun shadows are on,
nothing casts. Measured in a package: spec 0 -> no shadows; +e_ObjShadowCastSpec 2 alone -> still none;
+sys_spec 2 -> tree shadows. Fix: "sys_spec": "2" in Game.cryproject console_variables (applied at startup,
shipped in config.pak). A root system.cfg does not survive Package Build (it writes its own).

title: SUPERSEDED (see howto-complete-shader-cache-seeded): TRAP: PakShaders 'accumulative' packing destroys the stock ShaderCache.pak
source: Session 2026-09-24: measured entry-by-entry against the stock paks
content:
Full title: SUPERSEDED (see howto-complete-shader-cache-seeded): TRAP: PakShaders 'accumulative' packing destroys the stock ShaderCache.pak -- ship only ShadersBin.pak
SUPERSEDED 2026-09-25: the shrink came from generating into an EMPTY user cache; seed it with the stock cache first (shader_cache_gen.py --seed-stock) and all three paks merge complete -- the project notes
The manual says PakShaders.bat "processes in an accumulative way" (7za a into existing archives). But each
shaders/cache/d3d11/CG?Shaders/<shader>@<entry> file is ONE container holding all combinations of that entry; 7za
replaces it whole. With a user cache built from a list of only the global-cache misses (that is all the RSC
records while the stock cache is present), seeding C:\ShaderPak\Engine with the stock paks gave a ShaderCache.pak
where 56 containers shrank (Illum@IlluminationPS 1,122,526 -> 29,716 bytes, some to 16) and lookupdata.bin
10,476 -> 2,660. ShadersBin.pak merged cleanly (242 stock .cfxb/.cfib untouched + the project's). So ship only
ShadersBin.pak (what Release needs to parse project shaders) and keep the stock ShaderCache/Startup paks; PC
Release compiles the few missing combinations at run time (measured 9/9 + 4/4). Also: the script needs
Tools\7z.dll next to 7za.exe, and its root argument must have no spaces (unquoted).
