title: TRAP: a game plugin's own threads keep Game.dll loaded past engine shutdown -> crash on every quit
source: Session 2026-09-25: caught with a minimal Win32 debugger (crash_catch.py), fixed, measured
content:
Symptom: every packaged-game quit crashed in Game.dll (WER only shows one frame; the engine's crash handler
is already gone). Full stack (crash_catch.py): LdrShutdownProcess -> Game.dll dllmain_crt_process_detach ->
execute_onexit_table -> static Schematyc CClassDesc destructor -> CDefaultValue<CParticleComponent::SAttributes>
releasing a Cry3DEngine-owned object; then ~CGamePlugin reading a null gEnv->pSystem.
Why: launchers quit with ExitOnQuit 0 (SystemInit.cpp:4757) -> CSystem::ShutDown, where the plugin manager
FreeLibrary's Game.dll (CryPluginManager.cpp:63) BEFORE Cry3DEngine is unloaded (System.cpp:751). A std::thread
started from a DLL keeps that DLL loaded while it runs (C runtime), and our TCP bridge threads were only stopped
in the plugin destructor -- which runs at unload -- so Game.dll survived to process exit and its statics
(the plugin singleton, reflection copies) were destroyed against unloaded modules. Fix: stop every thread the
plugin started at ESYSTEM_EVENT_FAST_SHUTDOWN / ESYSTEM_EVENT_FULL_SHUTDOWN (join them, unblock blocking socket
calls, fail pending cross-thread work). Also: IEntity::GetOrCreateComponent<T>/GetComponent<T> read T's GUID via
Schematyc::GetTypeGUID<T>() (IEntity.h:811-815), which keeps a static reflection copy of T in YOUR DLL; for
engine components whose defaults own engine objects (CParticleComponent::SAttributes) use
QueryComponentByInterfaceID/CreateComponentByInterfaceID with the component GUID instead.
Measured: every quit crashed before; after, 6/6 clean quits over Profile and Release packages, 0 WER events.

title: HOWTO: a complete shader cache that keeps the stock shaders (seed the user cache first)
source: Session 2026-09-25: measured with examples/ashvale/shader_tour.py on Crytek-packaged Profile and Release builds
content:
Record: shader_tour.py <Profile build> --rsc (the whole game once, RSC on 127.0.0.1 records every
global-cache miss to Cache/Assets/ShaderList_PC.txt). Generate: shader_cache_gen.py <list> --seed-stock -- it
extracts the engine's D3D11 part of shadercache.pak + shadersbin.pak into the emptied <project>/user/shaders/cache
BEFORE running ShaderCacheGen, because the engine opens an existing user-cache file read-write and ADDS to it
(D3DHWShaderCompiling.cpp:2063-2098). Pack: PakShaders.bat D3D11 <root> with <root>/Engine holding FRESH copies of
the stock paks (so the Vulkan part survives) and only USER/shaders/cache/D3D11 staged. Ship all three paks into
the build's engine/ folder. Without the seed each file holds only the list's combinations and 7za's merge replaces
the stock file (2026-09-24: 56 files shrank). Checked per file: 0 lost, 0 smaller, Vulkan unchanged. Result over
the same route: stock cache 109 distinct misses, complete cache 1. Measure: <user>/shaders/ShaderCacheMisses.txt
(non-Release) or ash_shader_stats (EFQ_GetShaderCacheInfo; counts miss EVENTS, repeated per frame while a
combination compiles); start each run from an empty <build>/user/shaders -- a miss is only logged when the
combination is in neither the shipped nor the user cache. ShaderCacheGen logs to <engine>/shadercachegen.log.

title: TRAP: stock Water@WaterPS with rain ripples (%_RT_SAMPLE4) never compiles on D3D11 in 5.7.1
source: Session 2026-09-25: shadercachegen.log + river screenshots in a Release package
content:
error X4500: overlapping register semantics not yet implemented 't16' (ShaderCacheGen and at run
time). Rain (SetRainParams / r_Rain) enables dynamic water ripples, the combination cannot be built, and the
engine re-requests it every frame while ripples last -- still 20 s after the rain stopped (51 -> 618 miss events).
No shader cache can contain it, so it is the one miss a complete cache leaves. The river still draws (darker and
blurred in rain). A project can override an engine shader by putting a fixed Water.cfx in
Assets/GameShaders/HWScripts/CryFX (searched before the engine's), which also changes its cache CRC.

title: HOWTO: measure a packaged build's performance with Statoscope (and what Ashvale costs)
source: Session 2026-09-25: perf_tour.py on Crytek-packaged Profile and Release builds, RX 7900 XTX
content:
perf_tour.py <build> [--functions] [--specs 1,2,3,4]: fullscreen 2560x1440, r_VSync 0 and sys_MaxFPS 0
set live (Release drops those launch args), 17 stops each marked with e_StatoscopeAddUserMarker Ashvale <stop>
and sampled with the game's ash_perf. Profile only: e_StatoscopeLogDestination 0, e_StatoscopeDataGroups fgmtijOu
(+r = function profiler), e_StatoscopeEnabled 1 -> <build>/user/statoscope/perf_*.bin; statoscope_read.py prints
per-stop frame length p50/p95/p99, main/render/GPU load, draw calls, GPU time by pass, memory, top functions.
Log traps: the engine adds its own user markers (each global shader cache miss), so key sections on the marker
path; vidMemUsageInMB holds bytes; function records are "<thread>/<module>/<function>/" and idle threads show as
large "Wait" entries -- filter to Main and drop Waits. Ashvale 2026-09-25: Release 418-575 fps (1.74-2.42 ms),
worst frame 4.4 ms, Profile ~25% slower; Game.dll code < 0.01 ms; 3DEngine culling/submission ~1.2 ms, job
dispatch 0.5 ms; rain +0.4 ms particles. sys_spec 1-4 on the green: 1.76/2.19/2.57/3.17 ms.

title: HOWTO: a jointed breakable (GameSDK fence) broken by a component-game sword
source: Session 2026-09-25: breakable_test.py in editor game mode, with an impulse-0 control
content:
Find real jointed breakables by the node names inside the .cgf ($joint01.. with a "limit=" property,
pieces with "mass="), not by file name: GameSDK objects/architecture/fences/breakable_fence/wooden_fence4m.cgf (6 joints,
8 pieces), wooden_fence8m.cgf, wooden_fence_*_breakable.cgf, props/misc/jointed_breakable/jointedbreakable_example.cgf.
Place as a BRUSH (manual). To break it from game code do what GameSDK's melee does (CMeleeCollisionHelper::Impulse):
ray from the eye (and lower -- a swing sweeps down; a level ray at 1.7 m passes over a knee-high rail), then
pe_action_impulse{impulse, point, partid = hit.partid} on hit.pCollider. CryPhysics accumulates it on the structure part
and breaks joints (physicalentity.cpp:1202-1242); CryAction spawns the loose pieces (ActionGame.cpp:1686). Direct
breaks fire when impulse > limit*0.01 (physicalentity.cpp:1234): 0.1 N*s for limit=10, so the only valid "no break"
control is impulse 0. Measure with a physical-entity census near the object: whole = one PE_STATIC with N parts,
broken pieces become PE_RIGID. Broken BRUSHES are not restored by IGameFramework::ResetBrokenGameObjects -- CryAction
records part removals only for entities (ActionGame.cpp:4099) -- they come back on level load.

title: HOWTO: a Track View sequence authored as XML and played from C++ (camera hand-over included)
source: Session 2026-09-25: cinematic_test.py (7/7) in editor game mode
content:
Track View's Python (trackview.*) can create sequences/nodes/tracks but cannot bind an entity to a node
or set key values, so write the sequence in Track View's own XML (the <Sequence> inside a layer's SequenceObject /
a level's moviedata.xml; GameSDK woodland cinematics.lyr is a reference): Entity node with EntityGUID, Position and
Rotation tracks of three NewSubTracks (x,y,z; rotation in degrees, Quat::CreateRotationXYZ), keys timeTicks (6000/s),
value, ds/dd Bezier handles. Keys are sampled from the STORED handles (CAnimSplineTrack::SampleCurve) -- write
Catmull-Rom handles yourself (ds is the incoming handle stored negated). Load with IMovieSystem::LoadSequence(xml,
false) and PlaySequence; spawn the animated entity with that GUID (SEntitySpawnParams.guid) carrying a CCameraComponent
and Activate() it; when IsPlaying() turns false Activate() the player's camera again. An entity node caches the
EntityId it first resolved, so reload/RemoveSequence per play. make_intro_sequence.py (checks the path
against the heightmap) + Components/Cinematics.cpp; Track View can import the file (File > Import).

title: TRAP: level export hangs on 'pending unapplied changes to navigation data' -- Escape does nothing
source: Session 2026-09-25: two hung exports after placing brushes
content:
CAIManager::IsReadyToGameExport (AIManager.cpp:923-960) shows two modal dialogs: "There are pending
unapplied changes to navigation data ... cancel the export and update now?" (Yes/No, default Yes) when regeneration
requests are BUFFERED, and "processing ... still in progress, export with the old navigation data?" (Yes/Cancel,
default Cancel). Escape closes only the second; the first has no cancel button, so an Escape-answering script hangs
with the editor's main thread in the modal loop (queued bridge commands, Python included, never run) and the
watchdog then kills Sandbox as hung. Fix: run ai.regenerate_ignored (applies the buffered requests, what that Yes
does) before exporting, answer either dialog with Return (both defaults are right), and hold the watchdog lock
(claude_deploy_in_progress) during a long export. bridge.input.click takes coordinates RELATIVE to the Sandbox main
window, not the screen.

title: TRAP: the engine's own screenshot has no 2D UI in it -- capture the window to see menus and HUD
source: Session 2026-09-25: a wrong 'Release has no UI' conclusion, retracted after a screen capture
content:
bridge.screenshot (r_getscreenshot) is taken before the 2D overlays, so a menu, dialogue or HUD drawn
with IRenderAuxText::Draw2dLabel / aux boxes never appears in it -- in Profile or Release. Together with
RenderAuxGeom.h:5-7 (aux geometry only with ENABLE_PROFILING_CODE / !_RELEASE / the release developer console)
that read as "the Release build draws no UI"; a desktop capture showed the Release main menu drawn. The measure
of what a player sees is the window's pixels: examples/ashvale/ui_screens.py (PrintWindow with PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT,
works under an overlapping window), with the Profile build as the control. The editor viewport screenshot
(bridge.viewport.screenshot) does include the overlays.

title: HOWTO: verify a Release package the way the manual's last step asks
source: Session 2026-09-25: 26/26 on a clean package outside the project tree
content:
Package with Crytek's packager into a folder outside the project tree (a space in the path is a fair
test), copy the complete shader-cache paks into its engine/, and run examples/ashvale/release_playthrough.py <build>:
menus, the intro, walking, every quest dialogue, pause, two saves and both loads checked, the fight with death and
respawn, the ending, a second New Game from scratch, Quit to menu, Quit -- then the process must exit on its own
(GameLauncher exits with code 1 after a normal quit) and Windows must have no Application Error / WER event for
it. Check the layout against the manual's table: only bin/win_x64_release engine binaries (a Release package's
bin/win_x64 holds just the project's own Release Game.dll where the cryproject points), no PDBs shipped. With
vsync on a 180 Hz display the frame time is flat at 5.55 ms -- that is the refresh, not a measurement of cost;
use perf_tour.py (vsync off) for cost. Visual states: ui_screens.py.

title: Off-mesh links on a STOCK CryAISystem: attach the path follower to the segment from the game
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
CMovementActorAdapter::SetActorPath is empty in 5.7.1, so a component NPC's path follower stays on the
FULL path (NavigationComponent.cpp:543) and the first FollowPath never reaches its segment end -- the link block
never Begins ("STALLED at an off-mesh link entry"). Fix without touching the engine: register a movement action
ability per NPC (IMovementSystem::AddActionAbilityCallbacks) --
  addStartMovementBlocksCallback  -> new plan: linksDone = 0
  prePathFollowingUpdateCallback  -> once per (plan, segment): cut segment k out of getPathFunction()'s path the
                                     way MovementPlanner.cpp:366-437 does, CreateAndReturnNewNavPath (meshID set),
                                     SetPathPoints, context.pathFollower.AttachToPath
and ++linksDone in the link block's End. Abilities are dropped whenever the entity is re-registered with the
movement system (START_GAME, RESET, agent-type change), so call it before EVERY NavigateTo (Remove-then-Add is
idempotent: free-function functors compare by pointer). Ordering holds: OnPlanStart runs inside ProduceMoveToPlan
before the first block update, and End->Begin->Update happen in one Plan::Execute loop. Measured with the hook
off/on: editor STALLED 4.70 m / inside 0.22 m; Release STALLED / inside 0.32 m. Code: JumpLink.cpp
EnsureLinkFollowing, CVar claude_link_follow. A custom-navigation block factory must never walk to zero positions
when the link is gone: return CantBeFinished so the planner replans (MovementPlanner.cpp:241).

title: Answer an editor dialog by NAME: bridge.dialog.list / bridge.dialog.click (no focus needed)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
bridge.dialog.list -> every open Qt dialog (and Win32 #32770 box): title, question labels, buttons
{text, standard, enabled, default}. bridge.dialog.click <yes|no|ok|cancel|save|discard|default|text> [title part]
-> clicks it through Qt on the GUI thread with a QUEUED click(), exactly like a mouse click, so
CQuestionDialog::Execute returns that button (accept()/done() would return NoButton/Cancel,
QuestionDialog.cpp:142-150). They have their own queue, drained by the WM_TIMER pump even while the ordinary
queue is held by the command that opened the dialog -- before this, every queued verb timed out behind a modal.
Use instead of bridge.input.key return, which reaches the dialog only if Sandbox has the foreground. Self-test:
queued ai.regenerate_agent_type_all -> "MNM Navigation Rebuilding request" listed with Yes/No, click no closes it,
the command returns. MCP: list_dialogs, click_dialog_button. Closing the editor: bridge.window.close (WM_CLOSE,
the title bar's X) -- never a synthetic Alt+F4.

title: Synthetic input goes where Windows sends it, not where you aimed -- the bridge now checks and refuses
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
SendInput delivers clicks to whatever is under the pointer and keys to the foreground window.
SetForegroundWindow from a background process is refused silently (foreground lock), so with the Windows Firewall
prompt in front the old verbs typed into it and answered ok. Now: bridge.input.click/drag/scroll raise the target
without activation, work out from z-order which top-level window the point reaches, and refuse (naming it) when
it is another program's or one of ours blocked by a modal; the cursor is read back; key/text are sent only when
the foreground window is ours. Options before the coordinates: hwnd=<n> | modal | screen. Physical pixels
(per-monitor v2 for the thread), pixel-centre normalisation. bridge.window.list reports the real foreground
window whoever owns it. Diagnose a stuck unattended run with window.list first. The Firewall prompt is the
user's to answer, never the bridge's.

title: Building and deploying the bridge plugin safely: plugin-only build, hash check, .prev rollback
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
bridge_devloop.py build uses /p:BuildProjectReferences=false -- without it MSBuild also rebuilds CryQt,
EditorCommon, MFCToolsPlugin and Sandbox (an engine build nobody asked for). deploy: save, bridge.window.close,
claude_deploy.bat copies the running DLL to .prev before swapping, SHA-256 compared afterwards. rollback: task
ClaudeBridgeRollback (claude_rollback.bat) kills Sandbox, restores .prev, relaunches -- for a plugin that does
not load, when there is no bridge left. The plugin no longer imports GetIEditorImpl (EditorImpl() =
static_cast<CEditorImpl*>(GetIEditor())), the one export only the local Sandbox.exe had, so it should load in
Crytek's Sandbox.exe (untested: no stock copy on the machine).

title: TRAP: a night as bright as day -- the engine's default.env, legacy exposure, and a constant ambient probe
source: Session 2026-09-26: lighting_probe midnight 0.66 of noon, fixed to ~0.3 with the ground at 0.05
content:
Three causes stack up; fixing one alone does not make night dark (measured).
(1) The engine's %ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Shading/default.env keys Sun intensity at ~244,000 lux at 06, 12 AND 18 h
(203,800 at 21:00). At night the engine only moves the directional light to the moon; its brightness is still the
Sun curve (TimeOfDay.cpp:1111-1115, 1160-1175) -- the sun curve's night part IS the moonlight (manual: 5-300 lux).
(2) r_HDREyeAdaptationMode defaults to 2 (legacy), which ignores EV Min / EV Max / EV Auto compensation; set 1 in
the .cryproject (manual). In mode 1 a raised night EV Min stops auto exposure lifting the night to mid grey.
(3) An Environment Probe (white cubemap) gives the same ambient at every hour. With it on, the scene meters bright,
the EV clamp never engages, and night stayed at 0.92 of noon after (1)+(2). Scale the probe per time of day (the
manual's per-ToD probe sets), e.g. its slot light via IEntity::GetSlotInfo(...).pLight->GetLightProperties().
Also: never flatten ToD curves -- bridge.env.set and old game code wrote one value into EVERY key (the radial fog
multiplier at 2 kept the moon's glow on all night). Author curves per hour (bridge.env.keys).

title: HOWTO: make, key and ship a level's environment presets through the editor's own calls
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Create: Asset Browser New > Environment = CAssetType('Environment')::Create(path.env.cryasset), i.e.
AddNewPreset -> ImportPreset(default.env) -> SavePreset (EnvironmentAssetType.cpp:158-178); bridge.env.new_asset.
Add to the level: ITimeOfDay::LoadPreset(path) (bridge.env.load); default: SetDefaultPreset (bridge.env.default,
= 'Set as Default for this Level'); drop the engine default with RemovePreset. Key: IVariables::SetSplineKeysForVar,
times in HOURS (SAnimTime, 24 per day, EnvironmentPreset.cpp:18) -- bridge.env.keys <var> h:v,h:v [linear]
(use linear where values jump, a smooth spline through 300->120000 overshoots). Save: SavePreset (bridge.env.save).
Save the level: leveldata/timeofday.xml lists the presets; Export to Engine puts them in level.pak; the packager puts
libs/environmentpresets/*.env into the build. Switch at run time: SetCurrentPreset (= Environment:PresetSwitch; no
blending exists). Ashvale's values: author_environment.py; measure with lighting_probe.py.

title: HOWTO: rain that darkens the scene and brings clouds -- a rain preset plus volumetric clouds
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
SetRainParams / the Rain component only wet surfaces (diffuse darkening of wet albedo); they never touch
sun, sky or clouds. For weather: r_VolumetricClouds 1 (.cryproject; experimental but built in) and a second
environment preset for rain -- ~15,000 lux overcast sun (manual PBS page), Global cloudiness 1.0, absorption 0.5,
thickness 3000, grey fog, a higher daytime EV Min so auto exposure does not lift the overcast back to sunny, no sun
rays, no stars -- switched with ITimeOfDay::SetCurrentPreset when rain starts/stops. Cloudiness scales density, not
coverage, so small blue gaps remain. Rain drop particles authored additive + EmissiveLighting 1 glow at night
(night exposure ~5 stops higher): make them lit by the scene (DiffuseLighting 1, EmissiveLighting 0) -- done
through the editor particle database (bridge.db.load_library / export / import / save_library).

title: TRAP: a library particle effect on a component emits along the entity's FORWARD axis, not up
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Legacy library effects ("smoke_and_fire.campfire.small", "fire.torch") are converted to pfx2 at
load, and the conversion writes VelocityDirectional (0,1,0) -- the emitter's +Y -- with offsets keeping their y
(Cry3DEngine/ParticleSystem/ParticleConvert.cpp:734). The old engine aimed Y up when it spawned such an emitter; a
CParticleComponent does not, so +Y is the entity's forward axis. Symptoms: smoke drifting along the ground the way
the entity faces; a velocity-aligned flame (OrientToVelocity) lying on its side, and seen end-on (a wall torch
viewed from in front) not drawn at all. Fix: give the particle component a local rotation of +90 degrees about X
(maps +Y to +Z) -- ParticleUpRotation(effect) in ParticleProp.h, identity for a .pfx (authored in its own axes).
On a moving, pitching holder (a carried torch) recompute it each frame: (pitch * lean)^-1 * RotX(90).

title: TRAP: a default component's saved properties arrive after Initialize (no second Initialize)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
For an entity class registered with a default component, the component is created and Initialize()d
when the entity spawns; CEntity::LoadComponent then finds it by GUID and serializes the level's saved property
values into it WITHOUT initializing again (CryEntitySystem/Entity.cpp:1379). Whatever Initialize built from the
defaults stays. Ashvale: every NightLamp was created as a WallTorch (the default Kind) and then set to Lantern; the
lanterns first built a torch flame, and that particle component, no longer referenced, burned at every hour.
Fix: remember what was built (kind, brightness...) and rebuild when the members differ (checked on Update, plus
EEvent::EditorPropertyChanged in the editor); when a look has no part, remove any such component you find.

title: TRAP: the packager compiles nothing, and RC drops pre-split GameSDK textures
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Crytek's packager copies bin/ as it stands: after a code edit, a package made without first running
`cmake --build solutions/win64 --target Game --config Release` (and Profile) holds the OLD Game.dll -- noticed only
by grepping the DLL for a new CVar name. And RC's texture job refuses a .dds that is already split (.dds.1 ...),
which is how every GameSDK texture ships; a plain .dds compiles fine. Copied GameSDK props/sprites therefore
render without textures in a package -- an additive fire sprite with no texture is a WHITE SQUARE. Put such sets in
Assets/GameSDKTextures.pak (engine Tools/7za.exe a -tzip -mx0, paths relative to Assets). final_packages.package()
now refuses both: stale_sources() (a Code/ file newer than the DLL) and unpackaged_textures() (a loose .dds under
Assets missing from the package's paks), each with a control.

title: HOWTO: a lamp beside a wall without a white disc -- the bulb size, not the brightness
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
At night (r_HDREyeAdaptationMode 1, EV Min clamp) the exposure re-meters on a lamp, so scaling a lamp's
diffuse multiplier moves the whole frame and barely changes the burnt disc on the wall behind it. The engine's
falloff is flat inside the attenuation bulb and (b/d)^2 beyond it (Engine/Shaders/HWScripts/CryFX/shadeLib.cfi:193,
GetPhysicalLightAttenuation), so while the wall (0.35-0.6 m from the light) lies outside the bulb the near/far
contrast is fixed by geometry. Make the bulb reach the wall and scale diffuse by (b_old/b_new)^2 to keep the light
at distance. Measured at equal far light: bulb 0.4 -> 6.0 % of the frame clipped, 0.8 -> 1.6 %, 1.0 -> 0.2 %,
1.4 -> 0 %. Ashvale lamps: bulb 1.0, Brightness 0.25 (torch) / 0.2 (lantern). Sweep in one run with
ash_lamp_scale / ash_lamp_bulb (night_test.py --only sweep); let eye adaptation settle before each frame.

title: HOWTO: place a held prop by where its important part should be on screen, from the mesh's real bounds
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Read where things are on the mesh first: level/cgf_bounds.py reads each mesh chunk's AABB and the
nodes (helpers such as grab_onehanded_01). GameSDK props are not built around their origin: torch.cgf is the torch
as it stands in torch_base.cgf (the bracket alone) -- y 0.29..0.64, z 0.10..1.08, fire at ~(0, 0.47, 0.95).
Then choose the target in camera space (the torch's fire at (-0.41, 0.62, -0.09)), a lean (Quat::CreateRotationV0V1
from the mesh axis to the wanted direction), and origin = target - lean * (scale * point). Get the view's field of
view from something already on screen (the sword guard at 0.68/0.76 of the frame -> ~71 degrees vertical). Scale
the mesh in its component, not the entity, so lights and emitters keep their sizes. Put the prop's light ~0.5 m
ahead of it: at arm's length it burns anything held white once exposure settles on the far ground.

title: HOWTO: paint trees and grass with the Vegetation Editor's own brush, and erase where they do not belong
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
bridge.vegetation.paint <index> x1 y1 x2 y2 calls CVegetationMap::PaintBrush (VegetationMap.cpp:1123), the
Vegetation Editor's brush: it tries area/spacing^2 random spots in the world rectangle ('Density' = metres apart),
keeps those inside the brush's elevation band and under its slope limit (degrees, converted to a tangent), and
skips spots that are not free (CanPlace). It has NO terrain-layer filter (the layer list is exported to surface
types only), so take vegetation off roads the way a person does: the erase brush, bridge.vegetation.clear
<index> rect, along the road every 2 m. Grass also comes out of house footprints -- a floor 0.25 m above the terrain
does not hide a 0.5 m tuft. One brush per mesh; the editor allows the same mesh twice (limit 256 brushes), so
separate 'hill' brushes keep the valley's own untouched and can be cleared and repainted. Grass: GameSDK
field_grass with automerged 1 (level.pak then carries terrain/merged_meshes_sectors/*.dat) and no shadows.
Ashvale scripts: paint_hills.py, paint_grass.py; pictures hills_views.py. Measured cost at 2560x1440:
trees ~0.35 ms, grass ~0.15 ms (median of 17 stops 2.09 -> 2.47-2.61 ms).

title: TRAP: a cheat CVar set in a Release build changes nothing -- an A/B through it reads zero
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
e_Vegetation is registered VF_CHEAT | VF_CHEAT_ALWAYS_CHECK (Cry3DEngine/CVars.cpp:353). In a Release
package, setting it (bridge.cvar_set or console) leaves it as it was, so 'vegetation off' measured the same frame
time as 'on' and read as 'trees cost nothing'. Check a CVar's flags before building an A/B on it, and give the A/B
a positive control (a change that must show). e_MergedMeshes is VF_NULL and does switch merged-mesh grass off.
For a cost that cannot be toggled, compare builds: perf_tour.py before/after, or perf_tour.py --set cvar=value for
non-cheat CVars.

title: TRAP: fullscreen vsync-on frame times on this machine swing between runs of the same build
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
release_playthrough.py samples ash_perf fullscreen 2560x1440 with vsync on. Across consecutive runs of ONE
build its medians were a flat 5.55 ms (vsync at 180 Hz), then 10-14 ms with 34-37 ms worst frames, then 2.8 ms:
an A-B-A (grass on / e_MergedMeshes 0 / grass on) gave 2.8 / 12 / 2.8, the slow state following neither the grass
nor the build. It coincided with an unattended night (display likely asleep) and a GameLauncher left stuck in the
driver (Stop-Process 'stopped', one thread left). Do not read regressions from these numbers; use perf_tour.py
(vsync and fps cap off, 17 stops, repeats within ~0.15 ms).

title: TRAP: a malformed XML (a '--' inside a comment) is silently NOT converted, and the packager ships the previous converted copy
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
claude_ashvale.xml had ' -- ' inside an XML comment. The engine's own loader accepts it (the editor and the source file looked
fine); Python's expat and the Resource Compiler reject it: rc_log.log (Engine/Tools/rc/) says 'XML: Cannot read file ... not well-formed
(invalid token)' and 'Failed to convert file'. The packager does not stop: it packs what is in the RC temp folder, rc_out_PC_pure/
Assets_Assets/..., which still held the converted copy from the last good run (the stock cleanup deletes only rc_out_PC). So for a week every
package carried the 09-24 audio library; ash_vol_amb and every trigger added later did not exist, SetParameterGlobally on an unknown id is a
silent no-op, and volume_test read 93 % / 103 % ('no effect'). Guard (packaging/final_packages.py package()): strict-parse every text asset
under Assets, delete rc_out_PC_pure first, fail on 'Failed to convert' lines in the RC log written during the run. And always look at a pak's
CONTENT, not its existence (zipfile; CryEngine paks need the backslash-header workaround).

title: TRAP: Crytek's packager never packs a .wav -- its copy whitelist has *.ogg only. Encode audio to OGG
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
CryVersionSelector/rc_jobs/game_assets.xml: GameAssetsConversion copies only files in AllExtensions (*.bank;*.bnk;*.cal;*.cfg;...;*.gfx;*.lua;
*.ogg;*.pfx;*.txt;*.usm;*.wem;*.xls...). There is no *.wav, so a WAV under Assets/audio never reaches Audio.pak (SDL_mixer itself plays WAV, and
the editor plays it from the loose file). The first rain/crickets/wind loops were WAVs: silent in every package, while a random gust one-shot
made 'rain audible' look true. Synthesised sounds: assets/make_sounds.py writes WAV then encodes to OGG Vorbis with the ffmpeg already
installed (libvorbis, -q:a 5) and deletes the WAV. final_packages.package() refuses wav/mp3/flac under Assets/audio.

title: TRAP: GameSDK's menu movie draws ONE small image correctly; with two, every pin is whichever loaded last
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
AddImage(path, id, x, y, w, h) twice with different files (gold diamond, blue disc): both pins came out as the later one. Measured by
pixel counts at both pin positions: goal+you -> both blue; you+goal -> both gold; goal only -> gold; the goal twice (ids goal/goal2) -> both gold;
you only -> blue. Not the file name (renamed), not size (different file and shown sizes), not timing (0.6 s apart), not the file route
(img://TEXID:n texture ids: still both blue). The big map image (loaded first) is unaffected. The movie's CryImage.setImage gives every image its
own MovieClipLoader and target clip (read from the bytecode), so the cause is inside Scaleform. Workaround used: bake the second pin into the
big map picture (make_map.py writes one map per goal) and keep the player's pin as the only separate image.

title: HOWTO: show the movie's loader while a level loads, and take it down without a covered or black screen
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
FlashUI hands the elements that are visible to its load-time render thread at ESYSTEM_EVENT_LEVEL_LOAD_START_LOADINGSCREEN, which comes BEFORE
ILevelSystemListener::OnLoadingStart: set the element up (SetFlag eFUI_SHOW_AT_LOADING_TIME, Init, SetVisible, the movie's showLoader) BEFORE the
'map' console command. Two bugs that were only visible in frames: (1) the movie's loader is a full-screen overlay that stays until hideLoader is
called -- call it from the first page's Begin(), not from the level-load-complete callback (the load-time thread is still advancing the movie there);
(2) CFlashUI::LoadtimeRender sets FRT_CLEAR_COLOR on each player it draws and StopRenderThread resets it only for players still in its list; hiding the
element in OnLoadingComplete removed it from the list, so the movie kept clearing the framebuffer and the 3D world stayed black behind every page:
call IFlashPlayer::SetClearFlags(0) yourself. Test the PICTURE (loading_screen_test.py: pale loader frames while loading, menu frames after, no loader
frame once the menu shows), not the log: the log said 'page main built' while the window showed the loader.

title: TRAP: injected arrow keys are numpad keys without KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY; the menu movie ignores controller event Select (7), wants Action
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: TRAP: injected arrow keys are numpad keys without KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY; the menu movie ignores controller event Select (7), wants Action (4)
A test that sends VK_UP/VK_DOWN with keybd_event(vk, MapVirtualKey(vk), 0, 0) reaches DirectInput (Keyboard.cpp, DISCL_FOREGROUND) as scan codes
0x48/0x50 = NUMPAD 8 / 2 (eKI_NP_8 / eKI_NP_2), not eKI_Up / eKI_Down: set KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY (1) for the arrows, Home/End, PgUp/PgDn, Ins/Del.
Enter, Esc, J (non-extended) always worked, which hid it. The menu movie has no key handling (onKeyDown is for text fields); it answers the controller
events a gamepad sends through IUIElement::SendControllerEvent -> cry_onController: Up 0, Down 1, Left 2, Right 3, Action 4 (presses the highlighted
button), Back 5; Start 6 and Select 7 have no case. CAshvaleUI::Navigate maps Enter to eCIE_Action (what GameSDK's own click action sends), arrows
to Up/Down/Left/Right. Sending a controller event also hides the mouse cursor until the mouse moves.

title: HOWTO: ambient layers that follow the clock and the weather on SDL_mixer (rain, crickets, wind, one-shots)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Code/Components/Soundscape.cpp: four 2D looped samples, each with its own global level parameter in the ACE file (ash_vol_amb/rain/night/wind;
ash_vol_oneshot for four one-shots), set with SetParameterGlobally = master volume x level. Levels ease toward targets from AshvaleDay::Hour and
AshvaleWeather::IsRaining (bed 0.30+0.70*day, thinner in rain; wind 0.25+0.55*rain+0.20*night; crickets night*(1-rain); rain 1 while raining). A layer
starts its loop trigger when its target passes 0.01 and stops it (fade_out) once eased away. SDL_mixer detail: Mix_FadeInChannel captures the channel
volume at start and restores it when the fade ends, so push the parameter BEFORE the start trigger. Synthesis: numpy noise band-passed in the frequency
domain, periodic so the loop seam is smooth; crickets = trains of 3 ms pulses at 4.3-5.6 kHz in chirps. Balance by the output meter's 4-decimal mean
(audio_peakmeter.ps1 summary line), one layer at a time with ash_soundscape_solo, and with a control that reads 0.0000 (ash_ambience 0).

title: TRAP: a screen grab (BitBlt) copies whatever is in front of the game; a just-created window is full-desktop size and unpainted
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
PrintWindow cannot capture a window whose thread is busy loading, so loading_screen_test.py uses BitBlt from the screen. That reads whatever is
on top. Twice it copied the Claude app: first because another window was on top, then because a just-created game window is desktop-sized (1704x959)
and unpainted, so the desktop shows through while WindowFromPoint still says 'the game'. window_capture.capture_screen(hwnd, size) now refuses unless
the game owns the centre and four corners AND the client size equals the expected resolution. Delete any frame that shows anything else, and say so.
Never click into or capture a window that is not the game's. THIRD TIME (2026-10-14): the Undercroft playthrough's own shot() copied the screen rectangle with no check; another program's window (a private chat) was in front of the game and two pictures of it were saved in the package folder and looked at. Deleted; every picture-taking script now goes through window_capture.capture_screen (a refused shot is reported and skipped) and test_capture_safety.py fails if any script copies the screen itself. A new script that takes pictures must import capture_screen: never write CopyFromScreen / BitBlt / ImageGrab again.

title: TRAP: in GameSDK's menu movie a button added after a tile grid (AddUserStats) is not drawn -- use a list of buttons
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
The first inventory page used Tiles(...) for Coins/Bread/Health/Sword/Torch and then Button('eat', 'Eat bread'). The tiles appeared; the button
did not (text_bands found no row for it, the Back button was still there). Pages that mix a button column with a grid do not work: the controls
page (tiles + Back) is fine because Back is a different widget. Use a column of buttons, the info lines being buttons that do nothing
(unknown ids are ignored by MenuAction). A real click in ui_menu_test.py is what found it; a log line 'page built' proves nothing about what is drawn.

title: HOWTO: items lying in the world that E picks up, built from engine primitives, saved with the game
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
CPickupComponent (AshvaleObjects.cpp) on an entity class 'Pickup' registered with RegisterEntityClassWithDefaultComponent. The meshes are the engine's
primitive_sphere (flattened: a loaf) and primitive_cylinder (flat: coins) with project .mtl files -- no art. It finds its own static meshes with
GetAllComponents(meshes, false) each rebuild, never holds a pointer (docs/engine-lifetimes.md), and rebuilds when Kind/Amount differ from what it built
(saved properties arrive after Initialize on level load). E: FindUseTarget in Player.cpp adds a Pickup kind (range 2.0 m). Save: GameSerialize writes
'taken' and the game's save/load writes a <Pickup> child per entity; ResetWorld calls ResetForNewGame. Place with build_ashvale.py items (house floor
heights from building_top(), table top 0.71 m from cgf_bounds.py). Picture test: look from 3.5 m, the eye is 1.6 m up.

title: DECISION: the village houses got trim from primitives, not a Designer rebuild -- the Designer's tools are interactive
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
The bridge's designer module only ACTIVATES tools (box, extrude, boolean ...), the manual's Box tool is 'click on the terrain, drag, move the mouse for
the height, click', and the Create Object tab's Designer Box/Cone/Cylinder/Sphere entities expose nothing a script can set. Driving it means synthesising
viewport mouse input against grid snapping. build_ashvale.py trim instead adds half-timbering, windows (a dark pane through the wall, frame, sill, bar,
shutters), door frames and chimneys as brushes outside house()'s walls (named Trim_<house>_..., clear Trim_ removes them), leaving door cuts and the
navmesh interior untouched. house_views.py photographs them.

title: TRAP: a .cgf built by an older script names a material file that does not exist: every surface renders as the engine's flat default
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Symptom: a procedural mesh (FBX -> RC FbxConverter -> .cgf) stands in the game with the right shape and a flat colour on every surface; the editor shows
the red 'Replace Me' texture. The material file is read from the .cgf at LOAD time and stored as a name in chunk 0x1014 (first string: the name, then the
sub-material names). house_kit had been changed from 'materials/ashvale/house' to '.../world' but the nine .cgf files had been built before the change
and never rebuilt, so the engine looked for house.mtl, found nothing and used its default. What did NOT help (each cost a round): texture streaming off,
.dds against .tif paths in the .mtl, checking the DDS header (same DX10 header as Crytek's own loose textures), checking the packaged .mtl (it held the
edit). The measurement that settled it: swap two sub-materials for known-good GameSDK textures; if the picture does not change at all, the .mtl is not
what the mesh uses. Then read the name out of the .cgf (python: cgf_bounds.chunks(), type 0x1014, first printable string). house_kit.build() now does
that after every build (check_cgf_material). Rebuild a mesh whenever its kit's material path changes.

title: TRAP: bridge.object.list returns at most ~500 objects; a delete-by-name step built from it leaves the rest behind
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
house_kit.place() deleted 'every old Trim_ piece' from the names in one bridge.object.list call. The list is capped (about 500 of the level's objects),
so 316 of 435 old trim brushes stayed under the new house meshes and drew flat cream shutters and bars through them. Delete in batches of 60 and REPEAT
until the list holds none, then count the names in layers/main.lyr after saving (grep -c 'Name="Trim_'). Also: object.delete inside a long python batch
swallows errors; wrap each delete in try/except and re-list.

title: HOWTO: timber houses as one procedural mesh each: real relief, see-through windows, textures from numpy height fields
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
texture_lab.py makes each surface as a height field + albedo + gloss (numpy, periodic) and writes the normal map from the height field; RC compiles the TIFFs
(rc.ini presets by name: *_diff, *_ddna). house_kit.py builds each house in its own frame (x,y relative to the centre, z absolute) with styles: framed
(beams 7 cm proud, braces as slanted prisms in the clear panels), clapboard (boards every 20 cm, 3.5 cm proud, dark core behind), log (28 cm logs, ends
crossing at the corners, a bark texture whose height field is each log's round profile), board and batten, stone, stone_timber. Depth that matters is
real geometry; the normal maps add the fine relief. Parallax occlusion would need a Heightmap slot AND shader permutations the project's cache lacks; not
used. Windows: a real opening, a thin glass pane (Illum, Opacity 0.08, Specular 0.04, Shininess 40: gloss 255 mirrors the sky as a pale panel), frame,
sill, mullion cross, open shutters; the room is visible through it. New sub-materials are only ever APPENDED to world.mtl (a .cgf stores the index).
UVs in metres divided by a per-material tile size keep the texture scale on every part.

title: TRAP: resample + overlap-add 'pitch shifting' smears synthetic speech into a horror; resample alone
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: TRAP: resample + overlap-add 'pitch shifting' smears synthetic speech into a horror; resample alone, and let the synthesiser's rate fix the length
make_voices.py first changed each character's pitch by resampling and then time-stretching back with an overlap-add that does not align windows to the pitch
period. Measured with the raw System.Speech output as the control (voice_quality.py: the share of loud 40 ms frames whose normalised autocorrelation peak
exceeds 0.5): Garrick 0.65 -> 0.24, Oswin 0.65 -> 0.14, Edmund 0.74 -> 0.32, and Garrick's pitch tracker jumped an octave. The user, who can hear it, said
the NPC sounded like an eldritch horror. Fix: a plain np.interp resample (pitch and formants move together, 4-14 %), the SAPI rate chosen to cancel the
length change (rate += 10*ln(1/factor)/ln 3), and a guard in make_voices.py that stops if any line keeps < 80 % of the raw voiced share (the worst is 95 %).
The synthesiser itself (Windows David/Zira/Mark, one generation) is poor; that is a limit no processing removes. An offline neural voice (e.g. Piper) is
the real fix and is a download that needs the user's permission. Never ship audio processing nobody has listened to without a measured control.

title: HOWTO: an archer enemy on the existing bandit brain: a Shoot state and render-only arrows flown by hand
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
CNpcComponent property BowRange (0 = club). CBanditBrain: in Chase, if the player is inside BowRange, seen within 0.6 s, the cooldown is spent and a ray
(ent_static|ent_terrain) from the eye to the chest is clear, go to Shoot: stop, face the player, draw 1.1 s, FireArrow, 3.4 s cooldown; closer than
1.9 m -> the club's Attack; line or range lost -> Chase. An arrow is an entity (default class, ENTITY_FLAG_NO_SAVE|CLIENT_ONLY) with a render-only
CStaticMeshComponent (objects/ashvale/weapons/Arrow.cgf, tip along +Y, Quat::CreateRotationVDir(dir)), moved each frame at 24 m/s: a ray stops it in
walls and terrain (it stays 3 s), and the player is a 1.8 m bar of radius 0.5 sampled along the segment; a hit calls CHealthComponent::Damage so the
player's onFilterDamage (parry) and damage scale (guard 0.3) apply for free. The player's velocity (smoothed) gives half a flight time of lead. The brain
destructor removes its arrows. No draw animation exists in the clip set: he stands and looses. Test with the player where he can be seen: a first test
stood 18 m BEHIND the ruin's wall and nobody ever saw anyone. The scripted editor playtest had to learn the archers' names or they shot it dead.

title: LESSON: a check may fail a build only after its expected value was measured on a known-good and a known-bad state
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Cutting the suite (the user: 'so many tests, so long, some repeat') merged duplicates (package_test's boot/shader/sound checks, volume_test inside the soundscape
test, map_variants inside the menu test), and made tests that only PRINTED numbers assert them. One assertion added in the rush, 'the planner cannot reach
the inside without Martha's links', failed the first full run: the probe had read 1 and 1 in every run of the session, never 1 and 0. The expected value
had never been measured as a control needs. Removed; the crossing itself is what discriminates. final_packages.py runs a group only when a file matching its
patterns changed since its last green run (suite_stamp.json), --all is the release gate (30 min), run it detached (run_detached.py) because a background
shell command dies at 10 minutes. A group can show stale after a clean run because the editor re-saves the level when the suite closes it.

title: FACT: grass at half the size and 4.4 times the count costs about 0.2 ms
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
paint_grass.py brushes are found by mesh and retuned with bridge.vegetation.params (density = spacing in metres, size, sizevar, elevation, slope): size 1.0 -> 0.5
(tall grass 0.42), spacing 2.2/2.2/3.5/3.0 m -> 0.95/0.95/2.0/1.4 m: 34,735 tufts -> about 151,000 over x 405..620, y 150..470, then erased from the

title: TRAP: RC ignores /preset= and auto-selects an ALBEDO preset (BC3) for any TIFF with an alpha channel; the preset must be inside the TIFF
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
A height map is a *_displ TIFF with the height in the ALPHA channel (RGB empty), compiled by rc.ini's [Displacement] preset (BC4, swizzle aaa1). rc.exe stone_displ.tif /refresh
printed "Auto-selecting preset 'AlbedoWithGenericAlpha'" and wrote a BC3 file (dxgi 77, 349,676 bytes) whatever the file name, and `/preset=Displacement` on the command line changed nothing
(from git-bash it is also mangled into a path: run RC from python). Crytek's own *_displ.dds are dxgi 80 (BC4). What works is what the CryTIF Photoshop plugin does: the preset travels
inside the TIFF as TIFF tag 34377 (a Photoshop image-resource block): b'8BIM' + 0x0404 + 2 zero bytes + big-endian length + an IPTC record 1c 02 28 <len16> '/preset=Displacement'
(read from Crytek's own environmentprobe_cm.tif). texture_lab.crytif_preset() writes it; RC then reports the preset and writes BC4 (174,916 bytes for 512 px, like Crytek's).

title: HOWTO: height maps on Illum materials: the flags, the slot, the params, and what spec shows what
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Illum.ext: %OFFSET_BUMP_MAPPING 0x20000, %PARALLAX_OCCLUSION_MAPPING 0x8000000, %SILHOUETTE_PARALLAX_OCCLUSION_MAPPING 0x10000 (CORRECTED 2026-10-07: in the engine's common flag table 0x80000000 is SILHOUETTE_PARALLAX_OCCLUSION_MAPPING; %ALLOW_SILHOUETTE_POM is NOT a flag of Illum and is ignored). A material with BUMP_MAP + SSS (GenMask 80000081) becomes 88020081 with StringGenMask %ALLOW_SILHOUETTE_POM%BUMP_MAP%OFFSET_BUMP_MAPPING%PARALLAX_OCCLUSION_MAPPING%SUBSURFACE_SCATTERING,
a <Texture Map="Heightmap" File="..._displ.tif"/> next to Diffuse and Bumpmap, and PublicParams PomDisplacement (0.02-0.03: a fraction of the tile), HeightBias 0.5, SelfShadowStrength.
Enable BOTH flags as the manual says: the engine uses OBM on Low/Medium spec (the project ships sys_spec 2) and POM on High/Very High (sys_spec 3). Measured at a grazing angle on a stone
wall: relief at Medium, deeper mortar at High. New permutations are NOT in a shader cache built before: the shader tour showed 22 misses (see the shader-cache chunk). CORRECTION 2026-10-07: for Illum only the StringGenMask counts (the hex GenMask, 88020081 or any other, is not read), and the flag names that matter are those in shader_info('Illum'); see fact-material-genmask-is-ignored-stringgenmask-is-all-the-engine-reads.

title: TRAP: any change to a material's flags or texture slots makes the shipped shader cache stale; the shader tour is the only thing that says so
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Release does not compile shaders, and a missing permutation does not stop the game: the first POM materials rendered (some fallback) while the tour counted 22 GCM misses
(shader_tour_check failed, nothing else did). `shader_cache_refresh.py` (Profile package + shader_tour --rsc recording, ShaderCacheGen seeded with the stock cache, PakShaders, audit) fixed it
(0 misses on every leg). Then 16 more appeared after the camp's single-material brush files were retextured with the same flags: the cache was recorded BEFORE that change, and the next
recording added 17 entries (the %_RT_DISSOLVE variants for the same POM permutations on those brushes). Regenerate the cache after every such change and re-run the tour; matching
MtlFlags to the working materials' was tried and was not the cause. The recording needs the NEW assets in the Profile package, so do the asset work first, the cache last.

title: TRAP: a normal map made from a height field with strength x texture size too high looks fine by day and sparkles under a close lamp
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
normal_from_height scales the height gradient by (texture size) x strength, so on a 512 px grain-noise height field even strength 0.6 is steep. By day the relief looked good; at night
under the door lantern the plaster, thatch and beams showed black-and-white stipple. Controlled test on one frame (mean absolute difference from the 4 neighbours, 130x160 px of wall): 22.0 at
the first strength, 16.8 after a gentle first retune, 7.5 with the plaster's normals flat, 10.1 at 0.04 (smoothed 4 passes) where the plaster reads as soft rough plaster. The lamps cast no
shadows (read NightLamp.cpp first), so it was not shadow acne. Keep the depth in geometry (beams, boards, logs) and let the normal map add grain only; judge it at NIGHT, close to a lamp.

title: FACT: Piper runs offline on Windows from a zip, renders a game line in about 0.6 s, and is a clear step up from Windows' David and Zira
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
piper_windows_amd64.zip (github.com/rhasspy/piper release 2023.11.14-2, 22,477,236 bytes, MIT; archived Oct 2025) unpacks to piper/piper.exe with its own espeak-ng data and onnxruntime.
Voice = an .onnx (63,201,294 bytes for the 'medium' en_GB voices) + .onnx.json from huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices (en_GB-alan-medium, northern_english_male-medium, alba-medium).
piper.exe --model X.onnx --output_file out.wav --length_scale 1.1 --sentence_silence 0.15 reads the text from stdin (UTF-8): 5.6 s of speech in 0.19 s of inference (real-time factor 0.035).
34 dialogue lines render in 19 s. make_voices.py uses it by default; the voice_quality.py guard still checks that the shaping (a small plain resample) does not hurt it. Licences differ per voice
(CC BY, CC BY-SA, two model cards say nothing): check before any release.

title: TOOLING: the MCP server's editor-free tools: lint_assets, jobs, shoot_game, and the texture -> material -> mesh pipeline
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
These work with Sandbox closed: they act on the project folder and on Crytek's own tools (rc.exe, the packager). Order of work for a new asset:
make_texture(surface, name, size, folder) -> write_material('materials/<f>/<name>', [{name, texture, height_depth?}]) -> build_mesh({name, material_file, materials, parts}) ->
lint_assets -> place it in the level -> package (job) -> shoot_game to LOOK at it. Each pipeline call lints what it just wrote and returns the real state (the .dds formats read from the files, the
material name read BACK from the compiled .cgf, the compiled mesh's measured size), not "ok".
lint_assets(scope?) checks in about a second: L001 .cgf names a missing material (renders flat grey), L002 a USED sub-material index past the .mtl's list, L003 missing texture, L004 XML that does not parse
(a '--' in a comment: RC skips it and the packager ships a STALE copy), L005 parallax/offset-bump flags vs the Heightmap slot, L006 texture format (_displ must be BC4, _ddna BC5) / power of two, L007 .wav/.mp3
under audio/ (never packaged), L008 an audio event naming a missing sample, L010 level layers naming a missing mesh/material, L011 shader cache older than a material or texture. A clean result lists what it examined.
Jobs (start_job / job_status / read_job_log / stop_job / list_jobs; kinds: tests package shader_cache shoot ci voices music textures selftest) run DETACHED, so a 30-minute test gate or a 15-minute shader-cache
refresh survives a tool timeout. Jobs that package or launch the game close the editor (graceful save-and-close) and REFUSE while Sandbox.exe runs unless allow_editor_close=true: say so to the user first.
Test it all with test_asset_lint.py, test_pipeline.py and test_mcp_tools.py (31 checks through the real stdio protocol).

title: TRAP: a .cgf's sub-material NAMES and its declared COUNT say nothing about whether it renders right; only the material ids the subsets...
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: TRAP: a .cgf's sub-material NAMES and its declared COUNT say nothing about whether it renders right; only the material ids the subsets USE matter
A mesh stores the sub-material INDEX of each subset. First check written: compare the names in chunk 0x1014 with the .mtl's SubMaterials. Result: 174 stock GameSDK meshes flagged (wooden_fence.cgf says
'proxy_wood', its .mtl says 'proxy'; they render fine). Second check: the declared sub-material count (int at byte 128 of the 0x802 chunk) against the .mtl's list: 82 flagged (deco_rock_forest_a declares 19,
the .mtl defines 14; the mesh uses id 5). What matters is the highest material id the mesh actually uses: chunk 0x1017 (MeshSubsets): a 16-byte header (flags, count) then 36 bytes per subset
(first index, index count, first vertex, vertex count, MATERIAL ID, radius, centre); an id >= the .mtl's list length draws with the default material. A bare material name in a .cgf (no folder) resolves next to
the .cgf. The linter's self-test keeps a real stock rock mesh as its clean twin so this false alarm cannot return. The rule that stays true: append sub-materials to a .mtl, never reorder (the mesh stores the index).

title: TRAP: a subprocess started by an MCP stdio server inherits the PROTOCOL's stdin pipe and can hang; give every child stdin=DEVNULL
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
jobs.plan() runs final_packages.py --dry-run: 0.6 s from a shell, 8 lines. Called by a tool inside server.py it timed out at 120 s (the child, not the server). The server's stdin is the protocol pipe the client
writes requests into; a child that inherits it (Windows inheritable handles) blocked, and one that reads it (ffmpeg reads keyboard commands from stdin unless -nostdin) could even eat protocol bytes.
Every child the server starts must pass stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL: jobs.run() does it (but NOT together with input=, which supplies its own pipe: subprocess.run raises), `ffmpeg -nostdin`, and in-process library calls
that spawn (mesh_fbx.build_cgf's rc.exe). Detached job wrappers get stdin=DEVNULL too. Also: FastMCP returns an untyped `-> list` as ONE TEXT BLOCK PER ITEM (a one-item list looks like a scalar), a `-> dict`
as structuredContent; pictures are returned as mcp.server.fastmcp.Image(data=bytes, format='jpeg') items in a list.

title: HOWTO: run a job longer than a tool call or the 10-minute shell limit, and read its VERDICT from its output, not its exit code
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
A job is `python -u bridge/jobs.py _run <id>` started with creationflags DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP and stdin/stdout/stderr redirected (it outlives the MCP server, the shell and the Claude app). The wrapper starts
the whitelisted script, waits, and writes exit_code/ended into job_runs/<id>.json; job_runs/<id>.log is the script's own output. A wrapper that dies without writing an exit code shows as state 'lost'.
final_packages.py exits 0 even when tests FAIL: the verdict is its 'SUMMARY name=ok|FAILED n|rcN' line, which job_status parses. stop_job kills the wrapper's tree AND GameLauncher.exe (the game is started detached from the
tree) and removes the watchdog lock (claude_deploy_in_progress) that a killed script cannot remove. Only one job that needs the machine to itself (package, tests, shader_cache, shoot, ci) runs at a time; voices, music and textures
can overlap. Arguments are validated against fixed lists (test groups, texture surfaces, music tracks), numbers, a build name, and shot lines of a fixed grammar; there is no way to pass a command line.

title: LESSON: the linter's first self-test found 0 of 10 planted failures: its own walk skipped the folder the fixture lived in
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
asset_lint.walk() skipped any path containing '.cache' (meant for the pak index). The self-test built its fixture under .cache/lint_fixture, so every planted failure sat in a skipped folder and the
linter reported a perfect, empty result, identical to the real project's. Only the planted failures, each paired with a clean twin of the same thing, exposed it. Also from the same test: a clean twin built from a real mesh failed
because the fixture's .mtl had one sub-material for a mesh that uses several (a fixture bug, found by the same control). Every check the linter claims must have a planted failure that it finds and a clean twin that it leaves alone;
a clean report counts only with the number of files and references it examined next to it.

title: TOOLING: snapshot_project / list_snapshots / diff_snapshot / restore_files: the project's only backup, and how to use it
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
The project folder was NOT a git repository and nothing else backed it up (the only 'Backup' scheduled tasks are Windows' own; Documents is not under OneDrive). snapshot_project stores the project (minus
regenerable output: bin, solutions, .vs, logbackups, rc_out_PC_pure, ci_runs|job_runs|texture_src, *.bak, *.log), the notes folder, the ClaudeBridge plugin source (untracked in the engine repo),
Claude's memory, and engine/local_changes.patch (`git diff` of the engine repo: the edits to Crytek's own files exist nowhere else). Content-addressed: each distinct file once, as blobs/<aa>/<sha256>, plus a manifest per snapshot written
LAST and atomically (an interrupted run leaves no half snapshot). First snapshot: 8,353 files, 1.64 GB, 15 s; verify 26 s; a second one after editing two files: 1.0 s, 2 files stored. Take one BEFORE any bulk delete/overwrite/rebuild.
restore_files goes to a side folder by default; overwrite=true restores in place after taking a `before_restore` snapshot, so the restore is itself undoable; every file is hash-checked as it is written and a corrupt stored copy aborts.
Nothing deletes a snapshot (the module has no such function; a test asserts it). Limits: the store is on the SAME disk (mistakes, not a failed drive: copy `restore <id> **` to another drive); the fast path trusts size + mtime
(--full re-hashes); a file the editor holds locked is listed as skipped. Store: CRYENGINE Projects/_snapshots (CRYENGINE_SNAPSHOT_DIR overrides).

title: TRAP: two launches of the SAME unchanged package do not draw the same picture; an in-run repeat cannot see it
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: TRAP: two launches of the SAME unchanged package do not draw the same picture; an in-run repeat cannot see it; the visual check learns a per-cell tolerance from launches
visual_check captures 20 fixed views (14 by day, 6 at 22:00), each twice in a row, and compares with an accepted baseline. First run on an unchanged game: 15 of 20 views 'changed'. What was measured, in order:
(1) the merged-mesh GRASS layout is random per launch: the nine house views (standing in grass) differed from the baseline by a mean 24-28 grey levels with the same mean brightness, no camera shift (best integer and sub-pixel
shift 0), while the green/road views (no grass in front) differed 0.3-5.6; fix: e_MergedMeshes 0. (2) the engine default r_AntialiasingMode is 2 (SMAA 1TX: temporal filtering with projection jitter): use 1; r_VolumetricClouds 0; mask the HUD (the health bar
differs with the camp archers' arrows). With these, a frame is a function of the pose within a launch (in-run repeat difference 0.03-0.4) and the day house view matched its baseline to 0.13. Every setting is applied with a VERIFIED line
(`?cvar value` in view_shots: bridge.cvar_set reads the value back, a mismatch aborts) because a silent miss once changed every view. (3) STILL, other launches differed by 1.9, 3.7, 11.1 mean levels (trees, the near ground; not brightness, not
sharpness, not camera offset): cause not found. (4) the night sky's top-right cell drifted 9-12 levels from the baseline in two later launches. So the check LEARNS a per-cell tolerance: visual_check(calibrate=true) adds a launch of the unchanged
package (refused if the package is not the baseline's) and a cell is flagged only if it exceeds 3x its in-run noise, 8 levels more, AND 1.5x the learned launch-to-launch maximum + 2. After calibrating on 5 launches: 3 fresh launches read 0 changed,
and the fault (ash_brightness 0.7, picture 30 % darker) was flagged in 14 of 14 day views and 6 of 6 night views. Lamps-out could NOT be the fault: the unchanged night views differ between launches at lamp-lit cells by 12-21 levels, about what lamps-out
changes (10-25): the lamps' animated light style (m_style, speed 0.85-1.15 per lamp) is the suspect, unverified. The check sees visible regressions (a flat grey house, a missing texture, lighting that moved), NOT small tuning, and is weakest at night.
verified_note: Listed by the 2026-10-23 audit (K-14): the text holds a claim that was read or planned but never run or seen working (look for 'untested', 'NOT SEEN', 'not yet'); treat it as a hypothesis until shown.

title: FACT: r_AntialiasingMode defaults to 2 (SMAA with temporal filtering)
source: Session 2026-10-07: reading the engine source for the visual check
content:
Full title: FACT: r_AntialiasingMode defaults to 2 (SMAA with temporal filtering); the packaged game's bridge.cvar_set reads the value back; e_DefaultMaterial is a cheat variable and does nothing in Release
Renderer.h: eAT_NOAA 0, eAT_SMAA_1X 1, eAT_SMAA_1TX 2 (= eAT_DEFAULT_AA), eAT_TSAA 3. Modes 2 and 3 jitter the projection and keep history, so a frame depends on the frame count: use 1 for reproducible pictures (manual:
post-processing/anti-aliasing: 'r_AntialiasingMode 1 enables SMAA without any temporal filtering'). The packaged game's command server answers bridge.cvar_get <name> and bridge.cvar_set <name> <value> with the engine's value AFTER the call
(GamePlugin.cpp): that is how a setting is verified (view_shots line `?r_AntialiasingMode 1`, also accepted by shoot_game). e_DefaultMaterial ('use gray illumination as default') is DefineConstIntCVar ... VF_CHEAT: it cannot reproduce the
'every house renders grey' failure in a Release build; ash_brightness (0.6-1.4, ordinary, applied through Global_User_Brightness) is a usable global fault. e_MergedMeshes 0 switches the grass off in Release (a non-cheat variable).

title: TRAP: a file you have just written under Assets can be locked for a moment by the open editor (its asset scanner)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: TRAP: a file you have just written under Assets can be locked for a moment by the open editor (its asset scanner): reading it raised PermissionError
With Sandbox open (freshly reopened by the watchdog), make_texture failed reading selftest_stone_ddna.dds right after rc.exe wrote it: PermissionError: [Errno 13]. Two suites that had passed minutes earlier failed on it (the same
tools passed with the editor open on other runs: the scanner is busy for a while after a reopen). asset_lint.read_bytes / parse_xml now retry for ~5 s (12 tries, 0.4 s) before giving up; a file that stays locked is still an error. Regression test:
test_asset_lint locks a file with msvcrt.locking for 1 s and expects the read to succeed after it, and a permanent lock to fail fast. Any new tool that reads what it or RC just wrote should use read_bytes.

title: TOOLING: wait_for_editor: block until the bridge answers and the level is loaded; what the wait looked like
source: Session 2026-10-07: health.wait_for_editor; measured 255 s after a visual job
content:
The jobs that close the editor (package, tests, shader_cache, shoot, visual) leave the watchdog (every 5 minutes, scheduled task ClaudeBridgeWatchdog) to reopen it: measured 255 s (37 polls) after a visual job, plus ~15 s for the level to load
(the watchdog logs 'reopened levels/ashvale/ashvale.level: ok' and 're-applied 1 of 1 environment settings'). wait_for_editor(timeout 1-900, require_level) polls health._bridge_state (unreachable -> answers -> no-level -> level), returns at once when
it is already up, and on a timeout says why: Sandbox.exe running or not, the watchdog's last log line, the lock (held by a job: it stands down), jobs running. The task result 1 of the watchdog means 'I restarted the editor'. Do not write the polling
loop by hand (it was written three times in one evening before this existed).

title: LESSON: str.replace(old, new) with an old that is not in the file does nothing and says nothing: assert the anchor
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: LESSON: str.replace(old, new) with an old that is not in the file does nothing and says nothing: assert the anchor, and write backslash escapes with the Edit tool
I patched view_shots.py with a Python heredoc: s.replace(anchor, handler + anchor). The anchor's comment text differed by a word, nothing changed, py_compile passed, and the harness ran 24 s later into an IndexError. Rule: `assert anchor in s` (or
count == 1) before every replace in a patch script, and check the result is in the file. Separately the Bash tool turns a backslash-n inside a nested heredoc into a real newline (an unterminated bytes literal in test_mcp_tools.py): write such lines with the
Edit tool, or build the bytes without an escape (bytes([10])).

title: TOOLING: health_check, compare_shots, audio_report, place_object/delete_objects, tool_guide: what each is for and what it will not claim
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
health_check: one report (editor + bridge + level, both packages' freshness, shader cache, watchdog, locks, jobs, disk), ok/info/warn/fail with a fix. A packaged build older than the project's code, its Game.dll or
its loose assets means shoot_game and every test show YESTERDAY's game; shoot_game now says so itself (WARNING, or a Note when only the level file was re-saved).
compare_shots(a, b, control): '<job id>:<label>' pictures from shoot_game. Without the control (a second capture of the UNCHANGED view) it refuses to call anything changed. With it, 4x4 cells are judged each
against its own repeat difference, and it says where. Returns a difference picture: red = changed beyond noise, blue = within noise. audio_report(path, voice, loop): peak/RMS/LUFS/true peak/clipping/silences/loop seam/
spectrum/stereo correlation (+ voiced share and f0 with voice=true); I cannot hear: measurements and flags only. place_object / delete_objects: the open editor; every number and path is checked first, the object is read back
after; delete is a dry run until `really` equals the match count; the level is never saved by them. tool_guide(family) maps all 64 tools, built from the registered tools; the server also sends INSTRUCTIONS with the
handshake (work loop + the three rules), so a new session sees them without asking. test_mcp_tools fails on a tool no family claims.

title: TRAP: two captures of the SAME view differ (night sky 19 levels, grass 4): a whole-picture difference needs a noise floor per region
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: TRAP: two captures of the SAME view differ (night sky 19 levels, grass 4): a whole-picture difference needs a noise floor per region, or a real change reads as noise
Experiment (view_shots, 22:00, the chapel from 12 m): n1 and n2 are the same view twice; n3 is after `ash_lamps 0`. Whole picture: lamps-out mean abs diff 12.1, the repeat 8.9: 1.4x the noise floor, verdict
'no measurable change' -- WRONG. By region (mean abs diff, lamps-out vs repeat): sky strip 19.3 vs 19.2 (pure noise: stars, clouds, eye adaptation), door area 23.9 vs 4.5 (5.4x), the whole ground 8.3 vs 4.3 (diluted to 1.9x),
grass 3.3 vs 3.6 (noise). So the verdict is per cell: a cell changed if its a-vs-b is at least 3x its OWN repeat difference and 3 levels more; noisy cells (repeat > 8) are named because a change there would be hidden. Result:
3 of 16 cells changed, around the lit door (30.2 vs 7.8, 21.6 vs 4.7, 9.4 vs 3.0); the repeat against itself: none. A difference picture that paints every difference red made the sky look as changed as the door:
red is now only the cells beyond noise. Also run: a picture against ITSELF must read exactly 0 (the instrument's control, always computed). Take the control capture in the same job as the pair.

title: HOWTO: put objects in the level and take them out without surprises (the editor's calls, wrapped with checks and a read-back)
source: Session 2026-10-06 late night: level/objects.py, test_objects.py (24 live checks)
content:
Placing a brush: general.new_object('Brush', mesh, name, x, y, z) then object.set_scale / set_rotation(n, rx, ry, rz) / set_custom_material -- exactly what build_ashvale.Scene does; place_object adds: the mesh
exists (loose under Assets/ or Engine/, or in any pak: asset_lint.Names), the material exists, the name is a plain identifier and free (overwrite=true replaces), numbers are finite and inside +-4200 m / scale 0.01..500, and
afterwards `bridge.object.list <name>` is read back: position within 5 cm, scale within 0.01, yaw within 0.5 deg, a material present. Records: name, type, pos, rotDeg, scale, material, hidden, frozen, children. The list is a
case-insensitive SUBSTRING filter (Chapel_ also returns Trim_Chapel_...), capped near 500 (this level: 307 objects), so delete counts prefixes itself and refuses a match of ~490 or more (build_ashvale.py clear <prefix> repeats
until none remain). Delete is a dry run until `really` equals the match count (a wrong count deletes nothing). Neither saves: general.save_level() is the caller's; the jobs that close the editor save first, which is why the
level files are newer than the package after almost every job.

title: FACT: for Illum (and 7 other shaders) the engine computes the shader flags ONLY from a material's StringGenMask; the hex GenMask is not...
source: Session 2026-10-07: Cry3DEngine/MatMan.cpp:451-478, RenderDll/Common/Renderer.cpp:1316, ShaderCore.cpp mfCreateCommonGlobalFlags, the 8 shaders' .ext files; catalogs/shader_catalog.py (test_shader_catalog.py, 20 checks)
content:
Full title: FACT: for Illum (and 7 other shaders) the engine computes the shader flags ONLY from a material's StringGenMask; the hex GenMask is not read and a flag name the shader does not have is silently ignored
Cry3DEngine/MatMan.cpp:467: if the material node has a StringGenMask attribute the mask comes from CRenderer::EF_GetShaderGlobalMaskGenFromString, which for a shader that uses the COMMON flag table (Eye, Glass, Hair, HumanSkin, Illum, MultiLayeredMaterials, Terrain, Vegetation: their .ext files say UsesCommonGlobalFlags) returns mfGetShaderGlobalMaskGenFromString(StringGenMask) and ignores the numeric GenMask altogether; an EMPTY StringGenMask="" means mask 0 whatever GenMask says. Only a material with no StringGenMask attribute (or a shader outside the table) uses the hex GenMask (remapped from the legacy local masks). The common table is built at startup: every flag name in those eight .ext files gets bit n in sorted order (with legacy fixes) and the engine writes it to <user>/shaders/cache/globals.txt (51 names; the catalog's parse of the .ext files equals it name for name). The masks therefore DIFFER from the .ext's local ones: OFFSET_BUMP_MAPPING is 0x20000 in Illum.ext but 0x2000000 in the table; PARALLAX_OCCLUSION_MAPPING 0x8000000 in both; SUBSURFACE_SCATTERING is 0x4000000000000. Consequences measured on this project: 41 of its materials carry %ALLOW_SILHOUETTE_POM and 14 %BUMP_MAP: neither is a flag of Illum, both are IGNORED (the GameSDK's materials have 175 and 76: leftovers); write_material's hex GenMask (88020081, 80000081) is cosmetic: only its StringGenMask counts, so do not 'fix' one without the other and do not change a StringGenMask without regenerating the shader cache (it changes the permutation). The linter used the HEX for L005 (parallax without a height map): it now judges from StringGenMask like the engine, and L012 (info, one finding per shader+flag) reports names the engine ignores. A flag that is a real name of ANOTHER shader (e.g. WRINKLE_BLENDING on Illum) is also ignored: shader_info(flags=[...]) says 'wrong shader'.

title: TOOLING: shader_info / shader_search (flags, public parameters, texture slots of every shader, from engine/shaders.pak)
source: Session 2026-10-07 (ENGINE_LEARNING_PLAN B3 and A10): catalogs/shader_catalog.py, asset_catalog.py, asset_lint.py (L005 corrected, L012 new); test_shader_catalog.py (20), test_asset_catalog.py (14)
content:
Full title: TOOLING: shader_info / shader_search (flags, public parameters, texture slots of every shader, from engine/shaders.pak) and asset_info / asset_report (the engine's own .cryasset metadata: dependencies, users, triangle counts)
shader_info(shader, flags=[...]) and shader_search(text) read the engine's shader scripts straight from engine/shaders.pak: Shaders/<Name>.ext (the generation FLAGS: name, label, description, local mask, dependencies, the #ifdef they sit under), Shaders/HWScripts/CryFX/<Name>.cfx and the .cfi files it includes (looked up case-insensitively, as the engine does) for the public PARAMETERS (type, UI name, default, UIMin/UIMax/UIStep, and the `#if %FLAG` each needs: Illum.PomDisplacement float 0.025, 0..0.05, needs %PARALLAX_OCCLUSION_MAPPING; HeightBias needs OBM or POM or silhouette POM) and the TEXTURE SLOTS (register tN and the TM_ it binds), plus the 14 slot rows read from the source (Heightmap = _displ = TM_Height; Bumpmap = _ddn = TM_Normals; Diffuse = _diff; Specular = _spec; Smoothness = _ddna; Emittance = _em; ...). 65 shaders; Illum has 16 flags, 55 parameters (48 public), 24 material-slot textures. Control: the flag names parsed from the 8 common-table shaders equal the engine's own globals.txt exactly. flags=[...] resolves a set the way the engine does (honoured / ignored / wrong shader, the sorted StringGenMask, the local and the common-table hex): see the fact chunk on StringGenMask.
asset_info(path) / asset_report('summary'|'coverage'|'heaviest'|'unused') read the `.cryasset` file the engine's asset system writes next to an asset (XML: type, GUID, Files = a mesh's LOD chain, Details = what it measured: triangleCount, vertexCount, materialCount, textureCount, width/height/mipCount, and Dependencies with usage counts; './x.mtl' is relative to the asset's folder; a dependency on x.tif is one on x.dds). This project: 477 assets recorded (228 textures, 141 meshes, 72 materials, 13 characters ...), 769 dependencies; the heaviest mesh is loghouse_grey.cgf (32,546 triangles, 2 files). COVERAGE IS PARTIAL: 405 .cgf, 129 .dds and 28 .mtl of this project's files have no metadata (the engine has not recorded them). asset.generate_and_repair_all_metadata() through the bridge returned at once and, after 55 s, created NOTHING (477 files before and after; snapshot diff 0 added): not working from the bridge with the editor in the background; untested with the editor in the foreground, so it is not shown to be a no-op in general. Reading metadata does not need the editor.
