content:
Full title: TOOLING: search_manual / read_manual_page / manual_toc, cvar_search / cvar_info / spec_group, and the cvar_probe job: the documents and the console variables one call away
search_manual(query) searches Crytek's offline manual (1,725 pages, BM25 over chunks, one hit per page, an exact title first); read_manual_page(page id or title, heading=, offset=) reads one page in parts (an ambiguous title answers with the ids), also listing the CVar-like and class-like names the page mentions; manual_toc lists the 42 sections or a section's pages. The project rule 'read the manual first' is now one call, not a script.
cvar_search / cvar_info answer for 2,484 console variables and 278 commands: type, DEFAULT as written in the source (can be a symbol such as eAT_DEFAULT_AA), the value in the editor dump (differs from the default for ~5 % of numeric variables: a spec group, a config or a script changed it), flags (cheat, const, readonly, dev-only, dumptodisk, restart/reload), full help, file:line of the registration (97.7 % found by a source scan, the rest by name mention, 12 runtime-built q_Shader*/sys_spec_quality names not), the sys_spec groups that set it per level, and WHERE it can be changed (editor / Profile build / Release build, and the Release routes). spec_group reads Config/CVarGroups/sys_spec_*.cfg out of engine.pak (15 groups; effective values = [default] overlaid by [level]; level 1 low, 2 medium, 3 high, 4 very high, 5-8 console profiles).
Built from the engine's OWN tools: `DumpCommandsVars` (names, types, current values, help) and `audit_cvars cheat const readonly dev dedi` (the flags the first leaves out) run in the open editor through the bridge (python catalogs/cvar_catalog.py --capture --build), then joined with a scan of the source for defaults and locations. The job cvar_probe (start_job kind 'cvar_probe', allow_editor_close=true, ~25 s) sets variables in the PACKAGED game and reports accepted / refused / absent, scoring the catalog's prediction: engine_data/release_probe.json holds the last record and test_cvar_catalog compares the catalog with it without launching anything. Capture again after an engine or project change that adds variables.

title: FACT (measured): which console variables a RELEASE game accepts, and by which route
source: Session 2026-10-07: CrySystem/XConsole.cpp (OnBeforeVarChange, LoadConfigVar), SystemInit.cpp (dev mode, config loading), System.cpp, ProjectDefines.h, ConsoleRegistration.h; MEASURED with the cvar_probe job on Ashvale_final_release
content:
Full title: FACT (measured): which console variables a RELEASE game accepts, and by which route (code and user/game.cfg yes; command line and user.cfg no)
Reading CXConsole::OnBeforeVarChange / LoadConfigVar: a variable flagged cheat, const, read-only or deprecated is refused unless it is NOT deprecated AND (the system is in dev mode OR this is the editor). Dev mode (SystemInit.cpp): ON in every non-_RELEASE build outside the editor (unless -nodevmode), OFF in a _RELEASE build. So a Profile package accepts cheat/const variables, a Release package does not; the editor accepts all but deprecated. CVar GROUPS (sys_spec) are privileged and can set cheat/const ones. *_DEV_ONLY registration macros register NOTHING in a _RELEASE build (ConsoleRegistration.h), and variables registered under a feature macro that exists only outside Release (ENABLE_PROFILING_CODE, ENABLE_STATOSCOPE: defined in ProjectDefines.h from _RELEASE) are absent too. The first reading missed the second kind; the measurement found e_StatoscopeFilenameUseDatagroups (no dev-only flag, absent in Release).
HOW a value reaches a Release game (cvar_probe on Ashvale_final_release, 2026-10-07): (1) ICVar::Set from game code or the bridge: a plain variable was ACCEPTED, cheat/const variables REFUSED (20 of 20 each, in a 60-variable sample), dev-only/feature-macro variables ABSENT (15 of 15). (2) %USER%/game.cfg (loaded with no whitelist sink): the plain variable took effect, the cheat one did not. (3) The command line `+var value` and user.cfg (both loaded through the CVAR WHITELIST sink; the whitelist is compile-time and EMPTY unless the build adds ProjectCVarWhitelist.h entries): a plain variable was IGNORED, so was a cheat one. Exception, unexplained: +r_Width and +r_Height DID take effect (the launcher's window size); the mechanism was not traced. So: to change a plain variable in the shipped game use game code (the bridge, a console command from game code) or user/game.cfg, never +var or user.cfg; to use a cheat/const one the build must be Profile (or the editor). The catalog's prediction scored 55 of 55 on this sample (plus 5 variables whose existence the evaluator cannot decide, measured: 4 present, 1 absent). Not measured: the whole 2,484; the Profile build (predicted all accepted but deprecated).
Also from the CMake files: Configure.cmake sets _PROFILE for the Release configuration when OPTION_PROFILE is ON (the `bin/win_x64` binaries) and _RELEASE when it is OFF (the `win_x64_release` binaries our Release package uses); OPTION_DEVELOPER_CONSOLE_IN_RELEASE defaults ON (BuildEngine.cmake), so a Release build keeps the console object.

title: FACT: the engine dumps every console variable itself (`DumpCommandsVars`), but that dump hides the cheat/const/dev-only flags
source: Session 2026-10-07: CXConsole::GetFlagsString, DumpCommandsVarsTxt, AuditCVars (CrySystem/XConsole.cpp); cvar_catalog.capture()
content:
Full title: FACT: the engine dumps every console variable itself (`DumpCommandsVars`), but that dump hides the cheat/const/dev-only flags: `audit_cvars cheat const readonly dev dedi` shows them
In the editor (a non-Release build) `DumpCommandsVars [prefix]` writes consolecommandsandvars.txt into the editor's WORKING folder (the project root) and a ConsoleHTMLHelp/ folder of the same data as HTML: each variable with name, type, current value and help; each command with its help. Its flag column comes from GetFlagsString, which prints only READONLY, DEPRECATED, DUMPTODISK, REQUIRE_LEVEL_RELOAD, REQUIRE_APP_RESTART and RESTRICTEDMODE: e_DefaultMaterial is cheat and const and shows no flags at all. `audit_cvars cheat const readonly dev dedi` (ALLOW_AUDIT_CVARS, non-Release) logs every variable with [VF_CHEAT] [VF_CONST_CVAR] [VF_READONLY] [VF_DEV_ONLY] [VF_DEDI_ONLY]; the bridge returns the log lines (each twice: console and log mirror). Numbers for this editor: 2,484 variables (625 cheat, 371 const, 105 dev-only, 17 dedicated-only, 9 read-only) and 278 commands (the audit does not list commands: their flags come from the source). `DumpVars` writes consolevars.txt without the cheat ones. cvar_catalog.capture() runs both, moves the file out of the project root and deletes ConsoleHTMLHelp.

title: FACT (measured): C# works in this editor but its reload crashed Sandbox 2 of 2 on changed source, edits were not picked up
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: FACT (measured): C# works in this editor but its reload crashed Sandbox 2 of 2 on changed source, edits were not picked up, and the API lacks AI/UQS/FlowGraph/Schematyc env/movie: keep C++; the C++ compile is 8 s, the editor restart 13 s to ~4 min
Question (user, 2026-10-07): C++ or C# for the engine? Evidence. SHIPS: bin/common/Mono (455 MB; mono, mcs, csc, msbuild), CryMonoBridge.dll, CryEngine.Core.dll (C# API: 150 documented types in CryEngine.Core.xml: Entity/EntityComponent, physicalize params, audio, Animations incl. Mannequin, Input, Camera/View, ParticleEmitter, ConsoleVariable/Command attributes, DebugDraw, BehaviorTreeNode, FileSystem, LevelSystem, Log, Timer; CryEngine.Core.UI.dll 37 types) and the editor plugin EditorCSharp; NOT in the C# API: AI navigation, vision/audition/faction maps, UQS, UDR, Flow Graph, Schematyc environment registration (two attributes only), movie system, DRS, game tokens, terrain. Ashvale's 17,500 lines of C++ use the first group. HOW IT WORKS: in the editor every .cs under Assets is compiled into <project>/bin/CRYENGINE.CSharp.dll (CCompiledMonoLibrary); a packaged game loads that dll from bin. A new .cs was compiled and its [ConsoleCommand] ran in the editor with no action (and after a restart). EditorCSharp reloads managed plugins only while Sandbox IS IN FOCUS (CSharpEditorPlugin::UpdatePluginsAndSolution): an edited .cs was NOT picked up in 3 trials of 240/240/90 s nor 151 s after bridge.window.focus. `mono_reload` (console command, CMonoRuntime::ReloadPluginDomain) with UNCHANGED source survived (2 of 2, the bridge answers after its 20 s cap); with CHANGED source it CRASHED Sandbox 2 of 2 (EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION reading 0x10 in CrySystem.dll from managed frames; the second on a fresh editor with one edit): cause not found. The Release package has no Mono; what the packager does for C# is untested. C++ LOOP: touching Health.cpp and building Game (Profile) took 8.4 s (compile + a link refused because Sandbox holds Game.dll, LNK1168); restart-to-the-loaded-level was observed at 13 s (twice, in a row), 47 s, 118 s, 255 s and ~240 s (twice): deliberate (bridge_devloop.py deploy) or by the watchdog alike, so one iteration is 20 s to ~4 min, nearly all of it the restart; what decides the restart time was NOT found (cold caches is a guess). RETRACTED twice the same day: first '2-4 minutes per iteration' (from watchdog restarts), then 'about half a minute, because a deliberate restart took 13 s' (a later deliberate restart took ~4 min). RECOMMENDATION: keep C++ for Ashvale (C# could save at most the restart, and its reload crashed twice); wrap claude_game_build.bat as a job; never leave scratch objects in the level across a restart (a graceful close SAVES the level); revisit C# only if a person alt-tabbing into the editor gets a crash-free reload (csharp_experiment.py setup) or the crash is root-caused.
verified_note: The Release package's handling of C# is untested. Listed by the 2026-10-23 audit (K-14): the text holds a claim that was read or planned but never run or seen working (look for 'untested', 'NOT SEEN', 'not yet'); treat it as a hypothesis until shown.

title: TRAP: a Python patch sent through the Bash tool turns \n inside its replacement strings into REAL newlines and breaks the patched file
source: Session 2026-10-07: three patches in one day (jobs.py, cvar_catalog.py, cvar_probe.py)
content:
Full title: TRAP: a Python patch sent through the Bash tool turns \n inside its replacement strings into REAL newlines and breaks the patched file: use the Edit tool, and compile-check after any patch
Three times in one session a `python - <<'EOF'` script that replaced source text with a replacement containing "\n" (a newline escape inside a string literal of the file being patched) wrote an actual line break there: the patched file then failed with 'SyntaxError: unterminated string literal'. Asserting the ANCHOR of each replacement (as before) does not catch this; the damage is in the replacement. Rules: (1) anything whose text contains a backslash goes through the Edit tool (or Write for a new file), never a heredoc; (2) after any patch run `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open(FILE, encoding='utf-8').read())"` (or the module's test) before moving on; (3) in code that must hold a newline use chr(10) or a named constant (NL) so a later patch cannot flip it.

title: TOOLING: every editor object's properties (a River's Width, a Road's TileLength, a Rope's mass, a Decal's sort priority) are readable...
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, F1): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.object.xml, bridge.object.set), level/object_props.py, test_object_props.py (15 checks), test_mcp_tools.py
content:
Full title: TOOLING: every editor object's properties (a River's Width, a Road's TileLength, a Rope's mass, a Decal's sort priority) are readable and settable through the engine's own serializer; splines too
The Sandbox Python API has no property setter for these objects (object.* has get_position/set_scale/set_custom_material but no 'width'). The editor itself saves an object with CBaseObject::Serialize into a CObjectArchive (EDITOR_COMMON_API, Objects/ObjectLoader.h): that XML is what a layer file holds. Two plugin verbs expose it: `bridge.object.xml <name>` and `bridge.object.set <name> <base64 'key=value' lines>` (a key is an attribute of the Object node, `Child/key` an attribute of a child node, `@Tag=<xml>` replaces a child node; the object is saved to XML, edited and loaded back into the SAME object inside one undo step 'Claude: set properties'). MCP tools: object_types (36 kinds, the engine's own list), create_object(type, name, position), object_properties(name, set={...}) and spline_points(name, points). object_properties reports `not_applied` for every key the object does not end up holding (a misspelt key is reported, tested) and refuses Type, Id, Layer, LayerGUID.

title: A road or river is invisible or flat: spline points are LOCAL XML children, and a spline at exactly the terrain height hides in it
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, F1): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.object.xml, bridge.object.set), level/object_props.py, test_object_props.py (15 checks), test_mcp_tools.py
content: SPLINES (Road, River, SplineDistributor, WaterWave): CSplineObject is NOT exported from Sandbox.exe, so a plugin cannot call InsertPoint; the points are an XML child <Points><Point Pos Back Forw Angle Width IsDefaultWidth/></Points> with Pos LOCAL to the object (point minus the object's Pos). source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, G7): Editor/Scripts/viewmodes.py, environmentmodes.py, DebugViews/debug_views.py; screens/debug_views.py, test_debug_views.py (14 checks); RenderDll RendererCVars.cpp:1096
content:
Full title: TOOLING: the engine's own debug views (normals, albedo, smoothness, wireframe, texel density, LOD index, without fog/GI/shadows ...) as a catalog, and pictures of them from the EDITOR viewport (no game run)
The editor ships the definitions of its debug views as Python (Editor/Scripts/viewmodes.py: which variable to set to which value; environmentmodes.py: 'without X' toggles; DebugViews/debug_views.py: cycling views with auxiliary variables). debug_views() lists 68 of them parsed from those scripts and checked against the console-variable catalog; debug_view([ids]) sets the variables, takes a picture of the Perspective pane through bridge_shoot.py (the editor window capture cropped to the pane when the window is 1018x428), puts every variable back and READS IT BACK (`restored`). Measured: the same view twice differs by 0.5 grey levels (mean absolute difference); r_DebugGBuffer 1 (normals) by 65.8, wireframe by 89.0, texel density 512 by 79.8, albedo by 44.4. The world-normal view of the village is a clean pink/blue/violet map (checked by eye).
r_DebugGBuffer values (from the variable's OWN help, which agrees with viewmodes.py): 1 Normals, 2 Smoothness, 3 Reflectance, 4 Albedo, 5 Lighting model, 6 Translucency, 7 Sun self-shadowing, 8 Subsurface scattering, 9 Specular validation overlay. The engine's DebugViews/debug_views.py is STALE: it calls 2 'Gloss', 3 'Specular', 4 'Diffuse', 5 'Translucency', 6 'Baked AO', 7 'Subsurface Scattering', 8 'Specular Validation Overlay' (7 wrong labels, and no 9); it also names variables this editor does not have (e_GI, r_Beams). `e_DefaultMaterial 1` (viewmodes.py 'default_material') was accepted and read back but did NOT change the editor picture (4.8 against a control's 2.7: no visible effect).
The editor takes cheat and const variables (dev mode); a Release GAME would refuse almost all of these (cvar_info says). Camera: eye/target in world metres; the default is where the editor camera is. The pictures are small (488x284): enough for colour-coded modes, not for fine detail.

title: TOOLING: the particle system's 54 features, 11 modifier kinds and 13 legacy names from the engine's registry
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, G4): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.particles.features, bridge.particles.roundtrip), catalogs/particle_catalog.py, test_particle_catalog.py (27 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group particles); Cry3DEngine/ParticleSystem (ParticleEffect.cpp, ParticleFeature.h, Features/Modifiers.cpp)
content:
Full title: TOOLING: the particle system's 54 features, 11 modifier kinds and 13 legacy names from the engine's registry, and what the engine's own loader KEEPS of a .pfx (unknown names are dropped silently)
A .pfx is JSON (version 13 in this engine): Components -> Features -> parameters, each parameter {value, modifiers}. The engine registers 54 feature kinds (group + name: Render: Sprites, Spawn: Rate, Field: Size ...); the plugin verb `bridge.particles.features <file>` adds each to a fresh effect's component and saves the EFFECT, so every feature appears under the name a file holds it by, with every parameter at its default (the 3 Child features are lists of component names). The file name of a feature is its group and name joined (RenderSprites, SpawnRate); the one exception the engine writes is Appearance: Opacity, saved as FieldOpacity (a CRY_PFX2_LEGACY_FEATURE registered after the canonical name). Thirteen legacy names are registered (13 in the source, each probed through the engine by `bridge.particles.roundtrip`): FieldOpacity, AppearanceBlending, AppearanceSoftIntersect and the GPU names are accepted and mean the current feature; LifeImmortal becomes Life: Time; SecondGenOnSpawn/OnDeath/OnCollide and KillOnParentDeath keep nothing as a bare feature (the engine converts them with their parameters in an old file).
ONE SYMPTOM PER CHUNK (split 2026-10-23, every word kept): tooling-particle-modifiers-per-parameter-kind = Particle parameter modifiers: which kind a float, size or colour param; tooling-particle-effect-keys-ignored-what-the-loader-drops = Particle effect keys or features have no effect: the engine's loader D; tooling-particle-feature-roles-life-spawn-render = Particle component needs a Life, a Spawn and a Render feature: the rol

title: Particle parameter modifiers: which kind a float, size or colour parameter keeps (Random on a colour is dropped)
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, G4): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.particles.features, bridge.particles.roundtrip), catalogs/particle_catalog.py, test_particle_catalog.py (27 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group particles); Cry3DEngine/ParticleSystem (ParticleEffect.cpp, ParticleFeature.h, Features/Modifiers.cpp)
content: Modifiers (a parameter's modifiers list; "Modifiers" for a colour parameter): Curve, DoubleCurve, Random, Noise, Wave, Linear, ConfigSpec, Attribute, Inherit on float/size parameters; ColorRandom, ColorCurve, Attribute, Inherit on colour parameters. Which kind a parameter keeps is told by the engine (round trips), not guessed: Random on a colour is dropped, ColorRandom on a float is dropped.

title: Particle effect keys or features have no effect: the engine's loader DROPS unknown names silently (pfx_check, roundtrip)
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, G4): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.particles.features, bridge.particles.roundtrip), catalogs/particle_catalog.py, test_particle_catalog.py (27 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group particles); Cry3DEngine/ParticleSystem (ParticleEffect.cpp, ParticleFeature.h, Features/Modifiers.cpp)
content: `bridge.particles.roundtrip <in.pfx> | <out>` loads a file with the engine's own effect loader (LoadJsonBuffer into pfx2::IParticleEffect) and saves what the engine now HOLDS. Measured: a feature, modifier or key the engine does not know is dropped WITHOUT a message; a renamed parameter falls back to its default (the old AlphaScale {x,y} became {start,end}: the file's values are lost); a second Life/Motion/Render feature in a component is switched off and saved as "Enabled": false; missing parameters are filled with defaults; loading compiles the effect (a separate compile step changed nothing); the engine's own output is a fixed point (loads back to the same text); effects of version below 13 are CONVERTED while loading (renamed or restructured keys are moved, so 'dropped' entries of an old file may not be lost). `pfx_check` runs this and diffs the two documents (components matched by NAME because the engine writes a child after its parent; features and modifiers matched by name and occurrence). Findings: the project's own dust.pfx, leaves.pfx and rain.pfx (version 13) carry 28 keys this engine ignores (SpawnCount/Mode, LocationOmni/SpawnOffset and Mode, AlphaScale x/y); 12 of the GameSDK sample project's 16 effects are version 8 or 11 files. The only effect of the 19 that loads with no difference is the sample's omni/snow.pfx.

title: Particle component needs a Life, a Spawn and a Render feature: the roles and which feature fills an empty one
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, G4): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.particles.features, bridge.particles.roundtrip), catalogs/particle_catalog.py, test_particle_catalog.py (27 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group particles); Cry3DEngine/ParticleSystem (ParticleEffect.cpp, ParticleFeature.h, Features/Modifiers.cpp)
content: Roles (ParticleFeature.h EFeatureType): Life 1, Spawn 2, Render 4, Effect 8, Size 16, Motion 32, Child 64; a component may enable only one Life, Motion and Render feature, and a role no feature fills is filled by the feature whose default_for_type is that role (Life: Time, Spawn: Rate, Field: Size, Motion: Physics, Child: OnBirth).

title: TOOLING: write a particle effect from the engine's catalog, load it through the engine, and LOOK at it in the editor viewport (no game...
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, G4): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.entity.add_component, mirrors CUndoAddComponent::AddComponentInternal in Sandbox/EditorQt/Objects/EntityObjectUndo.h), assets/pfx_author.py, test_pfx_author.py (18 checks)
content:
Full title: TOOLING: write a particle effect from the engine's catalog, load it through the engine, and LOOK at it in the editor viewport (no game run); the traps found on the way
pfx_write composes a .pfx from a plain description (components with features and parameter overrides), every value starting at the engine's default; a feature or parameter the engine does not have is refused up front with the nearest names (the engine would drop it silently), then the file is loaded through the engine's loader and the result is reported (engine_check). It never replaces a file unless overwrite=True; the editor's CryPak CACHES a loose asset, so an overwritten effect keeps showing the old one until the editor restarts: use a new name.
pfx_preview: a scratch EntityWithComponent gets a Particle Emitter component by the new verb `bridge.entity.add_component <entity> <component GUID, class name or label>` (the Inspector's Add Component: CreateComponentByInterfaceID with the class description from the Schematyc environment, flagged UserAdded; no undo step), its FilePath is set through component_properties (read, change, write the COMPLETE set), the picture is taken after a wait, and the entity is deleted (object count checked: a graceful editor close SAVES leftovers). The control pictures are taken with the empty emitter already there (the editor draws an icon and a selection box for the entity).
What did NOT work (so nobody tries again): the legacy `ParticleEffect` entity class takes no component through the object XML (`@Components=` is read back unchanged) and bridge.component.properties finds no component on it; `particle.show_effect` + `particle.assign_to_selection` ran without an error and assigned nothing; and show_effect opens the Particle Editor as a FLOATING WINDOW (see the window trap).
Measured with the engine's own textures: Appearance: Material with textures/sprites/glow/glow_a.dds plus Appearance: Opacity BlendMode Additive draws glowing orange embers (0.35 m sprites, 80 per second, 3 s life, cone 25 degrees); textures/sprites/fire/ember.dds, glow_a.dds and smoke_a.dds with the default Alpha blend draw DARK dots (their RGB is dark: they are made for additive use); no texture draws tinted blobs; snow02.dds draws bright. Appearance: Lighting with Emissive 50 and Diffuse 0 changed nothing visible. Measure a preview with the BRIGHT PIXELS in the middle box of the pane against the same count between two control pictures: whole-picture 'changed pixels' counts the swaying grass (1,500 to 11,000 pixels between two pictures of one view), and the noise between two controls itself varied from 0.2 to 9.5 grey levels between runs.

title: TOOLING: a WaterVolume (any shape object) takes its points from world positions and RE-CENTRES itself
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, F2): object_props.set_shape / is_shape, test_object_props.py (17 checks); Sandbox/EditorQt/Objects/ShapeObject.cpp (CalcBBox), WaterShapeObject; sample gamedata.pak Materials/water/watervolumes/water_forest_a.mtl
content:
Full title: TOOLING: a WaterVolume (any shape object) takes its points from world positions and RE-CENTRES itself; a missing water material renders as a dark fallback, and the GameSDK water materials are not in this project
Shape objects (WaterVolume, Shape, VisArea, Portal, OccluderArea, AIShape, AIPath, NavigationArea) hold <Points><Point Pos="x,y,z"/></Points> LOCAL to the object, no Bezier handles (splines such as Road and River do have them). After the points are loaded the editor RE-CENTRES the object (CShapeObject::CalcBBox moves the object's position to the minimum corner of the points and shifts the points): measured, an object at 487,392,38 given points of +-10 m ended at Pos 477,382,38 with local points 0,0 / 20,0 / 20,20 / 0,20 - the WORLD points are unchanged. `spline_points` (the MCP tool, object_props.set_shape) takes world positions for shapes and answers with the new Pos and the world points the object now holds; a shape needs 3 or more points.
A WaterVolume's `Material` attribute is a plain string that nothing validates: 'Materials/does/not/exist', the GameSDK sample's water_forest_a/b, water_cave, water_rapids, oil, and the engine's EngineAssets/Materials/Water/ocean_default (a "Water" shader OCEAN material, not a volume material) all rendered the SAME dark fallback (mean colour 48,61,61), so those sample materials are not available in this project (they live in the sample's gamedata.pak; the engine's `EngineAssets` Materials/Water has only ocean_default and WaterOceanBottom). A material file written into the project with Shader="Watervolume" (GenMask 8000004B, no textures) DID resolve and drew differently (mean 55,71,74, with 17-29 levels of variation): the sample's water_forest_a.mtl is only the shader, one Environment cube map and PublicParams (NormalsScale 0.17, Tilling 2, FoamAmount 0.5, EnvCubeReflMul 4, WaterFlowSpeed 0.25 ...); the water normal map comes from the engine (EngineAssets/Textures/oceanwaves_ddn.dds). shader_info('WaterVolume') lists its flags (SSREFL, PBR, FLOW, FOAM ...) and public parameters.
What the EDITOR viewport shows is a dark, flat slate-grey surface with a cyan outline; whether the GAME draws it as water (reflections, flow, foam) was not tested: the game was not run. The editor has terrain.set_ocean_height / terrain.remove_ocean for the global ocean (e_WaterOcean is a cheat+const variable; sys_spec_water sets the quality).

title: TOOLING: build_mesh authors LODs the engine's way ($lodN_ nodes under the base mesh), proven in the editor; and the engine refuses ANY...
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, B5): assets/pipeline.py (build_mesh), mesh_fbx.py (Mesh.parent, Mesh.detail, lod_copy), asset_lint.py (cgf_lods, L013, L014), house_kit.py (--lods), test_pipeline.py (29), test_lods_live.py (6); Cry3DEngine/ObjMan.cpp:456; manual LODs and Blender LoDs pages; Tools/CryVersionSelector/rc_jobs/game_assets.xml (SplitLoDs=1)
content:
Full title: TOOLING: build_mesh authors LODs the engine's way ($lodN_ nodes under the base mesh), proven in the editor; and the engine refuses ANY mesh path containing '_lod'
The manual (LODs; Creating and Handling LoDs in Blender): the base mesh has no prefix; each further LOD is a separate object parented to it and named $lod1, $lod2 ... (first 5 characters count, `$lod1_<name>` is the usual form); up to 6 LODs; each step should save about half the triangles (RC warns above a 66% cut); the same materials; 'Merge all Nodes' must be off; RC embeds them in the .cgf and Crytek's asset jobs split them out (rc_jobs/game_assets.xml and engine_assets.xml carry SplitLoDs="1": the shipped GameSDK paks hold foo_lod1.cgf next to foo.cgf).
build_mesh(spec): `lods` 1-3 and a part's `detail` N (left out of LOD N and every coarser one); a cylinder halves its sides per level (not below 6). mesh_fbx.write_fbx connects a child model to its parent model, so the FBX has the hierarchy RC's importer wants. The compiled file is read back (asset_lint.cgf_lods: node chunks 0x100B with their parent ids, mesh chunks 0x1000 whose index count / 3 is the triangle count: Barn.cgf 5022/3 = 1674 = the engine's own .cryasset figure): each wanted LOD must exist, hang under the base node and have fewer triangles; a step that keeps over 67% is a warning. Measured (test_pipeline): 180 -> 76 -> 32 triangles. PROVEN in the engine (test_lods_live.py): a scratch brush of a mesh with a LOD, e_LodMin 1 (use LOD 1 even close up) -> the picture of the brush changes (7.1 grey levels in its box against noise 0.9, the studs are gone); a mesh without a LOD does not (0.4).
THE TRAP: CObjManager::LoadStatObj (ObjMan.cpp:456) refuses any file name containing '_lod' (case-insensitive substring of the WHOLE path): "Failed to load cgf: ..., '_lod' meshes can be loaded only internally as part of multi-lod CGF loading", and the editor draws its default sphere. A scratch folder called objects/zz_lod/ and one called _mcp_lodtest both did it; the engine's own message appears in the bridge.object.create reply's `log`. build_mesh refuses such a name or folder; lint L014 flags a layer that places one.
Also: L013 (info) lists meshes of 1,000+ triangles with no LOD: the nine generated houses (1,674-2,958 triangles). `house_kit.py build --lods=2 [--out=<folder>]` tags the fine parts (framing/boards, plinth, window frames, doors, corner posts: gone from LOD 2; mullions, shutters, flower boxes, ridge/hip rolls, rafter tails: gone from LOD 1; chimney and porch: gone from LOD 2): Reeve 1225 -> 655 -> 179 polygons, Barn 839 -> 425 -> 77. LOD 2 cuts about 70% from LOD 1 (above the manual's 66% warning): add a middle level if popping shows.

title: FINDING: what the GameSDK sample, GalaxSys and Homebound do for water, what the manual says, and what the editor viewport shows
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, F2, the user: check the open-source projects and the documentation): level_study.py on the GameSDK woodland level; grep of the GalaxSys and Homebound projects; manual WaterVolume Shader, River Tool How-To, Water Volume; shader_info('WaterVolume')
content:
GameSDK sample, woodland level: 5 WaterVolume objects, every one with materials/water/watervolumes/woodland_canyon_river (Shader Watervolume, GenMask 80000013 = realtime reflection + flow + specular map + the hidden tessellation bit; Diffuse 1,1,1; a gloss map and an Environment cube map; NormalsScale 0.17, Tilling 0.1, DetailNormalsScale 0.5, EnvCubeReflMul 16, EnvCubeScale 16, VertexWaveScale 0.125, WaterFlowSpeed 0.5), at z 34.5 to 53.6, VolumeDepth 1 to 10, FogDensity 0.01 to 0.5, 4 to 17 points each; the terrain has a river-bed surface type and road-like decals along it; the level has NO ocean (WaterLevel -1000000). GalaxSys and Homebound have no water volumes: only the level's ocean material reference (%ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Materials/Water/Ocean_default in leveldata/Environment.xml).
Manual: the WaterVolume shader is only for water volume objects (rivers, lakes, pools, oceans through volumes); parameters: Normals scale, Detail normals scale/tiling (the detail normals are generated by code), Tiling, Env reflection amount, Env projection scale, Flow speed / flow map (flow maps go in the Detail slot), Foam amount/tiling/soft intersection (foam texture EngineAssets/Shading/WaterFoam.tif), Vertex wave scale, Soft intersection factor, Rain ripples tiling, Realtime reflection amount; shader gen: Realtime Reflection, Water flow, Water flow map, Sun specular, Debug flow map, Foam. River Tool How-To: prepare the terrain first (the banks above the river's start, the bed painted differently), give the river a material that uses the Watervolume shader, 'By default the river color will probably be too bright; try lowering the color'.
Done here: the five river materials and their textures were copied into the project with import_gamesdk_asset.py (the sample's paks are not mounted by the project). A scratch volume with them resolves (mean 57,73,76 against the 48,62,62 of a missing material) but all five look the same in the editor. Water Volume properties that change the editor look: FogColor, FogColorMultiplier, FogDensity, VolumeDepth (a teal FogColor 0.05,0.25,0.3 turns the dark slab teal; density 0.05 or depth 1 lightens it); Caustics and FogShadowing change nothing visible. How the GAME draws it (reflections, flow, foam) is untested.

title: TOOLING: sequence_check loads a hand-written Track View sequence through the engine's own loader and says what it kept
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 2, A2): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.sequence.roundtrip), checks/sequence_check.py, test_sequence_check.py (13); CryMovie/Movie.cpp:345 (LoadSequence replaces a same-named sequence)
content:
The intro of Ashvale is raw XML (libs/ashvale/sequences/ashvale_intro.xml) because Track View's Python API has 87 functions but NO add-key function (sequences, nodes, tracks, snapping, playback, tangents). `bridge.sequence.roundtrip <in.xml> | <out>` loads the file with CMovieSystem::LoadSequence and saves it with IAnimSequence::Serialize. TRAP it avoids: LoadSequence deletes any previous sequence with the SAME NAME (Movie.cpp:353), so the copy is loaded under a throw-away name, GUID and id (zz_claude_seq_N, a fixed fake GUID, id 900000+N), removed again with RemoveSequence, and the saved XML gets the original name/GUID/id back so the documents compare.
Measured: the game's intro is accepted whole (1 node 'AshvaleCineCam', Position and Rotation tracks, 15 keys each, 13 s = 78000 ticks at 6000 ticks per second; the engine writes 512 where the file says 512.0000 and GUID halves without leading zeros: compared as numbers and as hex). Positive controls: an unknown attribute on a Key is DROPPED; a node of an unknown Type is dropped with all its tracks (nodes: 0); an unknown track paramType becomes a track named 'Unknown Entity Parameter' (and its place in the list changes); a key value that is not a number is changed; a key at 150 s in a 13 s sequence is KEPT unchanged (it never plays: sequence_check warns). Same method as pfx_check: the engine's loader silently ignores what it does not know, so compare what you wrote with what it holds.

title: FINDING: the GameSDK human has a bone-driven facial rig (16 FCL bones) and a 60-expression library with visemes
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 2, C4): files only: skeleton_player_generic.chr/.fxl, sdk_player/*.skin, sdk_player.cdf, the sample's animations.pak; CryHeaders.h chunk types
content:
Full title: FINDING: the GameSDK human has a bone-driven facial rig (16 FCL bones) and a 60-expression library with visemes; the villagers wear the non-animated head
skeleton_player_generic.chr carries 16 facial bones named FCL_* (Brow_L/R, C_BASE, C_Jaw_M, L/R Cheek_M, L/R EyeLid, L/R Nose, L/R Lip_Hi_M, Lip_Low_M, Lip_Cor_M ...) plus eye_left_bone / eye_right_bone. The expression library skeleton_player_generic.fxl (Facial Editor format) lists 60 expressions (an ARPAbet-like phoneme set AE AA AH DH SH TH ZH ..., Visime_AA/CH/EE/FF/II/MP/NN/OO, Blink, EXP_Angry, EXP_Angry_FACE, EXP_Happy_FACE, EXP_Happy_MOUTH), 108 bone effectors (each FCL bone moves on one axis: _tX _tY _tZ _rX _rY _rZ) and the groups Root, Phonemes, Visimes, Expressions, Expressions_Cut, BoneControls, _garbage. No head skin has a compiled morph-target chunk (0x2002 absent): the face is BONE-driven. No facial sequence (.fsq) ships in the sample (only the .fxl in animations.pak).
sdk_player.cdf attaches head_a.skin (10 bones with vertex weights, by the BonesBoxes chunk count) as 'head'; head_anim.skin has 27: it is the head to animate. So lip-sync is POSSIBLE in principle: use head_anim.skin, author facial sequences (visemes keyed over the audio length of each Piper line, which the project knows), play them with the facial system; the Facial Editor and Track View's Facial Sequence track are the engine's tools. Unproven: nothing was played (the game was not run).

title: TOOLING: audio_triggers cross-checks the ACE libraries against CryAudio::StringToId("...") in the game code
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 2, H1): catalogs/ace_catalog.py, test_ace_catalog.py (10); Code/Components/AshvaleGame.h/.cpp
content:
Full title: TOOLING: audio_triggers cross-checks the ACE libraries against CryAudio::StringToId("...") in the game code (a typo is silence, not an error)
The game names audio controls with CryAudio::StringToId("name") (a hash): an undefined or misspelt name makes no error, only silence. ace_catalog reads every Assets/audio/<middleware>/ace/*.xml (Triggers/Trigger with Event children: sample, start/stop, volume, loop_count, fades, panning; Parameters/Parameter; Switch, Environment) and every StringToId literal in Code/**/*.cpp,h (comments skipped). The real project (2026-10-07): 4 libraries (claude_ashvale 19 triggers, claude_lamp 5, claude_music 10, claude_voice 68), 102 triggers, 15 parameters; 46 names in the code, ALL defined; no missing sample; no duplicates; 68 triggers are built at run time from a literal prefix in the code (AshvaleGame.cpp: "ash_vox_" + dialogue id + "_" + index; the _stop twins too); 3 triggers nothing refers to (ash_test_2d, ash_test_2d_stop, claude_villager_line). The check complements lint L008 (event -> sample file).

title: FINDING: boids (ambient birds, fish, bugs) are GameSDK game code, not an engine feature: this project would have to port them
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 3, D7), editor only: Code/GameSDK/GameDll/Boids/*, sample scripts.pak (Scripts/Entities/Boids/*.lua, Scripts/Utils/Math.lua), a trial in the editor; manual Boids Entities
content:
The manual's Boids Entities page describes Legacy Entities (Birds, Bugs, Fish, Chickens, Frogs, Turtles, Crabs, Snake, BaldEagle) with Flocking, Movement, Ground and Options properties. In 5.7.1 the flock simulation (CFlock, CBirdsFlock, CFishFlock, CBugsFlock, CBoidBird/BoidFish ..., CBoidsProxy) and the Lua binding `Boids` (CScriptBind_Boids: CreateFlock, EnableFlock, OnBoidHit ...) are in Code/GameSDK/GameDll/Boids/, i.e. the GameSDK's GAME code: nothing in Code/CryEngine has "ScriptBind_Boids". The entity scripts are in the sample's scripts.pak (Scripts/Entities/Boids/Birds.lua + Boid.lua); Birds.lua uses __max/__min from Scripts/Utils/Math.lua (the GameSDK's Lua init loads it; this project does not run that init: `Script.ReloadScript("Scripts/Utils/Math.lua")` fixes it).
Trial (editor only): importing Birds.lua, Boid.lua, Math.lua, the crow and pigeon models (48 files) and registering `<Entity Name="Birds" Script="Scripts/Entities/Boids/Birds.lua"/>` in Assets/entities.xml made the class creatable (bridge.object.create Entity ... Birds); the script then failed at CreateFlock: "attempt to index global 'Boids' (a nil value)". So the C++ must be ported into the project's game plugin (a real piece of work: about a dozen files) before any bird flies. The bird animations are already in the project (Animations/animals/birds/{crow,pigeon,bald_eagle,seagull...} in animations.pak) and the models are in the sample's objects-part0.pak (Objects/characters/animals/birds/*). Everything imported was removed again.

title: TOOLING: nav_reach / nav_map ask the navmesh with the engine's own connectivity test from the editor; the houses are islands by design
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 3, D1), editor only: ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.nav.query), checks/nav_check.py, test_nav_check.py (6), selftest group navigation; CryAISystem/INavigationSystem.h; build_ashvale.py (house door cuts)
content:
`bridge.nav.query <agent type or -> <base64 lines 'label x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2'>` lists the agent types and meshes (agent type 'Villager' id 1, mesh 'AshvaleNav' id 65789) and answers, per line, INavigationSystem::IsPointReachableFromPosition (the engine's cheap test: 'are these two points connected, without a full path'; default snapping metrics vertical then box), the mesh volume of each end (FindEnclosingMeshID / IsLocationInMeshVolume, -1 = none) and a NavMeshRayCast. It does NOT know dynamic obstacles or OFF-MESH links (the entity parameter that would test links is null).
Measured on the village (the game not run): all outdoor cells from x 440 to 560, y 320 to 420 at z 36.5 are connected to the player start except the house footprints; the bandit yard and the camp fire (y 767-770) are connected; a point 3 km away is in no mesh volume and not connected; the open-sided barn (south side open) is connected inside. Every house WITH a door is an island: probing along y 371.4 through the Reeve's door (x 490 down to 470 in 0.5 m steps) is connected up to the doorstep at x 483, unconnected from the doorway through the interior (x 482.5 to 473), connected again beyond the west wall. That is the design: build_ashvale.py cuts each doorway out of the mesh with a `<House>_DoorCut` navigation area (exclusion) and the FarmGate component's off-mesh link (LinkDepth 1.4) is how villagers cross; regenerating the mesh (ai.regenerate_agent_type_layer0) changed nothing. So `nav_reach` is the check for outdoor destinations, patrol points and quest targets (they must be connected to the start), and a house interior is judged by its door's off-mesh link, which only a game run shows.

title: FINDING: the shipped LOD tool (generatelod.py + the LodTools shelf) is dead in CRYENGINE 5.7.1 LTS; LODs are authored nodes, not generated
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, B5): Editor/Scripts/generatelod.py, Editor/Scripts/Shelves/LodTools.xml, editor log, rc.exe /help, grep of <engine source checkout>; manual Vegetation 01 Grass (Patch) 3dsMax, Optimization Overview
content:
`general.run_file_parameters('generatelod.py','50.0')` (the LodTools shelf's macro) answers "Could not find 'generatelod.py' in .../user/sandbox/ or .../Assets/": it searches the PROJECT, not the engine's Editor/Scripts where the file lives. The script itself calls `lodtools.getselected()`, `generatelodchain()`, `createlod()` ...; there is no `lodtools` in the editor's Python (the bridge's globals hold asset, designer, entity, flowgraph, general, group, keybind, layer, level, level_explorer, material, meshimporter, object, particle, path_utils, physics, prefab, selection, terrain, tools, trackview, ui_action, uvmapping, vegetation, version_control_system) and the string appears nowhere in <engine source checkout> rc.exe /help (76 lines) has no LOD, simplify or decimate option. So the engine has NO automatic LOD generator in this build.
LODs are AUTHORED: child nodes named $lod1_<name>, $lod2_<name> ... in the source scene (the manual's grass tutorial: tutorial_grass_patch 652 triangles, $LOD1_ 412, $LOD2_ ...; the Optimization Overview: each LOD must cut at least 50% of the polygons and, where it can, the number of materials). Which LOD renders is shown by `e_DebugDraw 3` (the debug_view 'lods' view: red LOD0, green LOD1, blue LOD2, turquoise LOD3, yellow LOD4, purple LOD5). The project's own meshes are small (Barn.cgf 1,674 triangles, 12 materials) and carry none. build_mesh does not emit $lodN_ nodes yet.

title: TOOLING: render_tour switches one rendering variable at a time in the EDITOR viewport against a fresh control
source: Session 2026-10-07 (Wave 1, G1): screens/render_tour.py, test_render_tour.py (11 checks), the default tour run twice on the village view
content:
Full title: TOOLING: render_tour switches one rendering variable at a time in the EDITOR viewport against a fresh control; what visibly matters in the village view, and why a single control misleads
`render_tour(settings=['e_Shadows=0', ...])` (render_tour.py): for each setting a fresh control picture, the variable set and READ BACK, a picture, the variable put back and read back; the answer has the mean grey-level difference, the changed share and its 3x3 grid, the DRIFT (how far the unchanged view moved since the previous control) and a ratio over the larger of the noise and the drift; labels are the engine's own help text. At most 12 settings per call (two pictures each, about 15 s per setting). The game is not run; the editor takes cheat and const variables where a Release game refuses most of them.
Why a control before EVERY variable: the first tour used one control taken at the start and showed a constant 5.16 offset for ten different variables after a single early switch (e_Shadows): the scene had DRIFTED (shadow cache, streaming, eye adaptation), not ten features. With a fresh control each the same variables read 0.4-0.7 against drift 0.44. After e_Vegetation, e_MergedMeshes, r_PostProcessEffects or r_ssdo are switched and restored the next measurement drifts 2.7-4.6 levels: give those longer to settle or read their rows as 'undecided'.
Measured on the village view from the south (editor viewport, noise 0.46): e_Sun 0 = 39.5 levels (x86), e_Vegetation 0 = 15.1 (x33), r_Sharpening 1.0 = 8.1 (x7), e_Shadows 0 = 5.9 (x13), anti-aliasing mode 0 = 1.2 (x2.6), e_TerrainDetailMaterials 0 = 1.2 (x2.5), e_Wind 0 = 1.1 (x2.3), e_Clouds 0 / r_VolumetricClouds 0 = 0.9 (x2); undecided because of drift: e_MergedMeshes, r_PostProcessEffects, r_ssdo; NOT told from noise in this view: r_HDRBloom, r_MotionBlur, r_DepthOfField, r_HeightMapAO, r_ChromaticAberration 1.0 (0.45: no visible effect at all), r_SunShafts, e_Decals, r_Reflections, r_SSReflections, r_Flares, r_ColorGrading, r_FogShadows. 'Not told from noise' means not visible in THIS view and time of day in the editor viewport: it does not say the feature does nothing in the game (flares need flare lights in view, fog shadows need volumetric fog).

title: TRAP: a floating editor window (the Particle Editor) was picked as the 'main window', so the deploy closed THAT and the editor never exited
source: Session 2026-10-07: bridge_devloop.py deploy aborted with 'Sandbox never exited'; ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp FindSandboxWindow
content: FindSandboxWindow chose the LARGEST visible top-level window of the process. `particle.show_effect` opens the Particle Editor as a floating window (title = the effect's name, e.g. 'dust') which was larger than the editor's main window, so bridge.window.close, the screenshot verb and the deploy all acted on it: the deploy printed 'Sandbox never exited -- deploy aborted, nothing was swapped' (nothing was lost; `bridge.window.close` once closed the stray window and the next deploy worked). Fixed in the plugin: the window titled 'CRYENGINE Sandbox ...' wins, the largest is the fallback; the title is read with InternalGetWindowText because GetWindowText on a window of the SAME process sends WM_GETTEXT, which a wedged main thread never answers (the out-of-band verbs exist for exactly that case). The editor offers no close_pane (general.get_pane_class_names says 'for use with open_pane & close_pane', but the Python API has only open_pane / open_or_focus_pane): close a pane you opened by bridge.window.list then bridge.window.close, or do not open it.

source: Session 2026-10-08 (Wave 2, C1, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.mannequin.check, bridge.mannequin.clips), animation/mannequin_check.py, test_mannequin_check.py (22 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group mannequin); CryAction/Mannequin/AnimationDatabaseManager.cpp (LoadDatabaseData, LoadControllerDef), AnimationDatabase.cpp (Validate); manual Animation Database (ADB), Controller Definition File

Full title: TOOLING: mannequin_check loads a villager's .adb / controller definition / character through the ENGINE's Mannequin loaders, saves what it kept and runs the engine's own Validate; mannequin_clips lists the 27 procedural clip types
IMannequin (gEnv->pGameFramework->GetMannequinInterface()) is reachable from an editor plugin: GetAnimationDatabaseManager() (Load, LoadControllerDef, LoadTagDefs), GetMannequinEditorManager() (SaveDatabase / SaveControllerDef / SaveTagDefinition into an IMannequinWriter of your own: the XML the engine would write, nothing touches disk; RevertDatabase / RevertControllerDef / RevertTagDef re-read one file), GetProceduralClipFactory(). Verb `bridge.mannequin.check <out.json> | <adb or -> | <controller def or -> | <cdf or -> | reload` returns one JSON file: tags, fragments with every tag set and option (animations, flags, procedural clip types and whether the factory knows them), the engine's Validate errors and warnings, EnumerateAnimAssets (every clip with its animation id, -1 = the character cannot play it), the controller's scopes (layers, context, scope masks), the engine's saved XML and the log lines the load produced (log verbosity is raised to 4 for the load and put back; an ILogCallback on the stack removes itself). mannequin_check.py diffs file against saved XML (tag lists as sets, numbers as numbers: 0.3 is saved as 0.30000001; options matched by tag set because the engine re-sorts; same-name fragment elements merged because the loader adds them to one fragment) and adds rules: M002/M003 (log lines), M010 dropped, M012 changed, M020 animation not found, M022 unknown procedural clip, M030 scopes of one context sharing animation layers (the manual: the engine does not check), M031 FragmentID with no controller-definition entry (the manual: exactly one each), M033 database and controller definition using different tag/fragment files, M040 a fragment name the C++ asks for that the database lacks (GetFragmentId / SetDefaultFragmentName / ActionFragment returns: a typo is an invalid id and nothing plays), M041 a defined fragment no C++ asks for.

title: My animation does not play: the Mannequin loader drops an unknown fragment, option or blend entry, often with no log line
source: Session 2026-10-08 (Wave 2, C1, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.mannequin.check, bridge.mannequin.clips), animation/mannequin_check.py, test_mannequin_check.py (22 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group mannequin); CryAction/Mannequin/AnimationDatabaseManager.cpp (LoadDatabaseData, LoadControllerDef), AnimationDatabase.cpp (Validate); manual Animation Database (ADB), Controller Definition File
content: WHAT THE LOADER DROPS (AnimationDatabaseManager.cpp 1361-1490): a fragment element whose name is not a FragmentID (a CryLog 'Warning missing fragmentID X'), an option whose Tags/FragTags do not resolve ('Unknown tags for fragmentID'; also a CryWarning 'Invalid tag'), an option whose layers cannot be read ('Broken fragment entry'), and a FragmentBlendList entry whose from/to fragment is unknown, with NO line at all (only the file-versus-saved comparison finds it). The controller definition loader skips an unknown or duplicate fragment, scope or scope context with a CryWarning, and an unknown scope name inside a scopes="" list silently gives a smaller mask.

title: Mannequin Validate says OK although an animation is missing: only the LAST tag set's answer is returned
source: Session 2026-10-08 (Wave 2, C1, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.mannequin.check, bridge.mannequin.clips), animation/mannequin_check.py, test_mannequin_check.py (22 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group mannequin); CryAction/Mannequin/AnimationDatabaseManager.cpp (LoadDatabaseData, LoadControllerDef), AnimationDatabase.cpp (Validate); manual Animation Database (ADB), Controller Definition File
content: THE ENGINE'S Validate LIES: CAnimationDatabase::Validate assigns `noErrors = ValidateAnimations(...)` for every tag set, so only the LAST tag set's answer is returned (measured: a database with a missing animation in Walk returned true because the last fragment's last tag set was fine). The error CALLBACK reports are right, so mannequin_check counts those. Validate also needs an animation set, i.e. a character instance: sdk_player.cdf has 1,692 animations here; without one only the duplicate-tag-set warnings run.

title: TRAP: ICharacterManager::CreateInstance returns an instance with a reference count of ZERO
source: Session 2026-10-08: bridge.mannequin.check first version; CryAnimation/CharacterInstance.h:306 (CCharInstance::Release); the user's screenshot of the CRYENGINE FATAL ERROR dialog
content:
Full title: TRAP: ICharacterManager::CreateInstance returns an instance with a reference count of ZERO; Release() without an AddRef() is a FATAL ERROR dialog that freezes the editor
CCharInstance::Release(): `if (--m_nRefCounter == 0) delete this; else if (m_nRefCounter < 0) CryFatalError("CSkelInstance::Release")`. CreateInstance hands the instance back unowned (the callers keep it in a _smart_ptr, whose first AddRef makes it 1), so a plugin that creates a character just to read its IAnimationSet and then calls Release() takes the count to -1: a modal 'CRYENGINE FATAL ERROR: CSkelInstance::Release' box (one per call; two were stacked when the user saw it) blocks the editor's main thread. AddRef() after CreateInstance, Release() when done (or _smart_ptr<ICharacterInstance>).
HOW IT LOOKED FROM THE OUTSIDE: every bridge verb answered 'timed out waiting for the editor main thread to run this command (both the idle tick and the WM_TIMER pump failed to drain the queue -- the main thread is genuinely blocked, not merely not drawing)' after 20 s while the command's own output file had been written (the dialog is raised at the end of the verb, in the destructor); I took it for a slow character load and timed it, which was wrong. Rule: that exact timeout message means a MODAL dialog (or a real hang): ask list_dialogs / bridge.window.list first; the out-of-band verbs still answer. After the user clicked OK the editor exited (the fatal handler terminates), the watchdog was not needed because the deploy script launches Sandbox when none runs ('bridge not answering; assuming Sandbox is already closed'), and the level was unchanged (307 objects; saved by the previous deploy, nothing edited since).

title: TOOLING: bt_check loads a behaviour tree through the engine's own loader steps, strictly (the game) and leniently (the editor), and...
source: Session 2026-10-08 (Wave 3, D2, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.bt.nodes, bridge.bt.load), checks/bt_check.py, test_bt_check.py (19 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group behavior tree); CryAISystem/BehaviorTree/BehaviorTreeManager.cpp (LoadBehaviorTreeTemplate), CryCommon/CryAISystem/BehaviorTree/ (IBehaviorTree.h, XmlLoader.h), CryCore/Containers/VariableCollection.h
content:
Full title: TOOLING: bt_check loads a behaviour tree through the engine's own loader steps, strictly (the game) and leniently (the editor), and bt_nodes lists the node types the factory can create with their attributes
The behaviour tree loader is header-only (CryCommon: XmlLoader, Variables::Declarations / EventsDeclaration / SignalHandler, TimestampCollection, MetaExtensionTable, LoadContext) over the engine's node FACTORY (gEnv->pAISystem->GetIBehaviorTreeManager()->GetNodeFactory(), implemented in CryAISystem), so an editor plugin can repeat BehaviorTreeManager::LoadBehaviorTreeTemplate step by step without caching or starting a tree. Verb `bridge.bt.load <out.json> | <tree.xml>` does it twice: STRICT (isLoadingFromEditor=false: what the game does, an error refuses the tree) and LENIENT (true: the Behavior Tree Editor's mode, the tree loads with errors), captures the log lines (verbosity raised to 4 for the load, put back) and returns the lenient tree's own INode::CreateXmlDescription. Verb `bridge.bt.nodes <out.json> | <names file>` asks the factory to create each named type and returns the node's description (its attributes with defaults). Both need USING_BEHAVIOR_TREE_XML_DESCRIPTION_CREATION (on in every non-Release Windows build: BehaviorTreeDefines.h). A local variable named `signals` does not compile in a Sandbox plugin: Qt defines `signals` as `public`.

`bridge.uqs.check <out> | <name> [| register]` uses IHub::GetEditorService(): LoadTextualQueryBlueprint(name, consumer, error) makes the XML data source read libs/ai/uqs/<name>.uqs into the engine's textual blueprint, which exists only during the callback; the consumer copies it into plain data and, when ValidateTextualQueryBlueprint(consumer) calls back, writes it into the blueprint to validate with an ISyntaxErrorCollector attached to every element, so the engine's own validation errors arrive tagged with the element ("Query/Generator std::NoSuchGenerator: Unknown GeneratorFactory", "Query/RuntimeParam[npcPos]: Unknown item type", "Query/Generator .../Input: Incorrect number of parameters provided: expected 5, got 4", "Unknown function", "Unknown ScoreTransformFactory", "Unknown InstantEvaluatorFactory"). Nothing is stored in the library and nothing runs.

title: UQS registry: 16 item types, 33 functions, 11 generators, evaluators, score transforms and query factories (uqs_catalog)
source: Session 2026-10-08 (Wave 3, D3, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.uqs.catalog, bridge.uqs.check), checks/uqs_check.py, test_uqs_check.py (21 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group uqs); CryPlugins/CryUQS/Interfaces (core/IHub.h, IEditorService.h, IQueryBlueprint.h, client/IInputParameterRegistry.h), DataSource_XML/QueryBlueprintFileLibrary.cpp, QueryBlueprintLoader_XML.cpp; manual UQS pages
content: The UQS interfaces are header-only and reachable from an editor plugin (`#include "../../../CryPlugins/CryUQS/Interfaces/InterfacesIncludes.h"`, no CMake change; `UQS::Core::IHubPlugin::GetHubPtr()` finds the hub of the loaded CryUQS_Core plugin). `bridge.uqs.catalog` walks the hub's factory databases: 16 item types (std::Pos3, Dir3, Ofs3, float, int, bool, NavigationAgentTypeID, EntityId, each with a shuttled-items container), 33 functions (the _builtin_Func_Literal / GlobalParam / IteratedItem / ShuttledItems leaves per type, plus the operators), 11 generators (std::PointsOnGridProjectedOntoNavMesh, PointsOnNavMesh, PointsOnPureGrid and builtin::PropagateShuttledItems per type), 6 instant evaluators (TestMinDistance, TestMaxDistance, TestLocationInNavMesh [expensive], ScoreDistance, ScoreDistanceInverse, ScoreRandom), 1 deferred evaluator (TestRaycast), 6 score transforms (Linear, LinearInverse, Sine180, Sine180Inverse, Square, SquareInverse) and 3 query factories (Regular, Chained, Fallbacks), each input with the engine's name, 4-character id (CENT, SIZE, SPAC, AGEN, VTOL ...), type and description.

title: UQS query file written after editor start is 'not among the enumerated records'; RemoveQueryBlueprint DELETES the file
source: Session 2026-10-08 (Wave 3, D3, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.uqs.catalog, bridge.uqs.check), checks/uqs_check.py, test_uqs_check.py (21 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group uqs); CryPlugins/CryUQS/Interfaces (core/IHub.h, IEditorService.h, IQueryBlueprint.h, client/IInputParameterRegistry.h), DataSource_XML/QueryBlueprintFileLibrary.cpp, QueryBlueprintLoader_XML.cpp; manual UQS pages
content: THE XML DATA SOURCE ENUMERATES libs/ai/uqs ONCE AT STARTUP: a file written afterwards is 'not among the enumerated records'. IEditorService::CreateNewTextualQueryBlueprint(name) registers a record in memory (no file written); LoadTextualQueryBlueprint then reads the file at the record's path; RemoveQueryBlueprint(name) removes the record AND DELETES THE FILE (ICryPak::RemoveFile). So uqs_check checks a new or outside file as a temporary `zz_mcp_<stamp>_<name>.uqs` copy registered for the call and removed by the engine, and the verb refuses `register` for any name not starting with zz_mcp_ (a bug must not delete a real query).

title: UQS query validates but fails at run time: the engine's validation misses a non-numeric literal and accepts a misnamed Input by paramID
source: Session 2026-10-08 (Wave 3, D3, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.uqs.catalog, bridge.uqs.check), checks/uqs_check.py, test_uqs_check.py (21 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group uqs); CryPlugins/CryUQS/Interfaces (core/IHub.h, IEditorService.h, IQueryBlueprint.h, client/IInputParameterRegistry.h), DataSource_XML/QueryBlueprintFileLibrary.cpp, QueryBlueprintLoader_XML.cpp; manual UQS pages
content: WHAT THE ENGINE'S VALIDATION DOES NOT CATCH (measured): a literal that is not a number (`<Function name="_builtin_Func_Literal_std::float" returnValue="forty"/>`) validates fine and fails only when the query starts (uqs_check U015 parses float/int/bool literals); an <Input> is matched by its 4-character paramID when it has one, so `<Input name="sizee" paramID="SIZE">` is accepted (and must not be reported as a missing input: U014 matches by id or name). Full title: TOOLING: the engine writes its own level resource report (level.save_stats) and checks the level (level.validate); the report proves the house LODs, the checker found five undefined surface types
`level.save_stats` runs the engine's console command SaveLevelStats (CrySystem/Statistics.cpp, non-Release builds): two Excel workbooks in `<project>/user/testresults/`, `<level>.xml` and `depends_<level>.xml`. They are NOT well-formed XML (the ss: and x: prefixes are never declared; Excel does not mind), so level_stats.py declares them before parsing. Sheets of `ashvale.xml`: Summary (CGF objects 70 = 127 MB of which textures 116 MB, 630 textures, 681 meshes 63 MB, game memory 376 MB, virtual 2.7 GB), Modules Memory Info, Memory Stats, Static Geometry, Characters, Meshes, Brushes, Textures, Materials, Materials Unused Textures (empty here), Profiler, Peaks, Budget, Physical Entities (307), Entities (80), AnimationKeys Info, Streaming Info. In the editor it is a CENSUS of what is loaded (load time and fps read 0), not a profile. The largest 'textures' are engine render targets ($ShadowMapCached_* 6324 x 6324 D16 = 78 MB each, the terrain pool 64 MB, the shadow pools 64 MB each): not project assets; the project's own heavy ones are GameSDK sample meshes' textures (deco rocks 24 MB, the campfire 21 MB, each field-grass tuft 19 MB).
Method notes: `bridge.execute_command <cmd>` returns the engine's log for that command in the reply, which is how the validator's lines are read without touching editor.log; the Mesh component's label is 'Mesh' (class Cry::DefaultComponents::CStaticMeshComponent, default FilePath %ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Objects/primitive_sphere.cgf) for bridge.entity.add_component.

title: TOOLING: the Resource Compiler's 44 texture presets (with the file-name masks that pick them), 176 options and 13 converters, read from...
source: Session 2026-10-08 (B1): catalogs/rc_catalog.py, test_rc_catalog.py (12 checks); Tools/rc/rc.ini; rc.exe /help (RC 1.1.8.7); manual System Utilities: Resource Compiler (Presets, Command Line Arguments)
content:
Full title: TOOLING: the Resource Compiler's 44 texture presets (with the file-name masks that pick them), 176 options and 13 converters, read from rc.ini and `rc.exe /help`
rc.ini (Tools/rc/rc.ini, the file RC loads at start) holds global settings (imagecompressor=CTsquish, brdfGlossScale 16, the asset browser's type list), four [_platform] blocks (pc/tegra, ps4/orbis, xboxone/durango/xb1, gles3/es3/android), the [_presetAliases] table (37 legacy names -> current: Diffuse_highQ -> Albedo, DisplacementMap -> Displacement, Normalmap_highQ -> Normals, NormalmapWithGlossInAlpha_highQ -> NormalsWithSmoothness_Legacy ...) and 44 presets, each a section with pixelformat (pixelformat:es3 for mobile), colorspace, mipmaps, powof2, and `filemasks=`. The mask picks the candidates, the image content picks among them (manual, 'Automatic Adjustments': an alpha channel turns Albedo into a format that can hold it): `*_diff*` -> Albedo (BC1), AlbedoWithOpacity (BC7t), AlbedoWithCoverage (BC1a), AlbedoWithGenericAlpha (BC3), AlbedoWithGenericAlphaNoMip; `*_ddna*` -> NormalsWithSmoothness (BC5s + BC4 alpha, glossfromnormals) and the legacy one; `*_ddn*` -> Normals; `*_displ*` -> ONLY Displacement (BC4, swizzle=aaa1: the height is read from the ALPHA channel, which is why a height map left to auto-selection became BC3 and why the project's TIFFs carry the preset inside); `*_bump*` -> NormalsFromDisplacement; `*_spec*` -> the Reflectance presets. The project's texture pipeline names Albedo, NormalsWithSmoothness and Displacement: all exist with the formats it relies on.
`rc.exe /help` prints ~800 lines: the version (1.1.8.7), the 13 registered converters with their extensions (AlembicCompiler abc; ImageConverter tif hdr; TextureSplitter dds; StatCGFCompiler cga cgf i_cgf; ChunkCompiler chunk; LuaCompiler lua; FbxConverter fbx; MetadataCompiler cryasset; CharacterCompiler chr cdf skin; AnimationConverter i_caf; ColladaCompiler dae dae.zip; SubstanceConverter crysub; XMLConverter xml; the zip and pak compiler), and 176 options, each with the compiler that reads it in brackets ([TIF] /preset /autopreset /userdialog, [CGF] /vertexindexformat /vertexpositionformat, [ABC] /upaxis /usebframes, [cryasset] /assettypes), e.g. /targetnameformat, /threads, /zip_* ... RC reports an unknown key only as a warning ('Cannot find converter for ...'), so check a key here before relying on it.
TRAP: from Git Bash, `rc.exe /help` is rewritten by MSYS into `C:/Program Files/Git/help` and RC answers 'RC can't find file ... Cannot find converter for help'; call it from Python (subprocess, cwd = the RC folder) or set MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1. Running /help only prints text: nothing is compiled.

source: Session 2026-10-08 (B6, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.character.check), animation/character_check.py, test_character_check.py (12 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group character); CryCommon/CryAnimation (ICryAnimation.h, IAttachment.h); manual Creating Character Definition - Character Tool
content:
Full title: TOOLING: character_check creates every .cdf through the engine and reports skeleton, attachments and load log; ten of the project's 13 .cdf files point at meshes that are not there
A character definition (.cdf, XML) names a skeleton (<Model File=... Material=...>) and a list of <Attachment Type=CA_BONE|CA_SKIN|CA_FACE|CA_PROX|CA_PROW|CA_VCLOTH AName=... BoneName=.../Binding=.../Material=...>. The plugin verb `bridge.character.check <out> | <names file>` creates each through ICharacterManager::CreateInstance (the Character Tool's and the game's path) and writes, from the engine's resolved objects: the default skeleton's model file and joint count, every attachment (IAttachment name, type, joint name from the joint id, whether IAttachmentObject is bound, its type static/skeleton/skin/entity/light/effect and GetObjectFilePath) and IAnimationSet::GetAnimationCount, with the log lines the load wrote (verbosity raised to 4 for the load). sdk_player.cdf: 163 joints, 29 attachments of which 5 hold an object (shoes, jeans, arm_hands, head, jacket; the others are bone sockets: camera, weapon, eyes, hand), 1,692 animations.
TRAPS. (1) CreateInstance returns the instance with a reference count of ZERO: AddRef() after it and Release() when done; releasing without AddRef raises CryFatalError('CSkelInstance::Release'), a modal box that freezes the editor (it happened). (2) A binding the engine cannot load does NOT leave the attachment unbound: it logs `CGF Loading Failed: Failed to open file '<path>'` and `Failed to load cgf: <path>` and binds the engine's PLACEHOLDER object, so IAttachment::GetIAttachmentObject() is non-null and `bound` is true; only the log line (or the file's absence) shows it. (3) The engine logs a material's 'undefined surface type' only the FIRST time the material loads in a session: a second run of the same check is quieter. (4) asset_lint.Names also searches the GameSDK sample folder, which is not mounted in the editor or the game, so it says a path exists that CryPak cannot open: do not use it to judge a binding.
FINDING: 13 .cdf files are in the project's Assets (sdk_player and sdk_player_{blue,red}{,_beanie,_glasses,_helmet,_hipster,_sunglasses}), all created by the engine; the game's C++ names only sdk_player.cdf (Npc.h kCharacterFile), which is clean. The ten variants bind objects/characters/human/attachments/{beanie/beanie.cgf, glasses/glasses_helvetica.cgf, helmet/helmet_a.cgf, necklace/necklace.cgf, sunglasses/sunglasses_a.cgf}, which are not in the project: the engine binds placeholders. They are inert (nothing refers to them) and are packaged anyway; delete the ten files or import the meshes if variants are wanted. character_check reports them as warnings (errors only for a character the game refers to).

title: Illum GenerationMask: NORMAL_MAP and SUBSURFACE_SCATTERING are always set, %BUMP_MAP does nothing, a numeric GenMask needs no StringGenMask
source: Session 2026-10-08 (B3/B4, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.material.check), checks/material_check.py, test_material_check.py (32 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group material); Cry3DEngine/MatMan.cpp, SurfaceTypeManager.cpp, Sandbox Material/MaterialManager.cpp; manual Material Effects, Material Effects and Vehicles
content: THE GENERATION MASK (copies of cloth.mtl, Illum): the final mask ALWAYS carries NORMAL_MAP 0x20 (Illum.ext: DependencySet = $TEX_Normals: set when a normal map is present) and SUBSURFACE_SCATTERING 0x4000000000000, whatever StringGenMask says ('', '%NOTAREALFLAG%NORMAL_MAP', the original: identical); so %NORMAL_MAP, %BUMP_MAP and %SUBSURFACE_SCATTERING in a string do nothing; %PARALLAX_OCCLUSION_MAPPING adds exactly 0x8000000; a numeric GenMask counts ONLY when StringGenMask is absent (an empty one wins) and then its bits pass as they are (80000000 added exactly 0x80000000; 80000081 gave only 0x80000000: 0x1 and 0x80 were dropped). title: DECISION: eight surface types copied from the GameSDK, cloth->fabric and dirt->soil remapped, ten unused character variants deleted
source: Session 2026-10-08: Assets/libs/MaterialEffects/SurfaceTypes.xml, Assets/materials/ashvale/{cloth,cloth_pale,world}.mtl, GameSDK sample gamedata.pak (Libs/MaterialEffects/SurfaceTypes.xml), checks/asset_lint.py (L017), test_character_check.py
content:
Full title: DECISION: eight surface types copied from the GameSDK, cloth->fabric and dirt->soil remapped, ten unused character variants deleted (snapshot before_surface_types_and_variant_cleanup)
The user left the choice to me. The project's SurfaceTypes.xml defined 9 types; materials named 5 more that the engine did not know (level.validate / lint L017) and the imported GameSDK object materials named more. Decided and done: the eight that the GameSDK defines and the project's materials name (mat_flesh, mat_rock, mat_fabric, mat_plastic, mat_snow, mat_glass, mat_glass_unbreakable, mat_wood_breakable) were copied UNCHANGED from the sample's gamedata.pak into Assets/libs/MaterialEffects/SurfaceTypes.xml (17 types now); `mat_cloth` (cloth.mtl, cloth_pale.mtl) was remapped to mat_fabric and `mat_dirt` (world.mtl dirtroad) to mat_soil because nobody defines those two. Reasons: the game's C++ never reads a surface type, the project has no MaterialEffects.xml / FXLibs (so a surface type only sets physics: friction, bounce, pierceability, sound_obstruction), and the characters use kInertia 0 (velocity set directly). Unproven without a game run: that nothing feels different; the editor viewport cannot show it. Pak trap: the sample's paks store backslash names, so Python's zipfile refuses `z.read('Libs/MaterialEffects/SurfaceTypes.xml')` ('File name in directory ... and header ... differ'); set `zi = z.getinfo(name); zi.orig_filename = zi.orig_filename.replace('/', chr(92))` and read `zi`. The engine reads SurfaceTypes.xml at startup (CMatMan::InitDefaults) and `e_ReloadSurfaces` reloads it; the manual says to restart the editor. The ten colour/hat sdk_player variants (beanie, glasses, helmet, hipster, sunglasses x blue/red) bound meshes that are not in the project and nothing referenced them: deleted with their .cdf.cryasset; sdk_player.cdf, sdk_player_blue.cdf and sdk_player_red.cdf remain. lint L017 now scans Assets/objects too.

title: TOOLING: flow_nodes lists the engine's 642 flow node types with their ports; flow_check loads a graph XML through the engine's own...
source: Session 2026-10-08 (E2, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.flow.catalog, bridge.flow.check), checks/flow_check.py, test_flow_check.py (29 checks), bridge_selftest.py (group flow); CryCommon/CryFlowGraph/IFlowSystem.h; CryFlowGraph/FlowSystem/FlowGraph.cpp:1453 (ReadXML), FlowData.cpp:247; Code/Components/FlowNodes.cpp; manual Flow Graph pages, Creating a New Flow Node
content:
Full title: TOOLING: flow_nodes lists the engine's 642 flow node types with their ports; flow_check loads a graph XML through the engine's own loader and compares it with the file
`bridge.flow.catalog <out>` walks IFlowSystem::CreateNodeTypeIterator(), creates each type in a scratch graph (IFlowGraph::CreateNode(typeId, name)), reads IFlowGraph::GetNodeConfiguration (SFlowNodeConfig: nFlags, sDescription, pInputPorts / pOutputPorts arrays ended by a null name) and removes the node again; per input port: name, humanName, description, sUIConfig, defaultData.GetType() (index in TFlowInputDataVariant: 0 Void, 1 Int, 2 Float, 3 EntityId, 4 Vec3, 5 String, 6 Bool), IsLocked() (an unlocked port is 'Any'), the default as text; per output: name, humanName, description, type (-1 = Any). Result in the editor: 642 types, all created; category flags EFLN_APPROVED 0x10 (545), EFLN_ADVANCED 0x20 (75), EFLN_DEBUG 0x40 (19), EFLN_OBSOLETE 0x200 (3, hidden in the editor); core flags 1 targets an entity, 2 hidden in the UI, 4 dynamic outputs, 8 cannot be removed. The game's own nodes (REGISTER_FLOW_NODE in Code/Components/FlowNodes.cpp: Claude:Lamp, Claude:VillagerSays) are listed because the editor loads Game.dll and RegisterGameFlowNodes hands them over; a new node needs a Game.dll build and an editor restart.
`bridge.flow.check <out> | <graph xml, a CryPak path>` loads the file with LoadXmlFromFile and IFlowGraph::SerializeXML(root, true) into a scratch graph (NOT SetEnabled, NOT InitializeValues, so no node runs and nothing touches the level; the graph registers with the flow system and is released at the end of the verb) and writes the nodes (id, name, type, every input port with the value it holds via GetInputValue, output names), the edges by node and port name (IFlowGraph::CreateEdgeIterator) and the log lines.

content: LOADER RULES (FlowGraph.cpp ReadXML, FlowData.cpp SerializeXML), measured: node = <Node ID="name" Class="Type"><Inputs port="value"/></Node> (ID is the NAME attribute); edges <Edge nodeOut portOut nodeIn portIn enabled/>; a Class that is not registered, a node whose SerializeXML fails, or an edge that cannot be linked (unknown node or port) makes the engine log '[flow] ...
