title: TOOLING: env_check reads time-of-day presets by the engine loader's rules: version 4 is read POSITIONALLY, evaluated values are CLAMPED...
source: Session 2026-10-08 (G2): checks/env_check.py, test_env_check.py (21 checks); Cry3DEngine/EnvironmentPreset.cpp (Reset, Serialize, GetInterpolatedAt), CryCommon/Cry3DEngine/ITimeOfDay.h; bridge.env.list
content:
Full title: TOOLING: env_check reads time-of-day presets by the engine loader's rules: version 4 is read POSITIONALLY, evaluated values are CLAMPED to the file's range
The engine's time-of-day variable table (145 variables, enum ITimeOfDay::ETimeOfDayParamID PARAM_SUN_COLOR ... PARAM_TOTAL, plus deprecated ones after it) is built by CTimeOfDayVariables::Reset: one AddVar(group, displayName, name, id, TYPE_FLOAT|TYPE_COLOR, default0, default1, default2) per variable, where for a float the three numbers are (default, min, max) and for a colour (r, g, b) with the range fixed to 0..1. env_check reads that table from the source and it matches the RUNNING engine's list (bridge.env.list) name by name, group by group, in order (145 of 145).
LOADER RULES (CEnvironmentPreset::Serialize, EnvironmentPreset.cpp:627): a file whose version equals sCurrentPresetVersion (4) is read POSITIONALLY: for i in 0..PARAM_TOTAL it reads the next <var> element into variable i, and CTimeOfDayVariable::Serialize takes id, type, minValue, maxValue and spline0..2 from the file, replacing the engine's: a missing, extra or reordered <var> shifts every later variable and nothing is logged. An older file (no version, or < 4) goes through ReadVariablesFromXML: each <var> is matched by id (GetVar by NAME; an unknown id is dropped; SetValuesFrom copies type/range/splines), missing variables keep defaults, a version-0 file's times are rescaled from [0..1]; the Constants block is reset. Every evaluated value is clamp_tpl(spline.Evaluate(t), minValue, maxValue) (GetInterpolatedAt): a key outside the file's range is authored but never reached. Key times are in 1/6000 hour (sAnimTimeSecondsIn24h = 144000; 6:00 = 36000). The editor's current preset after a restart is %ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Shading/default.env (bridge.env.list says so); the game switches to its own presets.
FINDING: ashvale_clear.env and ashvale_rain.env are version 4 with all 145 variables in the engine's order and a Constants block; PARAM_NIGHSKY_MOON_COLOR_MULTIPLIER is 0.4 with range 0..0.1, so the moon multiplier is 0.1 (inherited from the template; author_environment.py does not set it; the engine's example.env has similar out-of-range keys). Clear vs rain differ in 16 variables (sun colour/intensity, fog colours, volumetric fog density, sky light multiplier, cloudiness, cloud thickness and absorption, sun rays visibility, saturation).

title: TOOLING: anim_check compares a chrparams and a .bspace with the joint and animation names the engine resolved for the character
source: Session 2026-10-08 (B6 rest, C2, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.character.names), animation/anim_check.py, test_anim_check.py (19 checks); CryAnimation/CharacterManager.cpp:2821; manual Character Parameters File (chrparams), Limb IK, Blend Spaces
content:
`bridge.character.names <out> | <cdf>` creates the character (CreateInstance, AddRef, Release) and writes every joint name of its default skeleton (IDefaultSkeleton::GetJointNameByID, 163 for the villager's sdk_player.cdf) and every animation name of its animation set (IAnimationSet::GetNameByAnimID, 1,692). anim_check compares the project's files with them. CHRPARAMS: <Params> holds <Lod><JointList level><Joint name>, <IK_Definition> (<LimbIK_Definition><IK EndEffector Handle Root Solver> or J0..J4, <AimIK_Definition> with <RotationList><Rotation JointName Primary Additive>, <PositionList>, <RWeaponJoint JointName>, <DirectionalBlends><Joint AnimToken ParameterJoint StartJoint ReferenceJoint>, <LookIK_Definition> (+ <LEyeAttachment Name> attachments, not joints), <Recoil_Definition> (<ImpactJoint Arm Delay Weight JointName>: Weight is a NUMBER), <FeetLock_Definition>, <Animation_Driven_IK_Targets><ADIKTarget Handle Target Weight>: Target and Weight are joints) and <AnimationList><Animation name path> where $-names are $AnimEventDatabase, $Include, $facelib, $TracksDatabase. A joint a chrparams names that the skeleton lacks is ignored silently by the engine. BLEND SPACE (.bspace, <ParaGroup>): <Dimensions><Param name min max cells scale> and <AdditionalExtraction><Param name> use the engine's 14 motion parameters (MoveSpeed, TurnSpeed, TravelAngle, TravelSlope, TurnAngle, TravelDist, StopLeg, BlendWeight, BlendWeight2..7); <ExampleList><Example AName> names animations of the character's set; <ExamplePseudo><Pseudo p0 p1 w0 w1> adds a point computed from two earlier points (w0*p0 + w1*p1); <Blendable><Face p0..p3> are triangles/quads over the point indices (examples first, then pseudo points). A blend space joins the animation set by its FILE NAME (villager_move is one of the 1,692) when the chrparams collects '*/*.bspace'.
FINDING: skeleton_player_generic.chrparams (the GameSDK's, used by the villagers) has every IK/aim joint; its LOD joint list names 'Bip01 L ForeTwist3' and 'Bip01 R ForeTwist3', which the 163-joint skeleton lacks (harmless: a LOD list only keeps joints). villager_move.bspace: 7 examples all in the set, indices in range, MoveSpeed and TurnSpeed are motion parameters.

title: TOOLING: cryproject_check compares Game.cryproject with what the engine's project manager parsed, and checks plug-ins, engine id and...
source: Session 2026-10-08 (L1, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.project.info), checks/cryproject_check.py, test_cryproject_check.py (21 checks); CryCommon/CrySystem/IProjectManager.h (SProject, SProjectFileParser<4>, SPluginDefinition), ICryPluginManager.h; manual Projects and Plug-ins (Project File Structure), Project Tools
content:
Full title: TOOLING: cryproject_check compares Game.cryproject with what the engine's project manager parsed, and checks plug-ins, engine id and console variables
The parser (IProjectManager.h, SProjectFileParser<LatestProjectFileVersion = 4>) reads: version, type, info{name, guid}, content{assets[], code[], libs[{name, shared{any, win_x64, win_x86}}]}, require{engine, plugins[{guid, type, path, platforms[]}]}, console_variables{name: value}, console_commands{}. A plug-in's type is read as EType ('EType::Native' / 'EType::Managed'); when that fails (input) it is read again as the older EPluginType ('EPluginType::Native'): both spellings work (Game.cryproject uses EType for the engine plug-ins and EPluginType for Game.dll). platforms is a list of EPlatform names (Windows, Linux, MacOS, XboxOne, PS4, Android, iOS; the enum value is the index); an empty list means every platform. Cry::IProjectManager gives name, GUID (CryGUID::ToDebugString), engine id, project directory, asset directory (relative and absolute), the .cryproject path and GetPluginCount/GetPluginInfo(index) (type, path, platforms); console variables are NOT exposed (only StoreConsoleVariable). `bridge.project.info <out>` writes those; the engine's read of Game.cryproject matches the file exactly (My Project, same GUID, engine-5.7, 7 plug-ins, CryGamePlatform for PS4 only). The launcher resolves require.engine through C:\ProgramData\Crytek\CRYENGINE\cryengine.json ({"engine-5.7": {"info", "uri"}}). A bare plug-in name is a DLL in the engine's bin\win_x64 (CryDefaultEntities, CryScaleformSchematyc, CrySensorSystem, CryPerceptionSystem, CryUQS_Core, CryGamePlatform); a path ending .dll is relative to the project (bin/win_x64/Game.dll). Console variables in console_variables apply at startup; a name the engine does not have is silently dropped: GenerateShaderCache.cryproject sets d3d9_NullRefDevice, e_profile_level_loading, log_FileVerbosity, r_shaderscacheinmemory and sys_rendersplashscreen, none of which exist in this engine's catalog (log_WriteToFileVerbosity does).

title: TOOLING: drs_check asks the running Dynamic Response System what it holds: action and condition types, dialog lines
source: Session 2026-10-08 (E5, editor only): ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.drs.dump), checks/drs_check.py, test_drs_check.py (23 checks), bridge_selftest.py; CryCommon/CryDynamicResponseSystem/IDynamicResponseSystem.h, CryDynamicResponseSystem/ResponseManager.cpp (_LoadFromFiles, Serialize, SerializeResponse), ActionSpeakLine.cpp; Code/Components/Dialogue.cpp
content:
Full title: TOOLING: drs_check asks the running Dynamic Response System what it holds: action and condition types, dialog lines, and each response as it serialises it
gEnv->pDynamicResponseSystem (DRS::IDynamicResponseSystem) gives: GetActionSerializationFactory() / GetConditionSerializationFactory() (yasli ClassFactory: size(), descriptionByIndex(i)->name()/label()): the action types CancelSignal, CancelSpeaking, ChangeVariable, CopyVariable, ExecuteResponse, ResetTimerVariable, SendSignal, SetActor, SetActorFromVariable, SetGameToken, SpeakLine, Wait and the condition types 'Execution Limit', GameToken, 'Inherit Conditions', Placeholder, Random, TimeSince, TimeSinceResponse, 'Variable equal to ', 'Variable greater than ', 'Variable in range ', 'Variable less than ', 'Variable to Variable' (the names are the registered type names and some END WITH A SPACE: a .response file must spell them exactly); GetDialogLineDatabase() (IDialogLineDatabase: GetLineSetCount/GetLineSetByIndex/GetLineSetById; IDialogLineSet: GetLineId().GetText(), GetPriority, GetFlags, GetMaxQueuingDuration, GetLineCount/GetLineByIndex; IDialogLine: GetText, GetStartAudioTrigger, GetEndAudioTrigger, GetLipsyncAnimation, GetPauseLength, GetCustomData); GetResponseManager()->SerializeResponse(ar, {signal}) which writes the response tree the engine KEPT (into a JSON archive via gEnv->pSystem->GetArchiveHost()->SaveJsonBuffer(buf, Serialization::SStruct(obj)) with a small struct whose Serialize(ar) calls it); ReInit() reloads the files from disk (Dialogue.cpp calls it).
LOADER (ResponseManager.cpp): every file under Libs/DynamicResponseSystem/Responses (recursively, through CryPak FindFirst) is loaded with Serialization::LoadJsonFile as ONE response whose signal name is the FILE'S BASE NAME (sg_villager_sees_player.response); DialogLines/*.dialog hold {lineSets: [{lineID, priority, flags, lineVariations: [...], maxQueuingDuration}]}. MEASURED with scratch files: a misspelt action or condition class is dropped from the engine's copy (D002/D006) with no log line; SpeakLine for a missing line loads (D003 only); a file that is not valid JSON still creates an EMPTY response ('(AUTO) unnamed', no actions) and nothing is logged. Response JSON shape: {BaseSegment: {name, SegmentConditions: {Conditions: [{Condition: {<class>: {...}}, Negated}], Negated}, Actions: [{Action: {<class>: {...}}, Delay}], ChildSegments: [...]}}; the engine's copy adds default fields (e.g. SpeakLine flags).
PROJECT: 2 responses and 3 lines, identical in the engine after startup and after ReInit(); the code sends sg_villager_sees_player and sg_villager_hears_player.

title: TOOLING: pbs_check applies the manual's PBS rules; final smoothness = the material's Shininess/255 times the alpha of the _ddna map
source: Session 2026-10-08 (B2, editor-free): checks/pbs_check.py, test_pbs_check.py (23 checks); manual Texture and Material Setup for PBS (44959244), Material Editor Lighting Settings (35259544), Creating Textures for PBS (54427668), Vegetation 01 Grass tutorial (24285888); Shaders/HWScripts/CryFX/Illum.cfx, Vegetation.cfx, Terrain.cfx, CommonZPass.cfi (in engine/shaders.pak)
content:
The material's Smoothness slider is the .mtl attribute Shininess (0..255); the shader reads it as MatSpecColor.w (= Shininess/255). Illum.cfx, Vegetation.cfx and Terrain.cfx compute `attribs.Smoothness = MatSpecColor.w * GetSmoothnessTex(smoothnessTex, uv)`: the FINAL smoothness is the slider TIMES the alpha channel of the _ddna normal map. With Shininess 255 the map decides; Shininess 50 with a map scales it to 20% of itself (the manual's 'set Glossiness to 255 otherwise the gloss map will not work'); a material with no _ddna map uses the slider alone (grass tutorial: 'it reads the smoothness value directly from the Smoothness slider'). Smoothness 255 = very smooth, tight highlight; 0 = rough, wide highlight.
MANUAL NUMBERS: Diffuse colour stays 255,255,255 on a textured material (colour lives in the texture; an albedo channel above 1.0 is impossible); non-metal Specular colour is monochrome sRGB 40..60 (55 typical; never above 80; water 38, skin 51, hair 65, plastic 53-61, glass high 79, diamond 115); metal Specular above sRGB 180 (iron 196,199,199; aluminium 245,245,247; gold 255,219,145; copper 250,209,194; silver 250,247,242) with a black or very dark Diffuse; a specular map is only for materials that mix metal and non-metal and then the Specular colour must be 255,255,255 (it multiplies the map); the smoothness map goes in the alpha of the _ddna texture (preset NormalsWithSmoothness lowers smoothness where normals are bumpy); Photoshop gray gamma must be 2.2; non-metal gloss values 53..61 as a rule of thumb.
PROJECT (88 Illum sub-materials): cloth_pale.mtl Diffuse 1.7,1.6,1.5 (S001); gold/steel/arrow_steel break the metal rules (S005); 27 villager sub-materials (jacket, jeans, buttons x 9 characters) use a specular map with Specular sRGB 97 (S004) and a tinted Diffuse used to recolour the GameSDK clothes (S002); 41 materials scale their smoothness maps to 20-63% by Shininess 50..160 (S006). Deviations from guidelines, tuned by eye: reported, not changed.

content:
Full title: TOOLING: gamesdk_audio reads the GameSDK sample's SDL-mixer libraries: 611 triggers, only 203 play a real sample (footsteps by surface yes, melee and collision sounds no)
audio.pak holds three sets of Audio Controls Editor libraries: audio/sdlmixer (37 library files, 124 .ogg samples), audio/wwise and audio/fmod. This project uses SDL mixer. In the SDL-mixer set 611 triggers are defined and 408 of them have only events that point at `do_nothing.ogg` (a silent placeholder: the trigger exists, nothing plays; the real content is in the Wwise/FMOD sets); 203 have a real sample. Real: c_player and c_npc (foley and FOOTSTEPS BY SURFACE: Play_c_player_fts_<surface> and Play_c_npc_fts_<surface> for concrete, dirt, fabric, grass, grass_tall, gravel, leaves, metal_chainlink, metal_grate, metal_sheet, metal_thick, mud, wood_hollow, wood_solid ..., samples c_player_fts_<surface>_walk.ogg of 0.3-0.9 s; the project already imported the dirt and grass ones), l_woodland (ambience loops of 18-31 s, e.g. l_woodland_amb_forest.ogg 30.8 s, the village ambience comes from here), l_global (owl, woodpecker, frog), p_pro (projectile impacts, e.g. bullet impact flesh / wood_hollow), weapons (w_pistol 18 of 18 real, w_rifle 26 of 32, w_shotgun 12 of 14, w_hmg 6 of 6, w_grenade 4 of 6). NOT real: p_col_mat (105 per-surface collision triggers: every one a placeholder), p_brk, p_col_obj, ALL 13 melee triggers (Play_w_melee_fire_fp/3p, Play_c_player_fbk_melee and Play_p_pro_impact_melee_hit_mat_{concrete,default,flesh,glass,grass,metal,rock,soil,water,wood}), vehicles (v_*), UI (ui_*). The per-surface naming mirrors the surface types the sample's SurfaceTypes.xml defines. Reading the pak: the sample's paks store backslash names, so zipfile needs zi.orig_filename = zi.orig_filename.replace('/', chr(92)) before read; an Ogg Vorbis duration is granule position of the last page divided by the sample rate in the identification header (bytes 'vorbis' + 6 + version 4 + channels 1).

title: TOOLING: decal_lab catalogs the GameSDK's 159 decal materials and looks at a decal in the editor viewport; measured: draws only within...
source: Session 2026-10-09 (F3, editor only): screens/decal_lab.py, test_decal_lab.py (16 checks); manual Decal Entity (36869871), Effects Components - Decal (44966055), Tutorial - Decal Component; GameSDK sample gamedata.pak materials/decals
content:
Full title: TOOLING: decal_lab catalogs the GameSDK's 159 decal materials and looks at a decal in the editor viewport; measured: draws only within ProjectionDepth of the terrain, all four projection types look alike
A Decal (editor object type Decal, properties Material, ProjectionType 0..3, Deferred, ViewDistRatio, SortPriority, ProjectionDepth, plus Pos/Rotate/Scale) projects a material onto geometry and terrain; the material is an Illum material whose StringGenMask contains %DECAL (global flag 0x800) with public parameters DecalDiffuseOpacity, DecalFalloff, DecalAlphaMult; the manual: everything under Materials/decals is set up that way; Planar is cheapest and only for flat surfaces; projected types are deferred passes; the decal looks DOWN its own Z axis. The default material of a new Decal object, Materials/Decals/Default, does not exist in the engine (LoadMaterial answers with the default material). The GameSDK sample has 159 decal materials: mud 35, dirt 32, rubbish 16, shadow 12, blood 10, water 8, metal 7, concrete 6, paint 6, vegetation 5, glass 4, rock 4, snow 3, footsteps 2 (footstep_dirt, footstep_snow), ice 2, sand 2, wood 2, rubber 1, and 2 in the root (default, default_blast); 158 are Illum with %DECAL. `import_gamesdk_asset.py` copies one material (a .mtl path) with its textures (footprint_sand_left.dds + its .1 .2 split mips) from the local pak into Assets.
MEASURED (editor viewport, scratch Decal object, two control pictures, object deleted, count checked): at (487, 392) over terrain (z 36.0) a 3 m footstep_dirt decal 0.3 m above the ground darkens the ground (changed pixels 14.8k vs noise 1.6k; mean 148,138,73 -> 113,101,55); lifted 2 m (ProjectionDepth is 1) NOTHING draws, for Planar too; ProjectionType 0, 1, 2 and 3 and Deferred 0/1 all drew the same patch over terrain (the manual says type 1 ignores terrain); a decal 0.3 m above a 3x3x1 brush slab (default cube material, or materials/stone) did not draw for any type. Unresolved: whether the property reaches the engine's decal node from the editor object, and why the slab shows nothing. The editor draws a small icon at the object: leave a box around it out of any measurement.

title: LEARNED: colour grading is a 256x16 LUT chart made from a reference image with the manual's RGBChart.bmp; the project uses none
source: Session 2026-10-09 (G3): manual Tutorial - Color Grading (26872965), Enabling Charts in Sandbox (27593341), Environment Editor Color Grading (56658466); RenderDll/XRenderD3D9/GraphicsPipeline/ColorGrading.cpp; CryCommon/Cry3DEngine/IColorGradingCtrl.h; Tools/rc/rc.ini
content: A colour chart is a 16x16x16 lookup table stored as a 256x16 texture (IColorGradingCtrl::s_colorChartSize 16, s_colorChartWidth 256, s_colorChartHeight 16). The renderer (CColorGradingStage) loads the identity chart %ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Textures/default_cch.tif at start (it logs 'Failed to initialize Color Grading: Default color chart is missing' otherwise), merges the active chart layers into an R8G8B8A8 render target ('ColorGradingMergedLayer' / 'ColorGradingFinalMerged') with the MergeColorCharts technique and applies the result with CombineColorGradingWithColorChart; r_ColorGradingCharts, r_ColorGradingChartsCache, r_ColorGradingFilters, r_ColorGradingLevels, r_ColorGradingSelectiveColor, r_FlaresEnableColorGrading, r_ColorGrading (default 2 here) switch parts. Authoring: take a reference image, paste the manual's RGBChart.bmp into it (RC finds the chart only with that bitmap), flatten, colour-correct the whole image, save as <name>_cch.tif; Tools/rc/rc.ini preset ColorChart (file mask *_cch*, X8R8G8B8, colorspace linear, option colorchart=1, no mips) extracts the chart into a .dds. Use it: console `r_ColorGrading 1` + `r_ColorGradingChartImage <path>`, the Environment Editor's Color Grading block (Constants/ColorGrading: UseStaticTexture, Texture), or the flow nodes Image:ColorGradient and Image:ColorGradientDefaults (effects ColorGradeTexture, FadeOutHitGradeTexture, FocusStartGradeTexture; TransitionTime blends). Ashvale: ashvale_clear.env and ashvale_rain.env have UseStaticTexture=false and no chart; the engine ships no chart except the identity; RGBChart.bmp is a manual attachment not present offline. The time-of-day HDR variables (Saturation, Color balance, Film curve shoulder/midtones/toe/whitepoint, EV Min/Max/Auto compensation, Bloom amount) are the grading the project can use without a chart.

content: FlashUI (gEnv->pFlashUI, CryAction/FlashUI) reads Libs/UI/UIElements/*.xml and keeps, per UIElement, the movie file (.gfx), layer, flags (mouseevents, keyevents, cursor, controller_input ...), constraints (Align mode/halign/valign/scale/max) and the functions, events, variables, arrays and movie clips it declares. The rules it reads them by (FlashUIElement.cpp SUIElementSerializer): section and entry tags are matched case-insensitively (the GameSDK file writes <Arrays>, <MovieClips>); a name is the display name, the movie name is funcname / fscommand / varname / instancename (default: the display name) with any '_root.' prefix stripped; a duplicate display name OR movie name (case-insensitive) is DROPPED with only 'X (Y) is not unique!' in the log; an unknown attribute, an Align word it does not know (it falls back to dynamic / mid) or a param type other than bool/int/float/string (read as any) is ignored silently. TRAP: CFlashUIElement::CallFunction(name, ...) uses GetOrCreateFunctionDesc: a name the XML does not declare is NOT refused, the engine makes a 'Dynamic Created Fct' definition and calls the movie by that name; so a typo in Call("SetupScren") is silence (an error is logged only in builds with UIACTION_LOGGING). The same lookup is case-insensitive on the display name.

title: TOOLING: asset_metadata makes the missing .cryasset files with the engine's own RC job, writing into a scratch /targetroot and copying...
source: Session 2026-10-11: assets/asset_meta.py, test_asset_meta.py (13 checks); EditorCommon/AssetSystem/AssetGenerator.cpp; Tools/CryVersionSelector/cryrun.py
content:
Full title: TOOLING: asset_metadata makes the missing .cryasset files with the engine's own RC job, writing into a scratch /targetroot and copying only the new ones
The manual's Asset System page (Generating Metadata): Asset Browser > Edit > Generate/Repair All Metadata. The editor's CAssetGenerator::GenerateCryassets and the launcher's `metagen` (Tools/CryVersionSelector/cryrun.py) both run Tools/rc/rc.exe /job=Tools/cryassets/rcjob_cryassets.xml /src=<the project's Assets> (job: cgf Mesh, chr Skeleton, skin SkinnedMesh, dds Texture, mtl Material, cga, anm, cdf Character, caf Animation, wav/ogg Sound, cax, pfx Particles, cs, schematyc_ent; levels/*.* excluded). TRAP 1: asset.generate_and_repair_all_metadata is registered with REGISTER_EDITOR_AND_SCRIPT_KEYBOARD_FOCUS_COMMAND: it acts on the focused Asset Browser, so from the bridge (Python or ICommandManager) it does NOTHING; this is why an earlier bridge call 'created nothing'. TRAP 2: the job REPLACES every existing .cryasset with a new one (the only difference is a new random GUID), so running it on the project would change the GUID of all the assets that have metadata. The tool runs the same job with /targetroot=<scratch> (the editor's own CAssetGenerator::GenerateCryasset passes /targetroot too), compares RC's output with the project and copies ONLY the files that do not exist and whose source file exists (apply=true; dry run by default; re-checked at the moment of the copy; never an overwrite). RC finishes the whole project in 13 s. Measured 2026-10-11: RC wrote 828 files, 457 already existed, 371 were created (158 .cgf, 129 .dds, 58 .ogg, 26 .mtl); the _lodN.cgf files, .adb, .bspace, .tif sources and .thmb.png get none (not asset types; a LOD file belongs to its mesh's asset). After it asset_report('coverage') shows every cgf (650), dds (360) and mtl (97) with metadata, and asset_info gives a texture's details and used_by (from the .mtl metadata). The game does not read .cryasset files and the project's packager ignores them (final_packages.IGNORED).

title: TOOLING: entity_check compares each level entity's component properties in the .lyr with the engine's live serialization
source: Session 2026-10-11: checks/entity_check.py, test_entity_check.py (21 checks)
content:
Full title: TOOLING: entity_check compares each level entity's component properties in the .lyr with the engine's live serialization; a misspelt or renamed property is ignored silently
A level layer (layers/*.lyr) holds each entity as <Object Type="Entity" Name=.. EntityClass=..> with <Components><Component TypeName=.. ><properties Key="value"> (a nested structure is a child element such as <MeshScale x y z/>); legacy Lua classes use <Properties>. When the level loads, a property name the component does not have (a typo, or a member renamed in the C++ Reflect) is IGNORED WITHOUT A MESSAGE, an unregistered component type is dropped, an unregistered entity class creates no entity, and a value that cannot be read leaves the default. The existing verb bridge.component.properties <entity> <component> serialises the LIVE component with the engine's serialization (the Inspector's values; an unknown component answers with the list the entity HAS, which includes components the game DLL builds at run time: a NightLamp also has CStaticMeshComponent x2, CPointLightComponent and CParticleComponent). entity_check.py reads the layers, asks the engine per component (77 calls in 0.5 s) and reports N001 entity not loaded (error), N002 component missing (error), N003 property in the file the component lacks (warning, lists the component's properties), N004 value differs (warning; floats within 1e-4, bool true/1/false/0, nested members compared by path), N005 editor entity no layer holds, N006 not compared. Ashvale: 77 entities (NightLamp 17, Pickup 17, Villager 14, VillagePoint 9, FarmGate 7, Chest 4, AshvaleMarker 3, Interactable 3, PickupItem 3), 9 component types, clean. Positive controls: an altered COPY of the real main.lyr (misspelt property, changed value, unknown component) against the same live editor. Unsaved edits in the open editor read as N004.

title: TOOLING: an editor undo step exists only inside a CUndo scope; place_object
source: Session 2026-10-11: bridge/editor_ux.py, test_editor_ux.py (17 checks); manual: Sandbox Programming > Undo system, Notifications and Error Reporting; EditorQt/Objects/ObjectManager.cpp
content:
Full title: TOOLING: an editor undo step exists only inside a CUndo scope; place_object (the editor's Python) is already undoable, the bridge's own object verbs are not unless bridge.undo.mode is on
Sandbox records undo through IUndoManager (GetIEditor()->GetIUndoManager()): CUndo undo("name") begins a recording scope; CObjectManager::NewObject and DeleteObjects record CUndoBaseObjectNew / CUndoBaseObjectDelete only when CUndo::IsRecording(); CBaseObject::StoreUndo("name") stores the object's state before a change. The editor's own Python functions are wrapped in such scopes: general.new_object (used by place_object) leaves the step 'Create new object (name)' and Ctrl+Z removes the object. The ClaudeBridge plugin's own object verbs (bridge.object.create / transform / material / delete) had NO scope and recorded nothing; with `bridge.undo.mode on` they open one ('Claude: create Brush (name)', 'Claude: move name'; transform and material call StoreUndo first). The mode is off by default so the scratch objects of the tests (made and deleted without a step) never appear in the user's Ctrl+Z; create_object (an object the user asked for) turns it on around its call. bridge.undo.info lists the newest 10 step names via IUndoManager::GetUndoStack() and GetCommandName; bridge.undo.step undo|redo n calls IUndoManager::Undo/Redo. Undoing a creation whose object was deleted afterwards without a step is safe (CUndoBaseObjectNew::Undo finds no object, clears m_redoIsValid). editor_undo refuses an undo unless every one of the newest steps contains `expect`, because the same stack holds the user's own edits. Notifications: INotificationCenter::ShowInfo / ShowWarning / ShowCritical (title, message) show a non-modal message in the Notification Center (the manual: 'restrain yourself from using modal dialogs'); bridge.notify returns the id; the message is not a top-level window (bridge.window.list shows only the main window), so it cannot be seen from the bridge.

title: TRAP: a level's saved environment-preset list (leveldata/timeofday.xml) can differ from the exported level.pak; the game reads only the...
source: Session 2026-10-11: checks/level_check.py, test_level_check.py (29 checks); Cry3DEngine/3dEngineLoad.cpp LoadEnvironmentSettingsFromXML; WorldTools.cpp FindPreset
content:
Full title: TRAP: a level's saved environment-preset list (leveldata/timeofday.xml) can differ from the exported level.pak; the game reads only the exported one and looks its presets up by name
A level has three places for its environment: leveldata/environment.xml (Level Settings > Settings: Fog.ViewDistance, Terrain, EnvState, VolumetricCloud, Ocean, OceanAnimation, DynTexSource), leveldata/timeofday.xml (Level Settings > Environment Presets: the level's LIST of .env presets, one with Default="1") and the exported level.pak, whose mission_<name>.xml carries <Environment>, <TimeOfDay> (the list) and <Objects> (entities). The 3D engine (C3DEngine::LoadMissionDataFromXML, OpenMissionDataXML 'mission_<name>.xml') reads ONLY the exported mission in the game. Ashvale's AshvaleWeather::SetRaining finds its presets BY NAME in that list (ITimeOfDay::GetPresetsInfos, a substring match on 'ashvale_clear' / 'ashvale_rain') and SetCurrentPreset; with no match it only writes one trace line and the sky stays on the list's default. INCIDENT 2026-10-11: leveldata/timeofday.xml listed only %ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Shading/default.env (Default) since at least 2026-10-06 22:50 while the exported level.pak (2026-10-06 19:31) listed ashvale_clear (Default) and ashvale_rain; the packaged game was fine, the NEXT export would have dropped them, and the editor opened with the engine default look. Repair with the editor's own calls (as author_environment.py's tail): bridge.env.load <rain>, bridge.env.load <clear>, bridge.env.default <clear>, bridge.env.remove <engine default>, general.save_level; the list then survived a level reload and an editor restart. The cause of the loss is unknown. level_check.py (V001-V009) catches it: the saved list, the open editor's list (bridge.env.presets) and the exported list are compared with the preset names the code looks up (string literals 'ashvale_*' in the files that call FindPreset/GetPresetsInfos/SetCurrentPreset); final_packages.package() refuses on a level_check error. The environment.xml attributes are read by the loader with atof/atoi: a misspelt name keeps the default, a word reads as 0, WavesAmount is clamped to 0.4..3, WavesSize 0..3, MaxGlobalCloudDensity and ShadingLOD 0..1, MaxRayMarchStep 16..512; SunShadowsClipPlaneRange is read only when e_ObjQuality >= 3 (CheckMinSpec(3)); Fog.ViewDistance blends with ViewDistanceLowSpec by e_MaxViewDistSpecLerp (1 from spec 2) and the camera height; the manual says ViewDistance should never be under 1000; the Ocean attribute is spelt CausticsTilling (double L).

title: TOOLING: editor_suite runs every editor-only test and checks the level around it
source: Session 2026-10-11: bridge/editor_suite.py, jobs.py kind editor_suite, render_tour.py settle
content:
Full title: TOOLING: editor_suite runs every editor-only test and checks the level around it; a viewport test's thresholds belong to the look it was tuned on
editor_suite.py (start_job('editor_suite') or python bridge/editor_suite.py [names]) runs every test_*.py of the MCP server in turn (49 tests, about 8 minutes, never the game, never closing the editor) and, around each, reads the editor's object count and open dialogs through bridge.object.list / bridge.dialog.list; afterwards it looks for zz_mcp_* files under the project. A test that exits 0 but leaves the level with another object count (or a dialog) FAILS; the result is engine_data/editor_suite.json. First run 2026-10-11: 43/48, no leaks; every failure was a test that encoded the project's state before the day's work (metadata gap closed by asset_metadata, undefined surface types removed in 2026-10-08, level.validate residue names mat_zz_undefined / ZzNoSuchShader) or an instrument tuned on the old look. TRAP (viewport tests): after the level's preset list was repaired the editor shows the real ashvale_clear look (clouds, HDR eye adaptation, merged meshes): the unchanged view's frame-to-frame noise is about 0.45 levels (0.14-0.3 before), and a CVar write such as r_Gamma, even to the value it already has, leaves the next frames stale or re-adapts the exposure for a moment, so the NEXT switch (e_Sun) measured 0.2 levels instead of 33 and a control read 1.7. render_tour.tour() therefore waits one settle after restoring each variable. A threshold in a picture-based test is a function of the lighting and the exposure mode; re-measure the noise and the control whenever the look changes. Also found: scratch-material warnings stay in level.validate for the editor session (project_audit treats names containing zz_ / ZzNo as session residue). Also: the picture tests run with ed_keepEditorActive held (an idle editor gives stale frames), but holding it for a whole run ended in an EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION inside AMDXX64.DLL (the AMD driver's own thread) during render_tour; the suite holds it only around debug_views, decal_lab, lods_live, pfx_author and render_tour, fingerprints about 64 CVars plus the time of day and the current preset around every test (a leak is reported and put back), and after a crash waits up to 10 minutes for the watchdog to bring the editor back. The editor runs sys_spec 3, the shipped game 2.

title: TRAP: the 3D engine classifies a vis area by a WORD IN ITS NAME (visarea / portal / occlarea)
source: Session 2026-10-13: checks/visarea_check.py, test_visarea_check.py (37 checks), plugin verb bridge.visarea.dump; Cry3DEngine/VisAreaMan.cpp UpdateVisArea, VisAreas.cpp IsPortalIntersectAreaInValidWay; EditorQt/Objects/VisAreaShapeObject.cpp
content:
Full title: TRAP: the 3D engine classifies a vis area by a WORD IN ITS NAME (visarea / portal / occlarea): a VisArea named without 'visarea' silently does nothing; an area needs 4+ points; a portal must cross a wall
CVisAreaManager::UpdateVisArea (Cry3DEngine/VisAreaMan.cpp) lower-cases the name the editor gives it and looks for a word, in this order: "portal" -> the portal list, else "visarea" -> the vis area list, else "occlarea" -> the occluder list, else a CVisArea is created and kept in NO list (it never exists as an area; no message). What the editor passes (VisAreaShapeObject.cpp UpdateGameArea): a VisArea object's OWN name, a Portal's "Portal_<name>", an OccluderArea's "OcclArea_<name>". So a VisArea called Reeve_interior does nothing; one called visarea_portal_room is a PORTAL (portal is checked first); an OccluderArea called visarea_hide becomes a vis area (occlarea_visarea_hide contains visarea). The editor's default name for a new VisArea (VisArea1) works, which hides the trap until someone renames the object. MEASURED 2026-10-13 in the open editor with the plugin verb bridge.visarea.dump (I3DEngine::GetIVisAreaManager: GetNumberOfVisArea / GetVisAreaById): a 6 x 6 m, 4-point VisArea named zz_mcp_va_visarea_room was held (box exactly the square, 5 m high); the identical one named zz_mcp_va_plain was not; one with 3 points and the right name was not (the editor registers an area only when GetPointCount() > 3); a shape loaded through the XML route (object_props.set_shape) with the right name was held (the route does not matter, the name does).
ONE SYMPTOM PER CHUNK (split 2026-10-23, every word kept): traps-portal-connects-nothing-must-cross-one-wall-edge = A portal connects nothing or the room stays closed: it must cross one ; traps-ashvale-has-no-vis-areas-indoor-dat-is-empty = Ashvale has no vis areas: indoor.dat declares 0, 0, 0, the houses are

title: A portal connects nothing or the room stays closed: it must cross one wall edge with 1 or 2 connections (IsPortalIntersectAreaInValidWay)
source: Session 2026-10-13: checks/visarea_check.py, test_visarea_check.py (37 checks), plugin verb bridge.visarea.dump; Cry3DEngine/VisAreaMan.cpp UpdateVisArea, VisAreas.cpp IsPortalIntersectAreaInValidWay; EditorQt/Objects/VisAreaShapeObject.cpp
content: Portals: CVisArea::IsPortalIntersectAreaInValidWay needs the portal's box to overlap the area's and, for a vertical portal, the portal's FIRST 4 points to form a quad of which exactly two OPPOSITE edges cross one wall edge of the area (the manual: 'half inside, half outside, thick enough to protrude on both sides'); the horizontal case is 4 bottom points inside and the top 4 out, or the reverse. A valid portal has 1 connection (to the outdoors) or 2 (room to room, opposite normals); more is invalid (IsPortalValid). IsConnectedToOutdoor: a portal with exactly 1 connection, or an area with such a portal. Measured: a 2 x 2 m quad (Height 3) across the room's east wall connected the room (portal connections [room]; both connected_to_outdoor true); the identical quad lying inside the room connected nothing (connections [], closed). GetVisAreaConnections of an AREA returns the neighbouring rooms behind its portals, of a PORTAL the areas it joins. A point test is exact: 8 m above a 5 m high room, or 7 m outside its wall, is in no area.

title: Ashvale has no vis areas: indoor.dat declares 0, 0, 0, the houses are open to the outdoors; visarea_check rules V001-V010

content: The exported level.pak holds the compiled manager in terrain/indoor.dat (SVisAreaManChunkHeader: int8 version 6, dummy, flags, flags2, int chunkSize, int visAreas, int portals, int occluders): Ashvale's is a 20-byte header declaring 0, 0, 0: the nine houses are open to the outdoors (no interior culling, none of the vis area lighting rules: AffectedBySun/IgnoreSkyColor/IgnoreGI). Adding vis areas would change the interiors' look and cost and needs a re-export and a game run: not applied. Tools: visarea_check (V001 name not classified as its kind, V002 under 4 points, V003 portal connects nothing, V004 area no portal reaches, V005 portal with 3+ connections, V006 layer object the engine lacks, V007 stale export counts, V008 engine area no object explains, V009 no areas, V010 portal over 4 points; project_audit validator 'vis areas and portals'); create_object returns a warnings entry when the name will not work. The earlier F4 trial (2026-10-07: a scratch VisArea 'changed the picture by 0.06 against noise 0.02') had a name without the word: it was never registered.

title: TRAPS: I3DEngine::GetVisAreaFromPos answers null when the area tree is stale (not 'outdoors')
source: Session 2026-10-13: plugin ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp bridge.visarea.dump and bridge.shape.add_points; Cry3DEngine/VisAreaMan.cpp UpdateAABBTree / SetCurAreas; EditorQt/Objects/ShapeObject.cpp CalcBBox, InsertPoint
content:
Full title: TRAPS: I3DEngine::GetVisAreaFromPos answers null when the area tree is stale (not 'outdoors'); a shape re-centres itself on its first point after every inserted point
GetVisAreaFromPos reads CVisAreaManager::m_pAABBTree, which every UpdateVisArea / DeleteVisArea deletes and only a rendered frame (SetCurAreas, when e_Portals != 0) or an intersection query (IntersectsVisAreas, ClipOutsideVisAreas) rebuilds. Asked cold it returns null, which reads as 'outdoors'. The plugin verb bridge.visarea.dump therefore calls p3D->IntersectsVisAreas(tiny box) before probing and ALSO reports 'inside': the direct per-area IsPointInsideVisArea test, which does not depend on the tree; positive and negative controls (a point in the room, 8 m above it, 7 m beside it) are in test_visarea_check.py.
CShapeObject::CalcBBox moves the object to its FIRST point and shifts the local points to match, after every InsertPoint. The bridge verb bridge.shape.add_points used to compute the world-to-local transform once before its loop, so an object that was not created ON its first point (the editor's create_object puts it at the position you give) had every later point displaced by the first point's offset (measured: a portal asked at x 102..104, y 99..101 held x 101..103, y 97..99). The verb now takes the transform per point (ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp, deployed 2026-10-13; the 6 x 6 m room's box is exactly the asked square). create_ai_path was never affected: it creates the path on its first waypoint. object_props.set_shape (the XML route) was never affected either: it re-reads what the object holds.

title: LEARNING: the 54 designer.* Python functions only SWITCH TO an interactive tool
source: Session 2026-10-13: Sandbox/Plugins/CryDesigner/Scripts/*.cpp, Tools/Modify/BooleanTool.cpp; Editor/Scripts/CryDesigner/HelloWorld*.py; manual: Designer Tool, Designer Tool Tab, Advanced - Tools, Advanced - Extrude/Delete
content:
Full title: LEARNING: the 54 designer.* Python functions only SWITCH TO an interactive tool; the scripting API the shipped HelloWorld.py uses is commented out in 5.7.1
The editor's Python module designer has 54 functions (allnoneselection, boolean, box, extrude, offset, slice, mirror, lathe, loopcut, weld, fill, flip, merge, export ...) and none takes an argument: each is REGISTER_DESIGNER_TOOL_WITH_PROPERTYTREE_PANEL_AND_COMMAND(.., "designer.boolean") and means 'switch to that tool', after which the work is done with the mouse in the viewport or a button in the tool's property panel. The Boolean tool's Union / Subtract / Intersection are Serialization ActionButtons (BooleanTool.cpp, BooleanOperation: the FIRST selected object is kept, the later ones are merged in and deleted) with no command behind them, and BooleanTool::Enter shows a MODAL MessageBox ('At least two designer objects should be selected') when fewer than two Designer objects are selected, which would block an unattended call. The scripting layer that would have made Designer scriptable (designer.start, designer.end, set_env, record_undo, update_mesh, add_box, add_sphere, start_polygon_addition, add_vertex_to_polygon, finish_polygon_addition, select, extrude(arguments), offset(arguments), subdivide, weld, flip ...) sits in Scripts/BasicScripts.cpp, ShapeScripts.cpp, EditScripts.cpp, ModifyScripts.cpp and SelectionScripts.cpp inside /* ... */ comments, so the two shipped examples Editor/Scripts/CryDesigner/HelloWorld.py and HelloWorld_3D.py cannot run (measured 2026-10-13: hasattr(designer, name) is False for start, add_box, start_polygon_addition, select, update_mesh). The classes (DesignerObject, Model with Union/Subtract/Intersect) are not exported from CryDesigner.dll, so a plugin cannot call them either. Consequences for Ashvale: door and window openings cannot be cut by script; the build_mesh / FBX route stays the way, and Designer objects stay a hand tool (the manual: the physics mesh of a Designer object is the exact render shape, so keep it simple).

title: TOOLING: frame_profile records the next N frames of the open editor with the engine's boot profiler (sys_bp_frames) and reports...
source: Session 2026-10-13: screens/frame_profile.py, test_frame_profile.py (22 checks); CrySystem/BootProfiler.cpp; manual: Loadtime Profiling
content:
Full title: TOOLING: frame_profile records the next N frames of the open editor with the engine's boot profiler (sys_bp_frames) and reports per-function CPU time, hitch frames with their cause, and A/B differences against a repeat control
The boot profiler (CrySystem/BootProfiler.cpp) writes sessions as XML to %USER%/TestResults/bp_<session>.xml, opened in Tools/ProfVis/ProfVis.exe (manual: Loadtime Profiling). Sessions: boot (-bootprofiler on the command line, or sys_bp_enabled), level (sys_bp_level_load 1) and frames: the console COMMAND `sys_bp_frames <n>` records the next n frames as bp_frames.xml. MEASURED in the Sandbox editor 2026-10-13: it writes nothing while sys_bp_enabled is 0 (its default, VF_DEV_ONLY), and an idle editor produces no frames, so the capture sets sys_bp_enabled 1, holds ed_keepEditorActive (live 0 -> 1) for about a second and puts both back (a long hold has crashed this machine's AMD driver). The file: <root><thread name totalTimeMS totalBlocks><block name totalTimeMS startTime stopTime args> nested; blocks shorter than sys_bp_time_threshold (0.1 ms) are not written; sys_bp_format 1 writes Chrome Trace JSON instead. One frame = a top-level CSystem::Update block on the Main thread plus what follows up to the next one. 13 threads in the editor: Main, RenderThread, AudioMainThread, JobSystem_Worker_0..7, Helpers.
Measured on the Ashvale viewport (editor, sys_spec 3, 240 frames = 1.2 s): the main thread costs 2.5 ms per frame; the largest single cost is PVRNUpdateSpines (the merged-mesh vegetation/grass animation), 3.76 ms per frame of WORKER-thread time over 8 workers; e_MergedMeshes 0 removes it entirely (repeat noise 0.001 ms), e_Vegetation 0 removes it plus COctreeNode::RenderVegetations (1.97 ms per frame) and takes the main thread from 2.54 to 1.95 ms. The A/B method is capture A, capture B with the CVar set, capture A again: a difference counts only above 3 x the A-vs-A noise and 0.05 ms. A hitch finder compares each frame with the median (ratio 1.8 and 1 ms more) and names the functions whose self time in that frame exceeds their usual: on Ashvale it found a 6.21 ms frame against a 2.48 ms median every second, CLog::LogV +1.96 ms and EntitySystem::UpdateEntityComponents +1.66 ms: the NightLamp bug (see the trap chunk). The editor's frame is not the shipped game's; the level-load session and MemReplay need a game run.

title: TRAP/BUG: a state-comparison guard that compares a field the builder never sets rebuilds every second
source: Session 2026-10-13: Code/Components/NightLamp.cpp (Build, BuiltAsIs, ProcessEvent); frame_profile capture; <engine source checkout>
content:
Full title: TRAP/BUG: a state-comparison guard that compares a field the builder never sets rebuilds every second; the NightLamp torches did it since September (found with the frame profiler)
CNightLampComponent::ProcessEvent(Update) checks once a second `if (!BuiltAsIs()) Rebuild("rebuilt"); else SetLit(WantLit(), ...)`. BuiltAsIs() compares m_builtKind, m_builtDiffuse, m_builtBulb AND m_builtRadius with the current properties, but Build() (the torch/lantern path) recorded only the first three; only BuildRoom() recorded the radius. For the eight non-Room lamps m_builtRadius stayed at its -1.0f initial value, so BuiltAsIs() was false every time and each lamp rebuilt itself every second for as long as the level ran, in the editor and in the game: mesh LoadFromDisk + ResetObject, light parameters, flame component (Activate(false) then true), slot material, plus LampTrace, which does CryLog AND an fopen/append/fclose on the hard-coded <engine source checkout> Evidence: that file reached 158 MB / 2.3 million lines with about 111,000 `Lamp_X: out (rebuilt, N h)` lines per lamp (the other big senders are the nav-link traces, ~125,000 lines each); the frame profile showed 8 CLog::LogV writes (0.2-0.4 ms each) in one frame per second, a 6.2 ms frame against a 2.5 ms median. A flame that restarts every second can also be a visible flicker. Fix (2026-10-13): Build() sets m_builtRadius = m_radius; built into Game.dll with the ClaudeGameBuild task at 13:20 (it also compiled the 2026-10-07 Health.cpp). Verified in the editor with the same 240-frame frame_profile capture: +32 lamp 'rebuilt' lines before, 0 after; longest frame 6.2 ms (median 2.5) before, 3.3 ms (median 2.4) after. The packaged builds still contain the bug until the next package. General lesson: when a guard decides whether to redo work by comparing a recorded state with the current one, every compared field must be recorded by EVERY builder path; a one-per-second log line in the trace file is the symptom.

title: TOOLING: a Python/PySide2 pane inside Sandbox without touching the engine folder: SandboxBridge.register_window at run time
source: Session 2026-10-13: bridge/editor_panel.py, test_editor_panel.py (25 checks); Plugins/SandboxPythonBridge; EditorQt/Util/BoostPythonHelpers.cpp LoadPythonPlugins; manual: Sandbox Python Plugins
content:
Full title: TOOLING: a Python/PySide2 pane inside Sandbox without touching the engine folder: SandboxBridge.register_window at run time, general.open_pane, closed through its own floating window
Sandbox runs Editor/Python/plugins/*/startup.py at start-up (crytools first), but only under the ENGINE install (BoostPythonHelpers.cpp: GetSandboxPythonPath() = <engine path>/Editor/Python); a project folder is not scanned. The supported alternative is the module SandboxBridge (the SandboxPythonBridge plugin): register_window(window_type, name, category="", needs_menu_item=True, menu_path="", unique=True) puts a QWidget subclass into the editor's class factory as a view pane (the factory keeps a reference to the type; call it ONCE per session: the registration is gone when the editor restarts, and a second registration would add a second class of the same name; check `name in general.get_pane_class_names()` first). general.open_pane("<name>") opens it (IEditor::OpenView; flagged 'modal' in the catalog by a heuristic, it is not). The widget is created by calling the type with no arguments. There is no close_pane (the help text of get_pane_class_names mentions one): measured, the pane opens as its own FLOATING plain QWidget titled like the pane (chain ClaudeStatusPanel > QWidget > QWidget > QStackedWidget > QWidget > QWidget[isWindow]), and is closed with top.close() on that window; a docked pane would have the main frame as top-level window, which must never be closed from code.
The editor's interpreter is Python 3.7.3 with PySide2 5.12.3, shared with execute_python (globals persist between calls) and running on the editor's MAIN thread. Rules that follow: no syntax newer than 3.7 (test with ast.parse(src, feature_version=(3, 7))); a refresh timer must never raise (wrap it); and nothing inside the pane may call the bridge socket, start a process or sleep: the bridge answers on the very thread that would be waiting, so the editor deadlocks. The Claude Status pane (editor_panel.py) therefore only reads small JSON files and cheap in-process calls (general.get_current_level_name, get_objects_count). Tool: editor_panel status|open|close; open it only when the user wants to watch.

title: TOOLING: object_check compares every non-entity layer object
source: Session 2026-10-13: checks/object_check.py, test_object_check.py (22 checks)
content:
Full title: TOOLING: object_check compares every non-entity layer object (brush, navigation area, probe) with the editor's live serialization; a component's instance guid changes at every load
A layer file (layers/*.lyr) stores each object as <Object Type=.. Name=.. attr=...> plus child nodes (CollisionFiltering, Points, Components/Component ...). The bridge's bridge.object.xml <name> (object_props.get_xml) writes the live object back through the editor's serializer: every property it keeps. object_check compares attribute by attribute (numbers within 0.001, comma lists member by member) and child by child: O001 object not held by the editor (error), O002 attribute in the file the live object lacks (the engine ignored it, silently), O003 value differs (clamped or not read), O004 only live (the file predates the property), O005 child node differs, O006 object count differs, O007 duplicate name. Ashvale: 230 objects (221 brushes, 8 NavigationAreas, the ValleyProbe EnvironmentProbe), all match, 1.1 s for 230 bridge calls. The only first-run difference was a Component's `guid` attribute (EnvironmentProbe's Components/Component): the editor creates a new component INSTANCE guid at every level load (stable within a session, different from the saved file's), so it is identity, not a setting, and is not compared. Brush files made by the editor itself (place_object, build_ashvale.py) always match; the check guards hand-edited layer XML and property renames.

title: LEARNING: layer streaming needs UseLayersActivation (level EnvState) AND e_ObjectLayersActivation
source: Session 2026-10-13: manual Layer Streaming Optimization; Cry3DEngine/3dEngineLoad.cpp:1461, 3dEngine.h:626, cvars.cpp:778; Assets/levels/ashvale/leveldata/environment.xml, layers/main.lyr
content:
Full title: LEARNING: layer streaming needs UseLayersActivation (level EnvState) AND e_ObjectLayersActivation, is scripted with the LayerSwitch flow node, and is off in Ashvale
Layer streaming hides and unhides whole layers at run time. It needs two switches: the level's EnvState UseLayersActivation (environment.xml; C3DEngine::m_bAreaActivationInUse, read in 3dEngineLoad.cpp) and the CVar e_ObjectLayersActivation (VF_CHEAT; default 0 in the editor, 1 in the game; setting 2 activates ALL object layers and 3 deactivates them all at once (C3DEngine::ProcessCVarsChange), 4 draws each layer's box labelled ON/OFF), then a flow graph with the Engine:LayerSwitch node (inputs Layer, Hide, Unhide, EnableSerialization; outputs Hidden, Unhidden). IsAreaActivationInUse() is the AND of both. The layer's DefaultLoaded flag loads it at level load but does NOT unhide it (the graph must unhide the first layers). es_LayerDebugInfo 1 shows the active layers, 2 stats, 3 memory per layer (brushes, entities), 4 pak stats, 5 activation. Limits (manual): intended for pure game mode, children of a hidden layer are hidden in the game but not in editor game mode, triggers in a hidden layer do not work, physics proxies and vegetation (stored in the cry file) are not affected. Ashvale: environment.xml has UseLayersActivation="0" and the level has one object layer, Main (221 brushes, 77 entities, 8 navigation areas, 1 probe, DefaultLoaded 0), plus the Terrain layer file: streaming is off and the flags are inert, which is right for about 300 objects in a 1 km area. A level-load profile (sys_bp_level_load) needs a game run.

title: PLAYBOOK: START HERE - how to build a game with these tools: the order of work and the rules that hold
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
ORDER OF WORK for any task. (1) health_check: is the editor up, is the package stale, what changed. (2) tool_guide() lists every tool by family; query_knowledge("<your question in plain words>") BEFORE any unfamiliar step; search_manual / read_manual_page read CRYENGINE's own offline manual (read it first, it is the user's rule). (3) Make assets: make_texture -> write_material -> build_mesh (each lints what it wrote), then lint_assets. (4) Put things in the level: place_object / create_object / spline_points / create_ai_path (the editor must be open; they never save), then check with object_check, entity_check, level_check. (5) project_audit runs 22 engine-owned validators in about 5 s and lists what is NEW since the accepted baseline: run it after any change. (6) snapshot_project BEFORE anything that deletes, overwrites or rebuilds in bulk (the project has no version control). (7) Packaging: start_job('package', {'config': 'release'}, allow_editor_close=true) closes the editor: tell the user first.
RULES THAT HOLD: use the engine's own tools and documented processes, never a home-made builder; the ENGINE FILES STAY ORIGINAL (the engine source is a read-only reference; the ClaudeBridge plugin DLL is the one project file in the engine folder); nothing is downloaded without the user's yes naming file, source and size; do NOT run the game unless the user says so (editor-only work: the viewport, files, catalogs); a graceful editor close SAVES the level, so every experiment's scratch objects need try/finally deletes; patch files with the Edit tool (a Bash-heredoc Python with backslashes broke six files) and ast.parse a Python file before writing it; measure with a CONTROL and say openly when a claim is retracted; keep reports short. If the editor is gone, any tool call brings it back by itself (about 25 s; wait_for_editor waits). Regression: python bridge/editor_suite.py runs all editor-only tests; tool_smoke.py proves every tool still answers.
DEEPER: playbook-symptom-to-tool (a symptom -> the checker), playbook-new-level-and-terrain, playbook-navmesh, playbook-material-pipeline, playbook-find-components, playbook-write-cpp-component, playbook-dialogue-and-voice, playbook-editor-recovery.
CURRENT COUNTS AND WHAT HAS NEVER BEEN SEEN WORKING: status-current (generated: tool, test and chunk counts, the chunks whose claims were never seen working).

title: PLAYBOOK: something does not work - which checker to run for which symptom
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
The engine drops many mistakes SILENTLY (an unknown property, attribute, feature, node, function or name). Each checker below asks the engine's OWN loader what it kept and compares with the file.
mesh renders flat grey -> lint_assets (L001: the .cgf names a material that does not exist) and material_check. A material looks wrong / a shader flag does nothing -> material_check, shader_info(gen_mask=...), pbs_check. A component or entity property you set has no effect -> entity_check (every entity's component properties vs the engine's live serialization), component_properties(entity, component) to read it live. A brush, area or probe property has no effect -> object_check. A UI function call does nothing -> ui_check (an undeclared name is a SILENT dynamic call). A particle effect is missing or its keys are ignored -> pfx_check (the loader DROPS unknown features/keys) and pfx_preview. An NPC will not walk -> nav_reach / nav_map (see playbook-navmesh), bt_check for the behaviour tree, uqs_check for a UQS query. A flow graph does nothing -> flow_check (an unknown class or port DISCARDS the whole graph). A sound is silent or has no distance falloff -> gamesdk_audio, audio_triggers, audio_report; on this machine's 7.1 output the SDL implementation never attenuates, the game does distance gain itself. Time of day / environment wrong after a restart, or a preset the game looks up is missing -> env_check, env_variables, level_check. A vis area or portal does nothing -> visarea_check (the engine classifies an area by a WORD IN ITS NAME: visarea / portal / occlarea). Animation or blend space broken -> anim_check, mannequin_check. A character floats or stalls -> get_entity_physics, sample_entity_physics, plan_character_collider. A frame hitch or 'what costs CPU' -> frame_profile (the engine's own frame profiler on the editor viewport). The decal does not show -> decal_preview. The sequence/cinematic does not play -> sequence_check. 'Is the project healthy / what changed?' -> project_audit. 'Is my package out of date?' -> health_check. A CVar does nothing in the packaged game -> cvar_info (cheat CVars are refused in Release). 'A tool says the editor is not open' -> tools restart it themselves now; playbook-editor-recovery.

title: PLAYBOOK: build a new level from scratch - create the terrain, layers, vegetation, borders, lighting, navigation, export
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: PLAYBOOK: build a new level from scratch - create the terrain, layers, vegetation, borders, lighting, navigation, export (the order that works)
1. PLAN zones as layers (parent layer per zone; only Main, Audio, Player_Collisions DefaultLoaded; layer streaming is optional and off in a small level). 2. TERRAIN: GenerateTerrain cannot make a specific landscape; build the heightmap outside (make_heightmap.py) and install it with bridge.terrain.set_heights_raw; read it back with bridge.terrain.info (elevationMin/Max/Avg) before judging a picture. Terrain layers use Terrain.Layer materials (diffuse/ddna/displ, TileU about 0.3): select_terrain_layer, set_terrain_layer_texture, then generate_surface_texture (it reports coveragePercent per layer: a near-zero layer's mask never opened). A level made by create_level renders its terrain BLACK until the terrain texture is exported: look for 'RGB multiplier: 0' in the load log and run bridge.terrain.export_texture 4096 8. 3. VEGETATION: paint with the editor's own brush (bridge.vegetation.paint = CVegetationMap::PaintBrush; paint_hills.py, paint_grass.py are the repeatable scripts), erase with bridge.vegetation.clear; grass auto-merged and dense. 4. BORDERS: create_collision_wall segments along the edge; kill volumes = shape + AreaTrigger. 5. LIGHTING: the look lives in the level's environment presets (libs/environmentpresets/<name>.env, authored through bridge.env.* calls, never bridge.env.set for a value you care about: it writes one value into every key of the day curve); an ambient probe per place; level_check makes sure the level's preset list holds the presets the game looks up by name. 6. NAVIGATION: playbook-navmesh. 7. PLACE content: playbook-material-pipeline for new meshes, place_object for existing ones. 8. EXPORT: export_level (exporter.export_to_engine) once geometry is final; it also saves the navmesh; then level_check (the exported pack must match the source), level_stats (triangles, draw cost, physics proxies over the limit), level_validate, project_audit. Deeper: a working note of the originating project (not in this repository) section 8 and the project notes NOW AS TOOLS: steps 2-3 (terrain, layers, vegetation) are the tools new_level, terrain_shape, terrain_height, terrain_layers, vegetation, save_level - see playbook-build-world-tools; the raw bridge.terrain.export_texture is safe to repeat since the 2026-10-13 plugin (trap-export-texture-sh-threads).

title: PLAYBOOK: bake (generate) the navigation mesh so AI characters can walk - areas, seed, regenerate, check, export
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content: 1. The agent type lives in Assets/scripts/AI/Navigation.xml and its SIZES ARE IN VOXELS (Villager: radius 4, height 16, voxelSize 0.125 = 0.5 m x 2.0 m); the component must be given the same name (SetNavigationAgentType("Villager")). 2. create_navigation_area(points, floor_z, height, exclusion, remove_inaccessible_triangles): a few big inclusion areas, exclusion areas for houses and rocks (a house door is cut out of the mesh on purpose in this project and crossed with an off-mesh link). 3. create_nav_seed_point on the MAIN walkable ground: with no seed nothing is removed, with a seed every island not connected to it is removed (a seed on a rooftop or in a rock makes most of the mesh vanish). 4. regenerate_navigation(0) = ai.regenerate_agent_type_layer0: no dialog (the 'all types' variants open a MODAL question dialog and block an unattended run). 5. CHECK with the engine's own connectivity test: nav_map (an ASCII map of what connects to the origin) and nav_reach (is each target connected; it does not know off-mesh links or dynamic obstacles). 6. EXPORT once (export_level): the mesh is saved as mnmnav<mission>.bai in level.pak; until then it is in memory only and every editor restart loses it (the symptom: the NPC log says 'route built, 0 of N waypoints usable (off the navmesh)'). 7. Patrol routes: create_ai_path(points, agent_type, closed) lays an AI Path and tests each point against the mesh; indoor waypoints use the walkable floor height, not the terrain elevation. Deeper chunks: nav-regen-no-modal, nav-export-persists, nav-seed-prune-rule, nav-agent-type, npc-duplicate-components (duplicate navigation components saved into a layer give velocity 0).

title: PLAYBOOK: make a new prop or building - texture, material with a normal map, mesh, LODs, lint (the pipeline and its rules)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content: Order: make_texture(surface, name, size) writes diffuse, normal (_ddna) and height sources and compiles them with the engine's RC; write_material(path, submaterials) writes the .mtl (every sub-material needs a SurfaceType the project defines in Libs/MaterialEffects/SurfaceTypes.xml, or the engine falls back to mat_default); build_mesh(spec) writes the .cgf with its material named INSIDE it and, with lods/detail, the $lodN_ nodes under the base mesh; then lint_assets. RULES: a final smoothness is Shininess/255 TIMES the _ddna alpha (pbs_check); a .cgf names its material inside (chunk 0x1014): when a mesh renders flat grey read that name first (lint L001); a mesh path must not contain '_lod' (the engine refuses it and draws the default sphere); height maps need the preset inside the TIFF; a normal map made with too high a strength looks fine by day and wrong by a lamp at night; Illum always ORs in NORMAL_MAP and SUBSURFACE_SCATTERING, a shader flag name the shader lacks does nothing (shader_info shows the real flags); material_check loads every .mtl through the engine and reports what it resolved. After ANY change to a material's flags or texture slots the shipped shader cache is stale (health_check says so): shader_cache_refresh.py, repackage, shader tour (0 misses). Place the result with place_object (kind, asset path, name, position). Deeper: build_mesh and make_texture tool docs, TRAP 'a .cgf built by an older script names a material file that does not exist'.

title: PLAYBOOK: which components, nodes, CVars and editor functions exist - the catalogs to ask instead of guessing
tags: what can I add to an entity
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content: schematyc_search(text) / schematyc_info(name): the engine's own registry of entity components (83 including the project's), 520 functions and 46 signals, read from the running editor; a component's registered NAME is the C++ class name (CNightLampComponent), shown in the error when you give a wrong one. component_properties(entity, component[, values]) reads or sets a live component's properties. entity_class_properties(classes) reads the default Properties of LUA entity classes (project first, then the GameSDK sample's paks; Door, RigidBodyEx, HealthPack ...). list_entities / list_objects list what the open level holds; object_types lists the 36 object kinds the editor can create (create_object); object_properties reads/sets any object's properties through the editor's serializer. editor_api(text) = the 586 editor Python functions with arguments; editor_commands = every registered command; editor_panes; cvar_search / cvar_info / spec_group = 2,484 console variables and 278 commands with where each can be set (Release refuses cheat CVars); flow_nodes (642 flow node types with ports), bt_nodes (65 behaviour tree nodes), uqs_catalog, particle_search / particle_info (54 features, 11 modifiers), shader_search / shader_info, asset_info / asset_report, rc_presets / rc_options. For concepts rather than names: search_manual / read_manual_page.

title: PLAYBOOK: write and build a new C++ gameplay component (the pattern of Health.h/.cpp, registration, build, traps)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content: Pattern (Code/Components/Health.h and Health.cpp are the smallest real example). Header: `class CHealthComponent final : public IEntityComponent` with `static void ReflectType(Schematyc::CTypeDesc<CHealthComponent>& desc);`, `virtual Cry::Entity::EventFlags GetEventMask() const override;` and `virtual void ProcessEvent(const SEntityEvent& event) override;`. Source: ReflectType calls desc.SetGUID("{NEW-GUID}"_cry_guid) (a fresh GUID per component), SetEditorCategory("Game"), SetLabel, SetDescription; a static function `Schematyc::CEnvRegistrationScope scope = registrar.Scope(IEntity::GetEntityScopeGUID()); scope.Register(SCHEMATYC_MAKE_ENV_COMPONENT(CHealthComponent));` is registered with CRY_STATIC_AUTO_REGISTER_FUNCTION(&Register...). GetEventMask returns the events wanted (Cry::Entity::EEvent::Update | Reset | EditorPropertyChanged ...); in ProcessEvent the Update event's event.fParam[0] is the frame time; return early with gEnv->IsEditing() when the code must not run in the editor. Saves: override GameSerialize(TSerialize) and NeedGameSerialize(). Add the .cpp/.h to Code/CMakeLists.txt (the build re-runs the generator). BUILD: Game.dll is locked while Sandbox runs, so it is built by the scheduled task ClaudeGameBuild (schtasks /Run /TN ClaudeGameBuild; it force-kills the editor, runs cmake --build of the Game target, relaunches Sandbox WITHOUT a level: reopen ashvale and re-apply the time of day); read <engine source checkout>; a failed build still relaunches the editor; snapshot_project first; the project's bin/win_x64/Game.dll is the only output (nothing in the engine folder). TRAPS: a character's components are rebuilt on entering game mode (docs/engine-lifetimes.md): never hold a component pointer across a frame, level reload or game-mode switch; use GetOrCreateParticleComponent, never GetOrCreateComponent<CParticleComponent>; a std::thread the DLL starts must stop at ESYSTEM_EVENT_FAST/FULL_SHUTDOWN; a guard that decides whether to rebuild by comparing recorded state must have EVERY compared field recorded by EVERY build path (NightLamp rebuilt itself every second for weeks because Build() never set m_builtRadius; frame_profile found it); since 5.6 entity timers are on the component and GetEventMask returns Cry::Entity::EventFlags. Verify without the game: frame_profile (no hitch), entity_check (the editor loads the component and keeps its properties), project_audit.

title: PLAYBOOK: NPC dialogue and voice lines - the Dynamic Response System, subtitles, voice rendering
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content: The engine's Dynamic Response System (DRS) separates WHAT HAPPENED from WHAT IS SAID: game code only sends a signal; the data in Assets/libs/DynamicResponseSystem (response files and dialog files) decides which line is spoken. In this project Code/Components/Dialogue.cpp registers it: VillagerSpeak(entity, "sg_villager_sees_player") makes that entity's DRS actor react to the signal; console commands claude_say <entity> <signal> sends one by hand and claude_drs_reload re-reads the files from disk. Subtitles are drawn by the GAME (ISpeakerManager::IListener), DRS only chooses the line. CHECK without the game: drs_check asks the running DRS what it holds (12 action and 12 condition types, its dialog lines and each response as it KEPT it) and compares with the files: a misspelt class is dropped silently and a non-JSON response file becomes an EMPTY response with no log. VOICE: render_voices / preview_voice use Piper, an offline text-to-speech (installed with the user's permission; a clear step up from Windows TTS, about 0.6 s per line); processing that smears periodicity ('resample + overlap-add pitch shifting') makes speech eldritch: resample alone. Audio is played through ACE triggers on SDL mixer (no middleware); the project's voice files are .ogg (the packager has no *.wav in its copy whitelist).

title: TRAP: a picture test's geometry depends on the editor window's layout, which a restart changes; a monochrome debug view is not 'blank'
source: Session 2026-10-13: bridge/editor_window.py, test_editor_window.py, debug_views.py, bridge_shoot.py
content: The editor's picture tests (debug_views, decal_lab, lods_live, pfx_author, render_tour) crop the editor window capture to the Perspective pane and measure boxes as fractions of that picture. After a watchdog restart the editor window comes back at its SAVED size and monitor (1018 x 763 on the second monitor, against 1018 x 453 when the tests were tuned) and the dock layout now imposes a minimum size of 1018 x 519 (QMainWindow.minimumSizeHint), so the old hard-coded crop box (debug_views.VIEWPORT_CROP, two sizes) no longer applied and the whole window with its panels was measured: 'the pictures differ in size', a LOD box change of 1.75 against a noise of 0.88, a decal control. Fix: editor_window.viewport_box() asks the editor's own Qt for the render surface of the first visible QFrame called Perspective (innermost widget of its chain) and subtracts the window's top-left corner; crop_viewport uses it for every size it does not know (489 x 374 at 1018 x 519, verified by looking at the crop). The shooter accepts a frame on SATURATION >= 8 because an undrawn viewport is flat grey; the wireframe debug view (white lines on dark) measures about 3.8 and was refused as BLANK ('1 shot(s) never settled'): bridge_shoot.py takes an optional 4th field with a lower bar and debug_views uses 2.0 for the wireframe, then requires a luminance spread of at least 10 so a blank frame still fails. Do not hard-code pixel boxes of the editor window: ask the editor.

title: PLAYBOOK: build a new level from scratch with the tools - new_level, terrain_shape, terrain_height, terrain_layers, vegetation, save_level
tags: create a new level with the tools
source: Session 2026-10-13: world_build.py / terrain_gen.py / test_world_build.py (42 live checks on a scratch level) and Code/Sandbox/EditorQt/{GameExporter.cpp, IndirectLighting/SHHeightmapAccessibility.cpp}, Code/CryEngine/CrySystem/SystemThreading.cpp
content:
Full title: PLAYBOOK: build a new level from scratch with the tools - new_level, terrain_shape, terrain_height, terrain_layers, vegetation, save_level (the exact order, the numbers, the traps)
All six need the editor open (health_check says if it is); none runs the game. They work on ANY level, not only Ashvale. Measured by test_world_build.py: 42 checks on a scratch level that is deleted again.
THEN: place objects (place_object / create_object with z from terrain_height), navigation (playbook-navmesh), level_validate, level_check, export_level.
ONE SYMPTOM PER CHUNK (split 2026-10-23, every word kept): playbook-world-tools-create-the-level-and-shape-the-terrain = Create a level and shape its ground: new_level(name, resolution, unit_; playbook-world-tools-ground-height-for-placing-things = Where is the ground? terrain_height(points) gives the z for every buil; trap-new-level-terrain-is-black-until-terrain-layers-bake = A new level's terrain is BLACK: terrain_layers add + bake (generate_su; playbook-world-tools-vegetation-add-a-brush-paint-clear = Add trees and grass: vegetation(add a brush from a mesh - the path is ; playbook-world-tools-save-level-does-not-write-navmesh-or-level-pak = save_level saves terrain, layers, vegetation and objects but NOT the n; trap-world-tools-heightmap-index-levels-prefix-zz-mcp-scratch = World-building traps: heightmap is [x, y], create_level wants 'levels/

title: Create a level and shape its ground: new_level(name, resolution, unit_size) then terrain_shape(style, flat_zones, erosion, preview)
source: Session 2026-10-13: world_build.py / terrain_gen.py / test_world_build.py (42 live checks on a scratch level) and Code/Sandbox/EditorQt/{GameExporter.cpp, IndirectLighting/SHHeightmapAccessibility.cpp}, Code/CryEngine/CrySystem/SystemThreading.cpp
content:
1. new_level(name, resolution=1024, unit_size=1.0): the editor's own general.create_level. resolution 128..4096 samples per side, unit_size 0.25..16 m per sample (1024 at 1.0 = a 1 km square). It SAVES the level it leaves first (leaving a modified level opens a blocking 'Save Level?' prompt), refuses a name that exists (nothing is overwritten) and answers the new terrain's numbers. A new level is empty (0 objects), flat at 32 m, water at 16 m, max-height setting 1024, and its terrain draws BLACK until step 4.
2. terrain_shape(style='hills'|'mountains'|'island'|'flat', seed, base_height, max_height, flat_zones, erosion, preview): call it with preview=True first: it reports min/max, the share of ground steeper than 30 degrees, and each flat zone's real height and spread, and installs nothing. flat_zones=[{x, y, radius, blend, height}] are WORLD METRES and cut level platforms for buildings (height defaults to the ground's mean there). Default relief scales with the terrain's size (a small map is not a cliff); erosion = droplets (about 250 per 1,000 samples is a visible drainage). The old ground is backed up first (engine_data/terrain_backups, newest 12): terrain_shape(restore=<that path>) puts it back. Same seed = same ground.
