title: TRAP: exporting the terrain texture twice in one editor session stopped the editor with 'Error spawning SHLighting__0 thread' - the cause
source: Session 2026-10-13: world_build.py / terrain_gen.py / test_world_build.py (42 live checks on a scratch level) and Code/Sandbox/EditorQt/{GameExporter.cpp, IndirectLighting/SHHeightmapAccessibility.cpp}, Code/CryEngine/CrySystem/SystemThreading.cpp
content:
Full title: TRAP: exporting the terrain texture twice in one editor session stopped the editor with 'Error spawning SHLighting__0 thread' - the cause (auto-export mode = high quality = indirect lighting) and the fix
SYMPTOM (2026-10-13): bridge.terrain.export_texture timed out ('waiting for the editor main thread'); the editor showed a modal 'CRYENGINE FATAL ERROR - Error spawning "SHLighting__0" thread.'; clicking OK opened 'Crash - Proceed with Save?' (ANSWER NO: never save a level after a crash); error.log then listed threads SHLighting_0..SHLighting_5 still alive. It happened on the SECOND export in one editor session (the first always worked).
CAUSE (engine source, read-only): CGameExporter::Export with SetAutoExportMode(true) calls SetHiQuality() (GameExporter.cpp): iExportTexWidth = 16384, bUpdateIndirectLighting = true, nApplySS = 1 - it OVERWRITES the resolution and settings the caller set. The indirect-lighting pass (CTerrainLightGen -> CTerrainGIGen -> CHemisphereSink_SH::Init, IndirectLighting/SHHeightmapAccessibility.cpp) spawns one thread per CPU core named SHLighting_<n>; nothing ever tells them to exit and CThreadManager (CrySystem/SystemThreading.cpp) keeps each registered under the ADDRESS of its task object. The next export builds a new sink; when a task object lands on a reused address, SpawnThread answers 'already exists', returns false and the caller ends in CryFatalError. So it is a stock-engine leak made reachable by a plugin choice, and it depends on heap luck.
FIX (the ClaudeBridge plugin, not an engine file): bridge.terrain.export_texture no longer sets the auto-export mode, so it is the call the terrain dialog's own 'Export Terrain Texture' makes: the requested resolution is honoured (measured 512 px = 655,444 bytes, 1,024 px = 2,752,724 bytes in cover.ctc) and the indirect-lighting pass does not run. test_world_build.py bakes twice in one session as the regression check.
RULES: do not call the exporter in auto/high-quality mode from your own code more than once per editor session; export_level (exporter.export_to_engine) is the supported full export. If you meet the dialog: bridge.dialog.click ok, then answer the 'Crash' prompt No, and let the watchdog restart the editor (playbook-editor-recovery).

title: PLAYBOOK: add a second level to the game - the travel table, Doorway/LockedGate entities, arrival markers, the loading page
source: Session 2026-10-13/14: Code/Components/LevelTravel.{h,cpp}, AshvaleGame.cpp, examples/ashvale/undercroft_kit.py, uc_geom.py, build_undercroft.py, build_hatch.py, test_undercroft_kit.py
content:
Full title: PLAYBOOK: add a second level to the game - the travel table, Doorway/LockedGate entities, arrival markers, the loading page, what carries over a level change
A level change DESTROYS every entity and every static of the old level, so anything that must survive is copied into AshvaleTravel statics (LevelTravel.cpp) before the `map` command and read back in OnPlayerSpawned: the RUN (flags, coins, bread, hour, health), a per-level entity memory (chests opened, pickups taken, who is dead) and the arrival spot.
THE ORDER: (1) a row in AshvaleLevels (name = the folder under Assets/levels, title for the loading page, underground yes/no: an underground level has no sun, weather or day clock and the surface hour is carried through it); (2) in the OLD level a Doorway entity (properties Label, Prompt, TargetLevel, TargetSpot, RequiresFlag, LockedText, Range; E asks for the level behind the LOADING PAGE; locked until the flag is set) and, in the NEW level, an AshvaleMarker of Kind Spot named exactly as TargetSpot; (3) in the new level a Doorway back whose TargetSpot is a Spot marker in the old one (the hatch's exit); markers PlayerStart / Respawn / MenuCamera are per level; (4) a LockedGate for story doors (RequiresFlag, SeenFlag shown the first time the player looks at it); (5) the story flags: a kill sets one through an NPC's DeathFlag, the door waits for it.
THE LOADING PAGE: the page's elements must be visible BEFORE the `map <level>` command (FlashUI hands visible elements to its load-time thread at LEVEL_LOAD_START_LOADINGSCREEN); the command itself is run deferred (ExecuteString(cmd, false, true)); the new level hides the loader once the player is in place (DropLoader). The spawn handler can run twice for one load: keep the arrival valid for ~15 s.
SAVES: a save game names its level; Continue, New Game and Load travel first when the level differs. Menus from an underground level travel back to the first level.
EVERY level needs the presets the game looks up: `level_check` caught a new level whose time-of-day list held only its own preset, so ashvale_clear / ashvale_rain (WorldTools.cpp) were missing from its saved AND exported list. Load them into the level with bridge.env.load, keep the level's own preset as the default (bridge.env.default), save, export, level_check again.
EXPORT EACH LEVEL on its own with export_level (regenerate the navmesh first); an unexported navmesh is lost on an editor restart.
PROVEN IN THE PACKAGED GAME (2026-10-14, undercroft_playthrough.py 34 of 34): the trip down and up, the run carried over, the arrival marker, a save made in one level and loaded from the other. The loading page needed a FRAME measurement (transition_frames.py): see trap-level-change-black-screen-flashui-unload. Without a game run none of this is provable: ask for one with a precise description (what runs, how long, what closes).

title: TRAP: a plan that names GameSDK props which were never copied into the project - level_validate says 'Geometry file ... Failed to Load'
source: Session 2026-10-13/14: Code/Components/LevelTravel.{h,cpp}, AshvaleGame.cpp, examples/ashvale/undercroft_kit.py, uc_geom.py, build_undercroft.py, build_hatch.py, test_undercroft_kit.py
content:
Full title: TRAP: a plan that names GameSDK props which were never copied into the project - level_validate says 'Geometry file ... Failed to Load', the brush draws nothing
SYMPTOM (2026-10-14): level_validate on the new level listed `[Error] Resource File objects/props/mine/minecart_pile.cgf not found` and `[Warning] Geometry file ... for Brush UC_Cart_C Failed to Load` for 11 brushes (minecart pile, planks, boards, pole, amphora x4, candle holder x2); the wooden barrels in the same plan were fine.
CAUSE: the GameSDK sample's paks are NOT mounted by this project. A prop works only if it was copied into Assets/objects (the barrels had been, for Ashvale). The plan's docstring said 'the engine finds them in its paks': that was never checked. The editor does not complain when the object is placed (the bridge answers ok): only level_validate shows it.
FIX: `python level/import_gamesdk_asset.py Objects/props/misc/pottery/amphora` for a folder, or `.../mine/pole01.cgf` for one model (a bare name without .cgf matches nothing: 'copied 0 files'). It copies the model with its LODs, materials and every texture including the split mip files, from the user's installed GameSDK sample (a local copy, no download). Then asset_metadata for the .cryasset files and a restart of the editor so it sees the new files.
GUARD: test_undercroft_kit.py checks that every mesh in gs_props() exists under Assets. Run level_validate on every level you build and read each 'Failed to Load' line; 'Geometry File in Slot N for Entity Bread_X not found' is a known false positive (the pickups use the engine's primitive_sphere: trap in tooling-level-stats-and-level-validate-the-engines-own-level-reports).

title: TRAP: write_material / pipeline accepted surface types the project does not define (mat_dirt, mat_gravel, mat_sand, mat_mud)
source: Session 2026-10-13/14: Code/Components/LevelTravel.{h,cpp}, AshvaleGame.cpp, examples/ashvale/undercroft_kit.py, uc_geom.py, build_undercroft.py, build_hatch.py, test_undercroft_kit.py
content:
Full title: TRAP: write_material / pipeline accepted surface types the project does not define (mat_dirt, mat_gravel, mat_sand, mat_mud) and refused the ones it does (mat_soil, mat_fabric, mat_flesh)
SYMPTOM (2026-10-14): the new level's material named mat_dirt for the cave floor and level_validate printed `'mat_dirt' undefined surface type, using mat_default`. The tool had allowed it because pipeline.MTL_SURFACES was a hard-coded list from the first week (it had mat_dirt, mat_gravel, mat_sand, mat_mud: none defined) and it did not list mat_soil, mat_fabric, mat_flesh, mat_plastic, mat_snow, which Assets/libs/MaterialEffects/SurfaceTypes.xml has defined since 2026-10-08 (17 types).
FIX: pipeline.MTL_SURFACES is now read from SurfaceTypes.xml (the file is the truth; the fallback tuple is the 17 types). The project's rule: dirt is mat_soil, cloth is mat_fabric. An undefined surface type is silently mat_default for physics and sounds. Check any material with material_check / lint L017 and level_validate.
SAME DAY, METALS: pbs_check (S005) flagged the new iron and gold because write_material gave every material the dielectric Specular 0.0212 (sRGB 40) and the colour in Diffuse. The manual's PBS rule for a metal is a near-black Diffuse and the colour in the Specular (iron sRGB 196, gold 255,219,145). write_material now takes `metal: true` on a sub-material: Diffuse 0.02, Specular = the tint (linear: iron '0.55,0.54,0.52', gold '1.0,0.71,0.28'). MEASURED CAVEAT (2026-10-14, editor pictures before/after, same view): outdoors under Ashvale's probe the hatch's iron bands read as mid-grey iron (kept); indoors in the sealed Undercroft, which has no environment probe, the same rule turned the dark iron cell bars PALE GREY, so the dungeon's iron and gold stay dielectric (two known S005 warnings; the reason is inferred, not proven). `bridge.object.set @Components=<Components ...>` on an EnvironmentProbe reports changed but leaves the component at its defaults, so a probe for the dungeon could not be configured that way. The project's older gold.mtl, steel.mtl and the arrow head are the other three S005 findings in the baseline.

title: PLAYBOOK: weave a new area into the story - dialogue hooks, a side objective, a journal row, a one-time hint, a pay-off line
tags: integrate a level into the story
source: Session 2026-10-13/14: Code/Components/LevelTravel.{h,cpp}, AshvaleGame.cpp, examples/ashvale/undercroft_kit.py, uc_geom.py, build_undercroft.py, build_hatch.py, test_undercroft_kit.py
content:
Full title: PLAYBOOK: weave a new area into the story - dialogue hooks, a side objective, a journal row, a one-time hint, a pay-off line - and prove with story_check that every flag can still be reached
HOW THE GAME'S STORY WORKS (Code/Components/AshvaleGame.cpp, AshvaleMenus.cpp, Assets/libs/ashvale/dialogue.xml): the story is a set of integer FLAGS. A dialogue <Node id= when="a,!b"> is chosen by FindNode: the FIRST node with that id whose `when` holds (so 'start' is listed once per stage of the story, most specific first, the unconditional one LAST); a <Choice> may carry when= / set="a,b" / action= (return_tithe, give_blade, feed_martha, heal, buy_bread, give_bread). Flags are also set by an NPC's DeathFlag, a chest's items (an item 'tithe' sets has_tithe), a LockedGate's SeenFlag, and by the game's code (SetFlag). GetObjective() is the one HUD line; the journal (AshvaleMenus.cpp) and the map read the same flags; saves keep every flag. Voice files are named by NODE INDEX (vox_<dialogue>_<j>.ogg): inserting a node shifts every later index, so re-render the dialogue's voices (render_voices) after ANY edit.
WHAT WAS DONE FOR THE UNDERCROFT (2026-10-14): foreshadowing in four existing conversations (Oswin, Edmund, Tom, a villager); a one-time Notify when Wat dies (flag hatch_hint, shown after the objective notice has expired: Notify replaces the previous message); GetSideObjective() = a second HUD line and extra 'What to do now' lines; one journal row; the sexton remembered underground (met_cuthbert) and on the surface; Edmund, Hilda and the ending card notice has_lordsword. The main chain (tithe -> Hilda -> ending) is unchanged: the new area is optional.
PROVE IT: `python examples/ashvale/story_check.py` (test_story_check.py, 15 checks, about a second, no editor, no game) searches the STORY STATES (sets of flags; 3,600 here) through every event and every conversation the levels make reachable: S001 a flag read that nothing sets (a typo), S002 a goto to a missing node, S003 a dialogue with no unconditional start, S004 a goal flag the story can never reach (it caught that Black Wat could not die in a planted copy and everything after him broke), S005 a node an earlier node with the same id hides, S006 an NPC naming a missing dialogue, S007/S008 information. A first version explored only the FINAL flags and called early-story nodes dead: a conversation says different things in different states, so the search must run over states, not over one fixed point. Limits: coins and bread conditions are assumed satisfiable; flags are monotone (cleared flags count as set); whether the player can walk there is nav_reach's job. SEEN in the packaged game (2026-10-14): the HUD's second line, the journal row (its first name overlapped the status column: keep a row label to about 17 characters), the map, the ending card with the sword. NOT checked: a human playing it, sound.

title: TRAP: after importing GameSDK props the package job stops with 'textures missing from the package: N' - pak_textures.py adds them
source: Session 2026-10-13/14: Code/Components/LevelTravel.{h,cpp}, AshvaleGame.cpp, examples/ashvale/undercroft_kit.py, uc_geom.py, build_undercroft.py, build_hatch.py, test_undercroft_kit.py
content:
Full title: TRAP: after importing GameSDK props the package job stops with 'textures missing from the package: N' - pak_textures.py adds them; and a Release package needs a Release Game.dll first
SYMPTOM (2026-10-14): `start_job('package', {'config': 'release'})` made the package (28 s, 0 resource-compiler failures) and then failed with 'textures missing from the package: 185 objects/props/mine/textures/chaff_ddna.dds, ...dds.1, ...dds.1a'. CAUSE: Crytek's packager (RC) compiles a plain .dds but refuses a set that is already split (.dds, .dds.1, .dds.1a ...), which is how the GameSDK ships its textures, and leaves some other loose .dds out too; the props imported for the Undercroft brought 185 such files (27 MB; also textures/cubemaps and textures/generic/water). Without the guard the game would draw them as white squares (the 2026-09-30 torch and fire sprites did).
FIX: `python packaging/pak_textures.py release` (or --list to look first): it adds the missing files to Assets/GameSDKTextures.pak with the engine's own 7za (zip, store, paths relative to Assets), keeping the pak's other entries (test_pak_textures.py); then start the package job again. final_packages.py now names it in its message.
ALSO: the packager compiles nothing. For `release` the Release Game.dll must be built first (`cmake --build solutions/win64 --target Game --config Release`, 8 s; the ClaudeGameBuild task builds Profile only and closes the editor); the job refuses when Game.dll is older than the sources. The package job closes the editor (bridge.window.close; it saved first) and the watchdog brings it back.
AFTER A PACKAGE, READ ITS PAKS (no game launch): both level folders under assets/levels/<name>/ hold level.pak (with the navmesh mnmnav*.bai) and the materials, meshes, voices, dialogue and presets are in Data/Objects/Audio/Textures.pak; the Release Game.dll hash must equal bin/win_x64_release/Game.dll.

title: TRAP: a loading page that worked at game start flashed for 0.1 s and left 3 s of BLACK on a level change
tags: map command from a running game
source: Session 2026-10-13/14: Code/Components/LevelTravel.{h,cpp}, AshvaleGame.cpp, examples/ashvale/undercroft_kit.py, uc_geom.py, build_undercroft.py, build_hatch.py, test_undercroft_kit.py
content:
Full title: TRAP: a loading page that worked at game start flashed for 0.1 s and left 3 s of BLACK on a level change - FlashUI unloads every element not flagged force-no-unload (found by frame-measuring the packaged game)
SYMPTOM (2026-10-14, the first time the game was run after the Undercroft was built): the playthrough passed 30 of 34 checks, but two screenshots of the loading page were black. `transition_frames.py` (a fast screen-grab burst from just before E to arrival, each frame classed black / loader / scene, the game's trace events placed on the same clock) showed in BOTH directions: scene -> loader for 0.1 s -> BLACK for 3.0 s (the whole real load) -> scene. The trace said 'loading page shown' every time: the page was logged, not seen.
CAUSE (engine source, read-only, CryAction/FlashUI/FlashUI.cpp): at ESYSTEM_EVENT_LEVEL_UNLOAD a RUNNING game makes FlashUI call Unload on every UI element that does not have eFUI_FORCE_NO_UNLOAD, then its load-time render thread draws only elements still visible with eFUI_SHOW_AT_LOADING_TIME. The menu element that carries the project's loader was unloaded before the real load began, so the load-time thread had nothing to draw. At the first level of a run nothing is unloaded, which is why the loader had always worked at game start (loading_screen_test.py).
FIX: CAshvaleUI::ShowLoading sets `eFUI_FORCE_NO_UNLOAD` on the element beside eFUI_SHOW_AT_LOADING_TIME (a UIElement XML can say force_no_unload="1" too), and HideLoading keeps the loader up while AshvaleTravel::IsTravelling() (BeginArrival -> DropLoader takes it down once the player is placed), because after the load completes there is still about a second before the world is drawn. MEASURED AFTER: loader on screen for the whole trip (23-25 frames, 3 s), zero black frames, in both directions.
METHOD: a level change that has a loading page needs a FRAME measurement, not a trace line: `python examples/ashvale/transition_frames.py <build> [--tour]` (window_capture.capture_screen is a BitBlt, so it works while the game thread is busy loading; `--tour` also stands at the 20 viewpoints of the Undercroft and saves a real-renderer picture of each). Note: AshvaleTravel::Go refuses to run in the editor ('go: not from the editor'): the editor's play mode never changes level, only the packaged game does.
verified_note: FIXED and proven in the packaged game 2026-10-14 (transition_frames.py: the loader stays up for the whole trip, zero black frames, both directions).

title: TRAP: the package job failed after 2 s with 'PermissionError: Access is denied ... Ashvale_final_release'
source: Session 2026-10-13/14: Code/Components/LevelTravel.{h,cpp}, AshvaleGame.cpp, examples/ashvale/undercroft_kit.py, uc_geom.py, build_undercroft.py, build_hatch.py, test_undercroft_kit.py
content:
Full title: TRAP: the package job failed after 2 s with 'PermissionError: Access is denied ... Ashvale_final_release' - a background task I had started while the shell's working directory was INSIDE the package folder was holding it open
SYMPTOM (2026-10-14): `start_job('package')` failed at once: release_project.py `os.unlink(path)` on the output folder -> PermissionError; the folder was left EMPTY, `rmdir` said 'Device or resource busy', and no GameLauncher or Sandbox was running. CAUSE: a `Monitor` (a `tail -f` of a log) had been started when the Bash tool's working directory was the package folder (an earlier `cd` into it persisted); a process keeps its working directory open, so Windows would not let the folder be removed until `TaskStop` ended the monitor. FIX: stop the background task (TaskStop), `rmdir` the empty folder, package again. RULES: never leave the shell's cwd inside a build or package folder (`cd /tmp` first), start long-running background tasks from a neutral directory, and use absolute paths. The packager's rmtree uses ignore_errors=True, so a held folder shows up only as this unlink error.

`python examples/ashvale/undercroft_playthrough.py <build>` (2026-10-14: 34 checks, 144 s, no crash report): a new game, the hatch locked while Wat lives, the foreshadowing conversations, Wat's death (flag) and the notice/HUD line/journal, the trip down, the run carried over (flags, coins, bread), the sexton, all eight enemies, Corbin's death, the vault door, the strongbox, a save made underground, the trip up, a load of the underground save from the surface, the ending with the sword, the shader-cache miss count, a clean quit. Pictures go to <build>/undercroft_shots.
TRAPS it found in the harness itself: the conversation helper must match the dialogue id in the trace (`talking to Father Edmund (edmund)`), not the NPC's entity name; an objective text with an apostrophe ("Wat's") breaks a regex written as '([^']*)'; `ash_goto <entity>` stands the player on the side the player already is, which from the far end of a dungeon can be INSIDE A WALL: use `uc_standpoints.py` (the point on a ring around each target that the engine's NAVMESH connects to the start, with the yaw that faces it, written to uc_stand.json) and `ash_goto_pos`. The harness does NOT ask Windows to keep the display awake (the machine's rules refused that request on 2026-10-13); 19 older scripts still do (tests job, release_playthrough, ...): they are the user's decision, not run by me.
READING A RESULT: PASS lines are checks; a FAIL is a game fault, a harness fault or a stale package: look at the trace around it (claude_npc.log) and at the picture before deciding which. The one real finding of the first run was the shader-cache miss count (3), then the black loading screen (see trap-level-change-black-screen-flashui-unload).

title: My textures look artificial, plastic or glossy: the cause was procedural noise and mixed looks, NOT the gloss maps
source: Session 2026-10-13/14: Code/Components/LevelTravel.{h,cpp}, AshvaleGame.cpp, examples/ashvale/undercroft_kit.py, uc_geom.py, build_undercroft.py, build_hatch.py, test_undercroft_kit.py
content:
THE USER'S COMPLAINT (2026-10-14): 'all of your created assets look very artificial, textures look unnatural, kind of glossy; the dungeon has random texture changes, I said variety not different'. The cause was MY procedural textures (texture_lab: noise-made, strong normal-map relief, saturated colour, regular patterns) and a dungeon that mixed unrelated looks (red brick ceilings, beige ashlar, white marble, blue slate: fifteen materials with nothing in common).
MEASURED, AND A CORRECTION: my own first explanation was 'my normal maps have no gloss channel, so everything shines at a flat Shininess/255'. WRONG: a BC5 normal map keeps its gloss as a second chain of BC4 mips after the BC5 chain; decoded properly (texture_preview.py) my gloss maps average 0.08-0.42, a smoothness of 0.03-0.26, no shinier than the GameSDK's (0.12-0.35). title: TRAP: I deleted 1,005 files the village needs because I told 'my imports' from 'the project's own' by file time - the import tool had...
source: Session 2026-10-13/14: Code/Components/LevelTravel.{h,cpp}, AshvaleGame.cpp, examples/ashvale/undercroft_kit.py, uc_geom.py, build_undercroft.py, build_hatch.py, test_undercroft_kit.py
content:
Full title: TRAP: I deleted 1,005 files the village needs because I told 'my imports' from 'the project's own' by file time - the import tool had rewritten existing files (fresh time); restore came from a snapshot
WHAT HAPPENED (2026-10-14): to preview GameSDK materials I imported ~4,200 files with import_gamesdk_asset.py, then cleaned up by 'delete the files newer than 14:30 that no project material names' (dry run first: '3,610 files, 588 MB'). But the import tool REWROTE files that already existed in the project (same bytes, new modified time): the village's wooden bridge (materials and textures), rocks (rock_forest), trees, haybales, ground_stones_rough. They looked new, nothing named them, and they were deleted. Found by test_asset_lint (its fixture rock_forest.mtl was gone) and by the editor suite's project_audit / level_validate ('Material ... file not found', M001 the engine returned its DEFAULT material). Nothing was lost: snapshot_project had run an hour before; diff_snapshot showed removed=1005, all under Assets; snapshot.restore (overwrite=true, exactly those paths) brought them back, then the editor was restarted (it had loaded the level while they were missing: its errors were stale).
THE RULES: (1) a modified time cannot tell your imports from the project's own: never delete by time. (2) The ground truth is a SNAPSHOT TAKEN BEFORE the imports: prune_imports.py <snapshot id> deletes only files that snapshot did not have and no kept material names (test_prune_imports.py: a baseline file is never a candidate, time plays no part). (3) import_gamesdk_asset.py now leaves an existing file of the same size untouched (same time) and prints how many it left. (4) A dry run only proves the tool does what you told it, not that what you told it is right: look at WHAT is on the delete list (here: the bridge's name was on it) and ask 'did this exist before?' by comparing with the snapshot. (5) After any bulk delete run diff_snapshot against the snapshot: 'removed' must be exactly what you meant.
RESTORE: `import snapshot; d = snapshot.diff(<id>, 'current', limit=100000); snapshot.restore(<id>, d['removed_files'], overwrite=True)` (or restore_files with the exact paths: it takes a before_restore snapshot first); the 'modified' count is your deliberate changes.

title: Open-air scene is bright and washed out (lime grass, chalk hills) though the frame mean looks fine: EV compensation +1.5
source: Session 2026-10-14: exposure_card.py, lighting_editor.py, lighting_audit.py, author_environment.py, Code/Components/WorldTools.cpp
content:
THE COMPLAINT (2026-10-14): 'fix the lightning in open areas, its bright; it also needs to be natural, investigate how natural lighting should look and work'. The packaged game's noon picture was lime-yellow grass (hue 63 deg, linear luma 0.27), chalk-white hillsides, a road at 0.26: bright and washed out, although the FRAME MEAN (0.43 sRGB) looked fine: auto exposure holds the mean whatever the scene is, so a frame mean says nothing about whether the light is natural.
WHAT WAS MEASURED: the engine's +1.5 EV rendered the grey card at linear 0.45 (sRGB 0.70) and clipped the 90% card; 1.0 -> 0.36, 0.5 -> 0.27, 0.0 -> 0.20, -0.5 -> 0.14. The sky at multiplier 50 read 0.18 of the card (a navy sky once the ground is exposed right), at 100 0.32, at 200 0.62-0.65. The ambient: fixed exposure (EV Min = EV Max = 14, which reproduces auto exposure at bias 0), sun on vs off: cards 0.052 / 0.214 / 0.454 against 0.003 / 0.018 / 0.113, i.e. the ambient is ~7-10% of the sunlit light (used 8.5%), 3.5 stops under the sun; natural is ~18%. So the +1.5 EV had been compensating for shadows that were too dark by over-exposing the sunlit ground.

title: How natural daylight works: sun ~100,000 lux, shade ~20% of the lit surface, sky ~0.6 of a sunlit grey card, an 18% card reads linear 0.18
source: Session 2026-10-14: exposure_card.py, lighting_editor.py, lighting_audit.py, author_environment.py, Code/Components/WorldTools.cpp
content: HOW NATURAL LIGHT WORKS (the manual, 'Lighting Levels Using PBS' + the tone-mapping pages, and Crytek's own sample presets): direct sun ~100,000 lux, the shade (sky light) ~20,000 lux = about 18-20% of the lit surface, overcast 15,000 lux; the sky is a blue about 0.6 as bright as a sunlit grey card; the camera/eye adapts so that an 18% grey card in the sun renders as mid grey (linear 0.18, sRGB ~0.46); the sun's own colour makes the warm light and the colour balance is left neutral by day (the sample's presets: balance 1/1/1, sky multiplier 200, sun 115,000 lux; they use the engine defaults EV Min 4.5, EV Max 17, bias +1.5).

title: PLAYBOOK: roads and paths - use the engine's Road object (it IS the terrain surface), not meshes laid near the ground; how it was found...
source: Session 2026-10-15: road_objects.py, road_float_check.py, road_trial.py, test_road_objects.py, village_kit.py; Cry3DEngine/RoadRenderNode.cpp
content:
Full title: PLAYBOOK: roads and paths - use the engine's Road object (it IS the terrain surface), not meshes laid near the ground; how it was found, measured, built and checked
THE ENGINE'S ANSWER (manual: Editor Tools > Misc Objects > Road Tool; source Cry3DEngine/RoadRenderNode.cpp, Compile): a Road object cuts the TERRAIN'S OWN TRIANGLES under its outline (GetZ on the heightmap grid, the same quad flipping) and blends its edges with the material's vertex colours (Illum %DECAL). It is the terrain surface, so it cannot float, follows any later terrain edit, and needs no lift. Properties (the engine's serializer; object_props.set_properties / set_spline): Width, BorderWidth (only for the 'Align Height Map' operator, which reshapes the terrain: not used), StepSize (1 here: smoother bends, the default 4 cuts corners), TileLength 8, SortPriority (higher draws over lower), EraseVegWidth (only for the Erase Vegetation operator), IgnoreTerrainHoles, Physicalize (0: the player and navmesh use the terrain; no 6 cm lip). Crytek's own levels (26 Road objects in woodland/airfield) use StepSize 1-2, TileLength 8, BorderWidth 6-12, EraseVegWidth 3, widths 3-10, materials roads/forest_path_stones, forest_trail, mud_road.
NOT SEEN IN THE PACKAGED GAME: the road shader permutation (Illum DECAL + POM + VERTCOLORS + NORMAL_MAP) is new to the shader cache; package, then shader_cache_refresh, then look, with the user's yes for a game run.

source: Session 2026-10-15: checks/prune_imports.py, test_prune_imports.py

Full title: TRAP: prune_imports deleted the textures of a material I was keeping (materials/roads) - the snapshot diff showed 'removed 0' because they were new files
2026-10-15, after choosing two road materials out of eight imported candidates: I deleted the six unused .mtl files by hand and ran prune_imports.py. The tool kept only the textures named by materials/ashvale/** and wood_dark.mtl, so ALL 230 files under textures/roads went, including the two materials I kept. diff_snapshot said removed 0 (the files were new since the snapshot: a snapshot protects only what existed), project_audit then showed 'Resource File textures/roads/..._diff.tif not found'. Nothing pre-existing was lost; the two materials' textures were re-copied (import_gamesdk_asset.py materials/roads/dirt_road_tracks.mtl materials/roads/forest_trail.mtl). FIXED: prune_imports.keeper_materials() now keeps every material outside its touched folders and every material a level layer (.lyr Material="...") names, and never lists a kept material file itself (test_prune_imports.py: 9 checks, two new). LESSONS: (1) after a clean-up, run project_audit / level_validate and look for 'not found'; test_road_objects.py checks the textures of the road materials exist. (2) A clean-up's keep-list must be everything that STAYS, not a short list of folders the author remembered. (3) A script that takes materials as arguments must not treat '--flag' as one (road_trial created a Road with Material '--close', in scratch, gone afterwards).

Full title: TRAP: GameSDK clip names carry meaning - _1p_ is the player's first-person view, a weapon word means a held weapon, 'add' means additive; NPCs that use them look wrong
A clip is named <stance>_tac_<what>[_<weapon>]_<view>_<variant>: relaxed/stand/alerted/crouch/kneel/prone/cover (stance), rifle/pistol/scar/hammer/bayonet/gren/c4/shotgun (a weapon is held or aimed), nw = no weapon, 1p = first person (the player's own view), 3p = third person, add/additive = it only adds to another pose. The villagers' database (Villager.adb) used melee_killingblow_rightkick_1p_01 for BOTH Startle and Attack (a first-person kick: bandits attacked with a kick; the villager startle looked like an unprovoked attack, which an earlier fix worked around in code), stand_tac_shootidle_rifle_3p_01 for the archers' bow, and a soldier 'relaxed' idle/walk under a weaponpose layer for everyone. anim_inventory.py classifies every clip by these tokens (--civ = weaponless, third person, not additive). A weaponless NAME is not proof the motion looks civilian (the whole set is soldier motion capture): it narrows the choice, a picture of the motion decides. The Crysis animation pack in the Launcher (crysis-animation-assets, 298 FBX) is ALL tactical soldier motion (rifle, pistol, jump, swim, vehicles): nothing civilian in it.

title: PLAYBOOK: MotionBricks (or any generated motion) -> a looping .caf for the villagers: record, retarget, cut a cycle, write the FBX, compile
source: Session 2026-10-15: motionbricks_{record,preview,retarget,loop,fbx,clip,validate}.py, anim_sample.py, fbx_to_caf.py, plugin verbs bridge.character.{bindpose,samplepose}, test_motionbricks.py, test_anim_sample.py
content:
Full title: PLAYBOOK: MotionBricks (or any generated motion) -> a looping .caf for the villagers: record, retarget, cut a cycle, write the FBX, compile, prove it in the engine (one command per step)
1 RECORD (MotionBricks venv Python, GPU): `C:\MotionBricks\venv\Scripts\python.exe motionbricks_record.py <style> --steps 600 --seed 1234` -> C:\MotionBricks\clips\<style>_<seed>.npz (qpos, 34 joint positions and rotation matrices in MuJoCo/motion space, fps 30). `--list` shows the styles the checkpoint knows. The demo's own headless loop: a pretend camera, a pretend key state.
2 BIND POSE: plugin verb bridge.character.bindpose (the engine's own bind pose of the character: 163 joints, absolute and parent-relative) -> C:\MotionBricks\clips\sdk_player_bindpose.json.
3 ONE COMMAND for the rest (project Python, numpy only): `python motionbricks_clip.py <style> <anim name>` (e.g. walk_scared mb_walk_scared): motionbricks_retarget.py (G1 -> Bip01: limbs by DIRECTION swing so different rest poses and proportions do not matter, pelvis and torso by frame transfer, root path scaled by the leg-length ratio 1.39, pelvis height from the lowest sole so the feet touch the ground; KNEES AND ELBOWS ARE HINGES, see trap-fbx-rotation-limits-clip-hinge-joints) -> motionbricks_loop.py (the pair of frames 0.6-2.4 s apart whose body pose and its velocity are nearest, after skipping the first second; the seam closed by a 6-frame crossfade; the travel replaced by a straight line along +Y at the mean speed = the locator, everything else relative to it) -> motionbricks_fbx.py (curves written into a copy of a Crytek locomotion FBX: Euler XYZ from the local rotations, continuous in time, gimbal-safe) -> fbx_to_caf.py with --start-frame 0 --end-frame <frames+1> -> motionbricks_clips.json (speed, duration: the C++ table reads them). The FBX forward kinematics are checked against the cycle before rc.exe runs (max 2e-6 m).
4 PUT THE .CAF in Assets/Animations/human/male/motionbricks/ (a NEW file name each time while the editor runs: it caches loose files by name), `asset_metadata apply=true` for the .cryasset.
5 PROVE IT IN THE ENGINE: the editor open, `anim_sample clip` (tool) or the plugin verb samplepose ... | reload, then `python animation/motionbricks_validate.py <anim name>` compares the engine's pose at 0, .25, .5, .75 with the cycle's own: tolerance 3 cm, measured 0.3-1.3 mm. test_anim_sample.py checks duration, speed (3 %), feet on the ground (2 cm), loop closure (1 cm) for every clip of the manifest.
6 Mannequin + code: villager_anim.py (GAITS table -> fragments WalkSlow/WalkScared/WalkInjured/WalkStealth + the C++ table with each clip's speed), then playbook-npc-gaits-from-motionbricks.
Seen in the contact sheet of engine-computed poses (motionbricks_gaits_engine_poses.png, sent to the user): scared walk upright with hunched shoulders, injured walk leaning with one arm out, stealth deeply crouched, slow walk upright.

title: MEASURED: what the engine does with a Crytek-rig FBX animation - world = Rx(+90) x FBX world, joint frames coincide, local rotations
tags: FBX local rotation equals engine relative
source: Session 2026-10-15: motionbricks_{record,preview,retarget,loop,fbx,clip,validate}.py, anim_sample.py, fbx_to_caf.py, plugin verbs bridge.character.{bindpose,samplepose}, test_motionbricks.py, test_anim_sample.py
content:
Full title: MEASURED: what the engine does with a Crytek-rig FBX animation - world = Rx(+90) x FBX world, joint frames coincide, local rotations and cm translations carry over, the RC re-roots the clip on the locator
All measured 2026-10-15 on relaxed_tac_run_nw_fwd_fast_3p_01: the pak's own compiled clip and a copy compiled by rc.exe, sampled by the engine (bridge.character.samplepose) against forward kinematics of the FBX (fbx_root_motion.Scene.world: parent x T x PreRotation x R(Euler XYZ = Rz.Ry.Rx) x PostRotation^-1).
* ENGINE WORLD POSE = M x FBX WORLD POSE, M = +90 degrees about X (FBX: Y up, forward = -Z, centimetres; engine: Z up, forward +Y, metres), minus the position of the locator at the clip's first frame. ROTATIONS: engine world rotation = M . FBX world rotation (NOT a conjugation: the joint frames coincide). So a joint's FBX local rotation (PreRotation . Lcl) EQUALS the engine's parent-relative rotation, and Lcl Translation (cm) = 100 x the engine's relative translation. Held to 0.1 degree and 1 cm for the body joints; fingers (a few degrees), twist joints (procedural) and the IK blend/target joints are the engine's own business.
* THE ROOT: the FBX 'Bip01' is the biped's centre of mass (Max): it carries the pelvis position and heading; 'Bip01 Pelvis' is a constant-ish child of it. The RC re-roots the clip on its motion node ('Locator_Locomotion', request field motionNodePath): the engine's Bip01 is the locator's path (identity rotation), the engine's Pelvis is relative to it. The skeleton's 'Locator_Locomotion' joint is a DUMMY the runtime never reads by name; in a converted clip it can carry the path a second time (relative to the root): read the clip's travel from Bip01, not from the locator joint (anim_sample does).
* THE TAKE: RC honours the take's LocalStart. The Crytek FBX starts at 1/24 s, so a clip compiled from it began one 30-fps frame late. motionbricks_fbx.Template.write puts LocalStart/ReferenceStart/TimeSpanStart at 0. RC frame range: startFrame 0, endFrame N+1 gives N intervals, N/30 s (endFrame is exclusive: 24 gave 23 intervals, 0.7667 s). Without a range the whole take is compiled (this FBX: 4.97 s, with 3.8 s of padding).
* UNCOMPRESSED: rc.exe writes the CAF from the FBX without lossy compression (24 frames x 200 bones = 135 KB); differences from the pak clip were never compression.
* IK BLEND JOINTS: 'Bip01 LHand2Weapon_IKBlend' and the like carry their blend WEIGHT in a tiny translation/rotation. Writing the bind offset there pulled the hands 17 cm toward the weapon IK targets. Only body joints get computed values; every other animated model keeps the template's constant.
Tools: fbx_root_motion.py (FK, speed and turn of the locator), motionbricks_fbx.py (the writer and these rules in its docstring), anim_sample (the engine's side).

title: TRAP: the villager rig's knees and elbows are hinges - the FBX limits X and Y rotation of Calf and Forearm, rc.exe silently clips...
source: Session 2026-10-15: motionbricks_{record,preview,retarget,loop,fbx,clip,validate}.py, anim_sample.py, fbx_to_caf.py, plugin verbs bridge.character.{bindpose,samplepose}, test_motionbricks.py, test_anim_sample.py
content:
Full title: TRAP: the villager rig's knees and elbows are hinges - the FBX limits X and Y rotation of Calf and Forearm, rc.exe silently clips anything else (12 and 35 degrees lost); give the twist to the thigh / upper arm
SYMPTOM (2026-10-15): a clip whose FBX forward kinematics were exact came out of rc.exe with the lower leg 12 degrees and the forearm 35-44 degrees different, hands 17-20 cm and feet 9-13 cm off; the engine's relative quaternion of Calf and Forearm was (w, 0, 0, z) only.
CAUSE: the template FBX has RotationMinX/MinY/MaxX/MaxY ACTIVE on Bip01 L/R Calf and Bip01 L/R Forearm (Properties70); the FBX SDK inside rc.exe clamps the Lcl rotation to the limits, so only rotation about local Z survives. My own forward kinematics ignore limits, so they matched the source and not the engine. Only these four models have limits (checked all 200).
FIX (motionbricks_retarget.py HINGES): the upper bone's frame is built from the bone direction and the plane of the three joints (the hinge axis is its normal, sign from the swing solution, blended with it when the limb is nearly straight), the lower bone only bends about local Z by atan2 of its direction in the upper bone's frame (the bind rotations are Rz(-4.5 degrees) for the calf and Rz(-31.6 degrees) for the forearm: bone length along local +X, hinge axis = local Z of both bones). test_motionbricks.py asserts the X and Y components of the four joints are 0 and that the check can fail.
GENERAL RULE: before writing curves into an FBX, read the model properties for Rotation Min/Max flags and Pre/Post rotations; compare the engine's pose with your own forward kinematics (anim_sample, motionbricks_validate) - a conversion that is exact on paper is not proven until the engine has been asked.

Full title: TRAP: sampling a clip's pose in the engine - CryAnimation updates a character once per frame (a second update is skipped), so every time returned the first pose; and a new .caf is not in the set until the folders are rescanned
SYMPTOM: bridge.character.samplepose returned the SAME pose for normalized times 0, .25, .5, .75 although the read-back normalized time was right (SetAnimationNormalizedTime worked, the layer queue held exactly one animation, CA_MANUAL_UPDATE|CA_FORCE_SKELETON_UPDATE, overrideDeltaTime 0 or 1/30, CS_FLAG_UPDATE_ALWAYS all tried).
CAUSE (read in the engine source, CSkeletonAnim::ProcessAnimations, SkeletonAnim.cpp): `if (m_CharEditMode == 0) { if (m_LastUpdateFrameID_Pre == currentFrameID) { Warning("several pre-updates"); return; } }` - a second animation update of the same character within one engine frame is skipped, so only the first job ran. A character in an EDIT MODE is exempt.
FIX: `pChar->SetCharEditMode(CA_CharacterAuxEditor)` right after CreateInstance (the verb samples several times in one frame). Result: the run clip's left foot moves 1.2 m over the cycle, poses differ per time, deterministic.
SECOND TRAP: a loose .caf copied into Assets/Animations/human/male/<folder>/ after the skeleton was first loaded is not in its animation set: `ICharacterInstance::ReloadCHRPARAMS()` (the Character Tool's reload; stops animations on all instances, harmless in the editor) rescans the folders collected by player.chrparams. anim_sample retries with `| reload` when the clip is not found. And an overwritten loose file keeps its old content in the editor session: use a new name or restart.
The tool: anim_sample(clip, times, joints) - pose, duration, root ground speed (from Bip01), lowest sole (about 0 = on the ground). Use it as the first question for any clip.

title: TRAP: running MotionBricks on an AMD GPU under Windows - ROCm PyTorch has no torch.distributed (two import errors)
source: Session 2026-10-15: motionbricks_{record,preview,retarget,loop,fbx,clip,validate}.py, anim_sample.py, fbx_to_caf.py, plugin verbs bridge.character.{bindpose,samplepose}, test_motionbricks.py, test_anim_sample.py
content:
Full title: TRAP: running MotionBricks on an AMD GPU under Windows - ROCm PyTorch has no torch.distributed (two import errors), the demo imports the 'keyboard' hook package, 'cuda' means the AMD card
Setup that worked (2026-10-15, RX 7900 XTX, with the user's permission for each download): AMD's Windows ROCm PyTorch wheels (torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.1, Python 3.12) in C:\MotionBricks\venv, the NVlabs MotionBricks code (Apache 2.0) in C:\MotionBricks\repo, weights (NVIDIA Open Model License) from huggingface.co/suvadityamuk/motionbricks-ckpts in repo\out. The code hard-codes 'cuda': under ROCm that IS the AMD GPU.
TRAP 1: the Windows ROCm build has NO torch.distributed: `import torch.distributed.group` fails, then `torch.distributed.is_initialized` is missing - vector_quantize_pytorch's lookup_free_quantization imports torch.distributed.nn at load time and uses it only when training across processes. motionbricks_record.shim_distributed() stubs is_initialized (False), get_world_size (1), get_rank (0) and the collectives (they raise if ever called) and a torch.distributed.nn module.
TRAP 2: the demo imports the Windows `keyboard` package at load time to poll keys; headless it is never asked: a stub (is_pressed -> False) stops a global keyboard hook from being installed. The controller is driven by a scripted key state and a fake viewer camera (azimuth 0, so 'w' walks along +X in MuJoCo space).
THE G1: 34 joints (pelvis, 3-DoF waist, 7-DoF arms, 6-DoF legs, toe dummies; no head, neck, fingers or clavicles), motion space Y up, Z forward, X = the character's left, 30 fps, about 1.3 m tall (the villager 1.75: leg ratio 1.39).
Styles of the released checkpoint: idle, slow_walk, walk, hand_crawling, walk_boxing, elbow_crawling, stealth_walk, injured_walk, walk_stealth (crouched), walk_happy_dance, walk_zombie, walk_gun, walk_scared, walk_left, walk_right.

content:
Full title: PLAYBOOK: how the NPC plays the MotionBricks gaits - a Gait property, speeds from the clip, Scared after a startle, Injured below a third of a bandit's health, normal locomotion for anything faster
ADDED (2026-10-15; Game.dll Profile built 13:07, NOT packaged, NOT run, so NOT seen in motion):
* `ENpcGait { Normal, Slow, Scared, Injured, Stealth }` and the property `Gait` (default Normal: nothing changes for a level that does not set it). villager_anim.GAITS lists the fragments (WalkSlow ... WalkStealth, one looping clip each) and writes the C++ table (VillagerAnimTable.h kGaits + kGaitSpeeds from motionbricks_clips.json).
* `EffectiveGait()`: Scared for a villager during `m_scaredRemaining` (14 s after a startled villager stops hurrying: UpdateReaction), Injured for a bandit below 33 % of its health (CHealthComponent::GetFraction), otherwise the property. `GetWalkSpeed()` = the walk speed, or the gait clip's own speed when it has a gait (so the patrol moves at exactly the speed the clip was made for: no sliding); `GetRunSpeed()` = the run speed, except a limping bandit hurries at 1.2 x the limp's speed. SetPatrolSpeed(GetWalkSpeed()) at start, when the villager calms down and when the gait in force changes (UpdateGait, every frame); the bandit brain sets its speeds per state, so CBanditBrain::RefreshSpeed() is called when his gait changes (a wound lands mid-chase).
* UpdateAnimation: a gait fragment replaces the Walk fragment while the measured ground speed is no more than 1.45 x the clip's speed (kGaitSpeedRange); hurrying or chasing is faster and uses the normal locomotion (the blend space reaches 4.2 m/s). The clip is played at body speed / clip speed (playback scale, smoothed, clamped 0.75-1.35) so the feet keep up: UpdateFootSlideProbe applies m_gaitScale while a gait fragment is active; the stride-match learning stays for Walk/Run only.
* Level use: set Gait = Slow on elderly villagers, Stealth on sneaking bandits, Injured/Scared are automatic. No level layer was changed.
CHECKS: test_motionbricks.py (32, includes source checks that the code reads the table and re-applies speeds), test_anim_sample.py (22, the clips against the manifest in the engine), test_villager_anim.py (18), mannequin_check (40 fragments, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1696 clips in the set, none missing), project_audit (0 errors, nothing new against the baseline), test_mcp_tools.py (69, 145 tools).

title: DECISION: Kimodo (NVIDIA text-to-motion, human SOMA skeleton) makes what the library lacks - attack, aim, death, sit, turn on the spot
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: DECISION: Kimodo (NVIDIA text-to-motion, human SOMA skeleton) makes what the library lacks - attack, aim, death, sit, turn on the spot - with its Llama-3 text encoder run by the user's llama.cpp
The user asked (2026-10-15 night): 'No MotionBricks idle, turn or start/stop clips yet. Nobody in the level has a Gait set. Attack, aim, death and sit are still the library's clips or missing. keep in mind: Llama-3 we could run locally on this computer we have llama.cpp'. The earlier answer had been 'Kimodo needs a gated Llama-3 encoder, only after the Hugging Face / Meta steps'; the user's llama.cpp removes that step.
DOWNLOADS (asked first, approved as 'Yes, all of it', about 10.5 GB): Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct Q8_0 GGUF, the two LLM2Vec LoRA adapters with config and tokenizer, Kimodo-SOMA-RP-v1.1, the Kimodo source clone and its PyPI packages into a COPY of the MotionBricks venv. All in C:\Kimodo (venv, kimodo, ckpt, llm, tools, out). Nothing else was fetched.
WHAT IT MAKES: 77-joint SOMA human motion from a text prompt ('A person ...', at most 10 s, 30 fps, metres, Y up, Z forward, X = the character's left; output npz posed_joints (T,77,3)). Trained on locomotion, gestures, everyday activities, videogame combat and styles; WEAK on props and sports (a bow draw came out poor; 'raises a rifle to their shoulder and aims' then mirrored left-right worked: the archer holds the bow with the LEFT arm). 3-4 samples per prompt were generated and one chosen by looking at contact sheets.
CLIPS (Assets/Animations/human/male/kimodo/): kd_attack_a/b/c (club swings, 1.07 s, the blow lands at 0.533 s = the right hand's speed peak), kd_aim_a/b (1.6 s), kd_death_a/b/c (3.4 s), kd_sit_down (2.9 s), kd_sit_idle (2.5 s loop), kd_stand_up (2.9 s), kd_turn_left/right (1.9 s, +97.5 / -91 degrees), kd_turn_180_left/right (2.7 s, +186 / -183). Every one proven in the engine: pose within 0.4-0.9 mm of what it was built to say (anim_validate.py), the root's heading within 0.1 degree.
HOW: playbook-kimodo-motion-to-villager-clip; the encoder: playbook-kimodo-llamacpp-text-encoder; the game side: playbook-npc-kimodo-variants-and-turns.
NOT SEEN IN MOTION: the game was not run. The Kimodo motions were retargeted onto the Bip01 rig by direction/frame transfer; foot skate was not post-processed (Kimodo's motion_correction wheel is not installed).
verified_note: Bandit swings (Attack_A/B/C, blow at 0.53 s) and the archer draw were seen in the packaged game 2026-10-23; turn-on-the-spot, sit, death and aim in motion NOT seen.

title: PLAYBOOK: running Kimodo's LLM2Vec text encoder on llama.cpp instead of Hugging Face - the recipe, injection point and four traps
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Kimodo conditions on ONE pooled vector per prompt: LLM2Vec on Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct (kimodo/model/llm2vec). C:\Kimodo\tools\llamacpp_encoder.py reproduces it with C:\llama\llama.cpp\build\bin\llama-embedding: base Llama-3-8B-Instruct Q8_0 GGUF + the MNTP LoRA + the supervised LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, additive), `--attention non-causal` (the bidirectional mask), `--pooling none` (per-token last hidden states after the final norm), the Llama-3 chat wrapper '<|start_header_id|>user<|end_header_id|>\n\n' + text + '<|eot_id|>', the MEAN over the trailing text tokens (LLM2Vec embed_mask, skip_instruction), float32, NOT normalised (norm about 132). Result (N,1,4096) with lengths [1]*N. Injected with `load_model('Kimodo-SOMA-RP-v1.1', text_encoder=obj)`; the object needs `__call__(texts) -> (tensor, lengths)` (a single string gives ((1,4096), 1)) and `to(device)`. Embeddings are cached on disk by prompt text.
TRAPS: (1) llama.cpp's HIP build fails on the GPU here ('device kernel image is invalid', even with -dev ROCm1): run on the CPU (`-dev none -ngl 0`, 16 cores, about 3 s per call at Q8_0). (2) `--lora` repeated keeps only the LAST adapter: pass one comma-separated list. (3) The default embedding separator is a newline, so a multi-line prompt becomes several sequences: `--embd-separator "<#sep#>"` and a prompt file. (4) The script's own directory is first on sys.path: a script in C:\Kimodo imports the clone C:\Kimodo\kimodo (no package inside, 'cannot import name load_model from kimodo (unknown location)') instead of the installed kimodo: keep scripts in C:\Kimodo\tools.
RUN: `C:\Kimodo\venv\Scripts\python.exe C:\Kimodo\tools\gen_batch.py batch.json` with a batch list [{name, prompt, seconds, seed, samples}] writes C:\Kimodo\out\<name>_<NN>.npz; a prompt of several sentences is a multi-prompt sequence.

title: PLAYBOOK: a Kimodo motion -> a one-shot or looping .caf for the villagers
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: PLAYBOOK: a Kimodo motion -> a one-shot or looping .caf for the villagers (retarget SOMA onto Bip01, cut, locator, FBX, rc.exe, engine proof)
1 Generate (playbook-kimodo-llamacpp-text-encoder), look at the contact sheets (kimodo_review.py), copy the chosen npz to anim_sources/kimodo/<name>.npz (the same prompt and seed repeat only on the same machine and library versions, so the motions are kept).
2 A row in kimodo_clips.CLIPS: cut='peak' (a window around the right hand's speed peak: attacks; pre/post seconds, the manifest keeps hit_time; `peak_after` seconds skips an earlier peak - the overhead strike's FIRST peak is the club going UP, found only by LOOKING at the engine-computed pose sheets (motionbricks_preview.py --samples): kd_attack_c now cuts at the downswing), 'range' (t0..t1), 'turn' (from the first to the last frame the body turns by more than 3 degrees, plus 0.15 s lead-in and 0.4 s settle), 'loop' (the nearest pose pair, closed by a crossfade: anim_oneshot.best_inplace_loop / make_inplace_loop); mirror=True swaps left and right (the rifle aim became the archer's bow draw); root='fixed' (the body moves relative to a locator that stays) or 'path' (the locator follows the pelvis' ground path, low-passed); yaw='follow' (the locator turns with the pelvis).
3 `python animation/kimodo_clips.py <name>` (project Python, numpy only): kimodo_retarget.retarget(SOMA 77 -> Bip01: limbs by direction, hinge knees/elbows through motionbricks_retarget.apply_hinge, pelvis and torso by frame, fingers by a palm frame; the root scaled by the leg ratio, the height from the lowest sole), anim_oneshot.make_clip, motionbricks_clip.finish (curves -> FBX written into a Crytek template -> forward-kinematics check -> expected.json -> manifest -> rc.exe). The manifest (motionbricks_clips.json) keeps source, model, prompt, seed, kind, checks {loop, feet_on_ground}, root_travel, end_yaw_deg, hit_time (attacks), yaw_profile (turns: degrees every 0.1 s), speed_profile (starts/stops).
4 `python anim_validate.py <name>` with the editor open: pose within 3 cm tolerance (measured 0.4-0.9 mm) AND the engine's root heading (Bip01 = the locator) within 1.5 degrees (measured 0.1).
5 Put it in a table of villager_anim.py (ATTACKS, AIMS, DEATHS, SITS, TURNS, TRANSITIONS), `python examples/ashvale/villager_anim.py write`, RESTART the editor (trap-mannequin-reload-after-change-crashes-editor), `mannequin_check` with reload=false, test_kimodo_clips.py, test_villager_anim.py, test_anim_sample.py (it reads each clip's `checks`: one-shots promise no loop closure, falls and sits no feet on the ground).

title: TRAP: the engine takes the locator's FIRST frame out of a clip - position AND heading; a locator that does not start at the origin...
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: TRAP: the engine takes the locator's FIRST frame out of a clip - position AND heading; a locator that does not start at the origin facing 0 moves every joint by the difference
Two bugs, same cause (2026-10-15): (1) the death clips were 5.5 cm off at every joint because the locator path (a low-passed pelvis path) did not start at the origin: anim_oneshot.make_clip now subtracts loc[0]; (2) the turn clips were 1-3 cm off, worst at the arms and feet, with opposite-signed offsets for the left and right foot (a rotation about the vertical, about 5 degrees), because the low-passed heading with its edges held was +4 degrees at frame 0: make_clip now subtracts loc_yaw[0]. The engine's Bip01 (= the locator) then shows the heading 0 at t = 0 and the clip's end heading at t = 1.
HOW IT WAS FOUND: anim_validate failed with a median error of 9 mm over ALL joints at t = 0 (a systematic offset, not a bad joint); per-joint difference vectors showed a translation (death) and a rotation (turn). motionbricks_validate.validate now also compares the root's heading (positive = left) with the heading the clip was built with (expected.json root_yaw_deg), tolerance 1.5 degrees; test_kimodo_clips.py reproduces the bug by hand (the unsubtracted low-passed heading is not 0) as its control.
RELATED: sampling a clip BETWEEN key frames compares the engine's slerp with a linear interpolation of expected positions (decimetres off during a fast fall): expected_samples snaps times to key frames.

title: TRAP: re-reading the Mannequin files in the RUNNING editor after they changed (mannequin_check reload=true) hung the main thread
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: TRAP: re-reading the Mannequin files in the RUNNING editor after they changed (mannequin_check reload=true) hung the main thread and then crashed Sandbox - restart the editor instead
2026-10-15 18:41: after `villager_anim.py write` grew Villager.adb from 36 to 63 fragments, `mannequin_check` (reload=true is the default: bridge.mannequin.check ... | reload -> RevertTagDef / RevertControllerDef / RevertDatabase) timed out ('the main thread is genuinely blocked') and the next call found the connection closed: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION reading 0xE0000800F in CryAction.dll, called from ClaudeBridgePlugin DispatchBridgeCommand (symbolize.py on the plugin's PDB; error.log in the project folder). The watchdog restarted the editor, which loaded the NEW files; `mannequin_check(reload=false)` then passed (63 fragments, 0 errors, 63 animations used, none missing). Earlier growths of the same files reloaded fine, so the cause is not simply the size: live NPC action controllers hold the old database.
RULE: after changing Villager.adb / VillagerFragmentIds.xml / VillagerControllerDefinition.xml restart the editor (the build task does) and check with reload=false. Reloading files that did NOT change (project_audit does it) is safe.

title: FACT (measured): MotionBricks' idle mode is a held stance that ignores the facing direction - no breathing idle and no turn on the spot...
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: FACT (measured): MotionBricks' idle mode is a held stance that ignores the facing direction - no breathing idle and no turn on the spot; the starts and stops were cut from scripted scenarios
motionbricks_scenario.py records scripted signal sequences (movement_direction, facing_direction, mode over time; the venv's Python). MEASURED: 'idle' = a static clip: no joint of the retargeted body moves more than 1.2 cm in 8 s; turn_left_90 / turn_right_90 / turn_180 scenarios (idle with the facing rotated) give a yaw change of about 0 and a root travel of 0.00 m. So MotionBricks cannot turn on the spot or breathe: the villagers keep the library's relaxed idle and the turns come from Kimodo. mb_idle exists (a 1 s loop of the stance) as the pose the starts and stops begin and end in.
START and STOP DO work: idle -> walk style (speed 0.01 -> cruise in about 1 s) and walk -> idle (decelerating over about 1 s), for slow_walk / walk_scared / injured_walk / walk_stealth. motionbricks_actions.py cuts them: start = from 5 frames before the speed passes 0.05 m/s to the frame, within 40 frames after the speed reaches 92 % of its cruise, whose pose (head, hands, feet, calves, chest relative to the pelvis, plus velocities) is NEAREST to frame 0 of the gait's walk loop (so the loop can take over; distance 0.002-0.038); stop = from at most 1.2 s before the body comes to rest (92 % mark) to 8 frames after it stopped. The root travels with the body (root='path'): starts cover 0.54-0.97 m in 1.5-1.7 s, stops 0.29-0.56 m in 1.57-1.67 s; manifest speed_profile has the locator speed every 0.1 s. Engine-proven (within 0.9 mm).
NOT USED BY THE GAME: villagers move by the navigation system at a constant speed (the path follower's acceleration 4 m/s2, deceleration 6 m/s2 by default), so a start or a stop needs nav acceleration/deceleration matched to the clip and a trigger from the remaining distance, both of which need the path follower's braking checked in the RUNNING game. The fragments (StartSlow/StopSlow ...) and the table kTransitions are there.

title: PLAYBOOK: how the NPC code uses the Kimodo clips - random attack/aim/death variants with a per-clip hit moment
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Full title: PLAYBOOK: how the NPC code uses the Kimodo clips - random attack/aim/death variants with a per-clip hit moment, turn-on-the-spot in conversations along the clip's heading curve, sit actions
ADDED (2026-10-15 night; Game.dll Profile built 18:47, NOT packaged, NOT run, so NOT seen in motion):
* VillagerAnimTable.h (generated by villager_anim.py) now holds kAttacks/kAims/kDeaths {fragment, clip, hitSeconds}, kSitDown/kSitLoop/kStandUp, kTurns {fragment, clip, signed degrees, normalised heading profile every 0.1 s} and kTransitions {start/stop fragment and clip, travel}. 63 fragments in the Mannequin database; mannequin_check: 0 errors, 63 animations used, none missing.
* PlayAction(Attack|Aim|Death) picks a variant at random (never the same twice running); the old clip is the fallback when no variant loaded. SetupGestures logs 'Kimodo clips 3/3 attacks, 2/2 aims, 3/3 deaths, 4/4 turns'. BanditBrain damages the player when m_attackTime reaches m_body.GetAttackHitSeconds() (0.533 s for the Kimodo swings, 0.55 for the old kick) instead of a constant. Aim stays a 1.5 s action (the draw is 1.1 s). The death clips are only seen with claude_ragdoll 0: the default turns a killed bandit into a ragdoll at once.
* Turn on the spot: BeginConversation calls FaceTowards(withWhom, true). A standing body (speed under 0.15 m/s) that is not busy and has to turn 50 degrees or more plays TurnLeft/TurnRight (50-135) or Turn180Left/Right (over 135) and is rotated each frame by total x the clip's heading profile (m_turn: UpdateTurn, TryTurnInPlace, CancelTurn); when the clip ends, or the body walks off, the slerp finishes the last degrees. If the body still moves when asked, UpdateFacing waits up to a second for it to stop. IsFacing() is false until the turn is over. Cvar claude_turn_in_place 0 switches it off. Combat facing (bandits) and the brain's Face steps (they time out at 1.2 s, shorter than the clip) keep the fast slerp.
* Sit: EVillagerAction SitDown/SitLoop/StandUp (SitLoop holds); `claude_npc_action <npc> SitDown` plays one. No bench or stool exists in the level, so no brain uses them; the clips carry 0.4-0.55 m of root travel that is not applied.
CHECKS: test_villager_anim.py 28, test_kimodo_clips.py 18, test_anim_sample.py 93 (one-shots promise no loop; turns: the engine's root ends at end_yaw_deg; attacks: hit inside the clip), test_motionbricks.py 32, test_anim_check 26, test_character_check 12.
