title: How do I change the map (M key) or move the player's pin on it?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
The M map is a FlashUI page, not a minimap. AshvaleMenus.cpp (page key "map", ~line 379) draws ONE baked image per goal (Libs/UI/Textures/ashvale_map.dds, ashvale_map_hilda/_tom/_chest.dds, made by make_map.py) and a separate 22x22 pin image (pin_you.dds) at the player's position.
The pin position is a linear map from world metres to screen pixels: constants at AshvaleMenus.cpp:24-25 (kMapX0/X1 = 340..710, kMapY0/Y1 = 100..840 world metres; image at 800,40, 320x640 px) and MapPixel() at lines ~33-38: u = (x-X0)/(X1-X0), v = (Y1-y)/(Y1-Y0), clamped. To show a bigger area, re-bake the image with make_map.py for the new rectangle and change these four constants together.
Trap (measured 2026-09-30, the project notes): the menu movie draws ONE small image correctly; with two images every pin draws as whichever loaded last. That is why the gold goal pin is baked into the map and only the player's pin is a separate image. A second moving marker (an NPC) needs a different route (see howto-compass-in-the-hud).
The goal logic (which pin the map shows) is the if/else on flags right above the image call: tithe_returned -> none, has_tithe -> Hilda, wat_dead or found_tom -> chest, met_hilda -> Tom, else Hilda.

title: How do I make a real minimap texture for a level with the engine's own tool?
source: manual 25534556 'Terrain Minimaps'; manual 23306542 'Invoking Flash Functions'; Code/Components/AshvaleMenus.cpp
content:
The manual's route (Terrain Minimaps, page 25534556, Editor Tools > Terrain Editor): open the level, Terrain Editor > Mini Map tab, choose the area, size and resolution, press Generate Mini Map. It writes a .dds plus an .xml with the start and end world coordinates next to the level. The CVars used while capturing come from Editor/MapScreenShotSettings.xml (r_PostProcessEffects 0, e_Vegetation 0, e_Shadows 0, e_ViewDistRatio 100000000 ...); back the file up before editing. The page says Scaleform must be installed.
To show it in a HUD: the manual's "Invoking Flash Functions" page (23306542, section Loading a Minimap) has the movie load the .dds with loadMovie("img://" + path, MiniMapMC) from a function you call by IUIElement::CallFunction, and move a player marker by converting world x,y into the .xml's start/end range (the page notes the map is rotated -90 degrees, so x and y swap).
Status in this project: NOT used. Ashvale's map is a baked image made by make_map.py and drawn by the menu movie (see howto-map-page-baked-image-and-pin-math). The menu movie draws one image reliably, so a live minimap needs its own UIElement and .gfx authored in Flash tooling that this machine does not have; that is why a compass drawn in code (howto-compass-in-the-hud) is the cheaper proposal.

title: How could I add a compass strip or a minimap to the in-game HUD? (proposal, not built)
source: Code/Components/AshvaleGame.cpp:1778,1868-1905; Code/Components/Player.cpp (m_lookYaw)
content:
PROPOSAL, not built. The HUD is drawn in code every frame by CAshvaleGame::DrawHud() (AshvaleGame.cpp:1868) with IRenderAuxText::Draw2dLabel and IRenderAuxGeometry quads (AshvaleGame.cpp:1778 DrawQuad); there is no Flash HUD. A compass fits that style: take the camera yaw (the player keeps m_lookYaw in Player.cpp), convert to degrees, and draw the letters N E S W (and tick marks) as Draw2dLabel calls at x = centre + (bearing difference) * pixelsPerDegree, clipped to a strip near the top; draw one quad as the centre marker. A goal marker is the same with the bearing to the goal (atan2 of goal minus player, the goal is the one the map page chooses from flags).
A minimap in the same style would draw the baked map image with a pixel rectangle through the engine's 2D image path, but this project has only drawn text and quads there, so treat it as untested; the menu movie route is documented in howto-map-page-baked-image-and-pin-math. Test it the project's way: the HUD only shows in the packaged game or game mode, so it needs the user's yes to run it (the editor viewport does not call game.Update).

title: How do I let the player remap keys, and where are the keys bound now? (no gamepad)
source: Code/Components/Player.cpp:190-300; Code/Components/AshvaleMenus.cpp:279-283; Code/Components/AshvaleSettings.h; CryEngine/CryCommon/CryAction/IActionMapManager.h:264-285; manual 29428286
content:
Today every key is bound in code and the Controls page is a fixed list. Player.cpp:~190-300 creates a CInputComponent and, per action, calls RegisterAction("player", name, callback) then BindAction("player", name, eAID_KeyboardMouse, EKeyId::eKI_X): moveleft A, moveright D, moveforward W, moveback S, sprint LShift, jump Space, interact E, torch T, menu F1, map M, menu_up/down Up/Down, menu_select Enter, menu_left/right Left/Right, attack Mouse1, block Mouse2, eat Q, quicksave F5, quickload F9, choice1-4 keys 1-4, pause Escape, journal J, inventory I, mouse_rotateyaw/pitch MouseX/MouseY (30 BindAction("player", ...) calls in all). The Controls page (AshvaleMenus.cpp:~279) is a hard-coded tile list, so it would lie after a remap. Settings are saved as "name value" lines in %USER%/ashvale_settings.cfg by AshvaleSettings (brightness, volume, music, mouse sens, quality only).
The engine's way (manual 'Input and Action Mapping', page 29428286, section Action rebinding): IActionMap::ReBindActionInput. Source: IActionMapManager.h:272 ReBindActionInput(actionId, szCurrentInput, szNewInput) 'rebinds ... to a new input of the same device type'; the overload at :280 takes (szNewInput, device, deviceIndex). The manual warns that a CInputComponent and your own use of the Action Map Manager should not be mixed; CInputComponent.RegisterAction creates the "player" action map itself, so test that ReBindActionInput on that map works before building UI on it.
PROPOSAL: (1) one table of {action, default key} used by both Player.cpp and the Controls page; (2) a Controls page of buttons "Move forward: W" that wait for a key (CAshvaleUI has no key-capture; the keyboard on pages is CAshvaleUI::Navigate); (3) save one "bind <action> <key>" line each in ashvale_settings.cfg and replay them at start. Gamepad is NOT wanted (user, 2026-10-23): bind keyboard and mouse only.

title: How do I add a new HUD element (a bar, a counter, a notice) to Ashvale?
source: Code/Components/AshvaleGame.cpp:78,1778,1868-1976; Code/Components/AshvaleUI.h; manual 23306537, 23306534
content:
Ashvale's HUD is NOT a FlashUI element. CAshvaleGame::DrawHud() (AshvaleGame.cpp:1868) runs each frame while playing and draws: a health bar (DrawQuad, AshvaleGame.cpp:1778) with "Health %.0f | Coins %d | Bread %d (Q)" text, a GUARD label, the objective line at (32,28) and a second side-objective line at (32,52), a '+' crosshair at the screen centre, the interact prompt (m_prompt) below it and a timed notice (m_notice) with a fade. Dialogue is DrawDialogue (:1911), the pause menu DrawMenu (:1951). Fonts are IRenderAuxText::Draw2dLabel(x, y, scale, ColorF, centered, fmt, ...): one line per call (WrapWords at :78 splits long text).
To add an element: add state to CAshvaleGame, set it where the event happens, and draw it in DrawHud next to the others. Layout rule found by the project: the dialogue box must stay above the health block (DrawHud draws from s.h-92 down), measure at 1280x720 as well as 2560x1440. Screen size comes from the renderer each frame; do not hard-code pixels.
The engine's alternative is a FlashUI UIElement (manual 'UI Element', page 23306537, and 'Using FlashUI from C++', 23306534): an XML in Libs/UI/UIElements declaring the .gfx and its functions/events/variables, then IFlashUI::GetUIElement(name)->CallFunction. Ashvale uses that only for menus (MainMenu.xml + GameSDK's Menus_Startmenu.gfx). A HUD movie would need authoring in Flash tooling; the sample's HUD .gfx files are not copied into the project.
Check: the HUD only runs in game mode or the packaged game (not in the editor viewport), so a look needs the user's yes to run the game; screenshots from the engine never contain 2D UI (trap-engine-screenshot-has-no-2d-ui), capture the window.

title: How do I add a new music track or looping sound to the project's audio library?
source: Assets/audio/sdlmixer/ace/claude_music.xml; Code/Components/Soundscape.cpp:54-64; assets/make_music.py:16-32,394-415; manual 44964959, 51347481
content:
Wiring in this project (SDL Mixer, s_ImplName CryAudioImplSDLMixer): (1) the file goes to Assets/audio/sdlmixer/assets/<name>.ogg (manual 'SDL Mixer Initial Setup' 44964959: 16-bit, 48 kHz, mono or stereo; Crytek's packager has NO *.wav in its copy whitelist, so encode to .ogg). (2) The ACE library Assets/audio/sdlmixer/ace/claude_music.xml holds, per track, a start trigger <Trigger name="ash_music_X_start"><Event name="ash_music_X.ogg" type="start" volume="-5" loop_count="0" fade_in_time="3.0"/></Trigger> (loop_count 0 = infinite), a stop trigger with type="stop" fade_out_time="3.0", and a <Parameter name="ash_vol_music_X"><Event name="ash_music_X.ogg"/></Parameter> for volume. The header counts (triggers="12" parameters="6") must be updated. assets/make_music.py writes this file for the six existing tracks (menu, day, night, danger, end, crypt) - add yours to its TRACKS dict (line ~394) instead of hand-editing, or the next run drops your entry. (3) Code: Soundscape.cpp:~54-64 holds an SLayer array {name, CryAudio::StringToId("ash_music_X_start"), ..._stop, ...param, bit, bMusic, speed}; add a row and the cross-fade logic that picks which track is the target (the layers ease at 0.33-0.5 levels per second; music is multiplied by the music volume slider).
Checks: audio_triggers (lists ACE triggers and events), audio_report (measures the file: duration, loudness, loop seam), then package: a malformed XML (a '--' inside a comment) is silently not converted and the OLD copy ships (trap-rc-malformed-xml-ships-stale-copy). I cannot hear; the user judges music by ear.

title: How do I translate the game, and which texts are hard-coded in Ashvale?
source: manual 25534808, 23306533; Assets/localization/; Code/Components/AshvaleMenus.cpp; Assets/libs/ashvale/dialogue.xml
content:
The engine's system (manual 'Localization System' 25534808 and 'UI Localization' 23306533): a text is written as '@key' (for example UseMessage = "@use_object"); the table lives in Localization/<Language>_XML.pak (or loose Localization/<language>/) as text_ui*.xml spreadsheets with columns KEY, ORIGINAL TEXT, TRANSLATED TEXT; g_language names the language pak (german -> German.pak); a label passed to a FlashUI text field via SetVariable("@somelabel") is translated on the way; the same folder carries the font library HUD_Font_LocFont.gfx. Loose xml files in Localization are read before pak content.
What Ashvale does: NOTHING of this. Assets/localization/ holds only english_xml/HUD_Font_LocFont.gfx (required so the menu movie exposes its functions), no text_ui file. Every shown string is a literal in C++ (AshvaleMenus.cpp buttons and the Controls tiles, AshvaleGame.cpp HUD and notices, journal and quest text) or in libs/ashvale/dialogue.xml (about 200 lines of dialogue, voice files named by node index).
PROPOSAL to make it localisable: route each literal through one function that looks up '@ashvale_<id>' (ILocalizationManager via gEnv->pSystem->GetLocalizationManager - check the header before use), ship Localization/english_xml/text_ui_ashvale.xml, keep dialogue in dialogue.xml with a per-language copy, and re-render voices per language (render_voices names files by node index). The proof needs a game run (the user's yes). No other language is requested; this is parked.

title: Can the player ride a horse or drive a cart in Ashvale? What does the engine offer?
source: CryPlugins/CryDefaultEntities/.../Physics/Vehicles/VehicleComponent.h:122, WheelComponent.h:60; manual 23306516, 26214869, 29798907, 29798905; GAPS audit E-13
content:
NOT BUILT. Ashvale has no vehicle, mount or animal (audit E-13, G-08, A-14). What exists to start from:
(1) Components for a component game: 'Vehicle Physics' (Code/CryPlugins/CryDefaultEntities/Module/DefaultComponents/Physics/Vehicles/VehicleComponent.h:122, engine and gear parameters) and 'Wheel Collider' (WheelComponent.h:60). They give physics driving only: no seats, no enter/exit, no damage; you write the driver logic.
(2) The classic Vehicle System in CryAction (manual 'Vehicle System' 23306516, 'Vehicle Editor' 26214869, 'Vehicle XML Reference' 29798907, 'Vehicle Entity' 29798905): vehicle classes defined in XML (Parts, Helpers, Seats, Actions, MovementParams), IVehicleSeat/IVehicleAnimation interfaces, Lua scripts under Scripts/Entities/Vehicles. The GameSDK sample has the data (HMMWV, Abrams, Blackhawk, boat, bike: see gamesdk-vehicles), but the IVehicleClient is implemented in the GameSDK game DLL, which this project does not use, so a component game must supply its own client.
(3) A horse is not a vehicle in the manual; the closest is a character with a rider attachment and your own locomotion. No mount animations exist in the library or in the Kimodo/MotionBricks clips.
Recommendation: skip unless the story needs it; a cart or boat as a scripted Track View ride is far cheaper than driving physics. Any vehicle needs a game run to judge.

title: Does Ashvale support multiplayer or online play? What does Release do with network code?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
NOT BUILT, and not planned. Ashvale is single player; entities are not bound to the network. The Release engine's CryNetwork is a PURE CLIENT build ('[Network Version]: RELEASE PURE CLIENT' in game.log), so a Release package cannot host: 'map <level> s' (Crytek's template default, a listen server) never loads, the game must boot with 'map ashvale' (trap-map-s-pure-client).
What the manual offers (all engine code, none used here): 'CryNetwork' 23308730 (purpose, channels, contexts), 'Network Serialization and Aspects' 26874253, 'Exposing an Entity to the Network' 23306593, entity 'Networking' 26216232 (INetEntity::BindToNetwork before IEntitySystem::InitEntity, SNetObjectID, compression policies, RMIs, spawn replication), 'Network Scheduling' 23306391. A component game would reflect state through NetSerialize and aspects on every component (player, NPC, health, quests, dialogue state), which this code base does not do; the save/load path is a custom XML, not engine serialisation.
Related and DIFFERENT: the editor bridge socket 127.0.0.1:37778 (the plugin) and the game's own command server on port 37777 (GamePlugin.h:111 kBridgePort, TcpCommandServer.cpp) are development tools, not game networking. The user decided on 2026-10-23 that the Release game must have no debug commands (see policy-release-has-no-debug-commands).

title: Trees pop in or vanish too early/late: which view distance and LOD settings apply?
source: the MCP server cvar catalog (cvar_info e_ViewDistRatio, e_LodRatio, e_ViewDistRatioVegetation, sys_spec_ObjectDetail); Game.cryproject:35; Assets/levels/ashvale/layers/main.lyr
content:
Values from the project's CVar catalog (cvar_info; source Cry3DEngine/cvars.cpp): e_ViewDistRatio 'View distance ratio for objects' source default 60 (:873); e_LodRatio 'LOD distance ratio for objects' default 6 (:865); e_ViewDistRatioVegetation default 30 (:881). All three are settable in Release only by game code (ICVar::Set) or user/game.cfg, not by the command line. They are set by the group sys_spec_ObjectDetail: level 1: ViewDist 50 / Lod 10 / Vegetation 50; level 2 (the project's Game.cryproject sets sys_spec 2): 75 / 15 / 75; level 4: 125 / 40 / 125; default level 100 / 20 / 100. The editor dump showed 75 / 15 / 75.
Per object: a brush has ViewDistRatio and LodRatio as PERCENT of the global value (the level's main.lyr brushes carry ViewDistRatio="100" LodRatio="100"); a vegetation brush has its own size/ratio fields in the Vegetation panel; lights have ViewDistRatio (manual Light Entity). Shadow casters have e_ShadowsCastViewDistRatio.
How to change safely: through the Quality setting (AshvaleSettings::Apply pushes sys_spec), not by raising ratios blindly; each doubling of view distance multiplies the objects drawn. Measure with perf_tour.py (vsync off) and remember cheat CVars do nothing in Release (trap-cheat-cvar-dead-in-release). LODs are authored ($lodN_ child nodes; the engine has no LOD generator in 5.7.1; a path containing '_lod' is refused).

title: Distant trees look wrong or I want billboard imposters for forests: is there such a feature?
source: the MCP server cvar catalog (cvar_search 'sprite'); Code/Sandbox/EditorQt/Vegetation/VegetationMap.cpp:410; manual 29449085
content:
In 5.7.1 the old vegetation sprite system is switched off. The CVar catalog lists e_VegetationSprites (default 0), e_VegetationSpritesDistanceRatio, e_VegetationSpritesMinDistance, e_VegetationSpritesBatching, e_LodTransitionSpriteMinDist/DistRatio, r_VegetationSpritesTexRes (128) and r_VegetationSpritesGenAlways/NoGen/Debug/MaxLightingUpdates ALL flagged DEPRECATED (several also CONST), none settable in editor, Profile or Release (cvars.cpp:355-381, RendererCVars.cpp:2748-2753). Only the editor command ed_GenerateBillboardTextures remains ('Generate billboard textures for all level vegetations having UseSprites flag enabled', Sandbox VegetationMap.cpp:410); nothing was found that draws them. The manual's only 'imposter' page is the ParticleImposter shader (29449085), an unlit particle shader, unrelated to trees.
So distant forest cost is controlled by: view-distance ratios (see fact-view-distance-lod-ratio-and-quality-groups), authored $lodN_ meshes on the tree models (the GameSDK trees ship with LODs), and merged meshes for grass (e_MergedMeshes works in Release). Ashvale has 8,045 slope trees and 34,735 grass tufts; the packaged Release run measured 418-575 fps, so there is no measured need for imposters.
Not tested: ed_GenerateBillboardTextures was never run here; do not promise it works.

title: NPCs never sit down: what benches does the level have and what is missing for sitting?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
What exists (counted from Assets/levels/ashvale/layers/main.lyr on 2026-10-23): 26 bench brushes = Objects/props/furniture/log_furniture/bench_a.cgf x18 + bench_b.cgf x8, and 7 tables (table_a.cgf). By place: Tavern 4 benches (Tavern_BenchA1/A2/B1/B2) plus Prop_Tavern_3/4, Reeve house Reeve_Bench/Bench2 plus Prop_Reeve_3, the chapel's 8 pews (Chapel_Pew0_0 ... Pew3_2, bench_b) plus Prop_Chapel_0/1, three cottages (CottageA/B/C_Bench plus Prop_Cottage*_3) and Tom's cabin (z 44). Origin z is ground level (36.25); rotations are quaternions (identity, 90 degrees about Z, or 180).
What exists in code: the sit clips kd_sit_down, kd_sit_idle (loop) and kd_stand_up (Kimodo, engine-proven) and the actions SitDown/SitLoop/StandUp (Npc.h:40, Npc.cpp:1679/1698, console claude_npc_action). The clips carry about 0.4-0.5 m of root travel that the game does not apply. NO brain plays them and there are no sit anchors. An earlier note said the level had no bench or stool: that was wrong (corrected 2026-10-23).
PROPOSAL (design, not built): (1) an anchor per bench = a position on the seat, a facing, a seat height, an approach point on the navmesh in front; either a small SitAnchor component placed beside each bench or a table generated from the layer file by a script (the bench's pos/rotation + a per-model offset measured once with cgf_bounds.py); (2) a villager brain step 'SitAt(anchor)': NavigateTo(approach), FaceTowards(anchor facing), play SitDown, move the character root by the clip's travel, hold SitLoop, StandUp on a trigger (time, dusk, conversation); (3) a test in the running game only (the user's yes). Conversations: a sitting NPC needs the turn and look logic to refuse turn clips.

title: How would I add blood splats or footprints when something is hit? (0 decals exist today)
source: Code/Components/Npc.cpp:1189,2059; CryEngine/CryCommon/Cry3DEngine/I3DEngine.h:1544, CryEngineDecalInfo.h:18-43; engine_data/gamesdk_decals.json
content:
Status: the level holds 0 decals and the game code never spawns one (grep of Code/ finds no CreateDecal). Material source: the GameSDK sample has 159 decal materials, 10 of them blood (materials/decals/blood/blood_splat1..5, blood_splatx1..3, flesh2, human_body) and footstep_dirt / footstep_snow; import one with import_gamesdk_asset.py (copies the .mtl and its textures into Assets). decal_materials lists them, decal_preview looks at one in the editor viewport.
Two ways: (A) a Decal level object (editor type Decal; properties Material, ProjectionType 0..3, ProjectionDepth, SortPriority, ViewDistRatio): fixed places only (puddles, road edge dirt). MEASURED trap (decal_lab, test_decal_lab.py): a decal draws only within ProjectionDepth (default 1 m) of the surface; 2 m above the ground nothing draws, Planar included; over a brush slab a decal did not draw (unresolved). (B) at run time from game code: I3DEngine::CreateDecal(const CryEngineDecalInfo&) (I3DEngine.h:1544); the struct (CryEngineDecalInfo.h:18-43) has vPos, vNormal, fSize, fLifeTime, ownerInfo, bSkipOverlappingTest, bDeferred and szMaterialName (path of the decal material). Not used or tested here; I did not find how blood on characters (ownerInfo for a skinned owner) behaves.
Where to hook: Npc.cpp PlayHitReaction (line 1189, called from the health callback at ~2059) knows the hit; raycast to the ground below the victim for vPos/vNormal, pick a blood_splat material at random, fLifeTime 30-60 s. Needs the shader permutation for the decal material in the shader cache (run the shader tour after adding it, trap-shader-cache-stale-after-any-material-change) and a game run to judge.

title: NPCs talk with a closed mouth: what does the engine offer for lip-sync and what is missing?
source: manual 29450435, 26874142, 23306439; ENGINE_LEARNING_PLAN.md C4; corpus finding-the-gamesdk-human-has-a-facial-rig-and-expression-library
content:
Engine tools (manual): the Facial Editor (29450435) has Lip Sync > Extract Phonemes (analyses a loaded waveform, optionally with its text for accuracy) and Batch Process Directory (audio -> .fsq facial sequences named like the audio file). Facial sequences play from Track View (the Facial Sequence track, 26874142) or code (Facial Animation Programming 23306439: CFacialSentence). The preview pane needs a model with at least one morph target OR an attachment; the Facial Editor also has LookIK and procedural eye/eyelid animation.
What the sample human has (earlier survey, see finding-the-gamesdk-human-has-a-facial-rig-and-expression-library): 16 FCL_* facial bones, an expression library skeleton_player_generic.fxl with 60 expressions (phonemes, Visime_*), no morph targets (bone-driven), no .fsq shipped. Villagers wear head_a.skin (10 weighted bones); head_anim.skin (27) is the animatable head.
What this project lacks: the head swap, any .fsq, any code that starts a facial sequence on the speaker, and the voice-to-phoneme step. Voices are Piper lines rendered per dialogue node (render_voices, files named by node index; 44 lines), so each line's audio length and text are known: a batch .fsq per file via the Facial Editor is the natural route, then the Mannequin or facial-system call when a node starts. Everything needs a game run to judge (the editor ticks no animation); I cannot hear or see mouths. Not started; facial work is listed as audit A-17.

title: Where do footstep sounds come from now, and how do I use animation events (.animevents)?
source: Code/Components/Player.cpp:945-962; Code/Components/Npc.cpp:1425-1440; skeleton_player_generic.chrparams:311; animations.pak events.animevents (parsed 2026-10-23); CryCommon/CryAnimation/Examples/ControllerAnimationEvents.cpp; manual 29450425, 44964889
content:
Today (Ashvale): the player's footsteps are by DISTANCE walked: Player.cpp:~948-962 adds the metres moved per frame and plays AshvaleAudio::kStepPlayer every kStride (one sound, no surface switch). NPC footsteps are detected from the foot bones: the stance probe in Npc.cpp:~1425-1440 sees a heel go down while the body moves (> 0.4 m/s, 0.25 s apart per foot) and calls AshvaleAudio::PlayAt(entity, kStepNpc). Neither uses animation events.
The engine's way (manual 'Animation Events - Character Tool' 29450425, 'Audio & Foley/Footsteps' 44964889): events are keyed on the animation timeline in the Character Tool and stored in a .animevents file named in the chrparams by <Animation name="$AnimEventDatabase" path="..."/>. The project's skeleton_player_generic.chrparams:311 points to Animations/human/male/events.animevents, which is inside animations.pak (305 KB; measured: 629 animations, 627 'footstep' events, 520 'foley', 222 'ForceFeedback', 70 'audio_trigger', 30 RagdollStart). The new Kimodo/MotionBricks clips (kd_*, mb_*) are NOT in that file, so they carry no events.
Receiving them in a component: ENTITY_EVENT_ANIM_EVENT with event.nParam[0] = AnimEventInstance* and nParam[1] = ICharacterInstance* (example: CryCommon/CryAnimation/Examples/ControllerAnimationEvents.cpp; the engine's AdvancedAnimationComponent.cpp:150 forwards it to the action controller). The sample then looks the surface up through MaterialEffects (footstep_player library, ACE switch per surface). PROPOSAL: add footstep events to the clips (a project .animevents or edit events.animevents in a copy), subscribe to the event in CNpcComponent, keep the heel probe as the fallback; surfaces need MaterialEffects (see howto-material-effects-surface-driven-footsteps).

title: Feet float on slopes or hands miss props: which IK is defined and which is actually used?
source: skeleton_player_generic.chrparams:1-111; Code/Components/Npc.cpp:1155-1182; manual 23308002, 23308004, 26873908, 23308003, 23307999; CryCommon/CryAnimation/Examples/LookIK.cpp
content:
Defined in Assets/objects/characters/human/generic/skeleton_player_generic.chrparams (the villagers' skeleton): LimbIK_Definition with four 2-bone IK handles (RgtArm01/LftArm01 root UpperArm end Hand, RgtLeg01/LftLeg01 root Thigh end Foot, Solver 2BIK); Animation_Driven_IK_Targets (10 ADIKTarget entries for rifle/pistol/pocket/weapon hand targets); FeetLock_Definition (both leg handles); Recoil_Definition; LookIK_Definition (eye attachments eye_left/eye_right, DirectionalBlends AnimToken LookPoses, ParameterJoint Bip01 Look) and AimIK_Definition (AimPoses tokens, pelvis/spine rotations, weapon joints).
Used by Ashvale: only Look IK, and through Mannequin, not through the chrparams blend: Npc.cpp UpdateLookAt() (line ~1155) sets the action controller's 'LookTarget' every frame on the LookPose scope (layer 15) using the engine's LookPose procedural clip. Aim: the Kimodo kd_aim clips play as normal animations; the archers do not use AimIK. No code calls the pose aligner, Limb IK handles or FeetLock (grep of Code/ for PoseAligner, LimbIK, FeetLock, AimIK finds nothing).
Manual: 'Limb IK' 23308002, 'Leg and Foot Ground Alignment' 23308004 and 'Ground Alignment' 26873908 (a script/pose-aligner setup), 'Animation Driven IK' 23308003, 'Look IK' / 'Aim IK (aimposes)' 23308006, 'Character Parameters File (chrparams)' 23307999 (an IK_Definition block, at most one LimbIK/FeetLock block). Engine example for Look IK from code: CryCommon/CryAnimation/Examples/LookIK.cpp (GetIPoseBlenderLook()->SetState/SetLayer/SetTarget).
Measured earlier: real foot slide was 5 % and is removed by claude_stride_match, so foot IK is not the first fix. Slopes: ground alignment is the engine's answer; needs a game run to judge. NOT seen in motion.

title: How do the villagers' Mannequin files use transitions, tags and scopes (and what could they)?
source: Assets/Animations/Mannequin/ADB/Villager.adb (grep counts 2026-10-23); manual 29450872, 29450874, 29450859, 29450870; examples/ashvale/villager_anim.py
content:
Measured on Assets/Animations/Mannequin/ADB/Villager.adb (2026-10-23): 65 fragment entries, 0 <Transition elements, and 63 of the fragments carry Tags="" (no tag used). Files: Villager.adb, VillagerControllerDefinition.xml, VillagerFragmentIds.xml, VillagerTags.xml, all generated from ONE table by villager_anim.py (never hand-edit; the Npc code refers to the generated VillagerAnimTable.h). Scopes: the main body scope plus 'LookPose' (layer 15, Persistent + AutoReinstall) for Look IK.
So every change between fragments uses the target clip's own blend time; there are no authored transitions, no tag-selected variants and no upper-body/lower-body split (a fidget plays on the whole body only while standing idle; a gesture ends when the body moves).
Manual: 'Mannequin Transitions' 29450872 (a Mannequin transition is a description of how to go from one fragment to another, edited in the Transition Browser/Editor, stored in the .adb; the default blend is the clip's), 'Mannequin Tags & Tag Definitions' 29450874 (tag names unique and case-insensitive, groups are mutually exclusive, definitions can include others only by XML editing), 'Mannequin Scopes' 29450859 and 'Mannequin Scope Contexts' 29450870 (a scope is a slice of the character with its own layers; scope masks decide which scopes a fragment uses), Tutorial 3 on transitions 23308485.
Uses worth doing: tags for Gait/Weapon/Mood so a single 'Walk' fragment picks the right clip (replaces the WalkSlow/WalkScared/... fragment names), an upper-body scope for the bow draw or a wave while walking, transitions for start/stop (the mb_start/mb_stop clips exist but are not wired). Checks: mannequin_check (the loader drops an unknown fragment, option or transition SILENTLY, a transition with an unknown fragment leaves no log line). NEVER reload the Mannequin files in the running editor (trap-mannequin-reload-after-change-crashes-editor): restart it.

title: Could LiveCreate replace closing the editor to rebuild Game.dll?
source: CryEngine/CryLiveCreate/*; CryCommon/CryLiveCreate/ILiveCreateManager.h; CrySystem/SystemInit.cpp:1241-1262; cvar sys_livecreate (SystemInit.cpp:5137); installed bin/win_x64/CryLiveCreate.dll; manual search (no page)
content:
Short answer from the source, NOT from the manual (the manual has no LiveCreate page; a search finds only a mention in the Resource Compiler overview and a FreeSDK release note): probably NO. CryLiveCreate (Code/CryEngine/CryLiveCreate, CryLiveCreate.dll is in the installed bin/win_x64) is a manager of remote HOSTS and PLATFORMS: ILiveCreateManager.h has IHostInfo (GetTargetName, GetAddress, GetPlatformName, Connect, Disconnect), IManager (CanSend, SetEnabled, GetHost, CreateHost(platform, ipAddress), platform handler factories), IRealtimeRemoteUpdate.h and LiveCreateCommands.h. It is for sending editor changes (objects, level data) to a running game on another device, not for swapping a compiled game module. CSystem::InitLiveCreate (CrySystem/SystemInit.cpp:1241) loads the module unless sys_livecreate is 0 (CVar help: 0 disabled/use Null implementation, 1 fully enabled, 2 disabled but initialized); NO_LIVECREATE is defined on Apple and Linux. There is no Sandbox LiveCreate plugin in the installed EditorPlugins folder, and a CVar offers a 'LiveCreate MoCap Editor' on startup.
Why the loop closes the editor: Game.dll is locked while Sandbox runs, so the link fails (claude_game_build.bat kills Sandbox, builds, relaunches; about 8 s compile, 13 s to ~4 min to be back). C# was investigated as the faster loop and rejected (a working note of the originating project (not in this repository)). Nothing here was run; LiveCreate was never started. Marked unread/untested: the real behaviour of the module is unknown beyond its headers.

title: When should a particle effect use the GPU, and does Ashvale use any?
source: manual 25526352, 36868272; Assets/Libs/Particles/; Code/Components/WorldTools.cpp:80-84
content:
Manual 'GPU Support' (graphics-rendering 25526352) and 'GPU Particles' (editor-tools 36868272): a particle component switches to GPU mode when its ONLY render feature is 'Render: GPU Sprites'. In GPU mode the particle data lives in GPU memory, is updated by compute shaders and is drawn from there, for high counts (rain, snow, dust fields); only a subset of the CPU features is available, and it adds features the CPU lacks, such as Screen Space Collisions. GPU particles can be spawned in isolation or by parent CPU particles (the CPU decides the number, the GPU initialises them); nothing is read back, so effects that need positions in game code (hit detection, lights on particles) must stay on the CPU.
Ashvale: uses none. Its effects are legacy-library effects (Assets/Libs/Particles: collisions.xml, fire.xml, smoke_and_fire.xml, weather.xml - campfires, footstep dust, rain) played through ParticleProp.h; no .pfx in the project uses GPU sprites (grep of Assets for GPU sprite names found nothing). Rain is a CPU emitter around the player (WorldTools.cpp UpdateRainParticles). A GPU rain/snow field is the natural first use; write it with pfx_write (the engine's loader DROPS an unknown feature silently, so check with pfx_check and look with pfx_preview in the editor viewport) and judge the cost with perf_tour in the packaged game. particle_search lists the 54 features including the GPU ones.

title: How do I make a light cast a pattern (window shadow, lantern cut-outs, a cookie)?
source: manual 29796937 'Light Entities'; Code/Components/NightLamp.cpp; the MCP server rc_presets
content:
Manual 'Light Entities' (editor-tools 29796937, rows Projector/ProjectorFov/ProjectorNearPlane/Texture): a light entity can project a texture along the light's Y axis. The Texture must use the LightProjector CryTif preset, be 512x512, and contain no alpha; ProjectorFov sets the angle; ProjectorNearPlane excludes surfaces nearer than the value. The older 'DiffuseSoftness', 'LightFov' and 'Texture' rows are marked DEPRECATED (3.7.0) - use the Projector rows. FakeLight disables the projection when you only want a flare; PlanarLight (area light) needs r_DeferredShadingAreaLights 1; CastShadows is limited by the min spec.
Ashvale: no light uses a projector texture. Lights are NightLamp entities (Code/Components/NightLamp.cpp: wall torches, lanterns, room lights; Kind Room brightness 0.13 x radius^2) built from default light components. A window-shaped cookie in the house room lights would be the first use: make a 512x512 grayscale with make_texture-style tooling, compile with RC preset LightProjector (rc_presets lists it), set Texture and ProjectorFov on the light component of a Room lamp, and look at it in the editor viewport at night. The light component's property names must be read from the component (schematyc_info / component_properties): a misspelt property is dropped silently (entity_check finds that).
Untested here: nothing was built; the NightLamp rebuilds its light, so the cookie must be set where NightLamp creates the light component.

title: Shadows are blurry or pop in the distance: which cascade and shadow settings exist?
source: manual 35848989, 56658466, 36869855; the MCP server cvar catalog (e_Gsm*, e_Shadows*, r_ShadowsCache*); Game.cryproject:35
content:
Where the engine puts them: (1) Level Settings (manual 35848989): Sun Shadows Min Spec, Sun Shadows Additional Cascade Min Spec (an extra cascade for a longer shadow distance on higher specs), Sun Shadows Clip Plane Range and Range Shift (the depth range of the shadow frustum: a larger range costs depth precision). (2) The Time of Day / Environment Editor (56658466, section Shadows): the sun's cascaded-shadow bias and slope bias per cascade, because 'cascade 0 is closest, the higher the cascade the lower the resolution' and acne shows on the 3rd and 4th cascade. (3) CVars (cvar catalog, all settable in Release by game code or game.cfg): e_GsmLodsNum (0..5 cascades), e_GsmRange (size of cascade 0 in metres), e_GsmRangeStep (each next range = previous x step), e_ShadowsBlendCascades / e_ShadowsBlendCascadesVal, e_Shadows (0 off, 1 on, 2 sun only, 3 point lights only), r_ShadowsCache (replace sun cascades above a value with a cached static shadow map), r_ShadowsCacheResolutions, e_ShadowsCacheUpdate; debug-only and cheat in Release: e_ShadowsCascadesDebug. (4) Per brush: Dynamic Distance Shadows (Brush Objects 36869855) because cached shadows do not update for moving objects; per light: ShadowBias (Light Entity).
The project: Game.cryproject sys_spec 2 turns shadows on (without it a packaged game had NO shadows: trap-launcher-spec0-no-shadows); the editor viewport and the packaged game differ, so judge in the package. Nothing here was tuned or measured; use render_tour (editor) or perf_tour --set cvar=value (packaged) with a control.

title: Can I add reverb, indoor sound or occlusion with the ACE? Why does nothing happen?
source: CryEngine/CryAudioSystem/implementations/CryAudioImplSDLMixer/Impl.cpp:1049-1052; manual 44964924, 44965000; Code/Components/Soundscape.cpp
content:
The engine side (manual 'Audio & Reverbs' 44964924): reverbs are 'Environments', an Environment audio-system control made in the Audio Controls Editor; AudioAreaAmbience and AudioAreaEntity attached to an Area Shape / Box / Sphere / Solid fade an environment in within a radius of the shape (Wwise & Reverb 44965000, FMOD & Reverb 44964953, ADX2 & Reverb 44967871 show the middleware side).
This project plays through the SDL Mixer implementation, which has NO environments: CryAudioImplSDLMixer/Impl.cpp:1049-1052 ConstructEnvironmentConnection returns nullptr, and a search of Object.cpp and Impl.cpp finds no occlusion or obstruction code. An Environment control connected in the ACE would connect to nothing, an AudioArea would do nothing audible, and the engine's occlusion rays have nothing to feed. The same implementation cannot attenuate or pan on this machine's 7.1 output either (the game does its own distance gain, AshvaleAudio::GainAt).
Options: (1) fake indoor ambience in game code like the soundscape does (Soundscape.cpp layers: lower the bed/rain/wind levels and raise an interior bed when the player is inside a house, using a volume parameter ash_vol_*); (2) a different middleware (FMOD, Wwise, ADX2 implementations exist in the engine; each is a download and licence: name file, source, size and ask first); (3) write the ACE environment anyway only if a middleware is chosen. Recommendation: (1). Not built; the vis-area route to know 'inside' is also absent (Ashvale has no vis areas, visarea_check).

title: How do I get different footstep and impact sounds per surface (grass, stone, wood)?
source: manual 29448756, 44964889; Assets SurfaceTypes.xml; Code/Components/Player.cpp:948; corpus gamesdk-material-effects, tooling-gamesdk-audio-catalog-real-versus-placeholder
content:
The engine's system: SurfaceTypes.xml defines surfaces, a .mtl names its SurfaceType, Libs/MaterialEffects/MaterialEffects.xml is a SpreadsheetML matrix (rows = effect names such as footstep_player, columns = surface types, cell = 'library:effect') and Libs/MaterialEffects/FXLibs/<library>.xml defines each effect, usually an audio trigger plus an ACE switch/state chosen by the surface (manual 'Material Effects' 29448756, 'Audio & Foley/Footsteps' 44964889: footsteps_player:metal_thick -> trigger Play_c_player_fts with a surface switch). Entities pick rows by properties (footstepEffect, foleyEffect); the character animation event 'footstep' triggers them. Debug with mfx_Debug / mfx_reload.
Ashvale: the project has NO MaterialEffects.xml and no FXLibs; its SurfaceTypes.xml (17 types, 8 copied from the GameSDK) only sets physics, and material_check proves each material resolves its surface. Footsteps are one sound each (AshvaleAudio::kStepPlayer, kStepNpc) with no surface switch; the audio files c_player_fts_dirt_walk.ogg and c_player_fts_grass_walk.ogg exist in the ACE assets. The GameSDK's footsteps by surface are real samples (gamesdk_audio: 611 triggers, only 203 real; melee, collision, vehicle and UI sounds are placeholders).
PROPOSAL, cheaper than the full system: a surface lookup by raycast under the foot (ISurfaceType id -> {grass, dirt, stone, wood}) choosing one of N trigger ids in AshvaleAudio, fed by the player's stride event and the NPC heel probe. The full MaterialEffects route needs the animation-event route first (howto-animation-events-and-where-footsteps-come-from) and Excel-format XML authoring. Not built; sound can only be judged by the user.

title: Can I use the engine's hit/death reaction system and body damage in Ashvale?
source: Code/GameSDK/GameDll/HitDeathReactions.cpp, BodyDamage.cpp; Code/Components/Npc.cpp:1189,2059; manual 23306580-23306584
content:
Not directly. The manual's 'Hit and Death Reactions System' (23306580), 'Implementing Hit Reaction' (23306582), 'Reactions XML Format Description' (23306581), 'Body Damage and Destruction' (23306583) and 'Body Damage' (23306584) describe classes that live in the GameSDK game DLL: HitDeathReactions.cpp/.h and BodyDamage.cpp/.h are under Code/GameSDK/GameDll, not in the engine. Ashvale is a component game that does not load that DLL, so those systems (a Lua reaction table parsed from XML, validation by hit direction/speed/health, animation events ForbidReactions and DeathReactionEnd, a per-body-part damage multiplier) are a design to copy, not a feature to call.
What Ashvale has: CNpcComponent::PlayHitReaction(source) (Npc.cpp:1189), called from the health callback (~line 2059): a short flinch picked from the four Hit_ fragments, from the side the blow came from, unless the NPC is mid-action or down. Death: random kd_death clip (only visible with claude_ragdoll 0; ragdoll is the default). No knockdown, no heavy hit, no per-limb damage, no stagger on guard, no block/dodge/finisher (audit A-09, A-10, G-11).
If you build more: keep the manual's rules, they are sound - a hit reaction may not interrupt another hit reaction; a death reaction may interrupt unless explicitly forbidden; every reaction must report its end (fallback after about 3 s); and drive it from data (one table, like villager_anim.py does for clips), then check the Mannequin files with mannequin_check. NOT seen in motion (hit flinches were never looked at in the packaged game).

title: How do I make a hinged door, a swinging sign or a breakable fence with engine components?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Engine components (Code/CryPlugins/CryDefaultEntities/Module/DefaultComponents/Constraints): Point Constraint, Line Constraint, Plane Constraint and Internal Breakable Joint (BreakableJoint.h). Manual 'Physics Constraint Components' (entities-and-tools 56655880): the Internal Breakable Joint connects two parts of a physical entity (or a part to the 'ground', parts found by intersection); on impulses it recomputes forces and breaks joints whose limits (Max Push/Pull/Shift Force, Max Bend/Twist Torque) are exceeded; a broken joint can leave a dynamic constraint instead (a hinge, 1 DOF, if the twist limit broke, else a bend, 2 DOF); separated parts become rigid bodies. Tutorials: 'Advanced Physics Constraints - Gears' 56656092 and '- Splines' 56656174.
In Ashvale: no constraint component is used. The village fences are GameSDK jointed breakables placed as brushes (breakable_fence/wooden_fence4m.cgf, found by their $joint nodes); the sword's StrikeWorld gives the hit part an impulse (pe_action_impulse) and breakable_test.py proves it (control: impulse 0 breaks nothing; any non-zero impulse breaks limit=10 joints). Broken BRUSHES stay broken until level reload. Doors and gates are NOT physics: they are Doorway/FarmGate components that lift or swing by script and use off-mesh links for NPCs.
If you want a physical swinging object: add a rigid body, attach a point/line constraint to the world or a parent entity, tune limits in the Inspector with component_properties (a misspelt property is dropped silently: entity_check), and test in game mode - the editor does not run the physics ticks the game does. Not built or tested.

title: Archers and bandits do not take cover or coordinate: what does the engine provide?
source: CryEngine/CryCommon/CryAISystem/ICoverSystem.h; manual 25535410, 44966037, 23306471, 23306493, 56658084, 25535306; Code/Components/BanditBrain.cpp, UqsSpot.cpp
content:
Not used by Ashvale (audit E-25, G-12). Bandits and archers run a hand-written CBanditBrain (Shoot state, arrows flown by hand, BowRange property) on top of Mannequin and the navmesh; they have no cover, flanking or squad logic.
Engine pieces: the COVER system in CryAISystem (ICoverSystem.h in CryCommon/CryAISystem; Components/Cover/ in CryAISystem), authored with the editor object type CoverSurface (AI Control Objects, manual 25535410; object_types lists it) or generated from geometry (ai.generate_cover_surfaces, a command in editor_commands; the level export writes cover<mission>.bai next to the navmesh, 'Exporting a Level for Playing' 25535306); the entity side is the 'AI Cover User' component (AI Components 44966037: Min Effective Cover Height, In Cover Radius, Distance To Cover, Blacklist Time); the Tactical Point System queries find cover points (tutorials 56658084 'How to use TPS to create cover surfaces'); UQS queries are the newer way and the project already runs one (BestSpotToStand, UqsSpot.cpp). Group coordination: the manual's 'Coordinating Agents with Behavior Trees' (engine-code 23306471, with examples), Signal Reference 'Group Coordination' (23306493), AI Territories & Waves (ai-and-navigation) and the Factions map the project already uses (Scripts/AI/Factions.xml; bandits are a faction).
Constraints: GameSDK behaviour-tree nodes in the sample (GameDll nodes) refuse to load in this project (bt_check); only the engine's registered nodes (bt_nodes: 56 creatable) work. A cover test needs the running game (nav_reach and bt_check only prove the files). Proposal order: CoverSurface objects near the bandit camp -> AI Cover User on the archer -> a BT/UQS step 'move to cover, peek, shoot' -> a game run. Not started.

title: How do I record a time demo or capture video/frames of the game for a trailer or perf check?
content:
Time demos (manual 'Recording Time Demos' 25535455): start the recording in game mode (Ctrl+G in the editor after the level has loaded, or a pure game); console 'record' / Ctrl+PrintScreen, 'stoprecording' / Ctrl+Break, 'demo <name>' / Shift+PrintScreen to play, 'stopdemo'. Related CVars: demo_fixed_timestep, demo_restart_level (0 off, 1 quicksave on first playback, 2 load level start), demo_ai, demo_savestats, demo_max_frames, demo_screenshot_frame. After each playback a log prints Play Time, Average/Min/Max FPS and triangles per frame, also to timedemo.log in the level folder. It records the player's input and camera; vehicle movement is not supported. Fixed timestep makes runs comparable, which is what the project's vsync-pinned perf runs lack (trap-vsync-fullscreen-frame-times-unstable).
Capture (manual 'Capturing Video & Audio' 25535453, 'Render Output' 25535442): the engine writes single frames (and optionally stereo or 5.1 .wav audio) to be assembled in a video editor; the size comes from the viewport or r_CustomResWidth/r_CustomResHeight (+ r_CustomResMaxSize 4096, r_CustomResPreview 1); a Track View sequence can capture its own output (Video:ClipCapture flow node, Video Nodes 29450648).
In this project: NOT used. Performance is measured by perf_tour.py (Statoscope, 17 stops, fullscreen) and pictures by shoot_game/view_shots (the window's own pixels). A time demo would add a repeatable CPU/GPU benchmark; trying it needs a game run (the user's yes) and the demo files should go to a scratch folder. The engine screenshot never contains the 2D UI, capture frames do not either (trap-engine-screenshot-has-no-2d-ui).

title: What debug code ships in the Release game today and what must be removed?
source: Code/GamePlugin.h:111; Code/TcpCommandServer.cpp; Code/Components/AshvaleGame.cpp:49; Code/Components/AshvaleUI.cpp:20; GAPS audit Q-01,Q-07; user decision 2026-10-23
content:
User decision 2026-10-23: the Release game must have NO debug commands. Not done yet. What the shipped Game.dll contains (read from source, audit Q-01/Q-07 'verify'): (1) a TCP command server on 127.0.0.1:37777 (GamePlugin.h:111 kBridgePort, Code/TcpCommandServer.cpp, Winsock bind at :160) that runs console commands without authentication; (2) the claude_* console commands and CVars (about 108 REGISTER_COMMAND/REGISTER_CVAR lines in Code/; 87 non-cheat test commands per the audit) such as ash_goto, claude_npc_action, claude_villager_do; (3) a trace file: 40 source lines mention <engine source checkout> (AshvaleGame.cpp:49, AshvaleUI.cpp:20, ...), which the game opens in append mode on the PLAYER's machine (the file is 167 MB on the dev machine).
Constraints from the engine: cheat/const CVars are dead in Release anyway (trap-cheat-cvar-dead-in-release), but console COMMANDS and plain CVars registered by game code are live; the command line cannot set variables in Release (compile-time whitelist).
Tools that depend on these (do not remove blindly): shoot_game, release_playthrough.py, undercroft_playthrough.py, the ash_* test commands and the TCP server are how the packaged game is driven. Proposal: compile the server, the test commands and the log writer out of the Release configuration (a macro such as ASHVALE_DEV_TOOLS defined for Profile only) and keep a Profile package for the test suite; add a package check that greps the Release Game.dll for the port constant and 'claude_npc.log' (audit tool item 11: version stamp, RELEASE_OK.json after the full gate). Then rerun the gate on the exact Release package. Also open: licences/credits file (Q-29/Q-30).

title: Should I add gamepad support? (the user said no)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Decision (user, 2026-10-23): gamepad is NOT wanted. Do not build gamepad bindings, a controller layout, rumble or on-screen button prompts, and do not count 'no gamepad' as a gap (audit item E-01 / G-22 is withdrawn; the project notes line ~2727 had already recorded 'not wanted'). Keyboard and mouse only.
What exists anyway: the menu movie answers controller events and CAshvaleUI::Navigate sends them (Action 4 = Enter, up/down/left/right) so the keyboard can drive pages; that is a keyboard route using the gamepad event names, not gamepad support. CInputComponent.BindXboxAction/BindPS4Action exist in the engine but are not called. Any future key remapping stays keyboard and mouse (howto-keyboard-rebinding-in-this-project). Reversing this needs the user's explicit word.

title: What has actually been SEEN working in the packaged game, and what is only built or tested in the editor?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
As of 2026-10-23 (copy of STATE.md section 2-3; STATE.md is the maintained version). title: Alerted bandits gave up the hunt a tick after the shout (m_lastSeen never set); bandit tests failed on leftover state, not on standpoints
source: Code/Components/BanditBrain.cpp, examples/ashvale/release_playthrough.py, gameplay_test.py
content: A man alerted by a shout (CBanditBrain::Alert -> SetState(Chase)) has never seen the player, so m_lastSeen is 1000 s; the Chase state gives the hunt up when m_lastSeen > kForgetAfter (9 s), so the log showed 'Guard -> Chase (heard the shout)' and a moment later 'Chase -> Return (lost the player)': the archers never walked far enough to see the player and loosed 0 arrows. Fix: Alert() sets m_lastSeen = min(m_lastSeen, kForgetAfter - kAlertGrace) (6 s of looking). My first diagnosis ('the tests' standpoints are stale after the 2026-10-14 world changes') was WRONG: measured with the new claude_bandit_status command (state, distance, facing dot, line clear/BLOCKED, sees yes/no, shot clear/blocked per bandit) the standpoint 515 750 88.1 is fine. title: How do I make 'the player enters here' start something (AreaBox, AreaTrigger, SensorVolume, flow graph, flow module)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Mechanisms: (1) area objects AreaBox/AreaSphere/AreaShape send ENTITY_EVENT_ENTERAREA/LEAVEAREA to the entities linked as their targets (stored as <Entities><Entity Id="{guid}"/></Entities> inside the area object, AreaBox.cpp:254-290); (2) the C++ entity class AreaTrigger (TriggerEntity.cpp:12-19) turns it into flow outputs Enter/Leave(EntityId), inputs Enable/Disable; (3) component SensorVolume (CrySensorSystem, loaded by Game.cryproject): Box/Sphere + Attribute/Listener tags, signals Entering/Leaving go ONLY to the Schematyc object; Enable/Disable are empty TODOs. C++ box around an entity: IEntityTriggerComponent::SetTriggerBounds (IEntityComponent.h:668, Examples/TriggerComponent.cpp).
TWO SILENT GATES: only entities with ENTITY_FLAG_TRIGGER_AREAS trigger areas (Entity.cpp:427,767); the audio ListenerComponent sets it (ListenerComponent.cpp:40) and Ashvale's player has one (Player.cpp:196), NPCs/arrows do not. And the engine AreaTrigger has NO player/faction filter; bOnlyPlayers etc. belong to the sample's Lua AreaTrigger.lua, which this project does not mount. ProximityTrigger is Lua only.
Steps: place the reacting entity (place_object); create_object AreaBox + object_properties Width/Length/Height; place_object kind entity AreaTrigger; LINK area -> trigger: NO tool (propose link_area_target: bridge.object.set with @Entities=<Entities>..., object_props.set_properties(children=)); reaction graph: a FlowgraphEntity object with a <FlowGraph><Nodes><Node Id Class="entity:AreaTrigger" EntityGUID=..>..<Edges><Edge nodeIn nodeOut portIn portOut enabled/> child (sample woodland ab01_gameplay.lyr; loader EntityLoadManager.cpp:604) - propose flow_graph_add; flow_check the same nodes as a standalone file. Flow modules: Libs/FlowgraphModules/*.xml or <level>/FlowgraphModules/*.xml, <Graph isModule="1" moduleName=..><ModuleInputsOutputs><Port Name Type Input/>; nodes Module:Start_/End_/Call_<name> appear after the scan (Module.cpp:55-100, ModuleManager.cpp:454-470,560-567).
Prove: object_check (Entities child kept), entity_check, flow_check 0 findings; control: wrong port name -> F002/F005. Game (user's yes): player placed inside the box -> one Debug:Log line in the packaged game's log; controls: spot outside, Disable first, NPC without the flag -> no line.
Traps: triggers in a hidden layer are dead; a trigger flush on terrain needs Height > 0.
verified_note: Nothing run. The claim that the player carries the flag is inferred.

title: How do I make prefabs, groups and layers from the tools (prefab.new_prefab, layer.new, toggle_auto_load)?

Moving objects: object.set_object_layer(name, layer), object.switch_layer. Saved layer attributes: Name GUID Exportable ExportLayerPak DefaultLoaded HavePhysics IsDefaultColor Color Specs (ObjectLayer.cpp:352-398) and Hidden Frozen Expanded Type (:323-341). Ashvale has ONE layer, Main.
Groups: group.create_from_selection / ungroup / open / close / attach_to / detach (selection based).
Prefabs are ASSETS in 5.7: a .prefab XML + .cryasset (PrefabManager.cpp:25-60; item names with dots become sub-folders). Python: prefab.new_item(itemName); prefab.new_prefab(itemName, prefabName, x, y, z) creates the item if missing, places an instance and returns the unique name; has_item, get_items, add_to_prefab, extract_all, clone_all, open/close, update_all_prefabs, delete_item. prefab.create_from_selection runs a dialog (modal: list_dialogs / click_dialog_button). Propose layer_tool(action,name,flags) -> select, command, save_level, read the .lyr attributes back; prefab_tool(action,item,objects,at) -> check prefab.get_items(), the .prefab file exists with N child objects, an instance has N children.
Prove: .lyr attributes equal the request; control: toggle twice returns to the start; delete_item removes both files. Snapshot first; a graceful editor close SAVES the level, remove scratch layers/objects before it.

title: How do I show and hide a whole layer at run time (Engine:LayerSwitch, EnableLayer, es_togglelayer, UseLayersActivation)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Two layer systems: object layers (needs level EnvState UseLayersActivation, 3dEngineLoad.cpp:1461, AND CVar e_ObjectLayersActivation, cvars.cpp:778, VF_CHEAT, 0 in editor / 1 in game) and ENTITY layers. IEntitySystem::EnableLayer(name, bool enable, bool serialize) / FindLayer is what the flow node Engine:LayerSwitch calls (inputs Layer Hide Unhide EnableSerialization DisableSerialization; outputs Hidden Unhidden), plus gEnv->pAISystem->LayerEnabled on enable (FlowEngineNodes.cpp:276-385). Game code can call EnableLayer directly (no graph). Console command es_togglelayer <LayerName> (VF_DEV_ONLY, case-sensitive, EntityCVars.cpp:238,392-410) toggles the same way. Related nodes: Entity:LayerSwitchListener, Engine:PrecacheArea (Position Timeout Activate), Engine:PortalSwitch, Engine:OcclusionAreaSwitch, Environment:OceanSwitch.
Steps: make layers (see recipe-prefabs-groups-layers-editor-python), DefaultLoaded=0 for streamed ones; set UseLayersActivation="1" in leveldata/environment.xml (level_check reads EnvState; snapshot first) and export_level; unhide from game code or an AreaTrigger.Enter -> Engine:LayerSwitch graph.
Prove (user's yes): in a Profile/dev build run_console_command('es_togglelayer Name') and es_LayerDebugInfo 1; control: toggling a name that does not exist changes nothing; toggle back. Editor counts mean nothing (the editor shows all).
Traps: AreaTriggers inside a hidden layer never fire; vegetation and physics proxies are not streamed; children of a hidden layer are hidden in the game but not in editor game mode; es_togglelayer is absent in Release.

Object attributes: VisArea Height DisplayFilled AffectedBySun IgnoreSkyColor IgnoreGI ViewDistRatio SkyOnly OceanIsVisible IgnoreOutdoorAO; Portal adds UseDeepness DoubleSide LightBlending LightBlendValue; OccluderArea/OccluderPlane CullDistRatio UseInIndoors DoubleSide. Lights/fog/probe have IgnoreVisAreas and OnlyAffectThisArea. CVars e_Portals (VF_CHEAT, 2-4 debug), e_PortalsBlend, e_PortalsMaxRecursion 8, e_CoverageBuffer, e_OcclusionVolumes. title: How do I create game tokens (quest flags, counters) and react to them in flow graphs and the DRS?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Libraries load at level load from <level>/GameTokens/*.xml (LevelSystem.cpp:1301-1316). Format: root tag EXACTLY GameTokensLibrary with attribute Name; every child (tag name not checked) has Name, Type (Bool Int Float String Vec3; Any/Void refused), Value, LocalOnly; the token is created as <Lib>.<Name>; an existing token is not overwritten (GameTokenSystem.cpp:591-650). Example: <GameTokensLibrary Name="Quest"><Token Name="TomMet" Type="Bool" Value="0" LocalOnly="0"/></GameTokensLibrary> -> Quest.TomMet. The editor's leveldata/gametokens.xml (Ashvale: an empty LevelLibrary) is a different file. The manual calls the Database View tab unsupported.
Flow nodes: Mission:GameToken (gametoken_Token, compare_Value, FireOnStart, FireOnlyOnResultChange -> Out, Equal True/False, Equals), GameTokenCheck, GameTokenSet, GameTokenGet, GameTokenModify, GameTokenCheckMulti, GameTokensLevelToLevelStore/Restore (carry between ashvale and ashvale_undercroft). DRS: action SetGameToken, condition GameToken {Token, MinVal, MaxVal} (sample sg_audio_demo_generator_rpm_decreased.response). Code: IGameTokenSystem::SetOrCreateToken / FindToken / RegisterListener. Debug: gt_Show 1|2|3, gt_showFilter.
Steps: Write Assets/levels/ashvale/GameTokens/quest.xml; NO checker exists: propose gametoken_check(level) (loader rules + a plugin verb bridge.gametoken.dump listing live tokens; the file must be in level.pak after export_level); then a Mission:GameTokenSet -> GameToken compare -> Debug:Log graph (flow_check) or a DRS response with a GameToken condition (drs_check).
Prove (user's yes): gt_Show 3 logs the change once; control: a token name not in the library changes nothing. title: How do I author and place a GPU or CPU particle effect (pfx_write, GPU Particles: Sprites, Particle Emitter component)?

Propose probe_bake(name): command + poll + before/after grey. AffectsOnlyThisArea outdoors lights nothing.

title: How do I grade the picture per area, drive post effects from code and add a lens flare to a light?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Post effects from code: I3DEngine::SetPostEffectParam(name, value) (measured via ash_post, ashvale-post-effects); the manager KEEPS the last value (write neutral back). Grading without a chart: time-of-day variables (env_variables, env_check, env_diff). Chart: 256x16 LUT; r_ColorGrading, r_ColorGradingCharts, r_ColorGradingChartImage <path> (loads immediately), flow Image:ColorGradient (Trigger, tex_TexturePath, TransitionTime). The manual's RGBChart.bmp is not available offline: derive a chart from the identity EngineAssets/Textures/default_cch.tif by pushing it through a colour function (inferred).
Flares: library file Libs/Flares/<Library>.xml containing <FlareItem Name="Item" Type="Root" ..><Params><Common Size Brightness ..> children; name 'Library.Item' is split at the first dot, the file read from <game>/Libs/Flares/<Library>.xml and the child matched by Name (OpticsManager.cpp:67-117, IFlares.h:40); the repo-root scratch claude_flarelib.xml shows a DataBaseLibrary form. A light uses Optics{Enable, LensFlare, AttachtToSun, FlareFOV} (ILightComponent.h:172-175); Projector Light has Flare{Angle, Texture}. CVars r_Flares, r_FlaresChromaShift, r_FlaresEnableColorGrading.
Steps: pick grading variables in the preset (existing pipeline) or make the chart; set_cvar('r_ColorGradingChartImage', path) in the editor; flares: propose flare_write(library, item, params) (writes the xml and asks the engine IOpticsManager::Load through a plugin verb: true for 'ashvale.item', false for 'ashvale.nothing').
Prove: get_cvar read-back + grey-level statistics of a fixed view vs control (the parameter read-back is the measurement, pictures are poor witnesses); the Load true/false pair for flares. Traps: r_PostProcessEffects is not settable in Release; a flare library outside the pak is not found in the package.
verified_note: Nothing run.

title: How do I put blood splats or footprints on the ground when something is hit (Decal object, Decal component, CreateDecal)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Three routes. (1) Fixed: level object Decal (Material, ProjectionType 0..3, Deferred, SortPriority 16, ProjectionDepth 1). (2) Component 'Decal' (AutoSpawn, Material, FollowEntity, ProjectionType, Depth, SortPriority, function Spawn; DecalComponent.h:65-70). (3) Runtime: I3DEngine::CreateDecal(const CryEngineDecalInfo&) (I3DEngine.h:1544) with vPos, vNormal, fSize, fLifeTime, fAngle, vHitDirection, bDeferred, sortPrio, szMaterialName, ownerInfo (CryEngineDecalInfo.h:18-43). MaterialEffects FX libraries can also spawn them: <RandEffect><Decal minscale maxscale lifetime><Material>Materials/decals/footsteps/footstep_dirt</Material></Decal></RandEffect> (sample FXLibs/footstep_player.xml). Particle feature 'Render: Decals' exists.
The project already imported the 10 blood materials (Assets/materials/decals/blood/blood_splat1..5, splatx1..3, ...). Measured (decal_preview): a decal draws only within ProjectionDepth of a surface; 2 m above the ground nothing draws; over a brush slab it did not draw.
Steps: decal_materials('blood'); decal_preview('materials/decals/blood/blood_splat1', x, y, lift 0.1, size 1) for the editor look; the runtime hook is game code at Npc.cpp PlayHitReaction (line 1189): raycast down from the victim, random blood_splat1..5, fLifeTime 30-60, bDeferred true (ask first); after adding materials rebuild the shader cache (shader tour).
Prove: decal_preview changed pixels above the two-control noise and darker mean; control: the decal 2 m above ground draws nothing. Game (user's yes): shoot_game pictures after a scripted hit; control: same hit with the call removed. Traps: Materials/Decals/Default is not shipped; the decal pool fills with long lifetimes.
verified_note: decal_preview behaviour measured in the editor; the runtime call was never made.

title: How do I get surface-dependent footstep and impact effects with the engine's MaterialEffects (matrix, FXLibs, ExecuteEffect)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Files: Libs/MaterialEffects/MaterialEffects.xml - an Excel SpreadsheetML workbook, rows = effect/event names (footstep_player ...), columns = surface types, cell = 'library:effect' (CMaterialEffects::LoadSpreadSheet, MaterialEffects.cpp:276-330 via IXmlTableReader); Libs/MaterialEffects/FXLibs/<lib>.xml loaded by file name (:95-135); an effect = <Effect name="dirt"><Audio trigger=..><Particle><Name minscale maxscale maxscaledist>..</Name></Particle><RandEffect><Decal ..></RandEffect></Effect>. API: IMaterialEffects::GetEffectIdByName(lib, effect), GetEffectId(surfaceIdx1, surfaceIdx2), ExecuteEffect(id, SMFXRunTimeEffectParams{pos, dir, srcSurfaceId, trgSurfaceId, audio rtpcs}) (IMaterialEffects.h:615-621). Debug mfx_Debug 1|2|3, mfx_Reload, mfx_ReloadFGEffects (most are VF_CHEAT: Profile build). Ashvale has only Assets/libs/MaterialEffects/SurfaceTypes.xml (17 surface types).
Steps: choose surfaces (grass dirt stone wood water); write FXLibs/ashvale_steps.xml with effects named like the surfaces; write a minimal workbook (copy the sample's header and styles from gamedata.pak Libs/MaterialEffects/MaterialEffects.xml, cut the data) - NO tool: propose materialfx_write(rows, cols, cells) + materialfx_check (plugin verb calling GetEffectIdByName for every cell, reporting unresolved ones; 'Identity mismatch' warnings, :462-468, mean a bad header); game code: raycast under the foot -> surface index -> ExecuteEffect (the cheaper table lookup in howto-material-effects-surface-driven-footsteps comes first).
Prove: N of N cells resolve; control: a cell naming a missing effect is reported. Sound quality is the user's judgement (gamesdk_audio: 203 of 611 triggers real). Traps: an unknown surface type becomes mat_default silently (material_check M002); footsteps need the animation-event route first.

title: How do I add a rope, a cloth banner, a swinging sign or a hinge with the engine components?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
ROPE: editor object Rope (entity class RopeEntity, RopeObject.cpp:132): spline-like points, both ends can be LINKED to objects (anchors); export writes <Rope ..params><Points/><Audio StartTrigger StopTrigger ..> (RopeObject.cpp:612-640). Defaults: flags 4099 radius 0.02 anchor_radius 0.1 num_seg 8 num_sides 4 mass 1 friction 2. Flow Physics:Params:Rope.
CLOTH: component 'Cloth': FilePath (cgf), Material, Mass, Density, Thickness 0.05, MassDecay, Friction, AirResist, Wind, WindVariance 0.2, Pressure, ImpulseScale, collisions CollTerr/CollStat/CollDyn/CollPlayer, Simulation{MaxTimeStep SleepSpeed Damping 0.3 Hardness 20 MaxIters 20 Accuracy MaxStretch BendStiff ShearStiff} (ClothComponent.h:70-104). Flow Physics:Params:Cloth.
CONSTRAINTS: components Point/Line/Plane Constraint and Internal Breakable Joint (Constraints/); flow Physics:Constraint (Create Break EntityA PartIdA EntityB PartIdB Type Point LocalFrames Breakable -> Id Broken). Rigidbody: Type, Buoyancy{Damping Density 1000 Resistance 1000}, Simulation, SendCollisionSignal. Editor python physics.simulate_selection / step / reset_state_selection (the editor does not tick game physics).
Steps: create_object('Rope', name, a) + spline_points([a,b]) + object_properties set {'Rope/num_seg','Rope/radius','Rope/mass'}; anchors by link (no tool: propose rope_anchor(rope, end, entity)); banner/sign: place_object an EntityWithComponent entity, add components (no tool: propose add_component), component_properties for values, build_mesh for the banner mesh; entity_check for typos (a misspelt property is dropped silently).
Prove (user's yes): sample_entity_physics after an impulse - the position moves and settles; control: the same entity without mass/constraint stays. The existing breakable_test.py control (impulse 0 breaks nothing) is the model. Traps: broken brushes stay broken until reload; ropes need endpoint height above their length; cloth vertex pinning comes from the mesh (unchecked).

title: How do I write a Dynamic Response System conversation with conditions, timers and variables (the Dialog Editor is deprecated)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
The Dialog Editor is no longer supported in Sandbox since 5.6 (manual 44959678); the DRS replaces it. Files: Libs/DynamicResponseSystem/Responses/*.response (JSON) and DialogLines/*.dialog. Shape: {"BaseSegment":{"name", "SegmentConditions":{"Conditions":[{"Condition":{"<Class>":{..}},"Negated":false}],"Negated":false}, "Actions":[{"Action":{"<Class>":{..}},"Delay":0.0}], "ChildSegments":[..]}}.
Condition classes (names carry TRAILING SPACES where shown): 'Variable equal to ', 'Variable greater than ', 'Variable smaller than ', 'Variable in range ' (collection, variable, compareValue{value,Type}, compareValue2), variable-against-variables, Random, ExecutionLimit, InheritConditions, TimeSince (collection, variable, compareValue), TimeSinceResponse, GameToken (Token, MinVal, MaxVal), Placeholder. Action classes: SpeakLine {lineToSpeak, speakerOverride}, ChangeVariable {collection, variable, Operation, Value, Cooldown}, ResetTimerVariable, SendSignal, CancelSignal, ExecuteResponse, SetActor, SetGameToken, CopyVariable, Wait, DelayAction. Collections: Context, Local, Global, LEVEL_<name>. Custom ones: REGISTER_DRS_CUSTOM_CONDITION/ACTION (manual 44961609); entity component 'DRS'.
Conversation pattern: signal -> response A (SpeakLine, then SendSignal to the partner with a Delay) -> response B; spacing with TimeSince + ResetTimerVariable; once-only with ExecutionLimit; token gate with GameToken.
Steps (existing tools cover them): write the .response/.dialog (snapshot first), add voice lines (preview_voice, render_voices), drs_check (D001 empty response and NO log on bad JSON, D002 unknown class dropped silently, D003 missing line, D004 unanswered signal), story_check.py. Prove: drs_check shows the tree as the ENGINE serialised it with your conditions; control: drop the trailing space of 'Variable equal to' -> D002. Run in the packaged game for the spoken line.
verified_note: drs_check itself is measured in the editor; the new conditions were not written.

title: Which Track View nodes and tracks can a cutscene use, and how do I author one when the Python API cannot add keys?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Node types (IMovieSystem.h:39-62): Entity, Director, Camera, CVar, ScriptVar, Material, Event, Group, Layer, Comment, RadialBlur, ColorCorrection, DepthOfField, ScreenFader, Light, HDRSetup, ShadowSetup, GeomCache, Environment, ScreenDropsSetup, Audio. Track params (:81-190): Position/Rotation/Scale (+X/Y/Z), FOV, Event, Visibility, Camera, Animation, AudioSwitch/Trigger/Parameter, Sequence, Console, Float, LookAt, TrackEvent, Shake*, DepthOfField, FocusDistance/Range, BlurAmount, Capture, TimeWarp, FixedTimeStep, NearZ, Goto, ColorR/G/B, ScreenFader, Light* (Diffuse, Radius, ...), Material* (Diffuse Specular Emissive Opacity Smoothness), TimeRanges, Mannequin, Physicalize, Sun/Moon Longitude/Latitude, DynamicResponseSignal. Python trackview.* has 87 functions but no key adding.
Authoring: write the sequence XML by hand (the project's make_intro_sequence.py is the model; ticks 6000/s; rotation in degrees; Bezier handles stored negated), validate with sequence_check (loads through IMovieSystem::LoadSequence and reports what the engine kept), play from C++ as Components/Cinematics.cpp does or with the flow node Animations:PlaySequence (seq_Sequence_File, Trigger, Pause, Stop, StartTime, PlaySpeed -> Started Done Finished Aborted SequenceTime). Frame capture: Video:ClipCapture. Extra tracks to add: Director camera cuts, Event/TrackEvent keys (fire graph events), ScreenFader black in/out, Light Diffuse, Audio trigger.
Prove: sequence_check node/track/key counts; control: an unknown track param is reported dropped; motion needs Track View playback in the editor or a game run. Traps: Entity nodes cache the EntityId they first resolved (reload per play); a same-named sequence is replaced on load.

title: How do I give archers and bandits real cover (CoverSurface, AI Cover User, ai.generate_cover_surfaces)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Authoring: editor object CoverSurface (SurfaceID, Sampler, LimitDepth 0.75, LimitHeight 2.75, LimitLeft/Right 12, SampleWidth/Height 0.25, MaxStartHeight 0.5, SimplifyThreshold) or the command ai.generate_cover_surfaces (EditorCommands_AI.cpp:56,167); the level export writes cover<mission>.bai next to the navmesh. title: What exactly would I copy to get hit reactions and per-limb damage (GameSDK data files and rules)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
The engine does not provide them: GameDll classes HitDeathReactions, BodyDamage, ScriptBind_HitDeathReactions. DATA MODEL in the sample's gamedata.pak: Libs/BodyDamage/BodyParts_HumanMaleShared.xml (<Part name flags="headshot|foot|knee|pelvis"><Bone name="Bip01 Head"/>), BodyDamage_Default.xml (<Multiplier part="head" value="1.4"><RifleBullet value="1.5"/>), Libs/HitDeathReactionsData/HitDeathReactions_Default.xml / _MP.xml (<DeathReactionParam reactionFunc="MeleeDeath_Reaction"><AllowedHitTypes><HitType value="melee"/>; part groups as DTD entities). Ashvale has CNpcComponent::PlayHitReaction (Npc.cpp:1189) with four Hit_ fragments by side.
Copy plan: (1) a table part -> {bones, multiplier} for the villager rig (anim_check / character_check list bone names), loaded like villager_anim.py loads clips; (2) resolve the hit part from the physics hit's partId to a joint name via the default skeleton (no tool; inferred API); (3) choose a Mannequin fragment by direction and strength (mannequin_check); (4) the manual's rules (23306583): a hit reaction may not interrupt another, a death reaction may interrupt, every reaction reports its end (fallback ~3 s).

title: How do I keep a forest and the texture set inside budget (view distance, LOD ratio, streaming pool, mip bias)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:

title: How do I profile a level load or a frame in the packaged game (bootprofiler, ProfVis, Brofiler, Profile build)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Tools in the installed engine Tools/: Brofiler/Brofiler.exe, ProfVis/ProfVis.exe, Statoscope/Statoscope.exe, memReplay. Boot profiler: records boot and level load automatically in builds with ENABLE_PROFILING_CODE (bp_boot.xml, bp_level.xml in TestResults); sys_bp_frames <n> writes bp_frames.xml; open with ProfVis (manual 23306664). CVars sys_bp_enabled, sys_bp_level_load, sys_bp_level_load_include_first_frame, sys_bp_frames_threshold, sys_bp_time_threshold, sys_bp_format (BootProfiler.cpp:907-917) are ABSENT in a Release build (catalog release_condition) - they need the Profile binaries (bin/win_x64; Profile ~25% slower, fact-cvar-gates-release-vs-profile-measured). sys_ProfileLevelLoading 1|2 logs loading (manual 36868666); profile_disk shows streaming IO (DiskProfiler.cpp:47). Brofiler (manual 24283922): start the game from disk (not from Visual Studio), Record; profile_deep 1 = all labels, profile_allthreads 1 = all threads; the game must mark frame start.
Steps: frame cost in the editor = frame_profile (exists); packaged frame cost = perf_tour (Statoscope); load time: package with the Profile config (user's yes), run 'map ashvale' with sys_bp_level_load 1, read bp_level.xml - propose loadtime_report(path): parse it the way frame_profile parses bp_frames and return total ms and the top self-time blocks.
Prove: total ms stable over two runs; control: an empty level (new_level) loads much faster. Traps: the editor's display-idle crash window; Release has none of these variables.
