title: Can I use the engine's own SaveGame for Ashvale (CCryAction::SaveGame returns false)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content: No. CCryAction::SaveGame (CryAction.cpp:3241) returns false at 'if (!pClientActor)' (:3253-3254) because a player made of components is not an IActor, and returns false for a dead actor (:3257). The engine's per-component serializer works on its own (GameSerialize(TSerialize) with IXmlSerializer), which Ashvale's hand-rolled save (F5/F9, ash_savegame/ash_loadgame) uses; see savegame-component-player for the three things it had to get right (default values omitted, death is derived state, health after transform). Decision stands; nothing to build. Cheap re-check: read the lines above, or run 'save <name>' in an editor game session (user's yes) and see that the log is silent. Game tokens, if used, are carried by the engine path that is not used here.
verified_note: Source lines read; the silent false was measured earlier (savegame-component-player).

title: How do I show a UI element on a prop in the world (UIElement dynamic texture, .ui material, UI actions)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Any UIElement can be a texture: a material whose Diffuse texture is <ElementName>.ui (or <Name>@<InstanceID>.ui) with TexType 'Dynamic 2D-Map' (manual 25535439); the renderer recognises the extension (Texture.cpp:3021,3044; eTT_Dyn2D in ShaderTemplate.cpp:791). A Projector Light can project a .ui/.swf/.gfx/.usm too (ProjectorLightComponent.cpp:107-111). UIElements are Libs/UI/UIElements/*.xml binding a .gfx movie (Ashvale has only MainMenu.xml with Menus_Startmenu.gfx plus StatusWindow.gfx, LangBar.gfx); UIActions are flow graphs Libs/UI/UIActions/*.xml with UI:Action:Start/End, UI:Display:Display, UI:Functions:<Element>:<fn>, UI:Events:<Element>:<event> (gamesdk-ui). Ashvale's HUD is immediate-draw because authoring a movie needs Flash tooling this machine lacks.
Steps: reuse a GameSDK movie (import_gamesdk_asset.py; USMPlayer, HUD2D); write the UIElement XML (outline_asset_xml shows the format); ui_check (an undeclared function name is a SILENT dynamic call); a material with the .ui texture (write_material - whether it can set the Dyn2D TexType is unchecked); a plane from build_mesh; material_check.
Prove: ui_check shows the element available; a picture of the plane vs a plane whose element name is wrong (control). Interaction needs a game run. Traps: the menu movie draws ONE image reliably (trap-flashui-menu-movie-one-image); the engine screenshot has no 2D UI.

title: Why does an ACE Environment (reverb) or occlusion do nothing here, and what are the options (SDL Mixer, FMOD, fake in code)?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
CImpl::ConstructEnvironmentConnection returns nullptr in the SDL Mixer implementation (Impl.cpp:1049-1052) and in PortAudio (:598): an Environment control connected in the ACE connects to nothing, so reverb areas and engine occlusion rays have no effect. Engine side exists: components Area, Environment, Occlusion, Trigger, Parameter, SwitchState, Preload, Listener (DefaultComponents/Audio) and legacy AudioAreaAmbience/Entity/Random, AudioTriggerSpot (an area entity feeds an RTPC area_fade_distance; AreaBox + AudioAreaAmbience fades beds, craft-audio-ambience). The installed engine ships CryAudioImplFmod.dll + fmod.dll, CryAudioImplWwise.dll and CryAudioImplAdx2.dll, but authoring needs the middleware's own tool (a download and licence: name file, source and size, ask first).
Options: (1) fake indoor ambience in game code - I3DEngine::GetVisAreaFromPos or a box test lowers the soundscape beds and raises an interior bed (Soundscape.cpp volume parameters) - recommended, no middleware; (2) keep SDL and use only AreaBox + AudioAreaAmbience fades; (3) switch implementation (ask).
Check: audio_triggers cross-checks trigger names; audio_report measures the interior bed loudness; judging the sound is the user's. This machine's 7.1 output cannot attenuate or pan in SDL, the game does its own distance gain.
verified_note: Source lines read; nothing run.

title: How do I cut a hole in the terrain (cave mouth, cellar) or render a minimap texture?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Holes are bits in the heightmap's layer-id bitmap: CHeightmap::SetHoleAt / MakeHole(x1,y1,w,h,bMake) / IsHoleAt (Heightmap.cpp:2764-2789) then UpdateEngineHole (:2940). It needs the plugin source (Code/Sandbox/Plugins/ClaudeBridgePlugin) and a rebuild: ask.

title: Is LiveCreate worth trying to avoid closing the editor for a Game.dll build?
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content: Probably not. CryLiveCreate manages remote hosts and platforms (ILiveCreateManager.h: IHostInfo, CreateHost(platform, ip)); CSystem::InitLiveCreate (SystemInit.cpp:1241) loads it unless sys_livecreate is 0; no Sandbox LiveCreate plugin is installed; the manual has no page. It sends editor changes to a running game on another device; it does not swap a compiled module. Close the item with two listings instead of a build: cvar_info('sys_livecreate') and the installed EditorPlugins folder (look for a LiveCreate dll). Control: a plugin known to exist in the same folder (ClaudeBridge) is listed. The Game.dll lock while Sandbox runs is why the loop closes the editor (claude_game_build.bat); C# was rejected (csharp-vs-cpp-verdict).

title: TRAP: a Mannequin fragment queued while the NPC is not drawn never shows: the villager 'works' or 'prays' standing in the bind pose
source: Npc.cpp UpdateAnimation (m_bRequeueHeld, m_heldFragmentId); 2026-10-25 shoot 1 vs shoot 2
content: SYMPTOM: claude_villager_do Edmund pray (or hammer, chop) logged 'clip Pray_Loop ... looping' and the brain's steps ran to the end, but the picture taken when the player arrived showed him standing upright with the arms slightly away from the body (the bind pose, not even the idle). CAUSE: CryAnimation advances only a character that is drawn (CS_FLAG_RENDER_NODE_VISIBLE). A fragment queued while the player is elsewhere is never played, and a HELD action (m_actionRemaining > 0) makes UpdateAnimation return early, so nothing queues it again when the body comes into view. The locomotion fragments were already re-queued after a draw gap; held actions were not. The 2026-10-23 sit sequence only worked because the player was standing next to the villager when it was commanded. FIX (Npc.cpp): remember the held fragment (m_heldFragmentId, set by PlayClip, PlayAction, PlayGesture and PlayNamedFragment), set m_bRequeueHeld while the body is not drawn and an action is still running, and queue the held fragment once more the first frame it is drawn again (trace 'drawn again -- the held fragment N is queued once more'). SEEN: the same commands given with the player far away showed Tom chopping, Will hoeing and Edmund kneeling after the fix. TEST RULE: a scripted look must give the command while the player is out of sight at least once, or it proves nothing about real play (the player is almost never next to the NPC when its errand begins).

title: PLAYBOOK: work, prayer, drink and bed stations derived from the level's own objects (stations.py, stations.xml)
source: stations.py, Code/Components/NpcLifeImpl.h, VillagerLifeImpl.h, NpcWork.h; shoots 2026-10-25
content: The 35 Kimodo clips need a PLACE. stations.py reads Assets/levels/ashvale/layers/main.lyr and writes Assets/libs/ashvale/stations.xml (31 stations): hammer = Smithy_Anvil, chop = Clearing_Logs* and Barn_Logs*, sweep = outside each <House>_Door (the ring points farther from Home_<House> than the door), hoe = six points outside the Field_Fence ring, pray = Chapel_Altar, drink = Tavern_Counter, sleep = every *_Bed brush and Camp_Bedroll*. Each station lists stand points; the game asks the navmesh (FindNavPoint) which is usable and reserves the station for the villager (AshvaleStations::Reserve/Release, dead owners are free again). The work rows (hammer/chop/sweep/hoe: fragment, session seconds, prop) are in NpcWork.h; the brain (VillagerLifeImpl.h) scores a station errand 0.57 by day (weights by home: Garrick -> hammer, Tom -> chop, Edmund/Hilda -> sweep, Will/Martha -> hoe), prayer and an evening drink 0.66, a meal 0.62 in three windows (7-8.5, 12-13.5, 17-18.4), a night in bed inside GoHome. Errands are 90-220 s apart. A conversation gives an errand up (OnConversation). TEST: claude_villager_do <npc> hammer|chop|sweep|hoe|pray|drink|meal|nap; claude_npc_life_status; claude_npc_react <npc> light|heavy|parry|knock|block|dodge|cower. SLEEP GEOMETRY comes from the clip manifest, not from guessing: kd_sleep_down travels (x right +0.263, y forward -0.913), kd_sleep_up (+0.633, +0.196). title: PLAYBOOK: the NPC life switches (claude_npc_life and one per behaviour) and the reactions they play
source: Code/Components/NpcLifeImpl.h, BanditLifeImpl.h, Npc.cpp; shoots 2026-10-25
content: Switches (all default 1 except the last three): claude_npc_life (master), claude_npc_work_on, claude_npc_pray, claude_npc_meal, claude_npc_sleep, claude_npc_greet, claude_npc_cower, claude_npc_idle_variants, claude_npc_talk_extras, claude_npc_carry, claude_npc_reactions; claude_npc_block, claude_npc_dodge, claude_npc_knockdown are percentages and default 0 (they change how a fight goes and no gate test has fought with them on). Every behaviour writes to claude_npc.log: 'clip <Fragment> (<why>)', 'will greet|bow to the player', 'takes up the carry walk (1.04 m/s)', 'lies down on <bed>', 'dodged the blow', 'blocked the blow', 'raises his guard', 'leaps left'. HOW: PlayClip(SActionClip row, hold, gesture, why) plays any table row; a bow for the chapel and the reeve, a wave for the rest, queued by BeginWatching (the player seen) and BeginConversation and played when the body stands idle; talk extras (point, plead, laugh, nod, shake the head) replace 55 percent of the talk gestures; idle variants are 45 percent of the fidgets and hold 1-2.5 loops; the Flee clip replaces the run during a panic (played at body speed over clip speed) and Cower holds 8-14 s at home; the Carry_Walk clip replaces the walk while a log is in the arms and the walk speed is capped at the clip's 1.04 m/s (a faster body slid); a bandit's CBanditBrain::Stagger plays ParryRecoil (>= 1.0 s), a heavy hit (>= 0.8 s) or a light flinch, and optionally a knockdown with GetUp chained. Block and dodge read CPlayerComponent::GetSwingTime() (the blow lands 0.2 s into a stroke) and roll once per stroke; a dodged blow no longer staggers (Player.cpp: if taken > 0). Also claude_npc_cower_crouch (1): the crouch at home after the run. claude_npc_react <npc> light|heavy|parry|knock|block|dodge|cower|idle plays one now (bandits through their brain). SEEN in the packaged game: extra talk gestures in a conversation with Edmund, Tom running with the flee clip (arms spread), Will carrying a log with the carry walk, an idle variant (look around) from the fidget roll, the cower pose (hands over the head), and on Garrick the heavy-hit, parry-recoil, knockdown-then-get-up, block and dodge poses. LOGGED, NOT SEEN: the bow (log only), the same reactions on a real bandit hit by the player (the player died twice in the camp), the Player.cpp call site.
verified_note: Pictures: talk extras, flee run, carry walk, idle variant, cower, reactions on a villager. Log only: bow, reactions on real bandits and the player's blow path (2026-10-25).

title: TRAP: scripting a shoot: z above the ground drops the player, ash_use leaves its dialogue box up, the bandit camp kills in 6 s
source: shoot jobs 20261025 (shoot 5 and 6)
content: 1) A shot line 'label x y yaw z' with a z that is higher than the ground at (x, y) drops the player: 'bd_c 516 733 0 88.1' (88.1 is the camp plateau) fell to the road, 'You land hard', health 1. Leave z out (terrain + 0.1) except inside buildings, and look the terrain up first (terrain_height). (515, 735) itself is inside a rock: the camera sees stone. 2) '!ash_use' starts a conversation that stays open for the rest of the script: its box covers the lower half of every later picture, and the NPC is held standing. End it with ash_choose 2 or do not use it before pictures of anything else. 3) The bandit camp kills a player who stands 7-12 m from the gate in about 6-10 s (three clubs and two archers); each '!' costs 3 s. Use '~' (no wait) between pictures there, or look from outside their sight (18 m, a 120 degree cone). 4) ash_goto puts the player 'on the side he is already on', which can be a wall or the back of the NPC: place the camera with a shot line at a point you worked out from the station file. 5) A command given while the player is far away is the real case (see trap-fragment-queued-while-not-drawn-never-shows).

title: GameLauncher dies at exit with a null call (WER: module unknown, offset 0): a component used while the entity's components are destroyed
source: Code/GamePlugin.cpp, Code/Components/Npc.cpp, crash_symbolize.py
content: Symptom: Windows Error Reporting lists GameLauncher.exe, exception 0xc0000005, 'Faulting module name: unknown, fault offset 0x0' (BEX64 type 5): the instruction pointer was 0, i.e. a call through a null function pointer, with no other information. Tool: a game started with -claude_test installs a crash catcher (GamePlugin.cpp InstallTestCrashCatcher) that appends to <engine source checkout> the exception, every loaded module and every word on the crashing stack that points into a module; `python crash_symbolize.py --pdb-dir <Ashvale_<version>_symbols of the CRASHED package>` resolves Game.dll offsets to function names with dbghelp (engine DLLs have no PDBs here: module+offset only). The first stack word after a null call is the CALLER. Cause found 2026-10-25: CNpcComponent::OnShutDown -> brain Stop -> CVillagerBrain::Abort -> FinishSleep -> CNpcComponent::Drive -> m_pCharCtrl->ChangeVelocity on a CCharacterControllerComponent that was already destroyed (vtable gone). Fix: OnShutDown sets m_pCharCtrl = nullptr first (Drive already returns on null). General rule: anything a brain does when it is stopped (Abort/Stop/Release) can run while the entity's other components are being destroyed: it must not drive the body. Crashes only occurred in tests that ran 3+ minutes (errands had started); a 30 s run never showed it; the WER history over 14 days had no GameLauncher crash before the NPC-life code (00:26 on 2026-10-25).

title: Tests that stand next to a villager or click the game window broke when villagers got errands and when the user browsed in front
source: examples/ashvale/gameplay_test.py, undercroft_playthrough.py, window_capture.py
content: After the NPC-life wave villagers walk to stations, so `ash_goto Oswin` can put the player beside lying coins and the economy checks read +2 coins: gameplay_test now sets `claude_npc_life 0` (master switch) after the new game. The undercroft kill loop only looked for '<name>: DIED' after its own swing started, but the sword hits whoever is nearest in its arc, so an enemy that died during ANOTHER enemy's turn counted as 'not killed' (Digger3): kill() now looks from the start of the whole fight (FIGHT_OFF). menus (ui_menu_test) and loading_screen_test refuse to click or capture when another window is on top of the game (window_capture: 'the window at (x, y) is <title>, not the game -- no click sent'): they fail, correctly, while the user has a maximised browser in front, and pass when the machine is left alone; this is not a game fault. A full shader record (`shader_cache_refresh.py` without --append) forgets the undercroft route: run `--append --only-undercroft` after it (39 misses before, 0 after); both need a Profile Game.dll newer than the sources (package profile build=true first) and a fresh CrySCompileServer (kill a stale one: its ShaderList_PC.txt was not written).

title: The stock AreaTrigger entity never fires Enter in a running game: use the Claude:AreaEvents flow node (proved in Release)
source: Code/Components/FlowNodes.cpp, server.py link_area_target / flow_graph_add, CryDefaultEntities TriggerEntity.cpp, DesignerEntityComponent.h
content: Chain proven 2026-10-25 in the packaged Release game (playground level): AreaBox pg_zone (BoxMin -5,-5,0 BoxMax 5,5,4) with the target entity pg_zone_trig (link_area_target) -> the player walks in (ash_hold w) -> the flow graph in the FlowgraphEntity pg_fg runs: Claude:AreaEvents.Enter -> Mission:GameTokenSet (Pg.Entered false -> true) and Engine:LayerSwitch Unhide pg_far (an entity in that layer: hidden 1 -> 0). Control: the same walk with the stock node `entity:AreaTrigger` changed nothing. Facts: (1) CTriggerEntity (the stock AreaTrigger) inherits CDesignerEntityComponent::GetEventMask = START_LEVEL | RESET | editor events, so ENTITY_EVENT_ENTERAREA never reaches its ProcessEvent and `entity:AreaTrigger.Enter` stays silent in the game (its bOnlyPlayers/faction filters exist only in the sample's Lua). The area manager DOES send ENTERAREA/LEAVEAREA to every target entity as an entity event (claude_area_listen <entity> logs them: 'ENTER by Player0 (area entity pg_zone)'): the game node Claude:AreaEvents (inputs Entity = target's NAME, Enable; outputs Enter/Leave with the EntityId) listens for them. (2) Only an entity with ENTITY_FLAG_TRIGGER_AREAS triggers areas: the player has it through its audio listener, NPCs do not. (3) The area box is BoxMin/BoxMax (an AreaBox object's Width/Length/Height edits do NOT change it: the exported Area component keeps the old BoxMin/BoxMax): set BoxMin/BoxMax with object_properties. (4) A TELEPORT (SetWorldTM without the POS reason, e.g. ash_goto_pos / PlaceFacing) does not register the player with the area manager: only a real move (ash_hold w) enters areas. (5) An area with ONE target delivered nothing in two runs; the same area with three targets delivered to the first: add a spare second target until this is understood (hypothesis: the resolve loop of CArea::ResolveEntityIds pushes into the vector it iterates). (6) link_area_target accepts any entity-holding object (Entity, EntityWithComponent ...); the target list is stored in the Area component's <Entities><Entity GUID=..>. Debug: es_DrawAreaDebug 2 (Profile) logs '<AreaManager> Area N Direct Event: ENTER'.

title: object_properties set changed the object but a save wrote nothing: the layer was never flagged modified (fixed in the bridge plugin)
source: Code/Sandbox/Plugins/ClaudeBridgePlugin/ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.object.set), world_build.save_level
content: Symptom: object_properties(name, {BoxMin: ...}) answered changed/not_applied [] and read back correctly, save_level answered saved true, and the .lyr file (and the next export, package, game) still held the OLD value; it only persisted when something else (a place_object, a delete) flagged the level or layer as modified. Cause: bridge.object.set loaded the edited XML back into the object (Serialize) but never called CBaseObject::SetLayerModified (what the editor's own undo does after loading an object back, BaseObject.cpp CUndoBaseObject). Fix 2026-10-25: after the load the verb calls SetLayerModified, SetModified(false, true) and IEditor::SetModifiedFlag; it also runs PostLoad for an `@FlowGraph=` child (an entity's flow graph is read in CEntityObject::PostLoad, not Serialize: before this a stored graph read back 0 nodes). Check any property edit by reading the layer file (the mtime of layers/*.lyr changes), not by the tool's answer. Layer flags (DefaultLoaded) set with layer.toggle_auto_load did NOT persist either: edit `<Layer ... DefaultLoaded="1">` in layers/<name>.lyr while the level is closed (open another level, edit the file, load the level again). object.get_object_layer / set_object_layer with a LIST argument crashed the editor (dialog 'Crash'): to put objects in a layer use layer.select(name) + layer.make_active() and then create them (place_object / create_object go to the active layer); answer the Crash dialog with 'No' (click_dialog_button).

title: Game tokens: a loose GameTokens folder is not loaded by a Release level load; make the library in the editor database
source: checks/gametoken_check.py, WorldTools.cpp claude_token, CryAction LevelSystem.cpp GameTokenLibs step
content: Measured 2026-10-25: tokens written by hand as Assets/levels/playground/GameTokens/pg.xml were packaged into GameData.pak and the PROFILE game loaded them at level load, but the RELEASE game held 0 tokens after the load (claude_token * = 0 held) while a later claude_token load playground (LevelSystem's own LoadLibs call on levels/<level>/GameTokens/*.xml) created them: the loader's step runs while the level's own pak is the one that is read. The supported route works in both: create the library in the editor's database with bridge.db.add_library gametoken <Lib> and bridge.db.import_library gametoken <Lib> <file.xml> (root GameTokensLibrary Name=<Lib>, children <GameToken Name Type Value LocalOnly>), bridge.db.save_library, then export_level: the exporter writes <level>/GameTokens/<lib>.xml INTO level.pak (lower-case gametokens/<lib>.xml; leveldata.xml gets GameTokensLibraryReferences). A library the editor knows is exported every time until the editor restarts (delete its scratch items; save_library writes Assets/<lib>.xml in the project root: delete that stray file). Types are Bool Int Float EntityId Vec3 String (case-sensitive); the flow node Mission:GameTokenSet takes gametoken_Token = Lib.Name; a listener registered on the token system is DROPPED at every level load (Unload frees m_listeners). Tools: gametoken_check(level) reads the loose folder AND the exported pack (G001-G011); claude_token <Lib.Name> [value] / * / load <level> in the game.

title: Layer streaming: with UseLayersActivation=1 every layer that is not DefaultLoaded is hidden, Main included; Engine:LayerSwitch Unhide proved
source: Assets/levels/playground, server.py flow_graph_add, WorldTools.cpp claude_entity
content: Measured 2026-10-25 in the packaged Release game (playground): with leveldata/environment.xml EnvState UseLayersActivation="1" the entities of a layer whose DefaultLoaded is 0 are created but HIDDEN (claude_entity: hidden 1), and that includes the level's Main layer (its AreaBox, AreaTrigger and the FlowgraphEntity were hidden 1 and nothing worked) until Main is DefaultLoaded="1" (edit the layer file: the layer toggle command does not persist). With UseLayersActivation="0" nothing is hidden and layers do nothing (pg_far's entity was hidden 0). With Main DefaultLoaded=1, pg_far DefaultLoaded=0 and the flow node Engine:LayerSwitch (Layer = pg_far) on Unhide, the entity in pg_far goes hidden 1 -> 0 when the player enters the area (proof chain: trap-stock-areatrigger-never-fires-use-claude-areaevents-2026-10-25). Brushes of an object layer were not probed (the probe is an entity). A new layer from layer.new is called New_Layer and starts DefaultLoaded 0. The level's environment.xml is rewritten by the editor on save: change it while another level is open.

title: WaterVolume in the packaged game: the surface is drawn, but GetWaterLevel stays at the ocean level (16) at three heights inside it
source: Assets/levels/playground (pg_pond), WorldTools.cpp claude_waterlevel, Cry3DEngine 3dEngine.cpp GetWaterLevel
content: A WaterVolume object (4 points at z 33, VolumeDepth 2, material materials/water/watervolumes/water_forest_a, over flat terrain at 32 m, level ocean at 16 m) is exported with the level (terrain.dat object tree, not the mission xml: CWaterShapeObject::Export returns null) and DRAWN in the packaged Release game (a pale-blue sheet seen from 27 m). But claude_waterlevel inside it (x 207 y 128, z 31.5 / 32.0 / 33.5, the player standing in it) always answers the ocean level 16.00: C3DEngine::GetWaterLevel(pos) takes the volume only from the physical world's buoyancy AREAS (m_pPhysicalWorld->CheckAreas, 3dEngine.cpp:2690), so no physics area exists for this volume (cause unknown: not yet tried a deeper volume, a volume whose bed is below the terrain, the Area component with Buoyancy{Medium Water}, or the e_WaterVolumes variable). Also: the new level's terrain is BLACK until its colour texture is baked (terrain_layers action bake), which made the picture dark.

title: Water in the game: an Area component (Medium Water) makes a physics area but GetWaterLevel ignores it; WaterVolume objects made none
source: Code/Components/WorldTools.cpp claude_waterlevel, Cry3DEngine 3dEngine.cpp:2690, CryDefaultEntities Physics/AreaComponent.cpp, Assets/levels/playground
content: Measured 2026-10-26 in the packaged Release game (playground; claude_waterlevel now also prints the physics areas that hold the point, i.e. what C3DEngine::GetWaterLevel asks via IPhysicalWorld::CheckAreas). Control: anywhere on the level the point is held by the OCEAN pair only (medium 0 water, plane origin 0,0,16 and medium 1 air). (1) WaterVolume object, surface 1 m above flat ground (pg_pond), and a second one 8 m deep over the ground (pg_pond2, surface 40, depth 8): both DRAW in the game but NO physics area holds a point inside them: GetWaterLevel stays at the ocean level 16. (2) The physics `Area` component (Schematyc category Physics, GUID ec7f145b-d48f-4863-b9c2-3d3e2c8dcc61; add with add_component; set Buoyancy.Medium Water, Density 1000, Resistance 1000): CAreaComponent::Physicalize builds a box from BoxSize as HALF extents centred 1 half-height ABOVE the entity (BoxSize 12,12,6 at z 33 holds x 248..272, y 116..140, z 33..45), and inside it CheckAreas returns the water medium with the plane normal FLIPPED to -z, so the physics sees water there; but its plane origin stays 0,0,16 and GetWaterLevel skips every area whose origin.x + origin.y is 0 ('it's not ocean'), so it still answers 16. For gameplay that needs 'is the player in this water' (PlayerSurvival's water rules read GetWaterLevel) use CheckAreas directly, or a game-side volume test, or a WaterVolume with a physics area that exists (not found yet: try one placed as an entity-attached volume / River object / ocean level raised with terrain.set_ocean_height). A point exactly on the box's lower face (z 33.0) was not inside (use the middle).

title: add_component works on EntityWithComponent objects: Projector Light and physics Area added with their members read back
source: server.py add_component
content: create_object('EntityWithComponent', name, pos) makes a real entity (place_object(kind='entity', asset='EntityWithComponent') made an object with HasEntity 0: a class that does not exist). add_component(entity, 'Projector Light'| class | GUID, values) adds the component and merges the values (read back, not_applied lists differences): Projector Light members Active, Radius, Angle (radians), ProjectorOptions{NearPlane, Texture, Material}, Optics{Enable, LensFlare ..}, Color{Color{r,g,b,a}, DiffMult, SpecMult}, Shadows{ShadowSpec ...}, Options{OnlyAffectThisArea (default TRUE: set false for an outdoor light), IgnoreVisAreas, GIMode ...}; the light points along the entity's forward: rotate with object_properties Rotate (w,x,y,z; 0.7071,-0.7071,0,0 points it down). Add CAshvaleMarkerComponent {Kind: PlayerStart} the same way for a level start. The effect of a cookie texture on the lit ground was not judged (daylight hid the cone in the picture).

title: Cut a hole in the terrain (cellar, shaft, cave mouth) with terrain_hole and prove it in the game with claude_ground
source: Code/Sandbox/Plugins/ClaudeBridgePlugin/ClaudeBridgePlugin.cpp (bridge.terrain.hole / is_hole), level/world_build.py terrain_hole, WorldTools.cpp claude_ground
content: Before 2026-10-26 a terrain hole could only be made with the editor's mouse brush (terrain.make_holes_tool). The plugin verbs bridge.terrain.hole <x> <y> <w> <h> <1|0> (world metres; CHeightmap::MakeHole, then the level is flagged modified) and bridge.terrain.is_hole <x> <y> and the MCP tool terrain_hole(x, y, width, height, make=True) cut or fill a rectangle and read it back (holes_in_rect == cells_in_rect, centre_is_hole; filling a sub-rectangle is the control). Steps: terrain_hole(60, 60, 6, 6) -> save_level -> export_level -> package -> in the game claude_ground 63 63 (nothing below: no collision) against claude_ground 70 70 (hit z 32, distance 268 from the 300 m start) and 58 63 (ground). Measured in the packaged Release game 2026-10-26: inside the hole no ground, 2 m outside ground. The hole is cell-sized (unit size of the heightmap, 1 m on a 256 m level). Not done: what the hole looks like (the terrain texture under it, a mesh to fill it) and the Minimap (the editor's Minimap Tool renders with the e_ScreenShotMap* cvars and a mouse tool; no verb).

title: prefab.new_prefab_from_selection eats the selected objects and the .prefab item file is saved EMPTY: do not use it headless
source: editor python sandbox.prefab / sandbox.selection, Assets/<item>.prefab
content: Measured 2026-10-26 in the editor: selection.clear + selection.select_object(name) x4 (accepts one name at a time; get_object_names lists them) then prefab.new_prefab_from_selection('pg_hutkit') returned None, the four brushes DISAPPEARED from the level (object count 21 -> 18) into a Prefab object at their centre, prefab.get_items() listed 'pg_hutkit.prefab' and has_item('pg_hutkit') was true, but Assets/pg_hutkit.prefab held `<Objects />` (empty) after save_level, update_all_prefabs, open_all and close_all, and the layer file only holds `<Object Type="Prefab" ...>` lines for the instances: a reload would show empty prefabs. prefab.new_prefab(itemName WITHOUT the .prefab extension, instanceName, x, y, z) places an instance and returns its name with a -1 suffix ('hutkit_b-1'); with the extension it fails ('Unable to create item'). delete_objects refuses names with '-' (letters, digits, _): remove instances with execute_python `sandbox.object.delete('name')`, and prefab.delete_item removes the item. The four brushes were recreated with place_object. Prefab authoring headless is NOT usable; use layers, groups or a code-side spawner until the asset's own editor save is understood. Related traps: object.get_object_layer / set_object_layer with a list crashes the editor.

title: A pfx2 Particle Emitter component and a Decal object placed in a level through the tools, seen in the packaged game
source: Assets/levels/playground (pg_fx, pg_decal), server.py add_component
content: Steps (2026-10-26): create_object('EntityWithComponent', 'pg_fx', pos); add_component('pg_fx', 'Particle Emitter'); component_properties('pg_fx', 'CParticleComponent', {'FilePath': 'particles/examples/omni/leaves.pfx'}) (a project .pfx under Assets/Particles; list with particle_search / find Assets -name *.pfx); create_object('Decal', 'pg_decal', pos) then object_properties set Material 'materials/decals/blood/blood_splat1', ProjectionType 2, Scale 3,3,3 (a decal projects into whatever lies within its box: put it a few cm above the surface). The Projector Light (add_component 'Projector Light', Radius 20, Angle 0.9, rotated down) could NOT be seen: the playground has only the engine's default.env (no night) and the shoot harness's time_of_day only drives the Ashvale presets, so the daylight hid it: judge lights in a level with a night preset or with the sun switched off. title: A vis area must enclose the pivots of its walls and roof: with the walls on the boundary the room showed sky from inside
source: Assets/levels/playground (visarea_hut, portal_hut_door, pg_hut_*)
content: Measured 2026-10-27 in the packaged Release game. A hut of seven cube brushes (walls 0.3 m thick centred ON the room's 8x6 m floor outline, roof centred over it) with a VisArea whose polygon was the floor outline passed visarea_check and claude_visarea said 'visarea_hut' inside, but standing inside and looking at the north wall showed ONLY SKY: the walls and the roof lie outside the area (their pivots are on or outside its edge), objects outside a vis area are drawn from inside only through a portal's opening. Fix: enlarge the area polygon so every wall and roof pivot is inside it (points 0.5 m beyond the wall centre lines, Height above the roof's top: 3.6 for a 3.3 m wall), and move the portal quad so it still crosses the NEW boundary edge (visarea_check stays clean: V003/V004). After that, from inside the room the dark walls, the ceiling and a bright floor patch are drawn (the whole interior). Rule for houses: area = outer faces of the walls plus a margin; props inside the room (pivots inside) belong to the room and are not drawn from outside unless a portal sees them. Not measured: the performance gain, the lighting rules (AffectedBySun, IgnoreSkyColor).

title: Load times and the day/night/storm look from the packaged game: game_levelloadtime.log and a shoot tour
source: Ashvale_final_profile/game_levelloadtime.log, the MCP server job shoot

title: Decisions: no minimap tool, no LiveCreate, no ACE reverb with SDL Mixer, no engine save path (and why)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content: Read from source 2026-10-27 and not built: MINIMAP: the editor's Minimap Tool is a mouse tool that renders through the 3D engine's screenshot-map mode (e_ScreenShotMap* cvars + an IScreenshotCallback, then a TIFF and RC conversion): no verb exists and none was written; a top-down image of the level is already available from the baked terrain texture (terraintexture.pak tiles, reassembled) or from a high editor camera, and Ashvale has a compass HUD. LIVECREATE: needs the LiveCreate plugin and a separate network session between the editor and the game; the project's build loop (package + shoot jobs, 1 minute) is the replacement; not worth it. ACE REVERB/OCCLUSION: the SDL Mixer implementation returns nullptr for environments (Impl.cpp:1049), so reverb zones cannot work with it; the audio chain stays SDL Mixer + the game's own distance gain. ENGINE SAVE PATH: CryAction's SaveGame refuses a component-based player (CryAction.cpp:3253): the project keeps its own XML saves (ashvale_slot1.xml, ashvale_auto.xml). If any of these is wanted later the recipes file has the steps.

title: Water for gameplay: GetWaterLevel misses a level's WaterVolume; read its physical area (foreign id 8): AshvaleWaterSurfaceAt
source: Code/Components/WorldTools.cpp AshvaleWaterSurfaceAt / claude_physareas / claude_waterlevel, PlayerSurvival.cpp
content: SOLVED 2026-10-27 (supersedes the open question of fact-water-physics-three-variants-measured-checkareas-2026-10-26). The level's WaterVolume objects DO create physical areas in the packaged game: claude_physareas x y z r (GetEntitiesInBox with ent_areas) lists them with foreign-data id 8 (PHYS_FOREIGN_ID_WATERVOLUME), a bounding box (x/y of the polygon, z from surface minus VolumeDepth to surface plus 10 m) and the plane origin whose z IS the surface (pond at z 33 -> 33.0; deep pond at 40 -> 40.0). C3DEngine::GetWaterLevel(pos) still answers the ocean (16) there because IPhysicalWorld::CheckAreas does not return them (CryPhysics has no source here: not explained), so the game reads the areas itself: AshvaleWaterSurfaceAt(pos) = max(GetWaterLevel, the plane origin z of every foreign-id-8 area medium 0 whose box holds the point and whose surface is at or above the point). Proven: inside the 8 m pond the answer is 40.00 at z 36, outside or above the surface it is 16 (the ocean), and the player standing in it logs 'survival: wading in deep water (7.8 m)' (PlayerSurvival now calls AshvaleWaterSurfaceAt). The volume is taken as its bounding box: exact for a rectangular pond; an irregular shape reports water over its box. The physics Area component's Medium Water area also exists (foreign id 2) but its plane origin stays (0,0,16): use WaterVolume objects for gameplay water. Rule for an AI building a level: WaterVolume object with 4+ points (UpdateGameArea needs more than 3), Material materials/water/watervolumes/..., then query AshvaleWaterSurfaceAt, not GetWaterLevel.

title: PLAYBOOK: hit zones (head, torso, arms, legs) from a data table: multiplier, reaction, limp, cripple (bodydamage.xml, claude_npc_hit)
source: Code/Components/BodyDamage.h, BodyDamageImpl.h (included at the end of NpcWave.cpp), Assets/libs/ashvale/bodydamage.xml, test_body_damage.py; packaged Release shoots 20261027_023312, _024022, _024223, _024344 (claude_npc.log '[BodyDamage]' lines, pictures in job_runs/*_shots)
content: The GameSDK's DATA model copied (Libs/BodyDamage: Part name+flags+Bone, a multiplier per part, a reaction per part), none of its GameDll code. Assets/libs/ashvale/bodydamage.xml: six parts head, torso, arm_l, arm_r, leg_l, leg_r, each with Bip01 bones (segment parent joint -> joint, extend, radius), multiplier (head 1.4, torso 1.0, arms 0.7, legs 0.8), reaction (auto|light|flinch|heavy|parry|knockdown), stagger 'light,heavy' seconds, limp 'light,heavy' seconds (legs 8,16), knockdown percent (legs 0,15), cripple = fraction of max health taken on that part after which the limp is permanent (legs 0.5). Code: BodyDamage::ResolvePart = the nearest bone segment of the character's CURRENT pose (distance minus the bone's radius); SwordPoint = where the view ray meets the NPC's vertical axis, lowered by bladeDrop 0.35 (the blade sweeps down). Player.cpp ApplySwordHit: ResolveBodyHit before Damage (amount x multiplier), ReactToBodyHit after (tally, limp, cripple, stagger with the part's reaction through CBanditBrain::Stagger / PlayStaggerReaction, which honours m_bodyState.szPendingReaction). A limp or a crippled leg makes CNpcComponent::EffectiveGait() return Injured (MotionBricks mb_walk_injured, run speed = the clip's x1.2); the old 'bandit below 33 percent health limps' rule reads injuredBelow from the same file. claude_body_damage 0 = the old uniform hit (torso keeps stagger 0.45/0.9 and reaction auto, so fights without aiming are unchanged). Test commands (-claude_test only): claude_npc_hit <npc> <head|torso|arm_l|arm_r|leg_l|leg_r|swing> [damage] [heavy] (a zone name aims at that part's reference point and logs MISMATCH if the resolver disagrees; swing = the player's real view ray), claude_npc_zone <npc> (the resolver's map of the body axis), claude_look <pitch deg> (a real ash_attack then meets another zone), claude_npc_limp <npc> <sec|crip|clear>, claude_npc_heal <npc>. The in-game measurements are in chunk measured-body-damage-zones-bodydamage-xml-claude-npc-hit-2026-10-27.
verified_note: Packaged Release 2026-10-27: zones, multipliers, reactions, limp, cripple, health-fraction gait by log; pictures of head (HitHeavy) and arm/leg flinches. Real-swing head/leg, gate tests with the new code and other levels not run.

title: TRAP: a shoot shot line 'name x y yaw' without z puts the player at the ASHVALE terrain height: in the playground he fell 158 m
source: job 20261027_022756 claude_npc.log: 'goto_pos: at 50.0 74.0 190.1', 'survival: fell 158.2 m, took 99 damage (health 1)'
content: shoot_game / start_job('shoot') computes the default feet height (terrain + 0.1) from the Ashvale heightmap, whatever level the game is in after '!claude_go playground pg_start'. Playground ground is z 32, Ashvale's there is about 190: the player was placed in the air and fell 158 m ('You land hard', health 1), the bandit then killed him, and every probe that used the player's eye (claude_cover_status: eye z 156.8) answered 0 spots for the wrong reason. Always give z explicitly after a level change: 'cvp 50 74 180 32'. A command that moves the player and a probe on the next line must be checked against the log line 'goto_pos: at x y z' before the result is trusted.

title: PLAYBOOK: AI cover proved: CoverSurface -> covermission0.bai -> ICoverSystem::GetCover -> a bandit runs to a hidden spot
source: Code/Components/CoverImpl.h (included at the end of BanditBrain.cpp), BanditBrain.h/.cpp (Cover state), playground objects cv_wall cv_surf_south cv_surf_north cv_navarea cv_bandit cv_tank, test_ai_cover.py; packaged Release shoots 20261027_022935, _023508 (claude_npc.log '[Cover]' lines, pictures c0..c4, side)
content: Steps that worked (playground, 2026-10-27): (1) a wall brush cv_wall (primitive_cube scaled 10 x 0.6 x 2.2 at z 33.1); (2) one CoverSurface object per FACE, 0.3 m in front of the face and looking at it: cv_surf_south at (50, 59.3) yaw 0, cv_surf_north at (50, 60.7) Rotate 0,0,0,1 (180 degrees); the sampler needs the wall within LimitDepth 0.75 m ahead and at least 0.85 m tall; (3) a NavigationArea (cv_navarea, create_navigation_area floor_z 28 height 12) and regenerate_navigation; (4) execute_editor_command('ai.generate_cover_surfaces') logs 'Loaded 2 AI Cover Surfaces' and writes the cover file, export_level packs it: level.pak holds covermission0.bai (184 bytes = 8 + 2 x (8 + 5 samples x 16); a level without cover objects has 8 bytes: test_ai_cover.py reads both). A cover surface belongs to ONE side: spots hidden from eyes on the north are the SOUTH face's. The game loads the file at level start (CAISystem::LoadCover). Game side: ICoverSystem* = gEnv->pAISystem->GetCoverSystem(); GetSurfaceCount / GetSurfaceInfo list surfaces and samples; GetCover(centre, range, &eye, 1, distanceToCover 0.5, locations[48], 48, maxPerSurface 12) returns floor positions HIDDEN from that eye. Each spot is then checked against the navmesh (FindNavPoint within 1.5 m) and by an INDEPENDENT physics ray from the eye to 1.2 m above the spot; the nearest reachable and ray-hidden spot is chosen. CBanditBrain::TakeCover -> EState::Cover: run to it (run speed), 'IN COVER' within 0.9 m, hold 6 s, then Chase. MEASURED in the packaged game: claude_cover_status: 2 surfaces, 5 samples each, height 2.15 m; 12 spots from a bandit 10 m from the wall, all 12 'BLOCKED (hidden)' by the ray and 12 navmesh-reachable, the nearest chosen. CONTROLS: a centre 100 m away returned 0 spots ('NO COVER'); the same bandit with the threat eye on the other side of the wall got 12 spots on the OTHER face (y 60.8 instead of 59.2); a 3 m range returned 0 and claude_npc_cover left the state alone. The bandit ran 15 m: 'IN COVER at 47.11 59.00 (0.89 m from the cover point), the player's eye cannot see him by a physics ray' (player 25 m away at 50,84); the picture 'side' shows him standing at the wall's south face. claude_bandit_cover <percent> (default 0) makes a bandit that is hit take cover; no gate test has fought with it on. NOT done: archers using cover in a real fight, peeking, flanking; the gate tests with the new Cover state were not run. Ashvale has no cover objects (0 surfaces): the natural control.
verified_note: Packaged Release 2026-10-27, playground only. Real combat with claude_bandit_cover on and the gate tests not run.

title: FACT: 'AI Cover User' registers in the game, but a C++ brain gets no CoverIDs from ICoverSystem: use GetCover positions and MoveTo
source: engine source CryAISystem/Components/Cover/CoverUserComponent.cpp:238-260, 438-458; CryCommon/CryAISystem/ICoverSystem.h:261-304, Components/IEntityCoverUserComponent.h; claude_cover_status line 'has a registered cover user'
content: add_component(entity, 'd3c6a814-dbee-4cb1-9322-9ac6028a3eb8') adds 'AI Cover User' (CEntityAICoverUserComponent: effectiveCoverHeight 0.85, inCoverRadius 0.3, distToCover 0.5, blacklistTime 10). In the packaged game ICoverSystem::GetRegisteredCoverUser(entityId) returned a cover user for the bandit that has it (params 0.30 / 0.50 / 0.85), so ENTITY_EVENT_START_GAME does start it; the bandit without it is the control (line 'has NO registered cover user' is in the code; not yet printed for cv_tank). Why the brain does not use it: GetRandomCover is a Schematyc-only function (it calls gAIEnv.pCoverSystem->GetCover(.., std::vector<CoverID>&), an internal overload); the public ICoverSystem::GetCover returns Vec3 positions, not CoverIDs; an ID is (surfaceID << 16) | a location index of the surface's interpolated path, which the public interface cannot enumerate; IEntityCoverUserComponent::MoveToCover(CoverID) then queues a Movement-system request, but this brain drives CEntityAINavigationComponent itself. So what works from C++ is positions + the body's MoveTo; the component is only worth adding for Schematyc graphs or behaviour trees that call it.
verified_note: Registration seen in the packaged game; the 'cannot get CoverIDs' reading is from the headers and source, MoveToCover was not tried.

title: TRAP: ICoverSystem::GetCover with maxLocationsPerSurface 0 ignores maxLocationCount and writes every spot it finds (a stack overflow)
source: engine source CryAISystem/Cover/CoverSystem.cpp:477-509
content: In CCoverSystem::GetCover the branch for maxLocationsPerSurface == 0 loops over every location in range and writes locations[outputCount++] without checking maxLocationCount; only the branch with a per-surface limit above 0 stops at maxLocationCount. A caller with a fixed array must pass a per-surface limit (CoverImpl.h uses 48 / 12). The spots returned lie on the face the surface was sampled from, distanceToCover (0.5) in front of the wall.

title: Level-authored colour grading: a preset, a colour chart and the flow nodes that switch them (editor-measured)
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
WHAT THE GAME ALREADY DRIVES: CAshvaleGame::UpdatePostEffects sets Global_User_Saturation/Brightness/Contrast/ColorY and FilterBlurring_Amount (hurt, dead, ending), read back with ash_post. Those are code. A LEVEL can grade by three data routes, none needs C++.
1) PRESET: the level's .env presets (leveldata/timeofday.xml). playground_env.py makes `pg_grade_cold` (Saturation 0.2, Color balance 0.6/0.8/1.0 all day, every other curve = ashvale_clear) with author_environment.author(), sets ashvale_clear as the default and adds ashvale_rain. In the game the flow node Environment:PresetSwitch (inputs Activate, Preset = the name as the level lists it, e.g. libs/environmentpresets/pg_grade_cold.env) calls ITimeOfDay::SetCurrentPreset. Measured (editor, noon, one view): control RGB 101.8/119.5/143.1 (repeat 101.8/119.6/143.2), cold preset 88.6/107.3/127.1, switching back 101.8/119.5/143.1 exactly. The effect of the HDR Saturation variable is MODEST (picture saturation 0.332 -> 0.316 although the variable went 1.0 -> 0.2): do not expect a black-and-white picture from it; the chart or the game's Global_User_Saturation does that.
2) CHART: a 256x16 lookup table. grading_chart.py <name> --saturation --tint --gamma --lift reads the engine's identity chart (EngineAssets/Textures/default_cch.dds in engine.pak, 16,512 bytes, X8R8G8B8, pixel (x,y) = R x%16, G y, B x//16) and writes the same file with the colours pushed through a function to Assets/textures/grading/<name>_cch.dds (control: its identity output is byte-identical to the engine's file). The manual's RGBChart.bmp route needs an attachment that is not offline. r_ColorGrading is already 2 and r_ColorGradingCharts 1: no CVar is needed; `r_ColorGradingChartImage textures/grading/pg_cold_cch.dds` loads it at once, and the flow node Image:ColorGradient (Trigger, tex_TexturePath, TransitionTime) calls IColorGradingCtrl::SetColorGradingLut. Measured (editor): cold chart R 101.8 -> 77.5, G 119.5 -> 109.6, B 143.1 -> 145.6; the identity chart 98.9/116.4/140.2 (3 levels off the control). Put the engine's default chart back with `r_ColorGradingChartImage EngineAssets/Textures/default_cch.dds`.
3) LEVEL ZONES: pg_gzone1/2/3 (AreaBox -> target entity -> FlowgraphEntity with Claude:AreaEvents.Enter -> PresetSwitch / ColorGradient) so a walk into a box regrades. The engine loaded the three graphs (flow_graph_add: 0 errors). A teleport enters no area: the shoot walks with `!ash_hold w`.
PROBE: `claude_grade` (game, -claude_test only) prints the current preset, the evaluated saturation / colour balance / EV / bloom, the grading CVars and the post-effect values. NOT YET SEEN in the packaged game. One unexplained editor crash (renderer access violation, CryRenderD3D11) happened while switching charts three times in a row; it did not repeat in the single-step rerun.
verified_note: Measured in the EDITOR viewport against a control and a repeat. The packaged game was not run for this (coordinator's instruction); the shoot script is the MCP server/pg_feature_shoots.py day.

title: Why the playground projector light showed nothing: default.env's 'night' is a 119,000 lux sun
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content: The earlier game test (slab mean RGB 103 with the light on against 119 off, `~claude_tod 0 0`) read the playground level, which listed only %ENGINE%/EngineAssets/Shading/default.env. Its curves, read out of engine.pak: Sun intensity 119,000 at hour 0 (243,854 at 6/12/18 h), Sky light sun multiplier 200 all day, EV Min 4.5, EV Auto compensation +1.5, Saturation 0.8 at night. So the 'night' there is half a noon sun: the white slab was already lit by 119,000 lux and a light of DiffMult 4 is a rounding error on it (the darker 'on' picture is auto exposure turning down for the brighter frame). No fault of the projector, the component, its Active flag or its radius. Cure: give the level a real night: playground_env.py adds libs/environmentpresets/ashvale_clear.env (sun 300 lux at night, EV Min 8.5, the project's measured look) as the level default (bridge.env.load, bridge.env.default, bridge.env.remove the engine default, save_level, export_level: the game reads the EXPORTED preset list). With it the same kind of light changes the picture by a factor of 3.4 (wall 70.9 against 21.0). Control worth keeping in mind: judge a light only after reading the sun and EV Min of the preset the level really holds (env_check, env_variables); the old chunk trap-bright-night-default-env says the same about a bright night.
verified_note: Explanation from the engine's own default.env (read out of engine.pak) plus the editor control. The old game picture (slab 103 on / 119 off) was not repeated.

title: add_component twice adds a second Point Light; Optics.Enable set via component_properties did not persist
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
1) Running add_component(entity, 'Point Light', ...) a second and third time on pg_lt_point did NOT refuse: the saved main.lyr held three CPointLightComponent blocks (the first with my values, two with defaults: Radius 10, DiffMult 1, OnlyAffectThisArea true). The tool text says a singleton is refused; a light is not a singleton. Check: grep the object in the .lyr for TypeName, or entity_check. Fix: delete_objects the entity and create it again, add the component once. playground_features.py is not idempotent for components for that reason (it refuses an existing OBJECT, not an existing component).
2) Point Light and Projector Light default to Optics.Enable true with an empty LensFlare; level validate then writes '[Error] Resource File textures/lights/lens_flare1.tif not found' (the engine's default flare texture is not in the project). component_properties(entity, 'CPointLightComponent', {'Optics': {'Enable': False}}) reads back False, but after save_level the .lyr still said Enable="true" and project_audit reported O003 (file true, live false) for five lights: that property did not persist. Open: set it in the Inspector, or leave the warning (harmless: it concerns a resource, the light itself works).
3) object_properties {'Pos': ...} does not move an object (not_applied empty, position unchanged): delete and place again, or teleport_entity for entities.
verified_note: Measured in the layer file main.lyr and object_check O003.

title: The impact table as engine MaterialEffects data (SpreadsheetML + FX library), written and checked by materialfx.py
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
WHAT THE GAME HAD: Sfx.cpp (ImpactFor: wood, metal, glass, vegetation, soil, stone by a strstr chain on the surface type name; 15 footstep surfaces; flesh sounds) and Blood.cpp OnWorldHit (4 particle effects by the same kind of chain). Hard-coded C++: a new surface or a decal means a rebuild; no decals, no per-weapon row.
THE ENGINE'S WAY (CryAction/MaterialEffects, read 2026-10-27): libs/materialeffects/materialeffects.xml = an Excel SpreadsheetML workbook read with IXmlTableReader. Row 0: the surface types as COLUMNS (SurfaceTypes.xml names; an unknown one is skipped with a warning). Rows 1..n (n = the number of columns) are the surface-vs-surface block (first cell = a row label). Rows AFTER that are CUSTOM rows: first cell a name ('ash_blade'), each column's cell '<library>:<effect>'. If the surface block has fewer rows than there are columns, a custom row is silently read as a surface row and never found (checker code M008). libs/materialeffects/fxlibs/<library>.xml defines effects: <Effect name delay><Audio trigger/><Particle><Name>ashfx.hit_wood.hit</Name></Particle><RandEffect><Decal minscale maxscale lifetime><Material/></Decal></RandEffect>. The engine calls CMaterialEffects::CompleteInit itself (CCryAction::CompleteInit and after a level's static world): the project only ships the two files. Code: IMaterialEffects* gEnv->pMaterialEffects; GetEffectId("ash_blade", surfaceIdx) then ExecuteEffect(id, SMFXRunTimeEffectParams{pos, normal, dir, trgSurfaceId, trgRenderNode/trg}). AshvaleMfx::Impact (Components/FeatureProbes.cpp) does that, sets the sfx gain parameter first, and returns false when the cell is empty so StrikeWorld keeps the old Sfx/Blood response.
TOOL: assets/materialfx.py write (the tables ROWS and EFFECTS in the file are the data; ash_blade has 13 cells, ash_arrow 8, 10 effects) and check (rules M001-M008: column not a surface type, too few surface rows, missing library/effect, audio trigger not in claude_sfx.xml, particle effect in no libs/particles library, decal material without .mtl, unused effect, custom row read as surface row). test_materialfx.py: 14 checks incl. a positive control per rule.
ENGINE READ-BACK (editor, `mfx_Debug 1` then `mfx_Reload`): '[MFX] RowCount=20 MaxCol=17', then 13 lines for row 18 (ash_blade: stone on concrete and rock, metal, leaf on vegetation and canopy, soil on soil/grass/snow, wood on wood and wood_breakable, flesh, glass on both glasses) and 8 for row 19 (ash_arrow); mat_default, mat_water, mat_fabric, mat_plastic resolve to nothing (those blank cells are the control). PROBES in the game (-claude_test only): claude_mfx_info (the same table as the game sees it, GetEffectIdByName control 'no_such_effect' must be 0), claude_mfx_hit [row] [surface] (ray from the camera, executes the cell; a forced surface name reaches mat_flesh with its blood decal). Stations: walls pg_mfx_wood/metal/stone/cloth (cloth = no cell).
verified_note: PARTIAL: the engine's real loader resolved the table in the editor (mfx_Debug 1 + mfx_Reload). The game call (Player.cpp StrikeWorld -> AshvaleMfx::Impact) and the claude_mfx_hit probe COMPILED (Release Game.dll 2026-10-27 06:52) but have not run: no packaged-game proof yet.

title: A UI element drawn on a mesh: UIElement PgBoard plus a material with Diffuse PgBoard.ui, TexType 5
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content:
Manual 'UI Dynamic Textures': the Diffuse texture of a material is '<UIElement name>.ui' (or 'Name@InstanceID.ui') with TexType 'Dynamic 2D-Map'. In the engine: CFlashTextureSourceBase::IsFlashFile treats a name WITHOUT a path and with extension .ui as a pseudo file looked up in the UI database (Texture.cpp:3012); TexType attribute in the .mtl is a name or the number 5 (eTT_Dyn2D, MaterialHelpers.cpp:368). A name WITH a path may also end in .gfx/.swf/.usm/.layout (a movie straight from the file system).
WHAT WAS MADE: Assets/libs/ui/UIElements/PgBoard.xml = MainMenu.xml with the element renamed PgBoard and its input flags off (same movie Menus_Startmenu.gfx, so its OWN player instance: the game's menus are untouched). Assets/materials/ashvale/pg_board.mtl: Shader AshFlat, GenMask 0 (the permutation the shader cache already holds), <Texture Map="Diffuse" File="PgBoard.ui" TexType="5"/>. A 4.8 x 0.1 x 2.7 cube `pg_board` at (200,14). The probe `claude_ui_board [hidden]` (game, -claude_test) Init()s the element, calls SetupScreen('NOTICE BOARD', true, 12, -200, 0, 40) and three AddButton calls (the movie builds screens from calls), and with `hidden` keeps the element off the screen so only the texture shows it. CONTROL: the board picture BEFORE the probe (the element has no screen) against after.
ENGINE EVIDENCE without the game: ui_check live says the engine kept PgBoard with 57 functions and loaded its movie; level validate warned 'UI-Element identifier "PgNoSuchElement" can't be found in the UI-Database' for a deliberately missing twin material and said nothing for PgBoard: the renderer really asks the UI database by that name. TOOLS TAUGHT: asset_lint Names.exists and material_check.compare know the .ui pseudo file (L003 only when no element of that name exists; material_check M009; M006/M008 skip it); tests extended (test_asset_lint ui_ok/ui_missing, test_material_check 2 checks, test_ui_check counts one movie per element). TRAP: the editor material loader reports M006 'texture not bound' for a .ui texture: that is not an error. A deliberately broken twin material in the project fails lint L003: use before/after of the same board as the control, not a second broken file.
verified_note: PARTIAL: element loaded by the engine and its movie asked (ui_check live: 2 movies, 57 functions, no error); the picture on the mesh is NOT seen (game only). The probe claude_ui_board compiled into Release Game.dll.

title: Proving a light, grade or chart in the editor viewport: retake flat frames, mask icons, sky ratio, a repeat
source: Measured in the originating project; the notes it was written from are not in this repository
content: python playground_editor_proofs.py lights | grade | grade_preset | grade_chart | embers (editor open on the playground; it sets `claude_tod` and restores 15 h / the engine's default chart). Method: debug_views.shoot(stem, eye, target) gives an editor viewport PNG (about 488 x 284). (1) A flat grey frame is an undrawn viewport: reject it when the standard deviation of the INTERIOR (10-90 %) is under 4, retake up to four times; a whole-frame test passed a flat frame once because of its border line. (2) Every view is taken twice: the repeat is the noise floor (the wall luminance repeated within 0.1). (3) Mask the editor's blue entity icons (B - R > 70) before averaging. (4) Exposure moves with the scene, so also give wall/sky (the sky strip, top tenth) next to the absolute value. (5) Preset switching in the editor: bridge.env.current <preset path>; the editor viewport has no game post effects. Limits: it does not draw the particle emitters of the level (see the GPU chunk), and one renderer access violation happened in a long run of chart switches.

title: A mesh with a .ui / .gfx dynamic texture is not drawn at all until EnablePerFrameRendering(true) allocates the texture (proved in the game)
source: jobs 20261027_105320/105524/110313/110751/111007/111254/111520 (Profile and Release), RenderDll ShaderResources.cpp:829-843, RenderView.cpp:2507-2522, Texture.cpp:2588-2670, FeatureProbes.cpp CmdUiBoard
content: SYMPTOM: a brush whose material has Diffuse '<Element>.ui' (or a path to a .gfx) with TexType 5 (Dynamic 2D-Map) is NOT DRAWN AT ALL (no colour, no black; claude_ground proves it exists) while a plain-plaster control next to it draws. The engine log has no warning. CAUSE (source, then measured): CShaderResources::RT_UpdateResourceSet returns early ('flash texture has not been allocated yet') while the dynamic source's GetTexture() is null, so the object is skipped. The texture is allocated only by CFlashTextureSourceBase::Update(), whose callers are (1) the shader-item update list, which only holds materials whose diffuse TexMod has an animated rotate/move, and (2) FlashTextureSourceSharedRT_AutoUpdate::TickRT, which only calls it while m_perFrameRendering is true. MEASURED: (a) a TexMod with TexMod_RotateType=1 (fixed) did NOT help (the board stayed invisible, jobs 20261027_110751); (b) calling IDynTextureSource::EnablePerFrameRendering(true) on the material's diffuse source DID: before the call GetTexture() was null, one call later it was '$Dyn_FlashTextureSourceUniqueRT_2D_R8G8B8A8' 1280x720 and both boards drew (the .gfx route shows the movie's text 'BUTTON CAPTION' / 'Tooltip'; the .ui route showed the game's own map (Libs/UI/Textures/ashvale_map.dds added with AddImage) once the sun lit the board, TOD 16:00; at TOD 12 the same boards read black/dark because the face was in shade, see the lighting note; seen in the Profile build AND in the packaged Release build, job 20261027_111948_shoot at TOD 16, same pictures). Game code (FeatureProbes.cpp CmdUiBoard): IMaterialManager::LoadMaterial(path) -> GetShaderItem().m_pShaderResources->GetTexture(EFTT_DIFFUSE)->m_Sampler.m_pDynTexSource->EnablePerFrameRendering(true), the same walk as CryScaleformSchematyc ElementFunctions.cpp PerFrameRender; no flash source is created until the material loads, the call is needed once per source after the level loaded. LIGHTING NOTE: a board in shade reads dark; the Emittance attribute (Emittance="1,1,1,6") does NOT fix it, it adds a flat grey wash that hides the picture (emittance is not multiplied by the dynamic texture without an emittance map). Other traps found on the way: the AshFlat test shader ignores the material; with a texture attached the element is drawn ONLY into the texture (CFlashUIElement::Render skips the screen when HasExtTexture) and AddTexture sets it visible, so `claude_ui_board hidden` can never work; a UIElement's AddImage takes the movie-relative path (Libs/UI/Textures/ashvale_map.dds).

title: PLAYBOOK: a tool says the editor is not open (connection refused) - the editor is gone or crashed: what recovers it, what it loses
tags: tool says the editor is not open
source: Playbook written from the project's measured findings
content:
Full title: PLAYBOOK: a tool says the editor is not open (connection refused) - the editor is gone or crashed: what recovers it, what it loses, what to rerun
With CLAUDE_AUTO_RECOVER=1 (off by default) a tool that needs the editor restarts it by itself: a refused connection triggers bridge_watchdog.recover(), which runs the scheduled ClaudeBridgeWatchdog task (Sandbox must be started from the Task Scheduler's context: one started by a tool's own process dies when that process tree ends), waits until the bridge answers AND the level is loaded, then the tool's call is retried once (about 25 s). It waits instead of launching when a deploy or an editor-closing job (package, shoot, tests) is running. wait_for_editor does the same on request. The scheduled watchdog (every 5 minutes) kills a Sandbox that does not answer: at once when error.log was written after it started (a crash), after two strikes otherwise. WHAT A RESTART LOSES: unsaved level changes (a graceful close saves, a kill does not), the navmesh until the level has been exported once, runtime registrations such as the Claude Status pane, the time of day (the watchdog re-applies 15.0 h), a Python global state. A known cause of crashes is the GPU driver after the displays blank (Windows turns them off after a period without input): keep the machine awake during long unattended runs. After a crash rerun the tests that fell in the window by name (python bridge/editor_suite.py <test names>); a suite run that meets a crash fails those tests by construction. Never leave scratch objects in the level: a graceful close saves them (object_props.scratch deletes in finally).
